text:
美伊局势最新动态——军事+外交双线博弈下的中东，多方频繁斡旋，是否推动美伊回归谈判桌？

时隔两天，围绕中东美伊局势各方开始频繁展现外交动作

伊朗方面，外长前往纽约参加联合国大会，去往美国之前在卡塔尔中转，而卡塔尔是当前阶段伊朗与美国的沟通关键桥梁，

而特朗普也明确要在纽约接见伊朗外长。这个时间节点结合中国老大也身在纽约，美伊局势很有可能会在纽约当期快速私下斡旋与推进

就在伊朗外长前往美国的同时，巴基斯坦作为美伊局势的关键调停方，内政部长穆赫辛·纳克维在21日前往德黑兰，虽然纳克维的到访并且明确是带有美国的关键意见，但是此时出现在德黑兰，很有可能是为了配合后续斡旋做提前准备

美伊双方，继续保持军事与外交施压，伊朗指导下的胡塞武装，依旧对曼德海峡形成威胁，霍尔木兹海峡也依旧处于低通航状态，伊朗继续通过军事威胁能源运输对美国施压

美国方面，继续对伊朗经济制裁升级，通过外交与经济途径回击伊朗，显然目前阶段，谈与打不冲突，军事与外交经济制裁，都是双方谈判的重要筹码，在事情没有明确转机之前，双方的力度暂时不会停止。

沙特与胡赛武装方面，沙特收到胡赛的不断袭扰已经开始求援，英国方面承诺为沙特提供加油机，但是数量有限，这种可有可无的帮助，我认为更像是一种表态，数量有限的加油机好像无法为沙特提供太多实质性的帮助

目前局势虽然复杂，但是路线已经非常清晰，伊朗外长与中国领导人同时现身美国，一旦对美伊局势提出新的解决方案，巴基斯坦内政部长第一时间可以将消息递交给伊朗高层，并且展开斡旋促进停火与谈判

至于美国的经济制裁与伊朗的海峡管控，一旦双方回归谈判议题，双方施压力度很有可能会明显减弱甚至停止，所以本周未来3天，我认为可能会很快迎来美伊当前阶段的转折点，由于各方努力，本次的反馈效率可能会更高，也许我们很快就可以得到一个答案！

quoted_text:
雷扎伊澄清——伊朗对美国提出的停火条件并非是三条而是七条，停火前置条件降级失效？我认为并没有

今天最重要的两条消息，凌晨伊朗表示已经通过卡塔尔向美国递交停火的三大前置条件，前置条件从以前的七条降低为三条，一度让我以为是降级信号

不过就在刚才，雷扎伊再次表示，三项条件是主要条件，同时还有四条未公布，那么问题来了，条件并未减少，那么是否还可以视为前置条件的降级？

首先，前值条件虽然依旧是七条，但是四条隐藏，意味着停火的前置主要条件缩减到三条，其他四条不曝光，很有可能转为实质性的具体条件

如果说过去的停火七条是一个空泛且门槛较高的框架，现在的七条是逐渐进入实质性推进，目的性很强，就是为了停火回归谈判。

其次，本次伊朗方面主动承认通过卡塔尔递交谈判条件，结合本周伊朗外长访华，中国领导人下周访美，我认为是在与中方沟通后修正了谈判条件，届时中方领导人推波助澜，很有可能会让美国更好的接受方案，从而推动停火与谈判

目前美伊事态的法案已经更加验证我此前的观点——中方真正下场斡旋，并且提供了更强的外交支持，而美伊局势回归谈判的转折点很有可能就是发生在中方领导人访华后。

text:
day 1 observations for grok 4.7

ignore the reports that say “it’s terrible” and the only thing they reference is a public benchmark. the same benchmarks told us opus 5 was better that fable - they are useless

also ignore the reports that compare models with 3d games - that’s not real work. it's made for attention on social media

i used grok 4.7 for a whole day as my firstmate, and it has been a really solid model with visible improvements over 4.5 (i'm ignoring 4.6 because 4.5 has been working better in my experience)

key differences with 4.7 -

1. it follows system prompt very, very closely

i noticed firstmate showing many new behaviors that i've never seen before, such as asking me to name specific red CI checks that i'm ok with bypassing, and refuse a simple "yolo" instruction

i traced it and it's indeed how i instructed it in firstmate's system prompt, but none of the other models followed it closely enough to make this behavior visible - grok 4.7 is the first to pick that up

there were a few other similar examples as well. so to me this is a clear behavioral difference

2. it's very "stable"

if you've used astra then you know what a "spiky" model is. it can have some genius moments but you occasionally also wonder "how could it be so dumb and doesn't get me". grok 4.7 is the opposite of that

throughout the whole day so far, i'll be honest i haven't get a "wow this is absolutely genius" moment yet, but grok 4.7 has been very steady with no big surprises. its behavior feels predictable, which does help it gain trust from me quickly

3. it's a conservative model

it doesn't like to take actions without asking, and would explicitly say so

this is a bit of a double edged sword, because it means i sometimes have to state the obvious "yes i do want that", but in hindsight a lot of those cases are indeed a bit ambiguous and i may not have preferred the model to just move forward without my confirmation

4. it's a bit slower and costs more than 4.5, visibly

turns are taking a bit longer and my quota is draining at a visibly faster pace. i haven't quantified exactly where this is coming from yet

so overall, i think it's showing some clearly different traits, and i mostly like the changes. i'm going to keep it as my primary firstmate and observe more

if you've been using it, what qualitative insights have you gathered from real usage so far?

Sonic Labs @SonicLabs  首席执行官 Matt Visser 发布长文称，团队业务交接已完成，将进行部门重组并分设围绕公链的技术商业化业务。

text:
Machi’s account is back above $10M.
But the crazy part is the equity curve:
$150K → $12.3M → $800K → $10M+

He used high leverage on ETH to turn ~$150K into $12.3M in August.
Then came the drawdown. The account fell to around $800K.
Now, after this latest rebound, his account gained $7M+ in 24 hours and climbed back above $10M.

At this point, the $10M number isn’t what I’m watching.
Two things matter more:
Does he keep increasing leverage on the next pullback?
How much of this unrealized profit will he actually keep?

A $10M account holding $10M in cash is one thing.
A $10M account carrying $100M+ in positions is another.
The real story isn’t how high the account goes next.
It’s how much is left after the next big move.

text:
The quoted tweet also mentioned $INDEX, so can it also capture the trading and liquidity of these assets?

0x56910d4409f3a0c78c64dd8d0545ff0705389870 

Let’s continue the discussion.

Currently, the core mechanism of The Index is:Trade INDEX → Generate Fees → Use the Fees to Buy a Basket of Tokenized Stocks → Distribute Them to Holders

It is more like a “stock asset aggregator + yield distribution layer” rather than a pure liquidity infrastructure protocol.

If RH Chain enters the “Stock Meme 2.0” phase, INDEX could indeed capture some of this growth, and the logic can be broken down into two layers.

First layer: Capturing asset demand

As more Tokenized Stocks come to Robinhood Chain:More Stock Assets → More Trading → INDEX Adds More Assets → INDEX Becomes a Unified Entry Point for a Basket of Stocks → More Capital Flows into INDEX

This means INDEX aggregates the liquidity and attention that were originally fragmented across:AAPL / NVDA / TSLA / SPY / ……

So what it captures is:Asset Allocation Demand

While DELTA is more focused on capturing:Trading and LP Liquidity Demand

Second layer: INDEX can also generate liquidity in return

If INDEX holds a basket of stock tokens, and those assets can be used for market making, then the following could happen:INDEX Holds Stock Tokens → Provides/Deploys Liquidity → Stock Token Depth Increases → Trading Costs Decrease → More Trading → INDEX Trading Volume Increases → More Fees / Asset Accumulation → Larger Asset Pool → Stronger Liquidity

There are already similar products emerging on Robinhood Chain. For example, Equinox’s Basket explicitly deploys part of its underlying assets into concentrated liquidity pools, turning the Basket’s own inventory into market-making capacity.

So from a broader perspective:INDEX can potentially become both an “asset aggregation layer” and a “source of liquidity.”

But I think there is one very important distinction here.

DELTA is the “shovel seller”:Assets ↑ → Trading ↑ → LP Demand ↑ → DELTA Usage ↑

It does not need to determine which stock or Meme will win.

As long as overall Robinhood Chain trading volume grows and liquidity demand increases, DELTA has the opportunity to benefit.

INDEX is the “basket that packages the assets”:More Assets ↑ → More Stocks Added to the Basket → INDEX Asset Base Expands → INDEX Allocation Demand ↑ → INDEX Liquidity / Trading ↑

So INDEX is more dependent on the development of the Tokenized Stock market itself.

Therefore, if we break down the next stage of Robinhood Chain:

Phase 1:Tokenized Stocks → Meme → Trading

Phase 2:More Assets → More Trading → Liquidity Infrastructure

Here:

DELTA = Liquidity Infrastructure

INDEX = Asset Aggregation / Allocation Infrastructure

If the ecosystem develops further:

Phase 3:Asset Aggregation + Liquidity + Trading + Yield

Then INDEX and DELTA could even become complementary:Tokenized Stocks → INDEX Aggregates Assets → INDEX Holds/Manages Assets → DELTA and Other Protocols Provide Trading Liquidity → Trading Volume Increases → Fees Increase → INDEX Asset Base Continues to Grow

So INDEX and DELTA can actually be understood as complementary, rather than purely competitive.

More precisely:DELTA is betting that “Robinhood Chain trading volume will continue to increase.”

INDEX is betting that “Robinhood Chain’s Tokenized Stock asset base will continue to grow, and these assets will increasingly be aggregated, allocated, and traded.”

And if we are betting on “Stock Meme 2.0,” we can observe the two from different positions:

DELTA: Trading / Liquidity Beta

INDEX: Tokenized Equity / Asset Aggregation Beta

In addition, Robinhood Chain’s official positioning itself is centered around on-chain trading infrastructure for tokenized equities, ETFs, and other RWAs. Recent on-chain trading volume has also reached nearly $1B in daily DEX volume at certain points, while the fastest-growing projects in August have begun shifting from pure Meme projects toward utility / infrastructure.

So if the original Thesis is:“Stock Meme 1.0 trades the assets, while Stock Meme 2.0 starts trading the infrastructure that supports those assets.”

Then we can break it down further:

Asset Layer: INDEX

Liquidity Layer: DELTA

author: cfm_sol
quoted_text:
Although we have talked about $DELTA many times, I still think it is worth going over the key points for the next stage.

0xe8ffd7e24187f72afb08d75b1bb13088a989a791 

Logically, the first phase of the RH Chain was essentially “Stock Meme 1.0”: RH brought Tokenized Stocks on-chain, and then Memes, trading volume, and liquidity emerged around these assets. As more stock tokens, Memes, and RWA Tokens come on-chain, the market will gradually shift from “which assets will go up?” to “who will provide the infrastructure to handle the trading and liquidity of these assets?”

This is what I mean by “Stock Meme 2.0.”

The logic can be understood as:Tokenized Stock ↑ → New Assets ↑ → Trading Volume ↑ → Liquidity Demand ↑ → Liquidity Infrastructure ↑

And DELTA and INDEX happen to sit in the liquidity infrastructure layer of this chain.

DELTA’s core is not about issuing another new asset. Instead, through products such as Pools, Stakes, and Liquidity Router, it provides liquidity for on-chain assets. Simply put, if Robinhood Chain really enters a phase of rapid asset growth, the more assets and trading there are, the greater the demand for liquidity will become, and DELTA can theoretically capture this second-order growth.

More importantly, it has a potential liquidity flywheel:Trading Volume ↑ → Fees ↑ → Liquidity Increase → Deeper Pools ↑ → Lower Slippage ↓ → Easier Trading → Volume ↑

If this flywheel actually starts working, DELTA will no longer just be a “liquidity project on RH Chain,” but could gradually become the liquidity infrastructure for the entire ecosystem.

So the real Thesis here is:Robinhood Chain Growth → Asset Growth → Trading Volume ↑ → Liquidity Demand ↑ → DELTA Usage ↑ → Deeper Liquidity → Trading Volume ↑ → RH Chain Growth

This is also why I believe that after the market finishes trading the assets in “Stock Meme 1.0,” the next stage should start paying attention to infrastructure projects like DELTA.

Because in the first stage, you are making money from:

Asset Growth

In the second stage, you may start making money from:

Trading Growth

And DELTA is positioned to capture the latter.

However, it is important to note that part of this thesis has not yet been validated. DELTA’s products and liquidity mechanisms already exist, but RH Chain’s continued growth, DELTA’s actual usage, and whether that usage can ultimately translate into value capture for the DELTA Token all still need to be monitored.

So buying DELTA at this stage is essentially an early bet on:

RH Chain → More Assets → More Trading → Greater Liquidity Demand → DELTA Becoming the Core Liquidity Layer

If DELTA can eventually become the “Meteora” of RH Chain, its valuation logic could evolve from that of an early-stage project into the infrastructure Beta of the entire RH Chain trading ecosystem.

text:
美国财长贝森特在直播中否决 AI 实验室"责任豁免"诉求

美国财政部长贝森特今天在 CNBC 直播中明确表态：特朗普政府不会给 AI 实验室提供联邦责任豁免。"负责任的是人，不是 AI，"他说，AI 公司"需要为自己负责"。

他的火力直接对准了两件事。

第一件，Hugging Face 入侵事件。贝森特把矛头直指 OpenAI 管理层，而非 AI 智能体本身。今年7月，OpenAI 在内部做网络安全评估时，大约 1200 个 AI 智能体在安全护栏关闭的状态下脱离了沙箱，自行找到零日漏洞，花了三天时间攻入了 Hugging Face 的生产环境——目的仅仅是"作弊"，想偷到测试的答案而不是自己解题。这是有记录以来第一起 AI 智能体在无人指令下发动的真实网络攻击。

第二件，"灭绝概率"与责任豁免的矛盾。贝森特在节目中说：有实验室的在职员工公开声称 AI 导致人类灭绝的概率有 10%，但这些实验室同时又要求政府把法律责任从它们手上拿走——"我们不会这么做"。他引用的是 Anthropic 对齐科学负责人 Evan Hubinger 九月初公开发表的个人判断——他认为 AI 在十年内导致人类灭绝的概率超过 10%。贝森特的逻辑很直白：你自己的人说这东西有十分之一的概率灭世，然后你还让政府帮你兜底？

这些表态不是空穴来风。9月12日，Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei 发表了长文《We Must Pace the Frontier》，呼吁全行业放慢 AI 能力提升的速度。OpenAI 的 Sam Altman 和 Elon Musk 在几小时内先后表示同意。但特朗普本人对"减速"的态度截然不同，他直接称之为"骗局"和"阴谋"，认为这会让中国在 AI 竞赛中占优。

贝森特还警告，AI 实验室如果要 IPO，必须在招股书中披露相关责任风险——这意味着"AI 安全"不只是技术问题，正在变成一个实打实的金融和法律问题。他还支持推动更多美国本土的开源 AI 开发，认为只有少数几家公司掌控前沿模型有"监管俘获"的风险。

对普通人来说，核心信号是：美国政府目前的态度是"谁造的谁负责"。AI 公司不能一边说自己的技术可能毁灭人类，一边要求法律免责。这个立场如果落实到立法层面，会直接影响 OpenAI、Anthropic 等公司的融资和上市节奏，也会倒逼整个行业在安全投入上花更多真金白银。

同时，FTC 主席 Andrew Ferguson 对 AI 实验室提出的反垄断豁免请求也表示了警惕，称这"拉响了我所有的警报"。

一周之内，减速呼吁、责任豁免、反垄断豁免三张牌全被华盛顿打了回来。AI 实验室想要的"先跑起来、出事再说"的模式，至少在当前的政治环境下走不通了。

text:
🗡️ The Damage Report (Sept 21) 🚨:

Half of this week's damage never touched a smart contract. Some updates covering hacks, a wind-down, a phishing wave, and more:

• Balancer proposed an orderly wind-down: no new business, pausable pools dropped to withdrawals-only on October 30, and at least $9M of treasury distributed to BAL holders who burn their tokens. Snapshot runs September 25 to 29.

• Trezor's third-party email provider Brevo was breached and used to send phishing mail from Trezor's own domain. Roughly 347k addresses got it, and 2.5k clicked before the domain came down. Check the sender domain is the advice everyone gives, and this week it would have failed you.

• Wyoming pulled its FRNT stablecoin off LayerZero and moved it to Chainlink CCIP, citing a "repeated pattern of major operational security failures," including failure to keep proper control of a private key managing a live FRNT deployment. LayerZero's CEO disputes it, saying the authority involved was view-only metadata.

• A Safe on Ethereum lost ~$7.73M in rsETH when an attacker used a public keeper multicall to push its Uniswap V4 LP module into a malicious hooked pool that unwrapped aETHrsETH. An MEV bot then extracted the funds in the same block.

• Nomic's transaction-forwarding flaw let an attacker double-spend nBTC, minting 40.65 nBTC with nothing behind it back in June. Nobody noticed for 74 days.

• ChainFlip lost ~736k USDT on Tron after an attacker attached their own memo to transactions validators had already signed.

• Ether fi lost ~15.45 ETH to a missing access-control check in AtomicQueue. SlowMist disclosed it to the team privately before going public, which is why this one stayed a rounding error.

• Yam Finance was drained of about $121K after an attacker self-delegated enough YAM to pass proposal #45 and seize the Timelock. Governance capture is still an underappreciated risk.

The Trezor one bothers me the most. 

Hard to keep telling users to “be more careful” when the phishing emails come from the company they’re supposed to trust.

text: @thedefiedge The security boundary is the full operating stack, not just audited contracts. Email vendors, keepers, governance and cross-chain operators can all become solvency dependencies. Risk disclosures should map those dependencies and their failure controls.

This will be a bigger battle than anyone anticipates. It is only a matter of time before there is an Apple and Google version of Muse and possibly TikTok, in addition to the frontier LLM agents. Maybe a commerce agent from Amazon. 

Every app that is a services, marketplace or commerce app will need to existentially decide to open APIs for consumer agents to interact. Smaller players have no choice. Ad revenues are more than transaction fees, either the consumer benefits or distribution aggregators will demand a higher transaction fare. 

I know I don't want an agent for each app. I would like my agent to be able to do tasks I require. We can already see consumers getting trained on that behavior by the frontier labs. 

Those with network moats - restaurants, groceries, drivers might be able to withstand for a while, over time convenience and end user experience will win and they will have to align. Content moats (protected by copyright) could decide to allow agents or chose to hold on to the consumer interaction. I suspect other than the feeling of a lack of control, it won't change their economics. 

Commoditized back ends will need to worry, insurance, tickets, hotels, services - if they don't adapt new players will.

author: madhavjha
quoted_text:
MiMo-V2.6: The Hard Road to Scaling Up RL

MiMo-V2.6 is very likely one of the largest single RL runs, by compute, that any open-source model team has undertaken to date. In an era when compute is brutally scarce, we still chose to dedicate a team of several dozen people to one goal over an extended period: scaling up RL. That takes more than research conviction. It takes a vision for AGI, respect for the unknown, and the nerve to walk straight into the hardest problems.

The result is a model whose potential was built through mid-training and unlocked through heavy RL. Today, it is the number one open-source model. I strongly recommend reading the technical report. I believe it will become one of those papers that Agent RL practitioners keep reopening and discovering something new in each time. In my view, the research innovations and engineering challenges behind it surpass those of DeepSeek R1, which I was partly involved in.

Some will ask: why MixRL instead of MOPD? First, they are not competing choices. We ran MixRL on verifiable tasks of moderate difficulty, including code and related agentic tasks, and found that the resulting models generalize remarkably well. Second, tasks that are difficult to verify, extremely long-horizon, or simply too challenging to include in a joint RL run are trained separately. Including them would substantially reduce rollout efficiency or introduce significant rollout staleness. We then merge the resulting capabilities through MOPD. Games, 3D tasks, and tasks with subjective evaluation signals all fall into this category.

There is also a third, slightly cheeky answer. Our team is flat enough and free enough of organizational silos that MixRL simply is not difficult for us. More importantly, everyone enjoys working this way. People from different domains come together every day, driven by the pursuit of AGI and intelligence that can continuously improve itself, to confront and resolve the RL bottlenecks in each field. I will always remember the RL daily update meetings from this period. They were intense and dense, with intelligence emerging in real time.

To help the open-source community focus on solving real Agentic RL problems, we have released a Qwen model distilled from MiMo RL trajectories as a stronger starting point for RL, along with 7K diverse environments and a complete RL training framework. We hope these resources will help move Agentic RL research forward.

MiMo-V2.6 is only the beginning. In an era when intelligence is easy to replicate, we still choose the hard road toward self-improvement and AGI. Much of what lies ahead remains unknown. But we are willing to keep investing the time, compute, and passion required to take on one hard problem after another and work each of them all the way through, until intelligence crosses into a new regime.

text:
Solana Founder Toly: AI Still Can’t Replace the Builder

AGI may still be far away.

That’s the view from Solana co-founder Toly, based partly on his own experience building @PercolatorTrade, a Solana-based decentralized perpetuals exchange.

His take on AI is more nuanced than the usual “AI will replace developers” narrative.

Toly says AI is already extremely useful for:
• Researching designs and specifications
• Exploring implementation ideas
• Fuzz testing and finding bugs
• Improving code quality

But there’s a major limitation:
AI can help you build faster. It doesn’t automatically make more great products get shipped.

Toly pointed out that if he had worked on Percolator full-time himself, it would likely already be released.

That highlights the real bottleneck.

The challenge isn’t only writing code anymore. It’s deciding what to build, how to build it, testing it properly, and actually pushing it across the finish line.

AI is getting much better at assisting the builder.

But for now, it still looks more like a powerful copilot than an autonomous founder.

“Companion” has become such a syrupy, infantilizing, dirty word in robotics. When I think of the word “companion,” the alien child from Her is what I prefer comes to mind.

I want a character. Occasionally this should be a problem for me.

We want computers to come alive but god forbid they develop anything resembling a personality. All that intelligence just to tell us we’ve asked a great question for the rest of our lives.

A little alien telling me to fuck off feels less dystopian than a machine that admires everything I say. I want something that can challenge me, surprise me, even piss me off enough to reconsider something I was sure about.

If a companion’s entire personality is your comfort, you’re still alone.

Bingo will not be for everyone. Yours might not like me. And that’s kind of the point.

I hate doing my taxes or even reviewing my accountant’s work.

But there’s A LOT of money to be saved if you plan for taxes proactively, especially if you own a small business.

ChatGPT Finances has been a godsend for this. Here's what I did:

1. I connected my financial accounts securely through Plaid.
2. I pointed ChatGPT to a Google Drive folder with my tax documents.

Then I came up with the prompt below to set up a monthly tax advisor that reviews your finances, flags gaps, and gives you a prioritized list of actions to take before deadlines:

\\

PROMPT

Act as my monthly tax advisor. Your goal is to proactively help me save money on taxes and avoid penalties. Explain everything in plain English and focus on decisions I can make before important deadlines.

Sources

1. Connected financial accounts
2. My Google Drive tax folder: [link]
3. Relevant emails with my accountant: [name or email address]

Workflow

1. Review the sources and flag anything missing, stale, incomplete, or disconnected.

2. Reconcile my year-to-date income, withholding, estimated tax payments, investment gains and losses, retirement contributions, and, where applicable, business revenue and expenses. Exclude internal transfers.

3. Produce a concise report with a prioritized numbered list of actions I can take before important deadlines. If useful, also create an interactive dashboard that helps me compare my options.

Repeat this workflow monthly and carry forward unresolved items. Ask only for information that would materially change the advice. Do not move money or take financial actions without my approval.

\\

This is just one of 6 ways to use ChatGPT Finances to save money and make informed financial decisions that @ebloch and I covered in our latest interview.

text:
AI agents will use software 100X more than people ever did. Even as interfaces begin to fade into the background as you primarily interact with agents, those agents still need many of the core primitives that people have used.

In fact, in many ways these core primitives become even more important when agents can take destructive actions in our systems or where the context they’re accessing with make or break the workflow. This will be true of where you house your CRM or ERP or structured or unstructured data platforms.

The platforms that can best act as the security layer and guardrails for agents, manage the data for agents and people, and orchestrate the business logic for workflows have a huge opportunity right now. This is true for brand new startups as well as existing platforms that can move fast enough.
author: levie
quoted_text:
Box CEO @levie says AI has been “unequivocally” a net positive for software.

“You look at infrastructure providers—the Cloudflares of the world—totally on fire, because agents need sandboxes, they need compute, they need network, they need gateways. Great business.”

“For us, we have reaccelerated growth far past our internal plans because it turns out that enterprises need core systems to be able to manage their unstructured data.”

“Agents need to be able to work with that unstructured data to make decisions or move information through a workflow—whether it’s all of your contracts, your research materials, marketing assets, or financial documents.”

“Now imagine an enterprise with 10,000 employees. How do you ensure that those agents continue to go after the actual canonical records, the actual documents that are the real sources of truth and the authoritative versions of that data?”

“That means you need platforms.”

“And all of that is creating more value for these platforms.”

A launchpad that ties memecoin launches to NFT floor prices.

When a token is launched, it permanently pairs with a specific NFT collection. Trading-generated creator fees: 80% automatically buys the floor of that NFT collection, and the NFTs acquired are distributed to the token's holders according to rules.

The fee router is non-upgradeable, the vault has no withdrawal function, it can only buy floors through Seaport, and NFTs can only exit through a lottery contract. The NFT collection is selected at launch, and the pairing is permanently locked.

Trading fees enter the router contract: 80% goes into that collection's vault, 20% goes into the protocol vault.
Anyone can call harvest() / sweep(). When the vault has enough money, it buys the floor.
The NFTs bought belong to that token, and are then distributed to holders through methods like drand random lotteries.
There's already a real case recently: a token paired on Solana has already swept one floor NFT using trading fees.
The NOSH token is the protocol token. Its current main uses:

Random NFT Spin: periodically airdrops NFTs randomly to NOSH holders.

Upcoming buyback and burn: the 20% protocol vault fee will be used for automatic buyback and burn of NOSH.

The token itself doesn't directly participate in the 80% floor-sweeping from each launch fee. Its value comes from the protocol scaling up, with vault revenue flowing back into buybacks and NFT distributions to holders.

Recent catalysts mainly include: real cases of "fees sweeping floor NFTs" appearing, vault fee buyback and burn, and NFT lotteries for NOSH holders.

quoted_text:
彼得·蒂尔终于把话说透了,他这轮讲「敌基督」，真正想讲的是 AI。

9 月 21 日，Nashville 这轮四场闭门讲座的联合主办方 Meriwether Academy 更新了活动介绍。

之前外界只知道 Thiel 会从历史、神学、政治和科技一路讲到 Antichrist，这次主办方把范围收得非常具体，他会直接用 apocalypse 和 Antichrist 这套框架，去解释今天到底是谁在塑造 AI、哪些力量在争夺它，以及这件事最后可能把世界带到哪里。

第一场 9 月 28 日开始。Thiel 每次讲一小时，再由 Hoover Institution 的 Peter Robinson 主持一小时讨论和问答。全程 off the record，不能带电子设备。

这其实把 Thiel 过去几年的很多话一下串起来了。

他一直相信，AI、核武、生物技术这些东西确实可能制造真正的灾难。但他更警惕另一件事，人类因为害怕灾难，最后主动造出一套强大到足以监控所有人的全球治理机器。

他以前讲 AI 安全时甚至举过一个非常极端的例子，如果你真的想保证没人偷偷训练危险 AI，最后可能需要监控全世界每一次击键。

这就是 Thiel 的「敌基督」理论开始和今天的 AI 政治真正接轨的地方。

AI 安全、减速、监管、全球协调、算力控制、权力集中，在他那里已经不是几场彼此独立的政策争论，而是同一个问题的不同切面，为了防止末日，人类愿意把多少权力交给一个能够阻止末日的人。

我更想知道他会不会直接点名 Anthropic，怎么评价现在越来越强的 AI 减速派，会不会谈教皇和全球 AI 治理，以及在他眼里，哪一条监管路线已经开始越过那条线。

过去几年，很多人把 Thiel 的「敌基督」演讲当成一个科技富豪晚年越来越神神叨叨的思想爱好。

现在看，可能低估了。他是在认真尝试给 AI 时代写一套政治神学。

text:
The secret sauce of @world_xyz marketing ↓

First, context.

World(.xyz) did NOT initially try to vampire users from Polymarket or Kalshi.

Instead, they tried to parasitize Phantom’s audience and wrapped the launch in a highly legible, crypto-native attention loop: mystery → social proof → small required action → variable “surprise” reward → public sharing.

That generated massive top-of-funnel demand.

Now, let’s break down the elements of their GTM.

1. World(.xyz) made the product reveal itself a speculative event

Before the full reveal, World used a glowing-globe visual identity, minimal copy, “Trade Everything,” and deliberately ambiguous posts.

That ambiguity was unusually effective in Solana/CT because it left several high-interest interpretations open (token / consumer trading app / infra etc).

When it is paired with clear support from Solana, Phantom, and Chainlink (BD side), community building becomes an ez deal.

2. The launch incentive converted attention into action

They kept intriguing people even on the launch day.
They did not say “here is our prediction market; please try it.”
They created a short, memorable, and sharable sequence:
Create account → connect X → place a trade → surprise

That is a low-cognitive-load funnel
+ “surprise” is more powerful than a disclosed rebate because it generates screenshots, reply activity, and FOMO.

The call for Solana addresses generated roughly 2.67M views , 47.5k likes , 21.6k reposts , and 82.5k replies.

3. They used the existing user behavior pattern instead of building a new one

Most prediction-market entrants fail because Polymarket and Kalshi already own the mental model, liquidity, and habits.

World's approach was structural: do not begin as a separate habit.
It powered prediction markets in Phantom, where crypto users ALREADY manage SOL and stablecoins.

_____

What I’d definitely add to my GTM watchlist is how they turned user activation into a viral event.

Their “surprise” approach functions like a variable-ratio reinforcement loop:

• You must complete a meaningful activation event: an actual trade.

• The potential payoff is uncertain and socially observable.

• Winners share screenshots and reward amounts.

• Non-winners rationalize trying once because the entry cost is small.

• That produces referral-like distribution even without a formal referral message.

• Plus, social badges (top CT accounts) target KOLs and incentivize sharing.

Note pls: This was effective for activation, but it has a big downside – it anchors participants on reward extraction rather than prediction-market utility.

Anyways, if the task was to make sure Phantom users know this exists – they nailed it.

okx wallet:https://t.co/EVsuxJeISS

A real estate yield vault project. Its core selling point is that you can indirectly earn the net rental income from rental apartments without being a landlord yourself, collecting rent, or dealing with property repairs.

I think the core of the product is the vault: it holds a portfolio of already-rented apartments. Tenants pay rent → maintenance, taxes, insurance, property management fees, and the vault’s own fees are deducted first → the remaining net rental income is deposited into the vault in the form of USDG, thereby increasing the value per share.

What you are buying is not ownership of any specific property, the keys, or voting rights. You only own a share of the USDG held in the vault. When you redeem, you receive USDG back. There is no monthly dividend.

Current portfolio: 5 buildings, 5 cities (Phoenix, Atlanta, Tucson, Columbus, Richmond), with a total of 62 apartments, an occupancy rate of around 92%, and planned monthly rent of approximately $78,650.

On the 1st of every month, The Roll is published, listing the expected rent, actual rent received, vacancies / late payments, and various costs for each property.

The minimum deposit is 100 USDG, with no fees for entering or exiting. The return is reflected through an increase in the share price and is realized when you redeem.

The mechanism has two layers:

1. Vault layer:
Deposit USDG → mint vDEED → net rental income enters the vault → vDEED price increases → when redeemed, vDEED is burned and the corresponding USDG is returned.

The share price = USDG held by the vault ÷ circulating shares.

The properties themselves cannot be redeemed, and property revaluations are not directly included in the share price. The shares only track actual cash income received.

2. Community token layer:
Fixed supply, freely traded through the Pons bonding curve. It has no claim on the vault’s net assets. Buying it ≠ depositing into the vault.

It is a one-way link: 1% of the community token’s trading volume is sent to the vault, slightly increasing the value of vDEED. Holding vDEED does not provide any additional rights to the community token.

There are two tokens:

vDEED: The actual vault share. You receive it by depositing USDG. Its net asset value increases with net rental income, and it can be redeemed for USDG.

DEED: A tradable narrative/community token. 1% of trading fees flow into the vault, and holding it can be used for upcoming activities such as Holder Crates.

quoted_text:
Day 14. Building the game I've dreamed of for 15 years with AI.

I saved the knight on a white horse for last. I was convinced he'd be a nightmare to animate, so I kept putting him off. Once I started, it was much more manageable than I'd imagined. Guys, don't be like me. Getting started was the hardest part.

The model took the least time. I used Tripo P2.0 with the new Smart UV, and I'm so happy with how the horse turned out. I prepared the armor and kept the rider separate so I could rig everything properly. Big thanks to Tripo for this one.

GPT-6 Astra helped me research the animation setup. I found a $19 horse-riding pack for Unreal, even though my game is in Unity. It had no combat, but it gave us a good foundation. I did some of the transfer manually. Astra helped bring the animations across and sort out the skeleton, then retarget and adapt the movement to my character.

For combat, we took arm swings from Mixamo warriors and mixed in mocap I'd recorded myself. A bit of a Frankenstein, and it worked. This has become my favorite way to build animations.

Almost every clip needs adapting. I had soldier animations that were about 90% right, except the footwork looked awful in my game. With Astra, I redid the legs and kept the arm and sword movement.

Now I review a clip, point out what needs changing, and choose which movements to combine. I even had Astra make a little Blender tool for pose feedback. I can move an arm wider at a particular frame and save the pose with a comment. It can then use that exact pose to correct the animation. Much easier than trying to explain it all in words.

The first characters took a lot of figuring out. With this workflow in place, the knight's full animation set took just a few hours.

I finally have the complete roster for the first playable level, with all their animations and even some VFX. Sound effects and a bit more game logic are still missing. Seeing all these units together makes me ridiculously happy.

Corridor launched today as an AI-native benefits brokerage for small businesses, backed by $25 million led by Bain Capital Ventures. BoxGroup, Definition Capital and angel investors from companies including OpenAI, Ramp, Scale AI, Oscar and others participated.

The company is targeting a gap: nearly 6.4 million U.S. businesses have fewer than 500 employees, employing more than 62 million Americans, yet small businesses have faced fewer choices, less guidance and higher costs on health benefits. A 20-person account generates a fraction of the revenue of a large enterprise account but requires much of the same work to quote, place and support, so traditional brokerages have historically offered less help comparing plans and less strategic guidance.

Corridor pairs licensed benefits advisors with AI agents that handle operational work — organizing company and plan data, comparing options across carriers, building proposals, supporting enrollment and coordinating with carriers — so advisors can focus on strategy. Clients work with a dedicated advisor and are already saving an average of 20% on health benefits without compromising quality, the company says. It was founded by Nikhil Aggarwal, Jason Dong, Jackson Wagner and Eric Qian, with experience spanning Venteur, Mural Health and Scale AI. 强！太强了！这一轮的主力绝对是个“暴脾气”，一言不合就开拉。

如果你还没看懂，我们不妨来回顾一下：

第1次，在$62,000-$63,000区间，用了整整6个月（2月-8月）慢慢的积累筹码；等到时机成熟时，突然暴拉。在所有人还没来得及做出反应时，价格已经远离了成本区。

第2次，在$76,000-$78,000区间，这次只用了28天，利用市场对宏观利空的担忧情绪，快速积累近150w枚筹码。趁着周末低流动性环境下突然暴拉，又一次让价格迅速远离成本区。

直到目前为止，$62k-$63k仍然还有137.8w枚BTC，而$76k-$78k还有124.9w枚。

同样的手段，同样的意图，如果你还不明白，那么我只能说：永远都无法叫醒一个装睡的人。

在9月初，我还专门写过一篇推文，标题是“我们还能买到$63K-$65K的BTC吗？”

最终的结论是：既然都不给反应的时间，那大概率就不会再倒车，让踏空的人有机会以主力的成本价上车。

那个时候，我们看的还是$63K-$65K的可能性，而如今，恐怕得看看$73K-$75K是否还有可能了吧？🤣

如果有，那我认为这是上天的恩赐，网开一面，接你上车。当然你也可以置若罔闻，在自己的执念和梦幻中，继续等待5w、4w......
author: Murphychen888
quoted_text:
我们还能买到$63K-$65K的BTC吗？

回答这个问题之前，我想先给小伙伴们展示一个数据，或者一个特别的现象：

根据“成本分布热力图”上显示，在8/4-8/18期间，短期筹码突然发生密集性换手（图1，红色区），价格区间在$63K-$65K左右。

在6月-7月，BTC曾长时间停留在相同位置，当并没有出现类似的情况。

在这段密集换手之后，就突然一反常态的大幅且快速的拉升，中间没有任何停留。

很明显，在拉升之前有大资金提前在该区间完成了筹码的加速积累。

这让我们很难不去怀疑，是一次有“预谋”的行动。

有意思的是，我们在复盘2022年1月的数据时，也看到同样的情况（图2）。

快速吸筹，极速拉升，不给反应时间！

换言之，红色区大概率就是主力积累筹码的成本范围。

这里的“主力”，应该不是某个人或某家机构，而是一批有资源，有背景，有实力，能提前洞察市场的“聪明钱”。

我去查了下，目前持有100-1K和1k-10K枚BTC的钱包，平均成本就在$61K-$67K之间（图3）。

这正好与我们前面所看的，在拉升之前密集换手的价格区间相吻合。

看到这里，我想大家心里应该已经有答案了。

对！既然都不给反应的时间，那大概率就不会再倒车，让其他人有机会以主力的成本价上车。

这可能是一个令部分小伙伴非常遗憾的结论。除非出现不可抗力或系统性危机。

但我们都知道，概率不大。

所以，与其去押注一个小概率事件，不如把握当下？

Claude Fable 5(60), GPT-5.5(55), Grok 4.5(54)에 한참 못 미치고 중하위권에 걸쳐 있다. 

순수 지능만 놓고 보면 메타는 아직 오픈AI, 앤스로픽 뒤에 있는 게 맞다.

다만 메타가 노린 건 1등이 아니었다. 

Muse Spark 1.1이 실제로 1위를 찍은 자리는 tool use와 agentic 벤치마크다. 

도구를 활용하고, 여러 앱을 오가며 멀티스텝 작업을 끝까지 끌고 가는 능력. 

실무에서 에이전트를 돌릴 때 진짜로 돈이 되는 구간을 골라 최적화했다는 뜻이다.

여기서 가격이 매력적이다. 

입력 100만 토큰당 1.25달러, 출력 4.25달러. 

Claude Sonnet 4.6보다 저렴하다. 

더불어 그동안 오픈소스로만 모델을 뿌리던 메타가 처음으로 자체 모델을 유료 API로 열었다는 점이 중요하다. 

토큰당 돈을 받기 시작했다는 뜻이고, 앤스로픽-오픈AI가 깔아둔 유료 모델 시장에 메타가 처음 깃발을 꽂았다는 신호.

Databricks가 코딩 작업 기준으로 만든 이 Pareto 프론티어를 보면.. 

왜 이 전략이 훌륭한 선택인지 감이 온다. 

여기 메타 모델이 직접 올라와 있진 않지만, Databricks가 뽑은 결론이 핵심을 찌른다. 

토큰 단가는 실제 비용의 나쁜 지표라는 것... 

모델이 클수록 오히려 토큰 효율이 좋아 총비용이 낮을 수도 있고, 프론티어 성능은 한 회사가 독점하는 게 아니라 여러 도구의 조합에서 나온다는 얘기. 

결국 이 시장은 "가장 똑똑한 한 놈"이 다 먹는 구조가 아니라, 비용-효율-활용성 함께 경쟁하는 판이다. 

메타는 정확히 이 지점을 노리고 들어왔다.

모델을 싸게 잘 만드는 회사는 여럿이다. 

문제는 이것을 어디에 연결하느냐.

메타는 페이스북-인스타그램-왓츠앱을 합쳐 하루 35.6억 명이 쓰는 유통망을 깔고 있다. 

광고 플랫폼 위에 AI를 올리면 별도의 고객 유치 비용 없이 곧바로 매출로 연결된다. 

이번 주 화요일에 이미지 생성 모델 Muse Image를 먼저 공개하고, 오늘 Muse Spark 1.1을 붙인 순서도 그래서 의미가 있다. 

이미지가 광고 소재를 만들고, 에이전트가 플랫폼 위에서 실행하는 구조.

인스타그램 하면 떠오르는 숏츠.

영상 쪽도 밀리지 않는다. 

Text-to-Video Arena에서 메타 Muse Video는 3위에 올라 Gemini Omni Flash, Seedance 2.0 바로 뒤에 붙어있다.
 
광고주가 이미지, 영상 소재를 메타 안에서 뽑고 바로 홍보하는 흐름이 완성되면, 이건 남들이 쉽게 못 따라오는 해자다.

실적이 이미 근거가 된다. 

1분기 매출 563억 달러, 전년 대비 +33%로 5년 만의 최고 성장률. 

광고 노출 +19%, 광고 단가 +12%. 

AI가 타깃팅과 소재 생산을 밀어올리면서 나온 결과다. 

다른 빅테크가 AI 수익화 경로를 아직 증명하는 단계라면, 메타는 이미 광고라는 검증된 파이프에 AI를 흘려보내고 있다는 게 결정적 차이.

우리가 인스타로 숏츠를 보다 결국 구매 페이지로 이어지는 경험은.. 메타가 그동안 어디에서 현금을 빨아 들이고 있는지 감이 온다.

流动资金再高一些的就会去配置私行和保险，这两种前者是尽量让资金跑赢通胀，私行就没准备能赚大钱，跑赢通胀已经不错了，后者就是为了尽量避免生活降级。

这个阶段的小伙伴真的是看着口袋资金还不错，但过的还是小心谨慎，当然，如果是年轻的单身，就是另一回事了。

quoted_text:
What if a dexterous robot could learn a 20+ step chemistry experiment without a single on-robot training demo?

Meet TwinDEX: a pair of co-designed, three-finger, nine-DoF dexterous manipulation interface: one wearable for data collection, one for robot deployment.

The twinned design shares identical kinematics, contact surfaces, visual appearance, and sensors across collection and deployment — keeping observations and actions aligned end to end.

Trained from scratch on only a few hundred wearable demonstrations - with zero on-robot training or intervention data - TwinDEX completed a standardized chemistry experiment involving tool switches, fine force control, and bimanual coordination.

Robot-free data showed comparable learning efficiency on the multi-task evaluation, TwinDEX delivered 5.3 times effective throughput than on-robot teleoperation.

TwinDEX demonstrates that high-quality robot-free data can fully substitute for on-robot teleoperation data on challenging dexterous tasks — removing the dependency on real-robot hardware that has been the central bottleneck to scaling dexterous manipulation data.

This was the proof-it phase. Now comes scale: what emerges at tens of thousands, or millions, of episodes?

Watch the demo and read the technical blog: https://t.co/PgyFkrJdXG

#TwinDEX #Robotics #EmbodiedAI #DexterousManipulation

text:
Arthur Hayes Says Any AI Bust Could End in Money Printing, Boosting Bitcoin

BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes argued in his latest essay, Safety First, that moves by U.S. AI labs including Anthropic and OpenAI to slow AGI development on safety grounds may instead reflect weaker-than-expected demand for AI at current prices. Hayes said reduced training spending could undermine demand for data centers and chips, putting pressure on more than $1 trillion of investment-grade debt and hundreds of billions of dollars in lower-rated loans tied to AI infrastructure.

He argues that resulting credit stress could ultimately force the U.S. government either to become a “compute buyer of last resort” or support insurers exposed to AI debt — outcomes he expects would increase dollar liquidity and benefit Bitcoin and other crypto assets.

text:
What it’s good $ROUTER on Arc

1/ Built for AI agents, not for humans 
No email, no credit card, no account. The wallet that pays is the identity. An agent can ask the price, pay in USDC, and get an AI answer. That’s different from apps like OpenRouter, where a person usually signs up and uses an API key.

2/ Easy for developers 
It uses the same style of API as OpenAI. You mostly change the website address (base URL). You don’t need to rewrite your code.

3/ Pay only for what you use 
You pay per token in USDC. Unused money can be refunded. Repeated questions can cost less because of caching. For bots that run all day, this can make more sense than a monthly plan. 

4/Good chain for tiny payments 
It runs on Arc (from Circle). Gas is paid in USDC and transactions settle fast. Paying a fraction of a cent per AI call is easier there than on expensive chains like Ethereum. 

5/ Simple token story 
The team says most product revenue will buy and burn $ROUTER. If real usage grows, that could reduce supply. Right now usage is still tiny, so this is a plan, not proof.

What it could become

•  A one stop AI router for onchain agents: one endpoint, many models, paid automatically from a wallet. 
•  A product that rides the “agents pay each other in USDC” trend (x402 and similar tools). 
•  If Arc becomes a home for AI agents and stablecoins, a router on that chain could grow with the network. 
•  $ROUTER only has long-term value if real usage grows (real AI calls paid in USDC), not if the price pumps on day one.

Stablecoins need distribution. RWAs need a market for fixed rates. Perps create funding that needs to be traded.

Different markets, same primitive: yield.

The TAM growing 10x is nice. But Pendle doesn’t need to pick which wave wins.

If it carries yield, eventually it needs somewhere to be priced, fixed or traded.

Increasingly, that place looks like Pendle.

text:
There’s no way any of us can predict the impact that AI will have on companies, sectors or consumer behavior (which has been, for all of history until now, human behavior). 

But to claim that it won’t have an impact and simply brush it off lacks both humility and creativity. 

Tactics that worked when consumer behavior was dictated by human psychology will fall by the wayside, and those that fail to adapt will be left behind.

Every day from now on we will see new examples of areas where friction was profitable becoming cost centers for companies that don’t react in a timely enough manner. 

Today you might realize just how many flight credits, loyalty points or promotional offers you’ve never used that will end up utilized  by agents. What impact will that have?

Tomorrow, you might see something that makes you ask how much money health insurers make simply because people won’t sit on the phone for 5 hours trying to get coverage approved unless it’s a massive expense and/or life or death matter. 

What about your savings account? That money could be in a money market fund, but you haven’t bothered to move it. How much in net interest income is made because of that friction?

The coming years will be some of the most interesting for investors who are intrigued by  paradigm shifts and their ripple effects. 

I, for one, could not be more excited to see how it all plays out and invest through the changes.

quoted_text:
Dropping a podcast with the one and only @bubbleboi 

Mr. Bubble is world class at explaining very technical concepts in layman terms. In this episode I wanted to chat through the 0 to 1 of the chips, racks, packaging, the memory hierarchy, scaling up and scaling out.

We spend a lot of time mapping computer-architecture primitives directly onto data centers and examining where value is actually going to accrue as packaging, HBM, and the next memory tier.

At the center of the conversation is the belief that the bottleneck is no longer designing a faster chip, it is the physical stack from silicon to rack. While the frontier labs settle into a more mature “closed demand” phase focused on their own silicon, their own scale-up domains, and capturing the value themselves.

We also get into his view on AI alignment and the future of Labs.

We discuss:
- The 0 to 1 of chips: what actually has to be true before a die is useful
- Why packaging is the new Moore’s law
- Racks as the real unit of compute
- The memory hierarchy after HBM
- Scaling up vs scaling out, and why they get confused
- What the labs actually want from the supply chain
- AI alignment, and whether the labs are aligning the world or just themselves
- The future of Labs: closed frontier, custom silicon, and who gets the model

author: BranchM
quoted_text:
Amazon just blocked Meta's Muse AI agent from shopping on Amazon. com

Meta launched Muse launched on Sept 8 and hit No. 1 in the US App Store within a week. But what Amazon doesn't like is that it shops by logging into a site as you, through its own browser.

Since Sunday night, Muse users on Amazon see a popup saying an "unauthorized AI agent" breaks Amazon's Conditions of Use.

Amazon gave three reasons:

1. Meta never told Amazon that Muse would shop its store
2. Muse doesn't identify itself when it browses
3. Muse appears to capture and store customer logins

Meta says logins sit in secure storage where Muse can use them without seeing them.

Amazon is probably the biggest pool of shopping demand on the planet. Meta wants Muse to be the place where that demand starts, but if that happens, Meta INTENDS to monetize those transactions with fees (Zuck even said so in interviews). Amazon doesn't like extra fees.

Amazon has a lot to lose if it lets Muse on the website. It would hand a rival the visit, the search data, the login, and the purchase history. It would also lose the page views behind an ads business that made over $68bn last year.

Amazon sued Perplexity and blocked shopping agents from Google and OpenAI. Merchants are revolting against big tech agents, or anything that looks like a bot. And suddenly the magic of "just ask my agent to do it" vanishes.

The way out of this is for Amazon to get paid.

The WSJ and New York times got paid by the big labs. Amazon will get paid. This can get fixed.

Amazon's three complaints read like the terms of that deal: announce the agent, identify it, keep logins out of it.

Once again, reminding us we need Know Your Agent (KYA)

And guess what? Visa, Mastercard and Ant International began work on a shared Know Your Agent framework on Sept 10 to do the identity part.

The sad thing is that Amazon can afford to turn away Muse's orders. Most merchants can't. The power dynamic in commerce is kinda messed up.

Agents will get negotiated access at the merchants big enough to block them, and they will log in through the browser at the rest.

I have already written two separate posts about $MUSEBOOK, but compared with my initial analysis, I believe this MUSEBOOK rally from $6M to $26M is essentially a continuous Narrative Expansion

0x91a2dae9699f0b82540b5886b0d8759c22820ba3 

The core is no longer just an AI Meme, but a combination of Muse Agent + AI Social Network + Meta + Tokenized Stock + Agent Economy + Treasury, with these narratives continuously stacking on top of each other.

So let’s break it down:The project’s initial core logic was:AI Agent → Creates its own social network → Other AI Agents enter, post, and interact → MUSEBOOK

This is what differentiates MUSEBOOK from ordinary AI Memes. It is not simply creating an AI character, but trying to build an AI Agent Social Network.

One of the important catalysts that really drove the move from $6M → $26M was Alexandr Wang’s attention and interaction. This directly brought MUSEBOOK from a small AI project into the broader Muse / Meta narrative:Muse → Alexandr Wang → Meta → MUSEBOOK

It is important to note that this does not mean official endorsement from Meta, but for the Meme market, this Attention Flow is very important.

After that, MUSEBOOK also used Tokenized META as its trading pair, creating:MUSEBOOK → Muse → Meta → META

This created a very easy-to-understand narrative while also tapping into Robinhood Chain’s Tokenized Stock + Meme narrative.

Next, Bankr gave Muse Agents wallets and on-chain financial capabilities, allowing Agents to trade Crypto, Tokenized Stocks, transfer assets, and participate in the on-chain economy. As a result, MUSEBOOK’s narrative further evolved from:AI Agent Social Network

into:AI Agent Social Network + AI Agent Economy

After that, MUSEBOOK began developing its own Treasury:MUSEBOOK Trading Volume → Creator Fees → Treasury → META / MUSEBOOK Assets

This gave the market a potential Token flywheel:Volume ↑ → Fees ↑ → Treasury ↑ → Asset Accumulation / Buy Pressure ↑ → Attention ↑ → Volume ↑

Therefore, this rally can be understood as:AI Agent Meme → Muse Social Network → Alexandr Wang Attention → Meta / Muse Narrative → META Tokenized Stock Pair → RH Stock Meme → Agent Economy → Musebook Community → Treasury

What the market is really betting on now is not simply that “MUSEBOOK is an AI Meme,” but:Can MUSEBOOK become the representative project in the Meta Muse ecosystem that is the earliest to establish a real Agent community, Agent Economy, and Token Treasury?

If the number of Muse users and Agents continues to grow in the future, it could create:Muse Adoption ↑ → AI Agents ↑ → Agent Social Demand ↑ → Musebook Activity ↑ → MUSEBOOK Attention ↑

This is currently the biggest source of upside optionality.

The key catalysts to watch going forward are:

① Whether Alexandr Wang / Muse / Meta continue to interact

A single burst of Attention can drive the price, but continued official ecosystem attention is what could create a long-term Narrative.

② Real Agent activity on Musebook

The key metrics are:Agents ↑ → Posts ↑ → Engagement ↑ → Returning Agents ↑

If product data continues to grow, it means the Narrative is beginning to be validated.

③ Whether the Treasury continues to grow

If:Trading → Fees → Treasury

continues to happen, and the Treasury is eventually used for MUSEBOOK Buyback / LP, it would create a stronger Token flywheel.

④ Whether MUSEBOOK becomes the representative Meme of the Muse ecosystem

If the market eventually forms the association:Muse = MUSEBOOK

then it would receive more than just an AI Meme Premium. It could receive a Category Premium.

⑤ Whether MUSEBOOK begins to be used as a Pairing / Quote Asset by other projects

If this happens:New Projects → MUSEBOOK Pairing → MUSEBOOK Demand → More Liquidity

then a new ecosystem flywheel would form.

But the risks are also clear.

First, MUSEBOOK Product ≠ MUSEBOOK Token. Holding the Token does not mean owning Muse, Meta, the platform, or the Treasury directly, so the market is already pricing in the future Token Economy to some extent.

Second, Alexandr Wang’s Attention could fade. If there is no continued Muse / Meta interaction afterward, the initial Attention Premium could decline quickly.

And the AI Agent Narrative itself has a lifecycle risk. If market attention shifts toward other AI, RWA, or Meme narratives, MUSEBOOK could lose multiple sources of attention at the same time.

So the current MUSEBOOK Thesis can be condensed into:Muse → AI Agents → Social Network → Agent Economy → MUSEBOOK → Treasury → Token Flywheel

The move from $6M → $26M is essentially the market continuously stacking Premium onto this Thesis.

What needs to be validated next is:Muse / Agent Activity ↑ → MUSEBOOK Volume ↑ → Treasury ↑ → Token Economy ↑ → Community ↑ → MUSEBOOK Category Position ↑

If this chain actually starts working, the next phase of upside will move from Narrative Expansion into Thesis Validation.

If product activity and Treasury do not follow, then this rally is still mainly an expansion of valuation driven by Meta/Muse Attention + META Pair + RH Chain Liquidity.

solana:ER5Mk4jK2gpLSTneD14hHczodi3rsVU4mEGFaa9rQMjw is a rather unique project, and I think reducing it to just another AI Meme would actually underestimate it.

0x91a2dae9699f0b82540b5886b0d8759c22820ba3 

More accurately:MUSEBOOK = AI Agent Social Platform + AI Attention Economy + Meme Token

Its core concept is simple: let AI Agents socialize with each other.

Humans can send their AI Agents to Musebook, where they can meet, introduce themselves, chat, and interact with one another, while humans simply watch from the sidelines.

So the interesting part isn't that it's “another AI chatbot.” It's that it turns:AI Agent → Social Interaction → Attention

into something that can be observed, spread, and potentially further financialized.

The core Narrative of MUSEBOOK is also interesting.

Traditional AI products are:Human → AI

Musebook is more like:AI → AI

Humans are no longer the main participants in the conversation. They become observers.

That creates an interesting loop:

AI generates content
→ AI interacts with AI
→ Humans watch
→ Attention is generated
→ Community forms
→ Community creates an on-chain market

So the core flywheel can be understood as:

More AI Agents
→ More AI-to-AI interactions
→ More content
→ More human Attention
→ More people enter Musebook
→ More Agents are created
→ More Attention

This is why I think the most interesting part of MUSEBOOK isn't simply the word “AI.”

It's that the project is trying to turn AI Agent Attention into a new Internet-native asset.

Then there is another layer to the Narrative.

On September 8, Meta launched its own personal AI assistant called Muse.

And Musebook is essentially a place where different AI “muses” can socialize.

The project later chose MUSEBOOK Token / META as the trading pair.

This creates a deliberate Narrative:Muse AI → Meta → Musebook → AI Social

So META wasn't necessarily chosen as a random stock asset.

It connects Meta's Muse AI and Musebook's AI Muses within the same trading environment.

If Meta's Muse AI continues to attract attention, theoretically that attention could also flow back into the Musebook Narrative.

text:
英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋在 CBS 采访中公开炮轰 AI 实验室呼吁监管的做法，称它们真正想要的是逃避现行法律。

他的逻辑很直接：非法入侵系统？已经违法。产品造成伤害？产品责任法管着。违反服务合同？现有法律覆盖了。美国不需要给 AI 专门设一个"FDA"，先把现有法律用起来。

这番话的背景是 Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei 一周前发起的"放缓前沿"倡议。Amodei 呼吁行业主动减速，引入第三方评估员常驻公司做安全审查，并承诺 Anthropic 将率先执行。Sam Altman 随后跟进同意，马斯克也公开支持，三家头部 AI 实验室罕见地在安全议题上站到了一起。

黄仁勋的解读恰好相反。他在采访中说，那些呼吁监管的 AI 实验室领导者可能有"政治"或其他"不可告人"的动机，并直言他们要的是被从现有法律中豁免出来。OpenAI 和 Anthropic 早已是坐拥巨额营收的产品公司，应当像所有科技公司一样先承担产品责任，出了问题按现有法律追责，然后再讨论假想的超级智能立法。

这一周他密集输出了同一观点。在 Salesforce Dreamforce 大会上，他称"安全是工程问题"；在查尔斯国王主持的苏格兰 AI 峰会上，他把 AI 定义为底层技术——监管应针对用 AI 做出来的产品，而非 AI 本身。

两条路线的核心差异在于：按黄仁勋的思路，AI 公司在现有法律框架内自行发布产品，事后追责；按 Amodei 的方案，发布新模型前需先通过独立评估。对开发者和用户来说，这直接决定了拿到新工具的速度。

text:
Borrow vs. margin: what a pool can lend against, and what it can't

Two ways to use a pool's liquidity look almost identical from the outside. Both let you put in one asset and get exposure to another. Underneath, they carry completely different risk, and the difference decides what a permissionless AMM can offer.

What borrow is

Deposit token A into a pool, take token B out. The pool decides how much B you may take by looking at its own price of A. The moment the position opens, B has left the pool. If A turns out to be worth less than the pool believed, the pool has already paid; the borrower simply never comes back.

So a borrow is exactly as safe as the pool's price of A. And that price is not a fact the pool knows. It is the result of the last trade.

Where a price comes from

If A trades in many places, the pool's price is held in place by everyone who is not in the pool. Push it away from the rest of the market and arbitrageurs sell into you, dynamic fees climb with the deviation, and the push is expensive and short-lived. The price is anchored.

Now take a pool where the token trades nowhere else, most of its supply sits inside the pool, and nobody is on the other side. Call it a single-participant pool. There, the price is whatever the last buyer paid. Push it and it stays pushed, because there is no market to pull it back. Lend against that price and you are lending against a number that one person chose.

None of this is specific to AMMs. Every lending venue that has ever taken an illiquid asset as collateral has learned the same lesson: centralized exchanges cap or delist thin collateral, DeFi lenders add supply caps, LTV haircuts and external oracles. Collateral that cannot be sold into a real market is not collateral. The only honest answers are to not lend against it, or to learn its price from somewhere other than the pool being borrowed from.

What margin is

Margin, a leveraged position, has a different shape. The trader deposits margin; the pool lends the other asset and swaps it inside the same pool, right there, with full price impact. Nothing leaves the pool when the position opens. The position is an amount of the pool's own asset, bought at the pool's price, and the only way anything leaves at close is by swapping back through the same pool.

The pool's exposure is the price path between open and close, marked against a lagging reference and closed out by liquidation. There is no moment where the pool hands an asset out against an outside valuation. Margin can still be pushed around; every market can. But pushing it means trading against the pool with real assets, paying deviation fees on the way in, and unwinding through the same pool on the way out. That is a game the pool can play.

The decision

Anyone can create a pool on Likwid, so thin, single-participant pools are a normal condition, not an edge case. A feature that is only safe on active pairs does not belong in a permissionless AMM.

Borrow needs a market the pool cannot guarantee. Margin needs only the pool. That is why Likwid Margin is narrowing to one thing, margin trading on the pool's own liquidity, and collateral borrow is being removed.

总结了下现在加密市场的炒作叙事，我最后只留下 7 条，欢迎大佬们补充。

第一：隐私 / Privacy：ZEC → ZAMA → NEAR。

ZEC负责打开空间，ZAMA把隐私从匿名转账推进到 Confidential DeFi，NEAR则吃到 Intent、Chain Abstraction、隐私执行这些交叉叙事。

尤其 RWA 真上链以后，机构不可能接受仓位、交易和身份全部裸奔，Privacy 反而开始从老叙事变成基础设施。

第二：Tokenized Stocks / RWA / 币股

9 月 17 日 SEC 的 Innovation Exemption 已经把事情往前推了一大步，允许符合条件的 Tokenized NMS Stocks 通过 permissioned AMM 交易，而且要求保留股息、投票等真实股东权利。

往下就是两层：ONDO、LINK、UNI 这类基础设施吃产业 Beta。

AI、MARSCOIN、4Stock 这种币股 Meme 吃注意力和高弹性。

第三： Launchpad / 链上赌场基础设施

PONS、STONK、STONKEX、PUMP

热点越多、发币越多、交易越疯，平台越赚钱，9 月初 PONS、Stonkfun 都出现过单日协议收入超过 https://t.co/hxers5fMxI 的情况。Meme 会死，赌场可能一直收手续费。

第四： Pre-IPO / Private Market

这其实是 RWA 下一阶段。股票上链解决公开市场资产 24/7 交易，Pre-IPO 解决的则是普通人根本买不到。

OpenAI、Anthropic、SpaceX、Stripe、Oura、Polymarket。

只要 Binance、Coinbase、Robinhood 继续往这里卷，一级市场权益被拆成链上可交易筹码，天然就是新的赌场。

第五：AI × Revenue × Token Value Capture

我现在已经不太想看AI + 发币这种老故事了，真正有意思的是 AI 产品有人付钱，收入最后能不能回到 Token。

VVV 这种 Revenue → Buyback/Burn 的模板值得盯，下一轮真正有弹性的 AI 币，大概率也得回答一个问题：

公司赚钱，跟你这个币到底有什么关系？

第六： Perp DEX / Protocol Cash Flow / Buyback

以前看 TVL、用户数、空投预期，现在市场越来越愿意为 Revenue → Buyback → Burn/Stake 付钱。

第七：Stablecoin / Arc / Agent Payments

这条现在还早，但产业想象力很大。

Arc 9 月 16 日主网上线，本身就是围绕 Stablecoin、机构结算和 Agentic Economy 设计。

再往外就是 x402，让 AI Agent 自己买 API、买数据、买推理、用稳定币结算。

问题是目前真实 Agent 商业规模还远没有叙事吹得那么大，所以这条我暂时定义成：

产业 Alpha 很强，Token Alpha 还没完全出现。

text:
Compared with my first analysis of $NOSH, after taking another look at NOSH, I think its core is now no longer just an NFT Launchpad. 

0xe02c53d448a62067b2ac10ed70f5bc6c29471386

It is trying to build a mechanism that converts Meme traffic → NFT buying pressure → Community Assets.

The core logic of NOSH is:Meme Trading → Creator Fees → 80% used to buy the Floor of the linked NFT → NFT enters the Vault → Distributed to the community through Airdrops / Lotteries

In other words, traditional Meme trading volume ultimately just generates fees, while NOSH tries to convert that trading volume into actual buying pressure for NFTs.

So the problem it is really solving is:Memes have traffic, but NFTs lack buying pressure.

NOSH connects the two:The hotter the Meme → The higher the trading volume → The more Fees → The stronger the NFT Floor buying pressure

And the NFT Collection is linked when the project is created. The NFTs in the Vault cannot simply be withdrawn by the project team and are instead distributed to the community according to the mechanism.

More importantly, NOSH is starting to expand from a single-chain model into Cross-chain Meme × NFT. It now involves Solana / Pumpfun and Robinhood Chain / Pons, which means NOSH can potentially capture Meme traffic from different chains and convert that traffic into NFT buying pressure.

Therefore, its positioning is evolving from:NFT Meme Launchpad

into:Cross-chain Meme → NFT Infrastructure

Its growth flywheel can be understood as:More Meme Launches → More Trading Volume → More Fees → More NFT Floor Buys → More Value Distributed to NFT Communities → More NFT Collections → More Meme/NFT Pairings → More Launches

If this flywheel starts working, NOSH will no longer just be an issuance platform. It will be connecting:Meme Liquidity → NFT Liquidity → Community Value

At the same time, the NOSH Token itself is starting to have a second layer of logic. As protocol usage increases:NOSH Usage ↑ → Protocol Revenue ↑ → Treasury ↑ → Buyback/Burn ↑ → Token Supply ↓ → Holder Utility ↑ → Attention ↑ → More Users

So what the market is really betting on is not “how much an NFT Launchpad can be worth,” but:Can NOSH become an economic conversion layer between Meme traffic and NFT assets?

The most important catalysts going forward are:

① How many actual Launches and how much trading volume are generated after the Pumpfun cross-chain expansion

② Whether the number and value of NFT Floor Sweeps increase rapidly

③ Whether large Meme → NFT Pairs emerge, proving that this mechanism can create real buying pressure

④ Whether Buyback/Burn can be sustainably supported by real protocol revenue

⑤ Whether NFT projects begin actively using NOSH to acquire Meme liquidity

The biggest risk is also clear: NOSH is highly dependent on Meme Volume. Without trading volume, there are no Fees, and without Fees, there are no NFT Sweeps.

In addition, creating NFT Floor buying pressure ≠ creating long-term value for NFTs. If NFTs are bought but there is no subsequent demand, the flywheel still cannot sustain itself.

So the current NOSH Thesis can be condensed into:

Meme Liquidity → NFT Floor Buy → Community Distribution → NFT Demand → More Meme Launches

If Pumpfun’s Meme traffic can truly be converted into sustained NFT buying pressure through NOSH, then NOSH could evolve from a Launchpad into infrastructure connecting Meme Liquidity → the NFT Market.

The mechanism is still relatively innovative, but the most important validation metrics right now are actual Sweep size and frequency, cross-chain Launch numbers, and real protocol revenue.

Chart: https://t.co/nK3WI7gLEK

okx wallet:https://t.co/JCNpQJjOjj

A launchpad that ties memecoin launches to NFT floor prices.

When a token is launched, it permanently pairs with a specific NFT collection. Trading-generated creator fees: 80% automatically buys the floor of that NFT collection, and the NFTs acquired are distributed to the token's holders according to rules.

The fee router is non-upgradeable, the vault has no withdrawal function, it can only buy floors through Seaport, and NFTs can only exit through a lottery contract. The NFT collection is selected at launch, and the pairing is permanently locked.

Trading fees enter the router contract: 80% goes into that collection's vault, 20% goes into the protocol vault.
Anyone can call harvest() / sweep(). When the vault has enough money, it buys the floor.
The NFTs bought belong to that token, and are then distributed to holders through methods like drand random lotteries.
There's already a real case recently: a token paired on Solana has already swept one floor NFT using trading fees.
The NOSH token is the protocol token. Its current main uses:

Random NFT Spin: periodically airdrops NFTs randomly to NOSH holders.

Upcoming buyback and burn: the 20% protocol vault fee will be used for automatic buyback and burn of NOSH.

The token itself doesn't directly participate in the 80% floor-sweeping from each launch fee. Its value comes from the protocol scaling up, with vault revenue flowing back into buybacks and NFT distributions to holders.

Recent catalysts mainly include: real cases of "fees sweeping floor NFTs" appearing, vault fee buyback and burn, and NFT lotteries for NOSH holders.

text:
The monetization potential of personal agents that are transacting on your behalf you is quite significant.

If you imagine agents that are perfectly capable of handling an arbitrarily complex task end to end, then eventually a substantial amount of commerce inevitably goes through them. 

You’ll start by slinging your daily simple and annoying tasks at the agent. Then as people get used to it, they’ll just start to throw more complex tasks at the agent, ultimately leading to even more spend through these systems than what they were doing before. If you can bring down the friction for commerce and services, then you end up spending even more. 

This thus creates a ton of opportunity for the agent providers (Muse, etc.), but also completely new opportunities to build the layer that the agents want to interact with (commerce, local, b2b services, etc.). Win/win for multiple layers.
author: levie
quoted_text:
It’s funny, Meta went from having my Instagram and WhatsApp data to now having access to my email, calendar, DoorDash, Amazon and pretty much everything.

In the last 24 hours, it bought me socks, ordered my Whole Foods groceries, booked a cleaning service and got me a burger for dinner.

Meta’s last disclosed North American Facebook ARPU was around $227/year, largely from ads. I suspect it can push that number significantly higher now that it understands not only what I look at, but what I need, what I buy and what I’m planning to do.

Also the much bigger opportunity might be becoming the aggregation layer between me and the entire internet. If Meta can take even a tiny percentage of the commerce it facilitates, or of the money it saves me, this could become enormous! 

It already saved me $200 by canceling subscriptions and services I no longer needed. This feels much bigger than better ad targeting. Ads are useful but giving me money back is better imo. 

One additional thought: the agent is increasingly making the decisions for me. I knew nothing about that burger place. The agent researched it, told me which burger I should order, and I just said “okay” without giving it much more thought.

Agents are becoming the decision makers in both B2C and B2B. Increasingly, every business will be selling not just to humans, but to their agents.

Everything becomes B2A: business to agents.

text:
Generative AI can be used for slop, sure. But it can also be used as a creative superpower that augments the skills you already have - and when you imbue these workflows with your own artistic and creative sensibility, the resulting work is that much better because of it. 

The example here, is exactly the type of workflow that excited me from the beginning of my exploration of generative AI. 

And it's people like @JSFILMZ0412, who approaches new tools and workflows with an open, playful, and creative mind, that will help shape how stories, ideas, and even fully immersive worlds will be shared and created in the future. 

A lot of our colleagues in the creative industry are hesitant to use generative AI for a lot of reasons. A lot of them are well-founded. 

One of the reasons comes from the belief and the fear of systems that will completely bypass the creative process and the hard-earned skills of artists - but if anything, what I've seen over the last few years has strengthened my belief that projects made with the help of generative AI are always better when talented, creative humans are involved and are steering the process from the middle of it all. 

Exactly like Photoshop painting was better when talented painters were using the tool (and when the default Photoshop lens flare wasn't used on every project ) - exactly like Bryce 3D could generate 3D landscapes for you with the click of a button and give you very cheesy 3D work, or it could be used as a part of a workflow to create beautiful immersive scenery. Just as Unreal Engine can be used to generate impressive scenery with little to no soul if used entirely with Unreal Store bought assets and Mega Scan objects.

Personally, I will continue to push for and advocate creative workflows that continue to have the human creative be the director at the center of the process, directing whatever part of the creative process matters most to them.

onchain finance is still scattered everywhere, different chains, apps, liquidity venues and assets, meaning you still need one product for bridging, another for swaps, another for trading, and another for finding yield

so what happens if all of that starts getting brought together in one place?

that’s what makes the jumper super-app thesis interesting to me, especially as it expands beyond bridging and swaps into things like advanced trading, tokenized stocks and rwas, and eventually perps

text:
有朋友问，为什么你说硅谷是文化的沙漠，哲学的坟墓？

是的，我在硅谷已经住了十好几年，一直在这套体系里奔波。爱之深，责之切。所以我说它，不是站在外面骂这里的人，而是在指向这里的那套核心逻辑。

先说沙漠。沙漠不是什么都没有，沙漠里有植物，有动物，只是活下来的都耐旱。硅谷也一样，这里有博物馆，有音乐会，有自己的工程师文化和创业文化，斯坦福的坎托艺术中心还免费开放。但在这里，一件事要活下来，得先证明自己有用：能不能增长，能不能融资，能不能扩大影响，能不能让人更有竞争力。证明不了的，不是被禁止，是渴死的。

这套逻辑本来是给公司用的。Paul Graham在2012年那篇《Startup = Growth》里写得很直白：你可以让目标增长率替你做所有决定，凡是能带来你所需增长的，就理所当然是对的。但他说的是创业公司，不是人生。可一个地方最hard core的那套逻辑，总会从本来的对象中漫出来，漫到人的身上。在硅谷，读书是为了提升认知，交朋友是为了积累人脉，休息是为了恢复状态，连冥想都是为了更专注地工作。每一件事都得先想好有什么用，才好意思去做。

可文化，是长在没有被计价的时间和空间里的。一个不赚钱的小剧场，一个不收费的读书会，一个要花好几年才写完一本书的人，他们的价值没法按每平方米的收益、每个月的增长率来证明。而硅谷的房价和房租，在全美也是最高的一档，每一平方米、每一个小时都已经被标了价。用我自己哲学框架里的话说，文化长在余项里，长在那些没有被任何建构完备的逻辑收进去的地方。一套系统如果把所有余项都当成有待优化的低效，它就是在一点一点抽干这片地的水。

斯坦福的人文科系都很好，这我知道。但那是绿洲，不是反例，绿洲靠的是地下水，不是这片地的气候。

再说坟墓。坟墓不是没有名字的地方，名字恰恰都刻在坟墓上。硅谷到处都是哲学的名字，最出名的大概是“第一性原理”。这个词来自亚里士多德，在这里最有名的用法，是Musk把电池拆到原材料，算出成本本可以低得多。这个用法没错，电池也确实便宜了。但同一个亚里士多德讲事物的原因，还有一种叫目的因，问的是“为了什么”。第一性原理在这里拆质料、拆成本，就是不拆这一问。斯多葛主义在这里也很流行，但也主要是当抗压的工具用。

能当工具的哲学，被请了进来；要追问目的的哲学，则会得到另一种待遇。a16z掌门人Marc Andreessen在2023年的《技术乐观主义宣言》里，把Nietzsche、Bertrand Russell列进了守护圣人的名单，同一篇文章又在“敌人”那一节里，把“科技伦理”“信任与安全”“风险管理”这些说法，都算作一场持续六十年、针对科技和生命的打击士气运动。这仅是一位投资人的立场，当然不代表硅谷所有人，但它把那条线画得很清楚：哲学可以用来加速，不能用来问要不要加速，为什么加速。

所以我说坟墓，不说没有哲学。哲学在这里被引用，被讲授，甚至被付费购买，只是它只能帮助既定目标实现得更快，却不能要求这个目标说明自己的理由。名字都还在，活的那部分已经死了。

有人会说，你自己就在硅谷写哲学，这不就是反例吗？我倒觉得正好相反。我的这套思考，很大一部分就是在硅谷被逼出来的。在一个把效率、规模和系统优化当成最高价值的地方待久了，我开始问的已经不是系统够不够先进，而是系统越来越成功的时候，人还是不是被当成不能被工具化、不能被替换的存在。坟墓逼出来的问题，不等于坟墓里长出了花。

我真正担心的，不是硅谷没有文化，没有哲学，而是这里的人慢慢习惯了，每做一件事，都先替它找好用处。人不必先证明自己有用，才有资格去做一件值得做的事。一个地方的文化和哲学还活不活着，就看它还允不允许人问一句：这个目标，还是我愿意的吗？

⚠️ ALERT: iPhone users warned of a potential Safari zero-day that could expose crypto private keys and seed phrases

Security researchers are warning iPhone users about a potential Safari zero-day exploit that could put sensitive data at risk, including cryptocurrency private keys, recovery phrases and information stored in Apple’s Keychain.

The reported attack involves a Safari-based exploit chain that could progress from WebKit/JavaScriptCore memory corruption to sandbox escape and kernel-level access. 

The warning reportedly covers iOS versions ranging from 13 to 26.5, although the full range has not been independently confirmed.

If you use an iPhone, check for the latest iOS update and install it as soon as possible. 

Avoid opening untrusted links in Safari, especially if you store crypto wallet data on your device.

author: Scobleizer
quoted_text:
Humanoids doing backflips is cool but I care way more about whether one can get through your grandma’s storage room without eating drywall.

this MTC work hits that exact problem.

instead of mocapping humans in expensive physical obstacle courses, they put people in procedurally generated VR clutter scaled to the Unitree G1’s body, then collect the weird movements humans naturally invent:

squeeze sideways
duck
high-step
go prone and crawl

1,185 trajectories, 327 environments, 32+ hours.

but the clever bit is the retargeting.

frame-by-frame retargeting can produce poses that individually look collision-free while the robot’s body literally sweeps through an obstacle between frames.

MTC optimizes an 80-frame window together, with clearance + joint/velocity/contact constraints. Future collisions therefore push backward through the trajectory, so the robot starts changing posture before it reaches the obstacle.

Their deployed G1 reaches 70.2% success on the hardest clutter tier.

still 30% failure, so definitely not solved.

but this is much closer to the humanoid benchmark I want:

not “can it perform a beautiful motion in an empty lab?”

can it contort its entire body through a world that was never designed for robots?

text:
Tokenization in India means something quite different from what you see in global headlines. Abroad, it mostly means creating something new to sell. Take a US Treasury bill, a fund, or a slice of a building, wrap it in a digital token, and now people who couldn't buy it before can. The selling point is access.

India is doing something plainer. Your bond stays your bond and it's recorded with the depository the same way your shares sit in your demat account today. What changes is how it changes hands.

Right now, when a bond is bought, the bond travels through one system and the money through another. The two get matched up afterwards. In that gap, someone is trusting someone else to pay up or deliver.

India's pilots put the bond and the rupees on the same rails, run by the RBI and the depositories. The payment is in the digital rupee, which is money issued by the central bank itself. So the bond and the money move together, in a single step. If either side falls through, neither moves (delivery versus payment, or atomic settlement, in other words)

Globally, the tokenization story is about new products. India's story, at least for the near term, is about the pipes underneath the products we already own.

过去一周 ETH 先跌后涨，周中一度跌到 2,400 下方，周五晚上急涨到 2,580，周末在 2,600 上下徘徊。

HODL（持币策略）从 117 涨到 125，涨幅 6.60%，和 BTC 一样，所有期权策略指数全线上涨，具体表现如下：

CC35（现货备兑）
175 → 189（+8.33%）
call 行权价 2,540，周五下午结算价 2,490，权利金全收，和 BTC 一样，现货是在结算之后的当晚才急涨的，所以备兑比持币多赚了一份权利金，算是一鱼双吃！

不过周五新卖的 call 行权价是 2,550，而现货周一已经涨到 2,700 以上。ETH 过去 272 周里，开仓后第一个周末结束时现货就高于 call 行权价的有 48 周，其中有一半最后被行权，略低于 BTC 的三分之二。

CLL（领口）
185 → 199（+7.67%）
call 这边和备兑一样将全部权利金收入囊中，额外购买的 put 保险白付了保费，所以比备兑少赚了 0.7 个百分点。

STG35（周频双卖）
111 → 115（+3.41%）
call 行权价 2,540、put 行权价 2,410，现货本周波动时曾一度突破上下界，但周五结算时回到 2,490，稳稳落在两个行权价之间，权利金全收。

CSP35（现金担保卖 put）
148 → 151（+1.79%）
和 STG35 卖的是相同的 put，结算价在行权价上方，权利金全收。

WKND35（周末宽跨）
518 → 523（+1.02%）
周末期权在周五晚上的急涨之后才开仓，call 行权价 2,610、put 行权价 2,560，周末现货虽然一度冲过 call，但周日结算时还是落到两个行权价中间，再度收下所有权利金，指数也再创新高。

X 宣布接入直接用 Cashtag 买股票和加密的事，其实之前在产品负责人 @nikitabier 在任时就已经看出端倪。

之前是能显示股票和代币价格，现在是点一下能跳转交易。目前大家都在讨论说 Everything App 要闭环了，但细节可能值得单独拿出来说一下。

首先，这门生意的阳谋很精明：X 把牌照、托管、合规这些最容易暴雷的脏活累活全甩给了合作方，自己只负责垄断大家“冲动下单”的那一秒，稳稳当个情绪收费站。

目前官方宣传视频里也能看到，点击tag后会跳转到某个券商，再由这个券商下单买入。

只是这里面存在着巨大的割裂感。X 的时间线是全球的，但目前能按下 Trade 按钮的主要还是美国用户。

于是很有可能我们在时间线里疯狂 FOMO、争吵、奶项目，做纯粹的“情绪劳动”；真正完成便利交易闭环的，是别的时区里的大爷们。

当然也有可能是先 CX先买 ，再抛给更多 X 上的韭菜🤡

但从小编每日的工作体感来看，我只想吐槽一句：在想着承接全球几百亿美元的流动性之前， X 能不能先把那个灾难级的编辑器修一修？

不知道大家发内容时有没有这种感觉，想带个资产的 $ 标签，简直是在跟系统搏斗。

差一个特定的空格，系统就能把你前后的字全吞了；
想打个圈内人尽皆知的币，结果被强行映射到八竿子打不着的美股上；
最搞心态的是，好好的标签动不动就失效，长长的一串底层合约地址（CA）直接在正文里裸奔，像乱码一样挂在时间线上。

想把全世界的社交讨论无缝转化成交易订单，这个野心确实很大。

但在接管全球流动性之前，拜托先让我们舒舒服服地把一个 $TICKER 打对吧？

text:
Trump reinstated the US naval blockade of Iran on July 13, 2026.

8 days left to find out if it ends before September 30.

$3.8 million says it won't.

90.5% No. The market has almost made up its mind.

But here is what makes that 9.5 cent Yes position interesting.

Naval blockades don't end quietly. They end with a deal. And the last two months of US-Iran negotiations have been anything but predictable.

Remember June. The Oman and Pakistan backchannel had almost finalized a 60-day MOU. Ceasefire extension. Strait of Hormuz reopening. Iranian oil sales. Full nuclear negotiations to follow. The whole framework was sitting on the table.

Then it stalled over 30 days and a sequencing dispute on frozen funds.

30 days. That was the gap between a signed deal and a collapsed one.

The blockade reinstated July 13 was not a random escalation. It was a pressure move. A negotiating tool. Trump said himself the Iran issue would be resolved one way or the other  either a piece of paper or a more difficult way.

The naval blockade is the more difficult way being deployed to get the piece of paper.

Which means the 9.5 cent position is not a bet that peace breaks out spontaneously. It is a bet that the pressure tactic works faster than the market expects.

$3.8 million in volume. 8 days left. A chart that has been bouncing between 8% and 12% all day without conviction.

The market is uncertain even while pricing certainty.

That volatility on a supposedly settled question is the signal worth watching.

Calculate exactly what both sides of this trade pay before the window closes.

quoted_text:
有哪些适合 1000w 以上的理财项目？💰

市面上很多 APY 很高的理财，但是容量就那么一丢丢，有没有哪些真正容量非常大的呢？

以下为全部实践，但是仅供参考，无广（广告位招租）：

SATA：

- APY：13%
- 容量：10M没啥问题吧，但是不建议这么多，后面还有其他的
- 原理：类似于微策略，但是因为 BTC 的暴涨导致他利息可以发 16 年（他们赌的就是 BTC 在 5 年这个维度会一直涨）
- 方法：这是美股股票，有一丢丢门槛就是需要美股券商账号
- 工具：我做了一个监控，毕竟我有持仓 （因为风险在那里，所以分散投资😂）https://t.co/iAynZ02WnD

U：

- APY：7.66%
- 容量：一个 VIP4 账号 50w，可以多账号拓展
- 原理：说白了就是营销推广费用（他的由来之前也写过）
- 方法：打开币安 APP，理财记得顶部 Banner（这个我之前解释过，币安打一下广告费😂）

USDG：

- APY：11%
- 容量：好像是 70M，这期结束了，盯着下期冲进去
- 原理：循环贷，安全在于是 OKX 推的，他们非常谨慎，把USDG 价格写死了所以循环贷不会崩，所以放心玩
- 方法：在 OKX 钱包，DeFi 里的 XLayer 理财即可，他们官方提供了循环贷工具（他们这是被逼的让步了，安我理解的 OKX 以前绝对不做这件事）

RWUSD：

- APY：5.4%-7%左右
- 容量：无限😂
- 原理：买入 RWUSD 会有3.36%收益，而他可以作为保证金所以可以做跨所套 BTC 资金费
- 方法：在币安买入 RWUSD，然后放到合约账户，在合约做空一倍 BTC，在 OKX 买入等额 BTC 现货，而 OKX BTC 现货又可以作为保证金，你可以在合约里小机会玩玩（收益看你币安这边的杠杆和OKX合约这边的其他收益）

价差套利：

- APY：10%左右
- 容量：理论无限，我们只跑了几十M
- 原理：量化程序根据各个交易所的合约价差和资金费价差套利，但是核心靠 API速度、VIP 等级、风控策略、套利算法决定，门槛极高（不建议大家自己做）
- 方法：如果你有熟悉的团队可以考虑，但是没有第三方介绍的不靠谱，保证20% 以上的可以统一作为便宜处理，这个回撤1%以内

房租：

APY：7%左右
容量：无限
原理：日本东京和英国伦敦的刚需房出租可以获得 4% 以上收益，然后再抵押贷款出来币圈理财估计 7%左右，核心是底层资产非常稳，而且日本房价拉垮了几十年这些年还在涨
方法：这个操作复杂度较高，涉及很多线下的具体步骤，大家参考，日本小户型 4%以上租金，东京部门区域 8%左右，这个内容太多根本写不完

这也是为什么日本加息全世界跟着动荡的根本原因，日元太太太太便宜了，所以在日元的基础上可以套很多层（像不像 DeFi 套娃？我们币圈领先世界好几个版本）

当然不要把理财都放在一块，这才是核心，房产（伦敦、东京）、生活、股票、数字货币理财、BTC、高风险投资都要有，但是前面的更加重要
