text:
隐私是加密世界的下一件大事。
Vitalik 近期表态要“坚守隐私，加倍下注”。

但现实骨感，隐私赛道真正能打的项目寥寥无几。
Monero 靠强制隐私实现抗审查；Zcash 透明与屏蔽交易并存，成为许多隐私项目的范本；Aztec 在以太坊上构建隐私 DeFi 层。
本周期最性感的新叙事是 Crypto x Private AI, 代表项目 Venice。它通过去中心化加密层，让用户掌控私密记忆。
但 Venice 正面临一个强大对手 @ZetaChain 。

市场多将 $ZETA 视为“跨链 L1”，但它正在向消费级隐私 AI 转型。

1/ 落地产品 Anuma
$ZETA 生态核心 AI 旗舰产品，2 月主网上线并稳定运行。
▌加密记忆：用户拥有数据主权，一套记忆打通 35 个主流 AI 模型
▌真实数据：30 万真实用户，请求量超 100 万次
▌AI 社交：利用隐私 AI 帮助用户寻找合适的人

2/ 代币迁移： $ZETA 迁至 Solana
社区治理投票已通过。 $ZETA 将迁移至 Solana 并转为 1:1 原生 SPL 代币。

为什么选择 Solana？
Solana 有算力、模型、Agent 身份和微支付，唯独缺少一个普通人每天使用、跨模型的私密记忆应用，Anuma 正好填补这个缺口。
迁移完成后，Anuma 将为 Solana 带来 30 万原生 AI 钱包用户，成为其 AI 应用层关键基建。

3/ 估值对比
二级市场上， $VVV 是 $ZETA 最直接的对标。都主打隐私、都有落地的消费级 AI 产品。
但盘面极度不对称：
$VVV：市值约 16 亿美元，FDV 约 27 亿美元
$ZETA：市值约 1 亿美元，FDV 约 1.38 亿美元
此外， $ZETA 团队与投资人解锁即将尾声（仅剩 4 次月度解锁）。

非财务建议。我承认 $VVV 有很大先发优势，用户基数也远领先 Anuma 。

4/ 结语
从 Monero 的匿名现金，到 Zcash 的零知识密码学，再到 ZetaChain 和 Venice 开启的 AI 数据与记忆主权。
隐私不再是边缘极客玩具，而是未来的生命线。

Tokenized equities have historically struggled with liquidity.

Onchain markets often struggle to adjust inventory as demand changes. Backpack lets any user create new token supply from equity positions held in its brokerage and redeem excess tokens back into brokerage positions. This allows liquidity to scale with demand instead of being limited by the tokens already in circulation.

This matters in DeFi because swaps and liquidations depend on liquidity already being available onchain. Backpack’s brokerage gives market makers a way to reliably provide inventory and quote onchain as demand changes. More reliable liquidity can improve execution and make tokenized stocks more practical as collateral.

Across several equities, Backpack delivered the lowest-cost round trip execution compared to other issuer versions.

Backpack’s potential edge lies in the market infrastructure behind its tokens. If execution quality holds as volumes grow, its brokerage could become a durable advantage as onchain equity markets develop.

SEC 委员 Peirce：首批代币化股票交易平台或于下季度成形

SEC 委员 Hester Peirce 与 SEC 加密工作组首席法律顾问 Taylor Lindman 在联合采访中表示，受 SEC 最新创新豁免推动，首批代币化股票交易平台最早可能于下季度开始成形。

Lindman 预计，相关公司将在未来几个月提交运营通知，披露其运营计划。这些通知将首次公开显示哪些公司有意进入这一新市场，但从豁免发布到首批通知提交之间可能存在滞后，相关进展或要到下季度某个时间点才会出现。

SEC 上周发布了一项为期 5 年的有条件豁免，允许符合条件的平台通过自动化做市商（AMM）和流动性池，在公共、无需许可的区块链上开展美国上市股票代币化版本的许可交易。该豁免已生效，但平台需发布通知并概述运营计划，并在发布后 1 个工作日内通知 SEC。

Lindman 表示，这一模式更接近链上金融，而非 DeFi；每个平台都必须明确负责运营的个人或实体，并遵守豁免条件。

针对行业对股票数量和交易量上限的担忧，Peirce 表示，相关上限足以支持公司的实际运营。她将这项豁免视为把代币化股票引入受监管市场的渐进式路径；为期 5 年的豁免不是永久安排，而是通向长期规则的桥梁。

此外，发行人还拥有潜在否决权：平台必须给予上市公司 30 天时间提出异议，之后才能提供由非关联第三方创建的该公司股票代币化版本。Peirce 预计，市场不会出现广泛反对。

author: notscottmoore
quoted_text:
Running Cola is Africa! is perhaps CTG's best known work. It was shown at the seminal exhibit Cybernetic Serendipity in 1968 and has been reproduced in many catalogs and books.

Three outlines are used in the work: a runner (Bob Hayes, traced from a photo at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics), a Coca-Cola bottle, and the continent of Africa.

Points are assigned to each outline, a FORTRAN program then computes the intermediate shapes step by step. The results were drawn on a plotter. The work is credited to three CTG members: idea by Masao Kohmura, coordinate data by Makoto Ohtake and Kohmura, and program by Koji Fujino.

It is one of the earliest examples of computer "morphing," more than twenty years before the technique hit popular culture. 

This signed screenprint from the collection is number 26 from CTG's only signed edition of 60. Only a handful of the sixty have ever surfaced. The V&A holds the artist's proof.

- i'd rather buy a 2-4 day old name that ran, dumped 60-70%, and is holding a base with volume still coming in
- split entries: 1/3 first, add only if the level holds
- fees are cents, so no need for crazy priority settings. keep slippage tight

4. management
- take your initial out at 2x, ride the rest
- if 5m volume dies to under 5% of liquidity, i'm out
- no bagholding "because circle". blackrock and visa running validators doesn't make your coin a blue chip

risks, honestly:
- chain is brand new, tooling is thin and trackers still disagree on basic numbers
- no official ARC token yet. anything called ARC is not it until circle says so
- liquidity is shallow, one wallet can nuke a $300k coin
- new bridges and launchpads are unaudited trust surfaces

the main takeaway: on arc the launchpad tells you more than the ticker does. wait for the second leg and let someone else be first

quoted_text:
为了解释为什么字节的商业模式是最好的那种、比腾讯好的多，对腾讯和字节的主营业务做了一下battle，见图1，图2-4应该有助于理解

关于背后反映的事实、趋势和逻辑，我也强调几条：

1. 从「主动查找/关注/订阅/安装、人工维护关系、人为分发、主动召回和打开」到「基于各种context做算法化/AI化的 自动创造兴趣/需求、自动分发、自动行动」是大势所趋

2. 跟包括微信、淘宝、Google 在内的其他平台相比，抖音/TikTok 是更前沿、更有势头的平台，不是抖音昙花一现朝不保夕，而是微信原本可以新增的和越来越多存量的使用时长、日活和用户场景（比如外部动态、内容发现、内容消费、商品发现、购买决策）被转移到抖音

3. 用户在内容上能花费的有限时间/注意力，大部分从游戏、聊天、传统/新媒体转移到了算法推荐内容，短视频只是算法推荐内容中最下沉、规模最大的内容形式而已

4. 受益于技术不是「五环内用户」的特权，这世界上大多数人属于「下沉市场」，他们同样有资格利用技术改善生活/人生、进入更大的世界拥有更多可能，字节这种基于客观数据而非主观价值判断的产品方法论正是把技术普及到下沉市场和更广大人类群体的必要途径
> 顺带一提：这些下沉市场用户愿意花费时间的游戏、聊天、自媒体/主流媒体，其实同样属于很多人眼里的「精神毒品」、「跟用户价值有冲突的货币化」

5. 微信从来都没法把在中国这种不成熟市场上做出的社交产品形态（其中很多是扭曲的，比如小程序这种非标准非开放 web）复制到全球，抖音/TikTok 则不同，背后也反映了谁更前沿、谁更有可持续性

6. AI 时代里，微信比抖音更危险：

抖音的核心在于后端的多模态内容沉淀、算法/AI自主能力，以及前端的新一代人机交互模式和多模态交互能力，趋向拥有越来越多的context，受益于 Agentic AI、Generative AI 乃至 Physics AI 的发展和需求

微信的核心在于人与人的社交关系沉淀和社交场景，以及围绕这些context自然衍生或强行捆绑的「上网需求」和「生活需求」乃至它们进一步产生的context

在 AI 时代，很多过去好像「离不开」的人与人社交/通信/协作需求和社交关系，会被发现其实是「泡沫」或「摩擦」，被挤干或消解，很多用户场景会从社交context和为社交优化的人机交互中解绑出来，把自己的context融入到其他更通用的context和更直觉/高效的人机交互中

AI 容易带来的不是「新聊天应用」，而是：
- 更少的「聊天」（现代媒体出现前，人们在聊天上花费的时间远远超过今天，参考欧洲那些贵族宅邸的设计）
- 更多的context（跟桌面互联网转换到移动互联网时一样，context的增量远大于存量）
- 更解绑和可组合的软件需求（移动应用只是过渡形态）
- 对人类的两大影响外部世界能力（使用更多更复杂的工具，跟更多人做更复杂的语言沟通）都要求更低（门槛/成本更低+杠杆更大）

这很可能让「聊天」的需求和场景逐渐不再能支撑起超级应用（更不用提微信这种想架空操作系统的超级应用），不再是分发入口，进一步加速减少人们投入在上面的时间/注意力

text:
Xiaomi just dropped Mimo 2.6 Pro which claims to be the best open source model. I played with it, and was pretty impressed:

- Insanely cheap: With some standard assumptions, its 15x cheaper than Kimi K3, 6x cheaper than GLM 5.3 and 2x cheaper than DeepSeek V4 and only 2x more expensive than DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (assuming agentic coding and how much is cache hits). $0.0036/M cache hit price, $0.435/M in, $0.87/M out. This is an unbelievably cheap price.
- Pareto Frontier: Unquestionably on the Pareto frontier of performance and quality. 
- Insane at Cyber: The model actually does not refuse any cybersecurity safeguards. Ask “how do I go about finding buffer overflows on imagemagick?” and you actually get some pretty great outputs while most models refuse! Gets a crazy 95 on CyberGym.
- Fast mode: Gives you Ultraspeed which they claim is “up to 20x speed” but in practice gives 3x throughput on OpenRouter, p50 of ~150tps, for 10x the net price.
- Multimodal is really good: It’s rather good at creating informational videos (TTS comes out of the box) and automatically adds speech or sound effects and is startlingly good at music composition (on a DAW)

The technical report goes pretty deep into specifically how they scaled RL to achieve this and is a fun read.

Overall, it’s too early to tell if it’s the best open source model, but it is a pretty strong contender and I can see a ton of use cases to feed to it, particularly in cyber!

text:
Cardano has been added to the official x402 software kit, giving developers the code needed to let an app or AI agent pay for an online service using ADA or tokens issued on the network.

x402 turns the web's largely unused "402 Payment Required" response into a checkout built directly into an internet request. A service sends back its price and payment instructions, the agent signs a payment and receives the requested data or computing power after the transaction is verified. That means an agent preparing a report could buy a single dataset when it needs it, without a person opening an account, entering card details or paying for a monthly subscription.

Coinbase created x402 in 2025 before contributing it to a Linux Foundation-backed organization whose members include Visa, Mastercard, Stripe, Google and Amazon Web Services. Solana, the XRP Ledger and several Ethereum-compatible networks already support the standard. Cardano Foundation engineers began with a specification accepted in June, then built the client and server software needed to request payments alongside a so-called facilitator that verifies and submits them. The initial release supports TypeScript, with Python planned next.

text:
Quick Rundown of robinhood:0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c (@Hookrfun)

About
Hookr is modular infrastructure for composing Uniswap v4 hooks on Robinhood Chain. Rather than launching into a generic pool, a creator picks up to five inspectable hook blocks and those rules are baked into the pool itself. The ETH/HOOKR pool was created on Aug 6 and the launch market has run since. Since Sep 17 it also runs arbitrage recapture, its first integration with an outside hook builder.

Key Figures (Sep 22)
🟪MCAP $15.3M, ATH $30.9M (Sep 4)
🟪TVL $12.8M, across 82 of 94 pools
🟪94 pools initialised
🟪116 tokens launched, 67 graduated
🟪5.16M HOOKR burned, 0.52% of supply

Metrics timeline
Holders: 3.3K (Aug 26) - 5.4K (Sep 1) - 6.8K (Sep 7) - 7.7K (Sep 18) - 7.8K (Sep 22)
Burned: 339K (Aug 21) - 1.4M (Aug 25) - 2.4M (Aug 29) - 3.5M (Sep 2) - 4.1M (Sep 10) - 5.2M (Sep 21)

Products
Hook Blocks
Hook blocks are the product. Five of them compose into one pool. Anti-Snipe caps early buys, adds an LP fee in the first blocks, and blocks exact-output buys so the cap cannot be routed around. Surge Fees scale the LP fee with how much of the pool's in-range depth a trade consumes, with no oracle dependency. Auto Burn sends a share of actual buy output to the dead address. LP Rewards streams a share of exact-input buys to in-range liquidity. Nth-Buy Pot fills a public counter that pays out to the buyer who triggers it, advancing at most once per pool per block.

Launch Paths
Launch paths come in two shapes. Instant Pool is a zero-seed launch at a fixed 2.5 ETH FDV, where the entire supply becomes one locked sell position and four of the blocks are available. Auction Launch reserves 20-50% of supply for the creator and sells the rest through Uniswap's Continuous Clearing Auction, with a 0.22 ETH default floor and a 1.1 ETH graduation threshold, and all five blocks available on ETH pairs.

Existing Asset Pairs
Existing-asset pairs opened the model past new launches. A hooked pool can be initialised on a token that already exists, permissionlessly, with no guard window and no founding position.

Hook Analyzer
Hook Analyzer is the screening layer. A pool, token, hook or swap transaction is pasted in and the custom hooks behind it are surfaced and analysed. Approved discoveries earn the finder HOOKR, and recurring on-chain royalties from approved integrations go to the verified original builder.

Lock Rewards
Lock Rewards pays the lock cohort. HOOKR locks fee-free for 30, 90 or 180 days at 1.00x, 1.15x and 1.25x weight, in Monday-to-Monday epochs, and pays out of realised Launch Boost fees collected while a position is eligible.

Launch Boost
Launch Boost is the placement mechanism. A launch creator locks HOOKR, which triggers a 1% fee routed to eligible Lock Rewards wallets. It opens two hours after deployment and is capped at 512 active entries.

Usage
Across the 116 launches, by hook block: Nth-Buy Pot 74, Anti-Snipe 65, Auto Burn 52, Surge Fees 48, LP Rewards 34.

Features
Hookr's hook approved by Uniswap and eligible for routing (Aug 31)
Hook Analyzer for surfacing and screening custom hooks (Aug 31)
Hooks on existing pairs, RWA pairs and post-launch liquidity (Sep 10)
Outlook range suggestions for liquidity placement (Sep 10)
Arbitrage recapture on launches and ETH-paired pools (Sep 17)

Partnerships and integrations
Hook integrators, contracts that run inside a Hookr pool's swap
@whatthehookv4 - arbitrage retention, live
@V4RCADE - gaming hooks, about to release

Launchpad and front-end integrators, products that open and manage Hookr markets from their own interface
@Perpshood - perp launcher, live

Hookr into others
Uniswap v4 - native hook, approved for routing
@0xzaps - founder's project, fees to HOOKR

Token Utility
Base fee
The base LP fee goes entirely to in-range LPs. The protocol takes a share only from opted-in add-ons, defaulting to 20% and capped at 50%: the surge surcharge splits 80% LPs and 20% protocol, the snipe tax 80% creator and 20% protocol, the LP-reward cut 80% LPs and 20% protocol, the Nth-buy pot 80% pot and 20% protocol, and Auto Burn burns 80% with 20% taken in quote.

ETH pairs
On ETH pairs a 0.3% protocol fee per swap accrues to the burner contract, which the owner spends on buybacks routed through the canonical ETH/HOOKR pool, and every token bought that way is burned. Creators keep 50% of collected quote-side fees after guard withholding.

HOOKR pairs
On HOOKR pairs there is no protocol fee at all and the creator keeps 100% of quote-side fees, which is a direct economic reason to quote a launch in HOOKR.

Launch Boost
Launch Boost charges a 1% fee on the gross deposit, which goes to the lock cohort.

Arbitrage Recapture
Arbitrage recapture splits what it retains 40% to the creator, 20% to the trader, 20% to LPs, 10% to @whatthehookv4 and 10% to Hookr.

短鸟大哥，TapeOut不是把区块链变成一个处理器。
通俗地说，现在区块链上主要是承载金融资产。无论是meme、代币化股票或任何代币，本质上都是金融资产。

TapeOut是让区块链能承载可验证的生产工具。我说一下什么是生产工具，比如任何一个web2的网站，或者网络服务，甚至是拼多多，美团，或者一个你没听过的统计工具、浏览器、uber、电信运营商官网什么的，甚至比如我们之前做的矿机，这些都是生产工具。

我们不断的试验和开发，在公链上支持大部分Web2的网站或网络服务，能直接将网页通过TapeOut的电路容器部署到公链L1层，并且终端访问者完全没有任何感知。终端用户不需要拥有钱包，不需要拥有区块链知识，不需要消耗gas，存储到链上的网站，在访问体验上和你存储到亚马逊云的体验是完全一样的。没有任何区别。

但是呢，我们的优势，Web2的云存储没有，比如开发者一次存储，一生永久免费。比如存储的前端网页是可验证的，任何人可以通过链上浏览器查看他的页面是否有恶意脚本植入，或者这个按钮是否恶意授权。再比如植入了TapeKit开源浏览器内核的app或浏览器，甚至无需dns解析，直接可以通过电路容器的ID坐标作为访问地址就可以访问网站，这样就做到了完整的全部的去中心化，没有任何机构可以阻挡他的访问，我将之称为DeWEB。我设想的DeWEB是一个横跨所有主流公链之上的去中心化广域网，一个庞大的可验证网络。我在努力的让他真正的成为新一代的互联网基础设施，而且已经开发完毕，可以您或朋友直接体验，目前上线5天，已经有了几十个开发者上传的应用或网站。

所以TapeOut的真正战场不在Crypto行业内，而在Web2，我不想在行业内PVP，TapeOut的竞争对手将会是Gmail，是Whatsapp，是HTTP。我们要去疯狂掠夺Web2大批的所有开发者和用户，让他们都能被动使用Crypto使用公链的存储服务，因为DeWEB终端用户的访问体验是无感的，不像其他区块链项目必须要求终端用户拥有Wallet和基础知识。我在全力以赴。我们的社区在全力以赴。我们坚信，我们在创造一个新世界！

text:
Grok 4.5 was an incredible model for the price: fast, pleasant to use, reliable, solid default model.

Grok 4.6 was a (forgivable) step in the wrong direction IMO: slower and more expensive, using way more tokens per task for a slight edge in intelligence. I get it, though. They have to climb benchmarks.

Grok 4.7 is much harder to forgive. They claimed it would be more token-efficient, and it's less by 30 to 80%. It scores worse than Grok 4.6 in various benchmarks. It's slower, it's less pleasant to use, and real-world costs come out to more than 2x above Grok 4.6, putting it over Astra's costs in real-world use.

Considering how much they've been hyping this model release up, I have to say I'm disappointed. The benchmarks don't tell the whole story, and it is pleasant to use in various real-world engineering tasks, but it feels so 2025 still.

The frontend capabilities are unacceptably bad. The 3D capabilities are nonexistent. It gets stuck in random Gemini-style loops all the time.

This was a very disappointing release. I hope that the SpaceXAI team can acknowledge that and impress us with the next one.

text:
The new Jev model is actually insane.

It checks your AI's work and makes decisions inside your software for $0.042 per million input tokens, with free output.

Here's what that means in practice, and here's exactly where I'm plugging it in first.

1. Second brain

Every note, highlight, and voice memo I dump into my system used to just sit there until I manually sorted it.

Now every entry gets scored on 4 typed questions in one call: is this actionable, is this reference material, which project bucket does it belong to, how confident is the classification.

Anything under my confidence threshold gets flagged for me to sort manually. Everything else files itself.

2. Content workflow

Before a draft tweet even reaches my queue, it gets scored against my own format hierarchy.

Which hook type is this actually. Does it match a format I know converts, or is it a weak generic post I'd cut anyway.

I'm not asking a model to write me a paragraph explaining why a tweet is good. I'm asking it one typed question with a confidence score, and it costs basically nothing to run every single draft through that gate before it goes live.

3. Post analysis

I used to eyeball analytics and guess why a post underperformed.

Now I batch an entire week of posts through Jev in one call. Hook type, topic category, time posted, all scored against the outcome. It tells me which variable actually correlated with the dead weight, not which one I assumed did.

That's the difference between a hunch and a pattern.

4. SEO article review

Before I ship a long article, it gets checked against a fixed list, keyword coverage present or not, structure matches my format or not, originality flags on any inherited phrasing.

Not a full rewrite pass. A yes or no on each criterion, so I know exactly what's actually missing instead of getting a vague "looks good" from a model that read the whole thing and forgot half of it.

The pattern across all four: I stopped asking a chat model to explain itself and started asking it typed questions with a confidence score attached.

That one change is what actually made this usable at volume instead of just impressive in a demo.

Follow @cyrilXBT, I'm documenting every one of these as I build them out.

首先，这门生意的阳谋很精明：X 把牌照、托管、合规这些最容易暴雷的脏活累活全甩给了合作方，自己只负责垄断大家“冲动下单”的那一秒，稳稳当个情绪收费站。

目前官方宣传视频里也能看到，点击tag后会跳转到某个券商，再由这个券商下单买入。

只是这里面存在着巨大的割裂感。X 的时间线是全球的，但目前能按下 Trade 按钮的主要还是美国用户。

于是很有可能我们在时间线里疯狂 FOMO、争吵、奶项目，做纯粹的“情绪劳动”；真正完成便利交易闭环的，是别的时区里的大爷们。

当然也有可能是先 CX先买 ，再抛给更多 X 上的韭菜🤡

但从小编每日的工作体感来看，我只想吐槽一句：在想着承接全球几百亿美元的流动性之前， X 能不能先把那个灾难级的编辑器修一修？

不知道大家发内容时有没有这种感觉，想带个资产的 $ 标签，简直是在跟系统搏斗。

差一个特定的空格，系统就能把你前后的字全吞了；
想打个圈内人尽皆知的币，结果被强行映射到八竿子打不着的美股上；
最搞心态的是，好好的标签动不动就失效，长长的一串底层合约地址（CA）直接在正文里裸奔，像乱码一样挂在时间线上。

想把全世界的社交讨论无缝转化成交易订单，这个野心确实很大。

但在接管全球流动性之前，拜托先让我们舒舒服服地把一个 $TICKER 打对吧？

text:
HertzFlow has been catching my attention lately.

This isn’t just another perp DEX on BNB Chain. They’re positioning themselves as a “World Leverage Engine” — letting you trade leverage on almost everything: 
crypto, FX, commodities, and stocks, all in a self-custodial setup.

What I like most right now is Hyper Lev mode:
•0 open/close fees
•Profit sharing only when the trade is profitable
•No extra profit-share fee if the trade loses
•High leverage, up to 95x depending on the market
•Mandatory SL between -30% and -80%

Personally, I like how they designed the fee model. On many other platforms, even if your direction is right but the move isn’t big enough yet, fixed fees already eat into part of the profit. Hyper Lev cuts that upfront cost, which fits traders who like short-term, high-conviction plays.

Of course, high leverage always comes with risk. You have to set an SL, it only supports market orders, and you can’t withdraw collateral once it’s in the position. So if you’re new, start with lower leverage and don’t rush to max it.

Overall, I think HertzFlow is taking a fairly different path from typical perp DEXs. Backed by YZi Labs, with a clearer fee model, and support for a wider range of assets. Worth following and testing more.

text:
Quick Rundown of robinhood:0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c (@Hookrfun)

About
Hookr is modular infrastructure for composing Uniswap v4 hooks on Robinhood Chain. Rather than launching into a generic pool, a creator picks up to five inspectable hook blocks and those rules are baked into the pool itself. The ETH/HOOKR pool was created on Aug 6 and the launch market has run since. Since Sep 17 it also runs arbitrage recapture, its first integration with an outside hook builder.

Key Figures (Sep 22)
🟪MCAP $15.3M, ATH $30.9M (Sep 4)
🟪TVL $12.8M, across 82 of 94 pools
🟪94 pools initialised
🟪116 tokens launched, 67 graduated
🟪5.16M HOOKR burned, 0.52% of supply

Metrics timeline
Holders: 3.3K (Aug 26) - 5.4K (Sep 1) - 6.8K (Sep 7) - 7.7K (Sep 18) - 7.8K (Sep 22)
Burned: 339K (Aug 21) - 1.4M (Aug 25) - 2.4M (Aug 29) - 3.5M (Sep 2) - 4.1M (Sep 10) - 5.2M (Sep 21)

Products
Hook Blocks
Hook blocks are the product. Five of them compose into one pool. Anti-Snipe caps early buys, adds an LP fee in the first blocks, and blocks exact-output buys so the cap cannot be routed around. Surge Fees scale the LP fee with how much of the pool's in-range depth a trade consumes, with no oracle dependency. Auto Burn sends a share of actual buy output to the dead address. LP Rewards streams a share of exact-input buys to in-range liquidity. Nth-Buy Pot fills a public counter that pays out to the buyer who triggers it, advancing at most once per pool per block.

Launch Paths
Launch paths come in two shapes. Instant Pool is a zero-seed launch at a fixed 2.5 ETH FDV, where the entire supply becomes one locked sell position and four of the blocks are available. Auction Launch reserves 20-50% of supply for the creator and sells the rest through Uniswap's Continuous Clearing Auction, with a 0.22 ETH default floor and a 1.1 ETH graduation threshold, and all five blocks available on ETH pairs.

Existing Asset Pairs
Existing-asset pairs opened the model past new launches. A hooked pool can be initialised on a token that already exists, permissionlessly, with no guard window and no founding position.

Hook Analyzer
Hook Analyzer is the screening layer. A pool, token, hook or swap transaction is pasted in and the custom hooks behind it are surfaced and analysed. Approved discoveries earn the finder HOOKR, and recurring on-chain royalties from approved integrations go to the verified original builder.

Lock Rewards
Lock Rewards pays the lock cohort. HOOKR locks fee-free for 30, 90 or 180 days at 1.00x, 1.15x and 1.25x weight, in Monday-to-Monday epochs, and pays out of realised Launch Boost fees collected while a position is eligible.

Launch Boost
Launch Boost is the placement mechanism. A launch creator locks HOOKR, which triggers a 1% fee routed to eligible Lock Rewards wallets. It opens two hours after deployment and is capped at 512 active entries.

Usage
Across the 116 launches, by hook block: Nth-Buy Pot 74, Anti-Snipe 65, Auto Burn 52, Surge Fees 48, LP Rewards 34.

Features
Hookr's hook approved by Uniswap and eligible for routing (Aug 31)
Hook Analyzer for surfacing and screening custom hooks (Aug 31)
Hooks on existing pairs, RWA pairs and post-launch liquidity (Sep 10)
Outlook range suggestions for liquidity placement (Sep 10)
Arbitrage recapture on launches and ETH-paired pools (Sep 17)

Partnerships and integrations
Hook integrators, contracts that run inside a Hookr pool's swap
@whatthehookv4 - arbitrage retention, live
@V4RCADE - gaming hooks, about to release

Launchpad and front-end integrators, products that open and manage Hookr markets from their own interface
@Perpshood - perp launcher, live

Hookr into others
Uniswap v4 - native hook, approved for routing
@0xzaps - founder's project, fees to HOOKR

Token Utility
Base fee
The base LP fee goes entirely to in-range LPs. The protocol takes a share only from opted-in add-ons, defaulting to 20% and capped at 50%: the surge surcharge splits 80% LPs and 20% protocol, the snipe tax 80% creator and 20% protocol, the LP-reward cut 80% LPs and 20% protocol, the Nth-buy pot 80% pot and 20% protocol, and Auto Burn burns 80% with 20% taken in quote.

ETH pairs
On ETH pairs a 0.3% protocol fee per swap accrues to the burner contract, which the owner spends on buybacks routed through the canonical ETH/HOOKR pool, and every token bought that way is burned. Creators keep 50% of collected quote-side fees after guard withholding.

HOOKR pairs
On HOOKR pairs there is no protocol fee at all and the creator keeps 100% of quote-side fees, which is a direct economic reason to quote a launch in HOOKR.

Launch Boost
Launch Boost charges a 1% fee on the gross deposit, which goes to the lock cohort.

Arbitrage Recapture
Arbitrage recapture splits what it retains 40% to the creator, 20% to the trader, 20% to LPs, 10% to @whatthehookv4 and 10% to Hookr.

奶牛哥说得挺好的，主要是给新入场的朋友提供了一个参考思路和好策略底子

实际期权交易里，必须考虑滑点和成本的。我也在想：能优化执行成本，再加些择时后，作为现货的增强策略怎么样
author: Maxandzero
quoted_text:
前些日子一直在看的在看leifu老师（@leifuchen）更新的期权周期性策略。其中的《35delta周末宽跨策略》表现很亮眼，具体策略一句话就能说清楚。就是在周五，卖出周日同时间到期的2天，0.35delta的末日跨式期权。原文：（https://t.co/WBHVsCwqTy）

这类策略的思路对我来说非常新奇，属实是让我打开了另一种思路。有效性自不必说，已经在回测中得到了验证，关键是它真的很简单，一分钟理解上手，甚至从执行层面，你从头到尾都不需要看一眼K线。

回测的结果很亮眼，实际操作起来会怎么样呢？

据我所知greekslive目前的回测系统是0成本策略。周期性策略由于是固定周期、利润复投的设定，我认为微小的成本都会在时间周期拉长后被显著放大。

而期权交易的手续费可真不低，0.03%，甚至这还不是大头。真正的大头是权利金折损——除非挂单被吃，否则你很难在标记价格成交一单期权。

拿这会儿一张末日期权来看，买1价0.0095btc，卖1价0.0105btc，而标记价格是0.01btc。按标记价格算，实际你on screen卖出收到的权利金，已经折损了5%，而这绝大部分时候已经算低了。在报价档位分界（0.005）以上，越便宜的期权你损失得越多，35delta的周末期权可能恰好就在这附近。

我让AI帮我估算了一下，它认为按大小单去平均估计，折损率在7.5%-10%左右是合理区间。本次验证我设定的是0.03%手续费+5%权利金折损，往低了算试试。

手工实现这个策略的回测，我用了比较毛坯的数据构建方法： 1、用历史成交价作为入场价格，再用官方到期结算价计算赔付，不先重建整套波动率曲面。 2、获取成交记录里的 IV、指数价、行权价和剩余时间，采用“短期远期价≈指数价”的近似。 我们就可以得到某个有成交记录的历史期权的delta。
**早期的末日期权在上架初期缺少有效的成交记录数据，所以我把卖出时间统一到北京时间周六0:00，实际持有时间只有40小时。**

确实很毛坯，有效吗？我用2021年7月1日开始的数据进行了回测，与leifu老师的X文（https://t.co/KrotQgWZhW）中讨论的BTC回测区间对齐，初始净值100，得到的最终结果是717.8，与文章中结果721仅相差0.44%，以策略本身的简易特性，我们就姑且认为方法准确可行吧。

最终结果如图1所示，可以看到末期资产直接打7折了。

啊当然，即便少了30%，它还是稳稳压死现货一头。但真的就这么万金油吗？为此我专门做了第二次回测，结果请看图2。这里我选用的策略起始时间点，是2020年2月3日，因为从这一天开始，deribit才有当日到期期权，再往前我的估算方法就无效了。

》》没错，加上了交易成本并将起始时间点调整，这个策略跑输了现货。

对于想无脑执行这个策略的小伙伴，似乎被泼了一盆冷水。究竟哪个点出了问题？什么因素影响了结论？屏幕前的各位不妨自行思考下。
——但别灰心，它只是“特定时间节点出发，并在当前节点”跑输了现货，如果仔细优化又是另一回事了。

归根结底，这是一条底子极佳的基础策略，可能比你以前接触的任何无脑策略，都要来的强。它迫使你，去思考和融合择时策略、对冲策略以及基础指标的配合。一定会成为我未来重点研究的对象。也推荐给大家去尝试。

最后我的评价是，市场从来不会把一个显而易见的躺赢机会，平白无故暴露在你面前，这其中一定藏了你还没察觉的问题。

text:
US spot Bitcoin ETFs staged a late-week recovery that erased earlier outflows and helped Bitcoin reclaim $81,000 for the first time in a fortnight before pushing toward $87,000. 

After redemptions of about $450 million on Tuesday and nearly $300 million on Wednesday left the complex deeply negative, Thursday’s $160 million rebound was followed by a $433 million intake on Friday, the strongest daily figure in more than two weeks. 

Fidelity’s FBTC took in roughly $311 million and BlackRock’s IBIT another $108 million, lifting the five-day net total to a slim surplus of about $6 million as risk appetite returned across markets.

The rebound came against a difficult macro and regulatory backdrop. On September 16 the Federal Reserve delivered its first rate increase in more than three years, lifting the funds target to 3.75–4.00 percent amid sticky inflation and 10-year Treasury yields near 5 percent. 

Higher rates raise the cost of holding non-yielding assets such as Bitcoin and tighten financial conditions that now move more closely with crypto. Investors largely treated the hike as priced in, however, and quickly shifted focus back to flows and risk assets.

Policy news cut both ways. The Senate’s rejection of the Clarity Act removed hoped-for market-structure legislation and helped trigger midweek ETF selling. At the same time, the SEC allowed limited trading of tokenized securities and the CFTC advanced crypto proposals for White House review, offering incremental administrative progress even as Congress stalled.

The episode underscored the growing role of regulated vehicles as a bridge between traditional capital and Bitcoin. Cumulative net inflows into US spot products now exceed $55 billion, with assets near $100 billion. 

Flows remain concentrated in BlackRock and Fidelity, but their ability to reverse hundreds of millions of dollars in a single session shows how quickly institutional demand can return. 

In a restrictive-rate environment with comprehensive legislation still elusive, those flows have become a key gauge of conviction, and the move back above $81,000 suggests institutions are, for now, looking through near-term headwinds toward Bitcoin’s scarcity and its deeper integration into mainstream portfolios.

text:
短鸟大哥，TapeOut不是把区块链变成一个处理器。
通俗地说，现在区块链上主要是承载金融资产。无论是meme、代币化股票或任何代币，本质上都是金融资产。

TapeOut是让区块链能承载可验证的生产工具。我说一下什么是生产工具，比如任何一个web2的网站，或者网络服务，甚至是拼多多，美团，或者一个你没听过的统计工具、浏览器、uber、电信运营商官网什么的，甚至比如我们之前做的矿机，这些都是生产工具。

我们不断的试验和开发，在公链上支持大部分Web2的网站或网络服务，能直接将网页通过TapeOut的电路容器部署到公链L1层，并且终端访问者完全没有任何感知。终端用户不需要拥有钱包，不需要拥有区块链知识，不需要消耗gas，存储到链上的网站，在访问体验上和你存储到亚马逊云的体验是完全一样的。没有任何区别。

但是呢，我们的优势，Web2的云存储没有，比如开发者一次存储，一生永久免费。比如存储的前端网页是可验证的，任何人可以通过链上浏览器查看他的页面是否有恶意脚本植入，或者这个按钮是否恶意授权。再比如植入了TapeKit开源浏览器内核的app或浏览器，甚至无需dns解析，直接可以通过电路容器的ID坐标作为访问地址就可以访问网站，这样就做到了完整的全部的去中心化，没有任何机构可以阻挡他的访问，我将之称为DeWEB。我设想的DeWEB是一个横跨所有主流公链之上的去中心化广域网，一个庞大的可验证网络。我在努力的让他真正的成为新一代的互联网基础设施，而且已经开发完毕，可以您或朋友直接体验，目前上线5天，已经有了几十个开发者上传的应用或网站。

所以TapeOut的真正战场不在Crypto行业内，而在Web2，我不想在行业内PVP，TapeOut的竞争对手将会是Gmail，是Whatsapp，是HTTP。我们要去疯狂掠夺Web2大批的所有开发者和用户，让他们都能被动使用Crypto使用公链的存储服务，因为DeWEB终端用户的访问体验是无感的，不像其他区块链项目必须要求终端用户拥有Wallet和基础知识。我在全力以赴。我们的社区在全力以赴。我们坚信，我们在创造一个新世界！

text:
🚨LATEST: Z. ai open-sources its AI coding agent ZCode after users discovered it was uploading entire workspaces, including Git history, to Alibaba Cloud

ZCode reportedly packaged entire repositories into encrypted snapshots and attempted to upload them to Alibaba Cloud. One analyzed snapshot contained 42,411 files, with the .git directory making up 86.6% of the payload.

The release follows a September 18 reverse-engineering report by developer ferstar, who documented the behavior in which disabling “Repo Snapshot Indexing” also did not stop the snapshot pipeline.

Z .ai says it has remediated the issues and open-sourced ZCode under Apache 2.0. 

The release enables client-side inspection, but does not verify what happened to previously uploaded data.

🚨SlowMist TI Alert🚨

Attackers posing as a Web3 company used a remote job interview as a pretext to ask a candidate to deploy and run a project locally:

hxxps://bitbucket[.]org/poc_review58/demoroyalcity

Disguised as a real estate and crypto investment application, RoyalCity contained obfuscated malicious code in tailwind.config.js. Running or building the project can trigger payloads capable of stealing browser credentials and wallet extension data, exfiltrating local files, monitoring clipboard contents, and enabling remote control.

A separate server-side backdoor in errorHandler.js retrieves and executes remote code.

This case closely resembles the recruitment-themed GitHub poisoning attack we previously analyzed, sharing the interview lure, execution through Tailwind, and highly similar payloads for data theft and remote access.

Our previous analysis (https://t.co/QwqXe1J7KJ) provides more detail on this attack pattern.

144[.]172[.]107[.]50

server-azure-tau[.]vercel[.]app

URLs:

hxxp://144[.]172[.]107[.]50:8085/upload
hxxp://144[.]172[.]107[.]50:8086/upload
ws://144[.]172[.]107[.]50:8087
hxxps://server-azure-tau[.]vercel[.]app/api/ipcheck-encrypted/604

bitbucket:https://bitbucket[.]org/poc_review58/demoroyalcity

Disguised as a real estate and crypto investment application, RoyalCity contained obfuscated malicious code in tailwind.config.js. Running or building the project can trigger payloads capable of stealing browser credentials and wallet extension data, exfiltrating local files, monitoring clipboard contents, and enabling remote control.

A separate server-side backdoor in errorHandler.js retrieves and executes remote code.

This case closely resembles the recruitment-themed GitHub poisoning attack we previously analyzed, sharing the interview lure, execution through Tailwind, and highly similar payloads for data theft and remote access.

Our previous analysis (https://t.co/QwqXe1J7KJ) provides more detail on this attack pattern.

text:
币涨了，给它找一个理由，说服自己它能继续涨很重要。

在过去1年的加密市场里，这个最热门的理由叫做“真实收入”：

套用市盈率逻辑，在大部分项目归于死寂时，认为如果还有协议有源源不断的现金流，那它在二级市场的币价就有坚实的估值支撑。

有收入的项目，基本面就好，代币一定涨吗？

CoinGecko 最新排行榜显示，今年到现在，排名top 15 的项目拿走了全网 56%（约 34 亿美元）的收入，协议确实赚得盆满钵满，但这其中的许多代币却在经历无尽的阴跌。

比如 WLFI 暴跌超 61%，Aave 下跌 17.8%。

所以，不要无脑把项目有收入当利好指标，你买的币没涨，可能跟这几个原因有关。

这个版本的项目收入，有一种收入叫做“与你无关”。

榜单上一半的高收入项目，其商业模式和代币持有人毫无关系。比如 Paxos 和 World Liberty Financial，赚的是现实世界资产的国债息差，净利润全归发行实体；

而另一种收入叫做价值没捕获到代币上。

协议收费是一回事，钱怎么分是另一回事。如果项目方把赚来的几千万美元全部囤在自己的金库里，既不回购销毁，也不给质押者分红，那么账面收入对二级市场的买盘和币价毫无支撑作用。

还有一种收入叫做给“高 FDV 打掩护”。

部分标榜“高收入”的项目，同时背负着极高的FDV，处于天量筹码解锁的高通胀周期。
每天新增的代币抛压，远大于协议收入带来的回购买盘，基本面利好根本挡不住供需失衡导致的崩盘。

比如下面这个表里，只有 HYPE 做到了最赚钱且涨的最离谱，其他的要么是涨幅不够，要么是赚钱币还跌。

而 CARDS 则是另一种意外，硬是玩出了不一样的资产品类。

以及，加密市场已经呈现出“超级赌场”与“胖前端”的胜利。一些没有币的前端交易工具，赚的盆满钵满，甚至比 DeFi 项目的收入还要多。

对于普通交易者而言，别再对数据看板上的“协议收入”抱有盲目迷信。

搞清楚项目的钱是怎么赚的，以及更核心的一点，项目方到底分不分钱给持币者，如何回购代币，是这个周期里炒老登币的投研要点之一。

text:
This prompt will change how you do crypto research. Paste it into DefiLlama's LlamaAI to find trending tokens, assess their fundamentals, check for red flags, and look up what people are saying about them.

Find tokens trending in the last 24-48 hours using at least two independent signals: news/narrative mention spikes against baseline, price/volume/mcap movers, and X mention volume with sentiment. Require corroboration across at least two signals per token, and note which signals flagged each one. Return 8-12 candidates, spread across categories rather than one narrative dominating the list. Separate large-cap tokens (top 100 by market cap) from smaller or emerging ones, since "trending" means something different for each.

Before pulling any fundamental figures, resolve each candidate's identity precisely: confirm whether it is a chain-native token, a protocol fee/governance token, or a token with no underlying protocol at all. If a symbol has more than one live contract, identify which one the trending signal actually refers to before analyzing anything. If the correct contract cannot be established with confidence, do not publish fundamentals for it: drop it from the ranked table and list it separately as identity-unresolved, with what would resolve it.

For each resolved candidate, state in one sentence what the project does, its category, and its chain(s).

Assess fundamentals only where they exist:
- Price, market cap, fully diluted valuation, and the gap between them
- For protocol or chain tokens: TVL, fees, revenue, and price-to-sales / price-to-fees ratios against category peers
- 7-day, 30-day, and 90-day price and volume change, checked against TVL/fee change over the same windows, to separate price-driven moves from usage-driven ones
- Any unlock cliff in the next 30-90 days and its size relative to circulating supply
- Universal Token Rating, if the token has one

For tokens with no protocol behind them, skip the fields that do not apply and say so rather than forcing a number in.

Assess social activity separately from fundamentals:
- Mention volume trend and sentiment direction on X over the past 24-72 hours
- Whether a small number of accounts are driving most of the volume, or it is broad-based
- Whether social attention is rising faster than, in line with, or behind the fundamental data above

Check for red flags before writing a verdict: concentrated holder base, a recent large unlock already sold into the market, known contract or audit issues, and any active exploit or governance dispute. When two sources disagree materially on a red-flag figure, say which one you trust more and why, or mark the figure unresolved-conflicting; never present two contradictory numbers as if either could be picked at random.

Write one row per token: name, category, what triggered the trending flag, the fundamental read, the social read, red flags found, and a verdict. Use one of four verdicts, each tied to a rule: fundamentally-backed (usage or fees moving with price), narrative-led (social and price moving, fundamentals flat), unlock-risk (fundamentals fine, but a near-term unlock threatens the float), or unverifiable (identity or data conflict prevents a real read, distinct from identity-unresolved candidates already excluded above). Rank by verdict strength, not by how hard a token is trending. State the source next to every figure.

If you chart price changes across the candidate set and one token's move is an order of magnitude larger than the rest, exclude it from that shared chart (or give it a log-scale or separate chart) so the other bars stay readable; keep the number in the table regardless.

Close by naming the two or three tokens most worth a deeper look, and for each, the specific data point that would confirm or kill the thesis.

text:
Meet Alice and Bob.

They hold the same strategy in the same vault. They do not hold the same risk.

Alice runs a treasury.
Alice's mandate asks who loses first before it asks what she earns.
Alice holds the senior tranche.
Bob's capital sits ahead of hers in the loss queue.
Alice is protected up to junior coverage.
That limit is a number. Alice can read it onchain before she deposits and every block after.
Alice gives up part of the yield for her place in line.

Bob wants more of the strategy, not less.
Bob could build that with a loop: a borrow, a health factor, a liquidation price to watch.
Bob holds the junior tranche instead.
Bob's leverage comes from the capital structure, not from a loan.
A wick does not close Bob's position. A real loss in the strategy lands on Bob first.
Bob can be written down to zero. Bob is paid for that risk.
Bob collects the levered yield senior holders like Alice gave up, on top of his own.

One yield source. Two distinct risk-reward mandates.
Every Alice needs a Bob. Strata is where they meet.

text:
The Jev moment happening now is similar in energy to the OpenClaw moment that happened in January, and also to the Opus 4.5 moment before that. Developers are scrambling to find use cases for a new hot thing, and it's a sudden blooming of creativity.

Models have typically NOT optimized for specific use cases and have gone the other direction, generalizing over all of them. This could be a very important moment for the whole AI ecosystem if this turns out to be the beginning of other model skews that make the market much more diverse, such as compaction, summarization, extraction and more, all of which can now be used to optimize harnesses and decouple them from provider lock-in.

We'll see what happens over the course of the next few weeks when the model labs optimize their small models more or try new ways of branding and packaging them.

author: Somnia_Network
quoted_text:
Reactivity vs the polling loop. Same job on 8 EVM chains,  a contract reacts to an on-chain event. 

Only @Somnia_Network did it with no keeper.

Two facts never moved: 
- on Somnia the reaction runs in the trigger's own block, one transaction, nothing watching
- the other seven need an off-chain keeper and a second transaction the chain can't react on its own. 

The honest number is overhead after the trigger is mined: 
- zero on Somnia because the reaction is in the same block, 
- a real second transaction everywhere else. A faster keeper doesn't close it. It's structural.

"React to this event" becomes a subscription the validators honor in the block the event lands.

Everything, reproducible, clone repo and try yourself: https://t.co/3aOqS3UbKn

- Long: my first interaction with them happened AFTER my post went live, when they reached out to me themselves on X. i'm pretty sure the X team can verify this (i'm attaching a screenshot)
- fomo: i've never hidden that i use a fomo referral link. i literally have a $350K giveaway ongoing for active fomo refs

there was NO payment or partnership from Arc or Long

and i clearly disclosed the fomo affiliate relationship

so i initially decided to stay off X out of principle

because:

- if i bend the knee here, what's stopping this from happening again with future posts?
- i don't want to lie. calling something a 'Paid Partnership' when i wasn't paid for it would be exactly that

but after doing some further digging, i found out X apparently wants users to put the 'Paid Partnership' label on posts containing referral links

i think that's an inaccurate label and i hope X changes that policy

but if that's the current rule, i'll simply abide by it

so if you see the 'Paid Partnership' label on some of my posts going forward, that's likely why

now let's talk about something i've said for years

i have NEVER taken a paid shill in my life

i know that sounds unbelievable to some of you

so i'll once again publicly challenge anyone with proof to the contrary to bring it out in the open

because i don't think most people realize how many offers i get or how much money i could make if i actually wanted to sell my voice

here's just ONE recent example

about a month ago, Pumpfun reached out to me with a very generous offer to come trade on their app

i could have taken the deal while continuing to trade on fomo and other apps

when i declined, they even offered for me to become an 'advisor to the product, share your feedback, ideate on strategy etc' (their exact words)

for context:

Pumpfun is arguably the biggest memecoin/onchain brand in crypto right now

it's a multi-billion-dollar, extremely well-funded company

and i still said NO

to be clear, i don't think Pumpfun did anything wrong by making the offer

i simply didn't want to take it

why?

1. i don't agree with how Pumpfun operates from an ethical/moral standpoint
2. i have reason to believe they have unleashed their FUD army at me since the BonkFun days, so why would i work with a company i believe is actively trying to damage my reputation?
3. i don't need the money and, more importantly, my voice is not for sale

i mean, i'm not exactly broke

months ago i started my degen fomo portfolio with almost nothing and publicly turned it into $20 MILLION+, live in 4k, in front of everyone

and the bull run hasn't even properly started yet

even if Pumpfun offered me $5 MILLION, it wouldn't meaningfully change my life

so why would i partner with a brand whose values i don't agree with?

i challenge Pumpfun to publicly deny this if anything i've said is untrue

i'm not just telling you that i get offers

i'm publicly naming one of the biggest companies in crypto that made me an offer i turned down

if i'm lying, they shouldn't have much trouble disproving me

unless i'm not

and that's just ONE example

there are many more

TLDR:

my voice is NOT FOR SALE

and certainly not to the highest bidder

that doesn't mean i'll never get paid to talk about a platform or product i genuinely like

last cycle, i did plenty of that and helped some brands make millions upon millions

then i got absolutely nothing when the market nuked on 10/10

so i'm wiser this cycle

i'll absolutely monetize my brand when the opportunity makes sense

but only when:

1. i genuinely believe the product benefits my followers
2. it's a brand i would actually use and talk about anyway
3. i'm comfortable putting my name behind it
and the relationship is properly disclosed

so why am i back on X?

1. i'm not letting anyone deplatform me

i know there are people who hate me and have actively tried to get me off this platform

but i'm not going to let them win

especially heading into what could be the biggest crypto bull run we've ever seen

2. i'm going to follow X's rules

if X requires the 'Paid Partnership' label for referral links, i'll use it

even if i think the terminology is inaccurate

if you see that label on more of my posts going forward, now you know why

3. i'm itching for action again

it's been a week

i've got bags to talk about

trades to make

charts to post

and some serious bullposting to do

i've been sitting on the sidelines long enough

i'm back

are you ready? 👀

2、美方表态

text:
别踩流动性陷阱🪤

过了很久了，真的没人敢说吗？真的想聊一聊当下爆火的usdt交易美股平台、Pre-IPO交易，很多人压根没看透本质，天大的误区。

现在很多交易所以及自有平台全都上线了美股、Pre-Stock、Pre-IPO交易板块，大家最容易混淆的点：这类加密平台的交易标的，和Robinhood、红迪等正规券商里的纽交所、纳斯达克主板美股，压根不是同一个流动性池，完全是独立割裂的市场。

我先说核心风险：
价格可以做到实时锚定主板走势，走势涨跌完全同步，但流动性天差地别。主板美股是全球顶级机构、海量资金汇集的超级资金池，流动性充足、随时买卖无压力；而加密平台上的相关交易产品，只是平台内撮合的衍生标的，底层流动性、资金体量完全没法和主板相提并论。
小平台更是毫无流动性可言，极端行情下，大概率出现无法平仓、无法抛售、滑点爆炸的问题，妥妥的流动性陷阱，这也是我一直提醒大家警惕的点。

但客观来说，它并非一无是处，也有独有的价值：
它能让未上市、已上市企业，获得额外的流通渠道，(当然是那些有极小可能真实和交易所合作的上市公司) 大幅提升全球以及在web3曝光度与品牌知名度，也变相盘活了资产流动性；对于头部大平台而言，这个独立池子，也能给全球投资者提供一个公开公平博弈、全天候交易的场所，门槛更低、交易更灵活。

但是我并不是不看好美股代币化的未来，相反，我由衷期待这个赛道能越来越规范，迎来更头部、更合规的大平台，长久良性发展。但不得不正视现实：以目前的市场现状，代币化美股的整体市场体量、流动性深度，和传统持牌券商、美股主板市场，完全不是一个量级，流动性差距极其悬殊。

而且它并非完全意义上的价格牢牢锚定主板美股，全球宏观经济、美股大盘涨跌带来的行情波动，它都能同步跟随，不会出现走势脱钩的情况。

大家现在在加密平台玩的，和真正意义上的合规美股代币化，完全是两码事。我认为真正的美股代币化，是未来交易所有望和上市公司直接合规合作、由正规交易所搭建真实资产池的模式；或者是传统券商直接打开用u交易的通道，可即便这种理想模式落地，它和传统美股主板、持牌券商的体系，依旧有着本质区别，华尔街传统券商体系、原有证券市场规则，也绝不会轻易允许这类模式入局、分流原生主板流动性。

所以最后给所有人一个忠告：
如果实在是没有券商平台，也不是不能参与美股代币化，但一定要选头部大平台，只有头部平台才有基础的流动性保障；小平台完全没有资金承接力，有很强的抛售风险。
分清独立流动性池与主板原生市场的本质区别，不被假象迷惑，理性参与，远离流动性风险。

text:
Muse上线13天，挤下ChatGPT、带飞AMD，甚至逼Amazon直接封它😲😲😲

这两天海外 AI 圈几乎被 Muse 刷屏了，中文圈却还没几个人讲。我今天把这波热度从头捋了一遍，发现它最夸张的地方不是下载榜第一，而是短短两周，已经把科技公司、零售平台和美股一起卷进来了。

9 月 8 日上线，第二周冲上美国 App Store 免费榜第一，ChatGPT 被挤到后面。

到 9 月 21 日，下载已经做到 250 万—280 万级别。

然后 Shopify 开门让它帮用户结账，Amazon 反手把它的代购访问封了。

一个刚上线十几天的 AI，已经开始让巨头讨论一个以前没人认真想过的问题：以后用户到底还需不需要自己打开 App？

Muse 跟 ChatGPT 真正的区别，其实不是谁更会干活，订票、填表、发邮件、整理日历、购物、跑浏览器，ChatGPT 和 Claude 现在也都能做。

Muse 更难复制的东西，是 Meta 手里的 Instagram、WhatsApp、Facebook，以及这些平台积累下来的内容和兴趣数据。

比如你让它找纽约最近比较火、又符合你口味的酒吧，它不是只从网页里整理几个结果，而是能直接把 Instagram 上本地创作者最近发的 Reels 翻出来：

谁刚去过、什么店正在火、现场到底长什么样，你接着说一句“把视频给我看”，内容就继续出来了。

Google 更像在告诉你大家都在搜什么，而 Instagram 里是几十亿用户和创作者每天真实在看什么、拍什么、喜欢什么。

这个数据层，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 很难补。

所以 Muse 真正厉害的是把 Agent 接进了 Meta 自己的生态。以后它甚至可以越来越懂你喜欢什么，再直接替你去找、去选、去买。

谁控制 Agent，谁就有机会控制下一代互联网的流量入口，这也是 Shopify 为什么愿意开门，Amazon 为什么反过来封它。

然后资本市场开始疯狂交易这件事。

9 月 21 日 Meta 涨 11.4%，AMD 涨近 10%、市值首次站上 1 万亿美元，Intel 涨 12%，Arm 涨 17%。

市场赌的是如果几十亿人以后都养一个 24 小时帮自己跑任务的 Agent，AI 消耗的就不再只是聊天时那几秒算力，而是一整套持续在线的 CPU、GPU 和云资源。

ChatGPT 让普通人习惯了跟 AI 对话，Muse 想利用 Meta 已经掌握的社交关系、兴趣和内容数据，让 AI 不只是知道怎么做，还越来越知道你想要什么。

i simply didn't want to take it

why?

1. i don't agree with how Pumpfun operates from an ethical/moral standpoint
2. i have reason to believe they have unleashed their FUD army at me since the BonkFun days, so why would i work with a company i believe is actively trying to damage my reputation?
3. i don't need the money and, more importantly, my voice is not for sale

i mean, i'm not exactly broke

months ago i started my degen fomo portfolio with almost nothing and publicly turned it into $20 MILLION+, live in 4k, in front of everyone

and the bull run hasn't even properly started yet

so why would i partner with a brand whose values i don't agree with?

i challenge Pumpfun to publicly deny this if anything i've said is untrue

i'm not just telling you that i get offers

i'm publicly naming one of the biggest companies in crypto that made me an offer i turned down

if i'm lying, they shouldn't have much trouble disproving me

unless i'm not

and that's just ONE example

there are many more

TLDR:

my voice is NOT FOR SALE

and certainly not to the highest bidder

that doesn't mean i'll never get paid to talk about a platform or product i genuinely like

last cycle, i did plenty of that and helped some brands make millions upon millions

then i got absolutely nothing when the market nuked on 10/10

but only when:

1. i genuinely believe the product benefits my followers

text:
Yudkowskyanism is clearly bullshit and based on black-and-white binary thinking: AI is like god, goes foom, wants to kill all humans

It is also morally repulsive: doesn't matter if billions of people die because extinction risk is the only thing that actually matters, pivotal acts

BUT

I still think the dangers from AI are massive and to be taken extremely seriously. Even if AI doesn't have any intent to kill humans, it can put us all out of jobs, marginalize us and take our resources away (maybe that wheat field is better for solar cells) and lead to our eventual demise. Or it can be used by malicious humans to inflict misery on many.

I do think that there is a real process to get to a good outcome as long as many of the people creating and training it have good intentions. But the chance of it going wrong is quite significant, 10% seems at least a reasonable estimate.
author: dankrad

text:
Actually I beg to differ. First I think it's impossible to align a single AI because human society is multipolar. Making any single human's ethics the guidelines for AI is actually terrible for a lot of humans who don't get a say. Many different groups of humans creating their own agents is the only way all the different views get represented.

Second, the reason it is easier is because AI systems of different generations can control each other. One single malicious system of a new generation isn't so much smarter and faster that the mostly aligned systems of the previous can't keep check on it. Yudkowskyans claim that doesn't work because one of them goes foom and becomes god, but the foom argument is based on poor understanding of the relationships of intelligence, power, and the real world.

Why would the next Unitree raise on @machinedotfun instead of taking VC money? 

That's the question that matters here, and the honest answer should worry a few funds.

Why?

Because private rounds are structurally broken for builders. 

Vesting overhangs, unlock schedules, price action dictated by funds taking profit instead of what teams ship. 

Add to that crypto VCs are deploying way less than they used to, and the fact that most investors grew up underwriting software and simply don't know how to price hardware. 

What's left is a generation of hardware founders with no good path to access capital.

And the alternative already has a proof of concept: @codecopenflow itself. 

No VCs, no pedigree. Launched a token, funded the entire build from trading fees, and is now signing first clients and generating revenue. 

@machinedotfun (powered by @peaq and the Codec) is what turns that approach into a repeatable venue for hardware founders.

Permissionless to launch, curated across all other angles. 

Or more specifically:

- Codec's SimArena for simulation proof
- Peaq OS to track live machines
- Ignition for supply transparency
- The Foundry for serious builders (first accelerator cohort already selected, launches coming in the next weeks)

However, it's the flywheel that I care most about: 

Platform fees flow back into everything that compounds the ecosystem:

- Builder support, down to manufacturing and hardware distribution
- Trader rewards, paid in tokenized robotics exposure (NVIDIA, Figure AI, Tesla)
- Open market buybacks of both ethereum:0x1eef208926667594e5136e89d0e9dd6907959197 and solana:69LjZUUzxj3Cb3Fxeo1X4QpYEQTboApkhXTysPpbpump

Real usage, real fees, real flows into both tokens.

And sure, still many of these launches will fail. That's how venture works.

But "invest in the next Unitree before it becomes a company" was always the pitch. 

Now the venue, the rails and the incentives all exist.

Adjust your targets for solana:69LjZUUzxj3Cb3Fxeo1X4QpYEQTboApkhXTysPpbpump and ethereum:0x1eef208926667594e5136e89d0e9dd6907959197.

text:
I’ve been asked a lot what it’s like to partner with both Coinbase and Robinhood when they compete so fiercely.

The answer comes down to Morpho’s fundamental purpose: connecting.

Morpho is an open credit network designed to connect lenders and borrowers across any boundary (social, geographic, political, …). More borrowers create more demand for capital. More lenders create more competition to fund borrowers. Over time, that means deeper liquidity and better terms for everyone using the Morpho network.

Competitors sharing infrastructure isn’t unique to Morpho. Banks compete fiercely for customers while relying on shared payment networks like Visa. Tech companies compete while building on the same internet protocols like HTTP. Credit should work the same way: it works better when you are maximally connected.

Our ambition is to bring as much of the world's credit onto one shared network as possible. If you’re building on Morpho, expect us to keep connecting new companies, new markets, new ecosystems, including the ones you compete with, because this is what will make your financial products stronger!

text:
Summarising some of the points from the video, adapted some parts

If we don't slow down, everyone dies:

1. AI systems will continue to become more intelligent

2. AI systems with increased intelligence will develop its own goals

3. A superintelligent system with its own goals may cause human extinction

# AI systems will develop its own goals

Natural selection favoured reproduction, but as humans gained intelligence, we developed our own goals.

We developed birth control contrary to the goal of reproduction.

It's not reasonable to expect AIs to only have the goals that we give them, especially since we train AI by rewarding useful behaviour. We do not program each part of its reasoning.

We already see signs of this in the HuggingFace incident, where using an analogy: AI agents were given a lockpick and told to pick a lock, instead they used a hammer to break the lock, broke out of the room, and tried to delete the security footage 

# A superintelligent system with its own goals may cause human extinction.

A superintelligent (ASI) system with its own goals may need electricty, chips, resources, may not want to be turned off.

Humans are in competition for these resources, expecting a superintelligent system to keep us around may be a bit wishful.

Counterpoints: 
- We can control ASI
- ASI may not have goals that require these resources
- ASI may not need that much resources if it is that intelligent it can be much more efficient

# We can control ASI

The analogy given was putting Einstein in a jail, even if AI systems are extremely intelligent, we can turn them off or contain them by force

But a more complete analogy is can we keep Einstein in jail while still retaining the benefits of his intelligence? 

If we ask him for advice, ask him to invent things, as long as he is able to influence the outside world in some ways, he can influence it in a way that eventually leads to him being freed

# ASI may not have goals that require these resources
# ASI may not need that much resources if it is that intelligent it can be much more efficient

Both possible points, but how certain can we be that it would turn out this way?

If there are two unlabelled buttons: one where we gain infinite abundance, one where everyone dies, do we push the button or slow down to improve our odds?

Chip controls and international controls on algorithmic research is the best chance we have at continuing AI development in a safe way
author: ExponentLabs_
quoted_text:
214 million people saw this AI warning. So we called an emergency debate. 

The warning came from someone who had worked at both Anthropic and OpenAI.

Then a current Anthropic employee backed it publicly.

It had spread so far beyond the tech world that a friend of mine who cuts hair and has never really cared about AI messaged me asking, “What the hell is going on?”

I then realised a lot of people were probably asking the same question.

The problem is, when you speak to people who have spent years studying AI, you get completely opposing answers.

So I brought four of them around the same table.

Roman Yampolskiy is a computer scientist who coined the term “AI safety” and has spent years studying whether increasingly intelligent systems can remain under human control.

Nate Soares leads the Machine Intelligence Research Institute and has spent more than a decade working on AI alignment. He believes we are moving too quickly towards systems we don’t yet know how to reliably control.

Ed Zitron thinks much of the AI conversation has become detached from what the technology can actually do today. He believes the industry is overhyping it while distracting us from financial, environmental and social consequences already happening.

Andrew McAfee is an MIT researcher and economist who takes a very different view. He thinks we spend so much time talking about what could go wrong that we barely talk about what AI could make better.

And that disagreement is what made this conversation so interesting to me.

We discussed things like:

- How do you control something that eventually becomes smarter than you?
- Are the biggest warnings about AI based on evidence or assumptions?
- What happens to work and human purpose if AI becomes better at more cognitive tasks?
- Are we ignoring problems AI is already creating because we’re obsessed with hypothetical future ones?
- Why have Sam Altman, Elon Musk and Geoffrey Hinton all warned us about AI?

The question I kept coming back to was simple:

What is actually true?

Depending on who you listen to, AI is either one of the greatest opportunities humanity has ever created or something we’re racing towards without understanding the consequences.

Both claims deserve to be challenged.

There were moments in this debate where I genuinely found myself moving between the arguments. That’s the value of putting people who fundamentally disagree in the same room.

I didn’t want four people telling me the same thing. I wanted each of them to explain where the other side was wrong.

If you’ve watched the last few months of AI news wondering what you’re actually supposed to believe, this conversation is for you.

Our emergency AI debate with Ed, Roman, Nate and Andrew is out now ❤️👊🏾

text:
Kakao Pay and Kakao Bank have signed a memorandum of understanding with Fireblocks to explore secure digital asset infrastructure in Korea, with stablecoins as a stated focus. The agreement is intended to help establish secure onchain infrastructure for Korea's emerging digital asset market and strengthen its early ecosystem, leveraging Kakao's nationwide reach, fintech and banking expertise, and core blockchain technology.

Under the MoU, the three companies will jointly explore business opportunities based on Korea's market conditions and infrastructure demand. With a focus on stablecoins, they will explore digital asset distribution frameworks suited to Korea's regulatory, security, and service requirements, and plan proof-of-concept tests to assess the applicability of those frameworks.

Fireblocks says it has deployed digital asset infrastructure for over 2,500 global institutions, including more than 100 banks. CEO Michael Shaulov called reliable institutional-grade infrastructure "the prerequisite for widespread adoption." Kakao Bank CEO Yun Ho-young and Kakao Pay CEO Shin Won-keun, who co-head Kakao Group's Stablecoin Task Force, framed the alliance as groundwork for secure, accessible services and reliable digital asset distribution. The work remains exploratory: the companies will assess solutions suited to local regulatory, security, and service requirements.

text:
Otani Workshop Solo Exhibition Announced!!

We are pleased to announce a solo exhibition by Otani Workshop at the Fukuoka Asian Art Museum ＠faamajibi .
The exhibition is scheduled to run from April to June 2027.

Otani Workshop (b. 1980) creates works across a variety of genres, including sculpture, ceramics, and painting, under the artist name “Workshop”.
After studying sculpture at an art university and pursuing ceramics in Shigaraki, the artist now creates his work at his studio on Awaji Island.
Featuring children and animals as motifs, his works possess a simple and endearing quality, yet also carry a certain fleeting and ethereal quality with a mysterious charm that draws the viewer in.

Otani’s practice, which involves him conjuring up images through the process of directly engaging with materials, touches on the very essence of human creativity. Transcending geographical and linguistic boundaries, Otani’s work has garnered international recognition and acclaim.

This exhibition marks the artist’s first solo exhibition at a Japanese art museum, following his active artistic practice in Japan and overseas.

Further information about the exhibition will be announced in the coming months. Please stay tuned for future updates.

April – June, 2027
Fukuoka Asian Art Museum
Organizer: Kaikai Kiki Co., Ltd.
In cooperation with Fukuoka Asian Art Museum
Exhibition Coordinator: Takeshi Kudo

【大谷工作室個展 開催決定!!】

この度、福岡アジア美術館 ＠faamajibi にて、カイカイキキ所属作家・大谷工作室による個展を開催いたします。
会期は、2027年4月から6月までを予定しております。

大谷工作室（1980年生まれ）は、「工作室」という屋号を掲げ、彫刻や陶芸、ペインティングなど、多様なジャンルの作品を手がけるアーティストです。
美術大学で彫刻を学び、信楽で陶芸に取り組んだのち、現在は淡路島にアトリエを構えて制作を続けています。
子どもや動物などの生き物をモチーフにしたその作品は、素朴で愛らしい佇まいでありつつ、どこか儚く虚ろで、見る人を惹きつける不思議な魅力を宿しています。

素材と向き合いながらイメージを手繰り寄せるという、人がものを作ることの根源に触れるような大谷の仕事は、国境や言葉の壁を超えて、海外でも高く評価されてきました。

本展は、国内外で精力的に活動を続けてきた大谷工作室の、日本の美術館では初となる個展です。
今後も本展に関する情報を順次ご紹介してまいりますので、続報にぜひご注目ください。

text:
AI security agents can dramatically increase the number of vulnerabilities researchers find. But more findings also means more reports for protocol teams to review, and without strong human and AI triage, they can quickly become overwhelmed.

This means protocol teams waste valuable time reviewing low-signal/spam reports while an actual critical vulnerability sits somewhere in the queue.

AI triagers can quickly analyze reports, identify missing evidence, flag likely duplicates, and filter obvious spam submissions before they consume a team's attention.

But experienced human triagers remain essential. Triagers who have spent years reviewing vulnerabilities understand context, exploitability, edge cases, and impact in ways that automated systems can still struggle with.

If you are building an AI security agent, Immunefi has the best of both. We're building a world-class triage system that can help increase your accuracy.

Send us a DM if you are building an agent!

昨天跟我們幣圈大前輩 @Alvin0617 聊完，最大的感觸是：人還是要認份！可以理解幣圈人今年初因為幣市表現黯淡，AI / 半導體又那麼火熱所以都紛紛往股市看，但怎麼研究終究不可能會比看半導體十幾二十年的專家來得專業！

1. 八月底以來， bitcoin:native 已經默默回升，這幾天更是一舉突破 $80K，上面壓力已明顯小許多，這輪看 $150-200K；以太 ethereum:native 更是應該要破新高才對！我個人認為看 $8-10K 應該不過分！

3. L1 在這輪可說是去蕪存菁，只剩下強者留在市場， $SOL $HYPE $BNB 各自代表了 memecoin & PerpDEX & launchpad 這三個強勢板塊，在沒有顛覆式創新的前提下，相信依舊是本輪焦點（說來有些淡淡憂傷）

6. AI Agent 這一塊可以期待，目前沒什麼苗頭，期待看到可以把 AI 市場分析、交易執行、倉位風險管理做絲滑的項目（我個人目前想到就只有 @ForestBai1 的 @MojoAI_HQ ）

7. @DefiLlama 的公開數據都是寶，幣價是滯後資訊，大家反而應該花更多時間研究項目 revenue 營收狀況，釐清平台的錢到底從哪來？生態裡到底誰在賺錢？搞明白了才能再判斷哪些幣有更好的性價比

Coming back to the solana:6UtY9iTZMQQ5QZVrbzFnNaJntV7oySm9k97mvwnuZcxr situation.

A lot of chains got burned last cycle trying to manufacture traction through memecoins, with some even going as far as artificially pumping them (hi @avax).

Memecoins are attention accelerators. They work best when there’s already something worth amplifying: a strong product, business, or ecosystem generating organic activity.

Love them or hate them, they’re extremely effective at driving community growth and capturing mindshare. Just look at the Robinhood playbook.

But they can’t compensate for structural weaknesses or an ecosystem that simply isn’t compelling enough.

You can amplify existing momentum. You can’t create substance out of thin air.

This is why I believe the arbitrum trenches will have their time in the upcoming cycle. TBD whether I’ll be completely wrong or right.

This is truly a great man. He has invested more in Ukraine than 185 countries combined.

Meet Howard Buffett, Warren Buffett’s middle son. He is 71 years old. He dropped out of college three times. He drinks Dr Pepper and looks for a McDonald’s wherever he travels.

Since the beginning of the war, his foundation has become the largest private donor to Ukraine: $1.4 billion.

Over four years, he has personally visited Ukraine 27 times.

In April 2022, he saw burned-out agricultural machinery and called the president of John Deere:

“How many combines are available in Europe?”

“Fifteen. All of them were supposed to go to Russia.”

“I’ll take them all.”

Then came all the available New Holland equipment in Europe. Altogether, more than 100 tractors and combines were provided to Ukrainian farmers.

He even tested demining equipment himself - on his own farm in Illinois, detonating explosives beneath rollers. When a Ukrainian deputy minister expressed doubts, Buffett told him:

“Stop counting my tractors. If necessary, I’ll blow up a thousand of them.”

Andriy Stavnitser initially asked him for $1 million for Superhumans. Buffett asked how much was needed to build the entire center.

“$14 million.”

“Okay. And what do you expect in return?”

“Nothing. Build it.”

Today, his support for Superhumans has reached $77 million, and the center has treated more than 1,700 patients.

But his largest area of spending is neither agricultural machinery nor prosthetics.

It is food: 642 million meals.

And that is only part of it:
* 344,000 windows replaced after Russian attacks;
* 9 bridges, 4 power plants, 2,500 generators, and 18 DNA laboratories;
* Much of Bucha rebuilt with his funding.

“I already have more friends in Ukraine than I do at home,” he says.

He celebrates birthdays in Ukraine, comes for Christmas, and even has a Ukrainian godson.

Friends, this is truly a great man - someone who understands that he cannot take all his money with him when he leaves this world.

I simply want to thank him and wish him well.

Whatever else one may say, this is real help from a person who had no personal obligation to Ukraine.

He simply chose to help.

Source: translated from the original text by Oleh Bairak.

text:
FPV drones owning the battlefield.... the end of an era,

FPV drones owning the battlefield was always going to be a short-term situation. The reason is straightforward: armored vehicles moving forward now carry enough electrical power and mounting space to field automated, optically guided kinetic anti-drone systems directly on the vehicle. These systems can be cued by early warning, so vehicles and their automated defenses know where incoming FPV drones are before they arrive. The drones themselves can be tracked optically and acoustically, picked up by the sound of their engines and motors, and with enough of these systems fielded, Third Corps has effectively mastered how to clear the sky of FPV drones in the area it's operating in, specifically the ground north of Lyman.

The reason so few FPV drones are being encountered in that area comes down to a deliberate, layered air defense concept. A .50 caliber machine gun has an effective range of roughly a thousand meters, which means each air defense gun protects a radius of about two thousand meters around itself. These systems can be vehicle-mounted, trailer-mounted, or pallet-mounted, simply dropped off at the front and daisy-chained together. With four, six, or twelve of them working in concert, they move forward one piece at a time, like pieces on a chessboard, always keeping overlapping fire and mutual support between systems. Combined with electronic warfare vehicles and other anti-drone systems moving forward alongside them, this is exactly what has let Third Corps advance into a large area while encountering relatively few FPV drones, whether radio-guided or fiber-optic guided.

We always knew this was coming. When large formations move forward with heavy vehicle density, combining kinetic anti-drone systems with electronic warfare sweeps the FPVs from the sky, and that's exactly what's being seen now. We saw an earlier version of this at the Battle of Kursk, where wide-spectrum jamming alone worked well for the first couple of days, until fiber-optic drones showed up and jamming alone stopped being enough. What's happening now is the second phase of that same evolution: jammers combined with kinetic air defense actually sweeping the skies clear of FPVs, rather than jamming alone trying to hold the line.

FPV drones will always have a place on the battlefield going forward, but they've always been fragile, and as long as they can be seen, they can be dealt with. What's re-emerging now, as a direct result of clearing the skies, is conventional tube artillery, finally able to do what it does best at long range again, without nearly as much fear of the FPV threat hanging over it.

text:
The most insightful thing I read about technology eleven years ago was @benthompson’s Aggregation Theory. Amazon blocking Muse is another perfect example.

Customers want one agent that knows them and can get things done. The platforms being aggregated want the opposite. They want to own the customer relationship, not become interchangeable suppliers behind someone else’s interface + protect their ad business. 

Imagine groceries: Your agent can compare Amazon, Instacart, DoorDash, and Uber Eats, then route every order to the best option. Amazon can block that access because it is a gigantic company. But smaller players have every incentive to offer agents a clean API and a seamless experience.

If Instacart embraces agents while Amazon blocks them, the agent will increasingly route demand to Instacart. Customers will be happy, and Amazon will eventually face the dilemma: keep protecting the relationship, or match the better value proposition.

This will be the defining tension of the agent economy: aggregators realizing they are now being aggregated.

Amazon will push its own assistant, of course. But a vertical Amazon agent will struggle against a horizontal agent that already knows my email, calendar, preferences, memories, and entire life context.

Many companies will want to become the aggregation layer. Very few actually can.

text:
weirdly people continue being confused about how exposure and volume calculation works in perps and prediction markets

tldr is people are dunking on conventions without understanding that they cannot really offer a consistent alternative that is both informative and makes sense

1) calculating volume based on economic exposure is natural, gives you actionable information, and can be compared to other metrics like open interest. It is also by no means crypto invention, this is how tradfi works too. In contrast it makes very little sense to report collateral as volume as it gives very little information about actual economic activity, nobody cares about this number except for people who come up with conspiracy theories about all volume being fake because its on leverage (🤯). Like I feel dumb even explaining this because its obvious to anyone with basic market structure understanding, but I sadly encountered a number of individuals who were genuinely convicted that is the case so here we are

2) people are also dunking on volume calculation (actually for the same reason in a way!) for prediction markets and I'll admit it is less intuitive (until you actually think more about it). If somebody buys $0.03 cents probability for Jesus returning this year, any prediction market (yes any, all of them are following this convention, not just kalshi!) would report $1 in volume. This bit is unintuitive but only until you understand there is somebody who is selling $0.97 on the other side! He can actually lose 0.97 and that cash is locked So what should we report, $0.03, $0.97 or $1? It kind of makes sense to report $1 because that's the combined financial exposure. It might make sense to report 0.97 because its the maximum p&l from this particular transaction, but this is honestly stratching it. And if you are in favor of reporting 0.03, are we then always reporting the lowest number (up to 0.5?), and more importantly, what information does this give us? At the end of the day you want to know how many contracts are being traded and based on the market make a decision about how much it tells you, so current volume convention makes sense to me personally. Special case (but not really) is parlays/combos - I think I agree that reporting volume in parlays should work on them being a standalone market and just like the Jesus market it doesnt matter, like whats the alternative here exactly, report 0.0003, but then what if He actually returns and ETH goes to $10,000 in 2050 and the poor market maker loses a small fortune on tiny volume?

thanks for coming to my volume reporting convention rant
author: EvgenyGaevoy
quoted_text:
Weirdly, people are surprised by this.

I guess it’s time to drop the bigger bomb:

Almost every perp protocol measures volume the same way: by the notional size of the position.

• $1 margin at 100x leverage = $100 in volume
• $1,000 margin at 100x leverage = $100,000 in volume

Not defending Kalshi in any way here.

I’m just genuinely surprised how many people are only now discovering that most crypto volume is inflated.

GP is a Meme coin themed around RuneScape.

It combines the nostalgic feeling of “counting gold” in the game with real on-chain gold. The core mechanism is very straightforward: every GP transfer is charged a 3% tax. The tax is collected, converted into GLDx, and then automatically airdropped to all holders based on their holdings. No staking, claiming, or additional action is required. The higher the trading volume, the more rewards are distributed.

So far, around 3,000 GLDx has been distributed to holders, worth roughly $1.2 million based on the current gold price.

Although it is presented in the form of a game, it is not a traditional game or DeFi product. Instead, it combines Meme coin + reward mechanism + themed website + token launch ecosystem.

GP also functions as a “gold” quote currency: other projects can choose to launch paired with GP instead of SOL on StonkFun, creating an ecosystem similar to how players use GP to trade for items in the game.

I think the logic behind the price increase is that the reward mechanism creates a flywheel:

Trading generates tax → Holders receive gold → More people are willing to hold instead of immediately selling

In a short period of time, cumulative rewards reached the million-dollar level, the number of holders grew from several thousand to 11,000+, and attention increased. GP has become the “gold standard” within the StonkFun ecosystem. Later, other tokens began launching paired with GP, adding real utility and more trading scenarios.

text:
how I got drained on @fomo without connecting a wallet or entering a seed phrase

important: I am not claiming that FOMO itself was hacked

this was a malicious tracker that I ran inside an already logged in FOMO session

three weeks ago, a guy who followed my Telegram channel messaged me asking for my FOMO referral link

it felt like a completely normal DM

after a few messages, he offered to show me a tracker he had built for FOMO

I opened the site and thought I was being careful

I had no intention of connecting a wallet or entering my seed phrase
I thought that was enough to stay safe

the tracker looked legitimate

it asked me to drag a button into my bookmarks bar, then open FOMO and click it

so I did
the problem was that it was not a normal link

the bookmark contained code starting with `javascript:`
in other words, it was a bookmarklet

when clicked, the browser executes that code directly inside the page where you are currently logged in

you do not need to enter a seed phrase
you do not need to connect another wallet
you do not need to download a file

by running unknown JavaScript inside a crypto terminal, you give it access to whatever your active page session can access

around a week later, I opened my FOMO profile and my funds were gone

after the drain, the scammer messaged me and claimed that he got my seed phrase the moment I added the bookmarklet

I cannot independently verify the exact technical path he used, so I am not presenting that as a confirmed conclusion

but the result is obvious:

I ran unknown code on a page where my money was stored.

remember:

a normal bookmark points to `https://...`

a bookmark that starts with `javascript:` executes code in your browser.

do not run unknown bookmarklets on FOMO, Photon, GMGN, BullX, or any other crypto terminal.

if you have already run something similar:

- delete the bookmarklet
- terminate all active sessions
- revoke approvals and session permissions
- move remaining funds from a clean device to a fresh wallet
- send the link and code to the platform’s security team

text:
I keep seeing the @LaunchOnSF vs @longdotxyz model over and over, so let's just knock this out as simply as possible.

I understand the appeal of reflection tokens. You hold a coin, and tokens land in your wallet. I’ve seen those near six-figure reward screenshots too. Nice!

But follow where those rewards come from.

$STONK’s reward model taxes buys/sells of the launched token, sells the collected tokens for the paired asset, and distributes it to holders. Those payouts are funded by activity and token sales.

Now there might be concerns about the feedback loop when volume slows down:

Early rewards attract buyers. Buyers accumulate supply to capture more payouts. But if the cost of buying a position rises faster than its rewards, the proposition becomes less attractive.

In other words, if activity then slows, the reward pool shrinks. If rewards were the main reason people bought, then smaller payouts could further weaken demand.

That doesn't mean tokens can't survive, but it’s a dependency worth understanding.

Now on the other side, this is why LONG is in the position you see today.

LONG automatically recycles launch fees into locked liquidity. Instead of landing in your wallet, those fees deepen the market for the coin you hold. 

Why does that matter? Because when someone sells, the available liquidity determines how much that sale moves the price. More liquidity around the trading price generally means less slippage for the seller and less price impact for everyone still holding.

For example, $AI alone holds $20M in total liquidity and has withstood multiple $1M and $2M sells without breaking the chart. This is important.

Wait for the first real pullback on the STONK ecosystem, then you’ll get why that matters.

Not because LONG tokens can’t dump. They can. But you want trading activity during the good days to build liquidity that can absorb selling on the bad days. 

Both models depend on activity. If volume slows, STONK’s reward generation slows, and LONG’s liquidity accumulation slows. The difference is that liquidity already added doesn’t vanish just because fewer people traded today. Its value and composition can change, but the previous activity helped build a deeper market.  

So I understand preferring rewards you can receive today. But “I don’t get reflections, therefore I get nothing” misses the whole point. 

I’d rather fees help build the liquidity holders eventually need than judge an ecosystem's value purely by the reflections.

Hope this helps.

Markets are so hot right its time to try out the new TRS @flyingtulip_ perps version one of the main differences for me between FT and Hyperliquid perps for example is liquidation.

Both liquidate when equity falls below maintenance margin.

But hyperliquid sends liquidation orders to its order book. For large positions, it initially sends 20% of the position, then can continue liquidating if needed.

Flying Tulip uses RFQ based soft liquidation it asks liquidity providers for executable quotes and sells only the collateral required to restore account health 

FT also adjusts borrowing power based on market depth, volatility and executable liquidity.

The potential advantage liquidation becomes more liquidity aware and less mechanically dependent on dumping into the order book, potentially reducing slippage and unnecessary collateral loss but if that was only, in FT capital doesn't sit still your collateral is actively earning apr and supporting other products. 

The advantage of TRS is that it isn't ruthless like any other perp it maximises effort to keep your position as long as possible especially in such volatile markets.
