text:
救命，这两天所有人都在讨论 JEV，说这个“哑巴 AI”是终极生产力。

上次小龙虾爆火你们也是这么说的。

面对新东西，“小聋瞎”小编还没跟上趟，但本着“我可以不会写代码，但我必须给兄弟们做电子菩萨”的原则，

小编连夜翻遍帖子，把这波 JEV 狂潮里的20多个前沿加密实战用例与叙事标的给盘了一遍，

发现大家已经搞出了各路自动交易、预测市场评估、链上投研、情绪监测等产品。

一波聚合如下，赚钱不一定，但收藏不亏：

1. 高频交易与自动化机器人

jev-trader
作者： Jarrod Watts，Monad 基金会首席 AI 工程师，@jarrodwatts
简介： 这大概是加密圈里最先火起来的 Jev 案例。
作者在 Monad 上搭了个会自己挂单的机器人，每个区块大约 300 毫秒，先看一眼 Kuru 上 MON/USDC 的买卖盘，再问 Jev 一句「现在该买还是该卖」。
Jev 只给方向和把握，代码负责把限价单挂到盘口里侧，等别人来成交。它更像在演示 JEV 的能力「判断快到能跟上出块」，作者自己也写了这不是稳赚策略。
默认可以空转看盘，接上私钥才会真下单，可以当启蒙和喂给自己的 AI 训练用。

项目地址： https://t.co/BzVuajtoLb
演示： https://t.co/aH8hG5H8fG
原帖连接： https://t.co/EX2lZudCUN

Jev-trade
作者： aowang（GitHub：aowang-ai）
简介： 把上面那套思路搬到了 Hyperliquid。还是 Jev 看盘、代码下单，但这次同时盯 BTC、ETH、SOL、DOGE、BNB，五个币各用一个钱包，互不影响。
Jev 这次可以选买、卖，也可以说先别动。页面上能看到实时 K 线、成交点和盈亏，看起来像一个小型交易台，不是只给开发者看的仓库。

项目地址： https://t.co/tZtg0o5VZV
演示： https://t.co/ikQluwUNud

jev-market-reflex
作者： zzsong1023（GitHub 作者名） 
简介： 接的是 Kraken 上 BTC、ETH、SOL 的真实行情，但目前是模拟盘。
程序先把盘口压成一小段状态，问 Jev 买、卖还是持有，再用固定规则去做模拟成交。适合想先看「Jev 面对活行情会怎么决策」，又暂时不想把真金白银接进去的人。

项目地址： https://t.co/0du0PwOBxt

给 Jev 1 万美元做比特币交易
作者： Abol，@abolbuild

简介： 直接把一笔钱交给 Jev 相关的交易流程，看它拿着比特币会怎么选买、卖、加仓还是减风险。

原帖连接： https://t.co/dsXPD81e5m

BTC/ETH 合约模拟系统
作者： Michael Hudsonrt，AI Agent Builder @Mrooo03

简介： 中文圈里比较直白的一篇实操记录。作者觉得 Jev 判断很快，就拿去跑合约自动买卖，结果第一轮亏得挺狠，后来把过程写成文章。用的话，价值主要在分析「别人真实踩过的坑」，给自己的 Build 提供参考

原帖连接： https://t.co/cxOXxmLAWS

5 秒决策的 Jev Trader
作者： Gencay，LearnWithMeAI 作者

简介： 作者从币安公开行情里抽了十几个信号，比如价差、买卖力量、盘口是否有毒，每隔 5 秒打包给 Jev，让它判断方向、市场状态和这单值不值得进。
适合看「高频问询」怎么搭，不适合直接当实盘模板。

项目地址： https://t.co/Nsm21LOoEx

2.市场情绪与链上投研

Jev X Sentiment Analysis
作者： brainstormity，https://t.co/TXwWrrJ0ga 创始人，@brainstormity
简介： 这个更像情绪研究，不只是下单机器人。
你丢进 BTC、ETH、SOL 这类标的，它去拉几十到一千条最新推文，再叠上资金费率、RSI、成交量。Jev 给出现在偏多还是偏空、情绪热到哪一档，最后吐一张带入场、止损、目标的卡片。

项目地址： https://t.co/yaMEKvmwDu
原帖连接： https://t.co/aNdSXu83lo

jevscan
作者： jevbook 团队，@jevbook
简介： 面向「代币合约安全监测」。你给它一个 EVM 代币地址，它让 Jev 在 ape、watch、avoid 里选一个，并带上概率。
作者把它做成命令行，也接了 MCP，意思是你的交易 Agent 也可以直接问它「这个盘要不要上」。更像投研里的第一道过滤器，不是完整策略。

项目地址： https://t.co/IwChLV4KQo
原帖连接： https://t.co/3pvgnVGVLk

VerdictJEV
作者： 匿名
简介：项目打分检测器。 打开网页，贴合约地址或项目 GitHub，Jev 会看曲线、持仓集中度、部署者历史，以及仓库是不是空壳、刷星、停更。输出的是质量、爆发潜力、rug 风险这类判断。

站点还绑了一个 $VJEV 代币：判好的会回购，判差的会销毁。研究工具和代币玩法叠在一起，值得警惕。
项目地址： https://t.co/KSpYZkejoc

3.预测市场
Jevymarket
作者： Markus Haas（GitHub：markusbug）

简介： Jev 自己不上网、也没有「今天发生了什么」的记忆，所以先让一个会搜索的模型把新闻证据写成简报，再把简报交给 Jev 定价。
Jev 给出的概率如果比 Polymarket 盘口更好，机器人才考虑下单。思路很清楚：聊天模型负责找材料，Jev 负责拍板。

项目地址： https://t.co/gQpr5sZfgO

https://t.co/Q2dEYhgzCH 的 Jev 价格问答实验
作者： https://t.co/Q2dEYhgzCH News 编辑部

简介： 记者没有让 Jev 去跑策略，直接拿当下市场材料问它：比特币会不会先打到 8.5 万、9 万、10 万。报道里 Jev 给 8.5 万的概率大约一半出头，当时盘口更乐观。

小编评价这属于“同行卷我”，加密媒体开始把它当成可以快速给概率的研究助手。 

原帖连接： https://t.co/ox5mNtlYYh

4.圈内机构实验

TradeRank 上的 Jev
作者： TradeRank 赛事平台收录的项目；模型来自 TypeSafe

简介： AI交易大赛。把 Jev 丢进一个公开模拟赛里，和其他大模型一起做加密货币和美股。每天用同一批标的、同一笔虚拟本金做一次决策。
好处是能横向看它 quietly 选仓时表不表现；坏处是赛季还很短，现在基本看不出稳定优势。更适合当对照实验，不适合当跟单信号。

项目地址： https://t.co/IFxHNsUn9O
平台说明：https://t.co/le4vcDhxvZ

Bitget AgentHub 上的 Jev BTC 策略演示
作者： Bitget 官方，@bitget
简介： 交易所把自己的市场数据和 Jev 接在一起，给黑客松参赛者玩。
有个演示是每 5 秒扫一遍盘口、清算和巨鲸动向，零点几秒内让 Jev 做一次方向判断，再在平台里模拟成交。
更像「你们可以在我们这儿用 Jev 做交易 Agent」，不是已经验证过的公开实盘产品。

项目地址： 需进入 Bitget AgentHub
原帖连接： https://t.co/Gybq5uOUcr

还有一些高风险的 AI meme 币，这部分仅做展示，也有不少同名币，DYOR：

1. AI 充当项目方与金库管理员

JevBall / JevBallAgent： 核心叙事是“AI 当 Dev”。交易税进入专属金库，由 JEV 模型决定何时等待、回购或销毁。项目方强调智能合约中剥离了“卖出”功能。

Just Jev ($JEV)： 主打“无人掌握金库钥匙”。手续费进入合约后，每分钟由 JEV 决策进行回购、销毁或购买股票代币。

2. 收益分配与生态代币

OpenJEV ($JEV)： 在 Robinhood Chain 发行，交易手续费进入公开金库，专项用于支付 JEV 的 API 调用费用，以支持更多人免费测试该模型。

Jevpay ($JEVPAY)： 一场链上分红实验。交易税的 75% 用于分红，每次分红前将持币钱包数据喂给 JEV，由 AI 来判断谁有资格获取奖励。

Jevons ($JEVONS)： 除基础的税收回购销毁外，新增了持有该代币等于让 JEV 协助接触 NVDA、GOOGL 等代币化 AI 股票的叙事。

3. 衍生基建与代币化股票

Jevdesk： 
存入 USDG 后，JEV 会在每个 Tick 根据行情给出代币化美股的“多/空/平”指令。产品本质是现金结算的方向押注，而非真实买入对应股票。

JevPad： 
建立在 Robinhood Chain 上的发射台。发行的代币锁定 2% 税收，专属的 JEV Agent 负责利用这些资金进行宣发、回购或销毁。

最后提示：
新工具只要没太大门槛，加密永远是最新的试验田之一。

这里面不一定所有东西都有用，但面向注意力的表演和演示 Demo，有时就已经比其他项目快一步了。

对于普通玩家来说，那些工具层理的东西可以拿来用用，但“炒作 AI 自治概念”则需要谨慎操作。

text:
打算把自己下图的一些工作流统一到一个内部平台，看了市面上一些工作流工具。
比如引用里的codejury，和评论里作者用AI评论推广的orbi，这些工具实际上是把作者自己的整个工作流套在了里面，没有办法根据自己的需要灵活改造。
比如测试阶段的code review部分，有的人会倾向于多个不同的llm并发review汇总评审意见，有的人会倾向于Claude/Codex多轮一审一改，像我的话还会分两个阶段，第一阶段仅对test部分review，第二阶段再仅对业务代码review，防止llm同时修改测试代码和业务代码伪造通过测试的假象，诸如此类一些小环节有这种自定义的工作流需要适配。

我理想中的这个内部平台主要用来管理llm的自动化和项目看板可视化，然后最好是基于Github的，不要自己搞一套状态机数据库；
可以每个环节拆开管理工作流，比如研发团队的工作流，就负责把issue推到pr就算完成了，后续交给测试团队的工作流，不需要一个session开始从issue一杆子捅到底release才算完。
拆开管理工作流之后，每个子环节到时候都是可以自由替换的，比如生成issue的环节，我现在是用一些硬规则（预期利润之类）和LLM判断排的优先级，后面可以切换成jev做优先级定义。
同时每个环节最好是人和机器都可以介入，比如pr不一定全部都是llm自动从issue推过来的，有时候也可以是我手动从Claude cli推过来的，甚至有可能是我古法编程推过来的。

基于这些需求，又调研到现在比较火的一些人机交互工作流平台：
- @jiayuan_jy 团队开发的 @MulticaAI ，不是基于Github，要做一套自己的issue数据库，并且我其实只是一个人OPC，不太需要团队协作的那部分，暂时排除了；
- @istdrc 团队开发的 @raft_hq ， 这个更偏人机im解决方案一点，看上去也不太适配
- kandev，目前看来最适配我的需求，但是有点过于复杂，一眼就是技术背景的开发做的，不太产品化，还没搞明白怎么设置。

不知道各位还有没有别的工具可以推荐下？

text:
THE MOST UNDERRATED THING ABOUT JEV ISN'T THE PRICE. IT'S WHAT IT REFUSES TO DO.

It won't write you a paragraph.
It won't explain itself.
It won't hedge.

You give it real input. Notes. A draft tweet. A week of analytics. An article and a keyword.

author: nunet_global
quoted_text:
Dear SingularityNET Community,

On September 19, an unauthorized party gained access to part of our cloud infrastructure and used it to mint tokens and withdraw assets through our bridge infrastructure. Treasury and exchange wallets were not affected, and FET held in your own wallet or on an exchange was not impacted. We revoked the compromised access and deactivated the affected bridges and conversion contracts, and our team and security partners responded as soon as the activity was detected.

Actions Taken:

- We revoked the identified compromised access
- Deactivated the bridges and conversion contracts
- Paused AGIX and NTX transfers on Ethereum
- Tracing and monitoring are ongoing, and we are working with exchanges and security partners

Current Status:

- FET: FET was withdrawn from the token converter. FET has been secured, and its minting controls were not affected. No action is required from token holders; your own wallets are not at risk from this incident.

- AGIX: Our team is working on a secure and compliant way for eligible holders to transfer their tokens, and we will share details as they are confirmed.

- NTX, WMTX, CGV: Unauthorized tokens were minted. We recognize the disruption this has caused these communities and their project teams, and we are in direct contact with each of them.

Next steps:

- Independent security review: We have been working closely with our security partners since the incident began. The bridges will stay deactivated until an independent security review confirms they are safe to restore, and we will share additional findings as they become available.

- AGIX holders: AGIX migration is paused. We are working on a legitimate, verified path forward for eligible holders, in a way that is legally sound, and we will share details as they are confirmed.

- Other affected tokens: We are working with each project team on next steps. Each team will communicate about its own token through its official channels.

- Exchanges and tracing: Monitoring continues, and we are sharing data with exchanges and partners who need it.

- Law enforcement: We are working with law enforcement in the relevant jurisdictions and will provide updates when available.

We are committed to working with every affected community and project team, and we will keep updating you as facts are confirmed. All updates will come only through our official channels. Do not trust information from any other source.

This was a coordinated, multi-stage attack with a high degree of automation. Our systems are audited regularly and we follow industry security standards, but attacks like this are accelerating and becoming more sophisticated. We encourage every team in this space to review their external cloud critical infrastructure now.

text:
This is something Rockefeller would have done: 

1. Identify a critical dependency.
2. Acquire the only company that produces it. 
3. Cut off the supply to your competitors. Force them out of business.
4. Recruit the founding team of your dead competitors to work for your company. 

This is how @PeterRahal did this:

1. Peter discovers a breakthrough ingredient. Epogee had developed EPG, a patented modified fat substitute that could provide the taste and mouthfeel of fat with fewer calories.

2. Peter’s company becomes overwhelmingly dependent on EPG. David Protein was buying roughly 90% of Epogee’s available supply. Because Epogee was the sole source, losing access could cripple Peter’s business. “We’d be dead if we lost this ingredient.”

3.  Peter recognizes the dependency immediately. “This is a nasty dependency. This is going to end in litigation, extortion, or we’re going to buy them. All my attention was on this.” 

4.  Peter protects David before acquiring Epogee. He negotiates a strong supply agreement with protections including favorable pricing and priority over available inventory. (His competitors fail to do this)

5.  David’s growth begins exceeding Epogee’s production capacity. David eventually needs about 150% of what Epogee can produce.

6.  Epogee proposes that Peter take over the company. The two sides begin negotiating an acquisition.

7.  Peter acquires Epogee. Instead of merely buying a critical ingredient, he now controls the company producing it.

8.  Peter prioritizes his own demand. Peter’s competitors lacked contractual supply guarantees. With David consuming more than Epogee could produce, those companies lose access.

Peter has no sympathy: “I don't have sympathy for stupidity. I don't have sympathy for incompetence. It was so obvious that if you're going to use an ingredient that has a single source, you better make sure you have a supply agreement. It's like fundamental. And their response was like, "Well, I didn't know that [buying the supplier] was an option." It's like, "What the fuck? What are you doing all day?" 

9.  This move generates an antitrust lawsuit. The claim was dismissed three times. 

10.  Some of the former founders of his dead competitors join Peter’s company and now run individual business units. Peter says “the most talented people in our company are former founders.” 

Watch the full episode. Peter is an old-school founder type: a combination of ruthless efficiency and hyper competence.

text:
在港澳，新加坡，马来西亚一些东南亚地区让我很“羡慕”的一点就是他们成熟的佣人文化。不管是菲佣还是印尼佣大多会经过专业培训，基本都会英语和简单的粤语，会煮符合当地口味的家常菜，吃饭的时候不上主人的桌子，不参与家庭的任何话题，有天然的主仆意识，有一些还会建立起浓厚的主仆情谊，在一个家庭一干可以是几十年，带大两代人。

十几年前我在港澳住过一段时间，当时用过一个印尼佣人，她会煲地道的西洋菜汤和青红萝卜猪骨汤，第一次见我会用广东话叫我太太，我猜她压根就不知道太太是什么意思，只是机械性的把家里的女主人称为太太。

来澳洲之后我时常会怀念有佣人帮手，把我从繁琐的家务中抽离的日子，但确实羡慕不来，一是人工太高，香港请佣人现在一个月大约6000港币，新加坡一个月800新币，一般中产阶级完全请的起，而在澳洲按照最低时薪算下来要贵上十倍。

二是澳洲没有这个文化土壤，没有天然高人一等和上下阶层的心里，请人都是请钟点工和清洁人员，他们属于雇员而不是佣人，你只是对等的付钱换服务，相互之间保持着客气和小心翼翼的尊重。下人或者佣人这种字眼和工种，在澳洲这种环境下会让人心里上不适，所以这种羡慕现在我只能加上引号，因为即使给我一个佣人，我大概也无福消受。

前段时间新加坡的好朋友一家四口来澳洲玩，随行就带了一个佣人，家里还有一个佣人在待命。我打趣说：你是没手了吗生活完全不能自理？她笑笑回答：没办法，习惯了。

text:
#STEPN & #STEPNGO September Townhall Recap 📝

5 years of STEPN. 2 years of STEPN GO. And still moving!

This Townhall was a special one, celebrating our anniversary while looking at the latest developments across the ecosystem and what’s coming next.

Here’s what we covered:
🔹 Challenge Capsule and Marathon Season 3
🔹 #STEPNEMBER5 Anniversary
🔹 STEPNathon 3
🔹 Polygon Realm and the new Capsule event
🔹 Upcoming STEPN Badges
🔹 Community questions

Missed it? We got you covered 👇

🎂 5 Years of STEPN

Yawn opened the Townhall by reflecting on the early days of STEPN, from its original concept as a gamified DeFi project to the decision to build a game around real-world movement.

Five years later, the product has evolved significantly, but the core idea remains the same: encouraging people to move.

A special thank you went to the community for staying with us through the highs and lows and continuing to support the ecosystem.

🎉 #STEPNEMBER5

September marks 5 years of STEPN and 2 years of STEPN GO!

To celebrate, #STEPNEMBER5 brings a month-long anniversary event across both apps, with new challenges and rewards every week.

The challenges cover different aspects of the ecosystem:
🔸 Gem and Raw Stone Upgrades
🔸 Energy consumption
🔸 Distance
🔸 Enhancements
🔸 Challenge Capsules

Rewards range from Uncommon Sneakers and Raw Stones to Legendary Genesis Sneakers!

And Week 4 comes with an extra surprise: Anniversary Soulbound Sneakers on Polygon.

🏁 Marathon Season 3 and STEPNathon 3

Marathon Season 3 is still underway, and STEPNathon is returning for its third edition!

From October 26 to November 2, Season Pass holders can take on the ultimate endurance challenge.

The format remains simple:
🔹 Complete 21 km or 42 km in a single session
🔹 Participate using STEPN, STEPN GO, or both
🔹 Every finisher enters a Genesis Sneaker raffle

Two Genesis Sneakers are waiting:
🎁 1 STEPN Genesis Sneaker
🎁 1 STEPN GO Genesis Sneaker

The further you run, the better your chances:
🔸 21 km gives 1 raffle entry
🔸 42 km gives 2 raffle entries

Completing the challenge on both apps allows you to enter both raffles.

Additional rewards are also available:
🟢 STEPN
🔹 Exclusive Badge, Background, and 5 GGBoxes for each distance tier
🟣 STEPN GO
🔹 Exclusive Background and 5 GGBoxes for each distance tier

Completing 42 km also unlocks the 21 km reward tier.

You still have a few Marathon rounds left to prepare. Time to build that endurance!

🟣 Polygon Realm

The Townhall also highlighted the significant improvement in community sentiment around the Polygon Realm.

Interest in Polygon Sneakers has grown considerably, and the Realm has become a much bigger part of community discussions again, especially among our Japanese community, who affectionately call it the "P-Country".

To build on this momentum, we're introducing a limited-time Polygon Challenge Capsule event!

The first round runs from September 22 to September 29.

Here's what to expect:
🔹 5 Common Shoeboxes up for grabs
🔹 Low entry fee to encourage participation from all Realms
🔹 Participation limited to one entry per user

The goal is to give users another reason to explore Polygon while putting Polygon Sneakers directly into the Challenge Capsule reward pool.

And if the community enjoys this first round, more Polygon Capsule rounds could follow!

🏅 More STEPN Badges

More Badges are coming to STEPN!

The team is working on new Badges designed to recognize different types of players, from the most competitive Leaderboard participants to those who enjoy more unusual achievements.

The new batch will include Badges for reaching specific positions on the Monthly and All-Time Leaderboards.

Some achievements will reward players who manage to reach and maintain some of the highest positions. And yes, there will even be a badge for reaching number one on the All-Time Leaderboard!

But not every badge needs to be about being the best.

Some upcoming Badges will reward players for landing on very specific Leaderboard positions, including:
🔸 777th
🔸 6,767th
🔸 8,888th

The idea is to create a badge collection that reflects the way each player interacts with STEPN.

The new Badges will be released in two batches, with the first batch arriving on September 23!

🙋 Community Questions

The Townhall also included community questions collected from X.

A few highlights:
🔹 STEPN's original branding returned to celebrate the 5th anniversary of STEPN.
🔹 Shiti and Jerry are still with the team, handling behind-the-scenes operations and development respectively.
🔹 Gas Hero badges that were never transferred remain visible or tradable in STEPN, but the original transfer process cannot be reversed.
🔹 The possibility of allowing community developers to build applications using ecosystem tokens and assets has been discussed internally, and the team will explore what can be done.

📅 A New Townhall Format
One final update: Townhalls are moving to a quarterly format!
The goal is to keep each Townhall relevant and packed with meaningful updates for the community.

That's the September Townhall recap.

Five years of STEPN, two years of STEPN GO, a full month of anniversary celebrations, STEPNathon 3 on the horizon, renewed activity on Polygon, and more badges coming soon.

Thank you to everyone who has been moving with us throughout this journey.

Here's to the next steps! 💚

JPYC went from a $5K–$35K weekly market to $191K in one week.

The catalyst was Upbit's Sep 17 listing, which opened JPYC to a new Korean trading market. At the same time, issuance on Ethereum and Polygon was temporarily halted, while JPYC traded well above its ¥1 peg.

That explains the volume spike much better than simply calling it a demand surge: the listing created the demand, and the supply disruption made the arbitrage much larger

JUST IN: 🇸🇦 Saudi Arabia restarts a major oil route capable of moving 7 MILLION barrels per day around Hormuz.

The East-West oil pipeline carries crude to Yanbu, where exports are expected to resume later Tuesday, Reuters reports.

Before the shutdown, it moved around 4M bpd, roughly 4% of global oil supply.

At full capacity, it can carry 7M bpd, with around 5M available for export.

By carrying oil to the Red Sea, the pipeline gives Saudi Arabia a critical escape route from Hormuz.

Get a hardware wallet. (and update iOS).
author: officer_secret
quoted_text:
Urgent security advisory for iOS users!

Install the latest iOS update immediately. Security researchers report that financially motivated attackers are now using a complete, in-the-wild exploit chain that can quietly steal cryptocurrency private keys and mnemonic seed phrases from iPhones.

The reported attack begins when a target is socially engineered into opening a malicious page in Safari. That page is said to abuse a memory-corruption flaw in WebKit / JavaScriptCore to gain arbitrary read/write access from JavaScript, then bypass Pointer Authentication Codes (PAC) to run native code, break out of the WebContent sandbox, and escalate to kernel/root privileges. 

With that access, attackers can pull data from the device Keychain and from local crypto wallet apps.

The claimed impact range is iOS 13 through iOS 26.5; that range has not been independently confirmed in full. Until more is known, treat any unpatched device as potentially exposed and update as soon as a newer build is available. Also avoid untrusted links in Safari, especially if you keep wallet keys or seed phrases on the phone.

I’ve been following @vibevibefun pretty closely from the testnet side and the last few updates have made me look at the project a little differently.

Stock pairs are live on testnet now, the product feels faster and cleaner, more builders are showing up and @meta_alchemist has been talking about a graduation airdrop system that could use onchain behavior, social activity and AI to get a better sense of who actually supported a project before it graduated.

I also like the way Meta treats new builders.

If you actually have something to say, something useful to contribute or you want to build, you don’t feel invisible here. Reputation matters of course, but you don’t have to already be well known for people to take what you’re doing seriously.

That’s a big reason I’ve been spending more time around Vibe/Vibe.

I started running my own testnet indexer because I want to understand the ecosystem properly before I decide what to build. I’m not interested in putting out some random product just so I can say I shipped something.

As of September 18 the indexer had tracked 97,733 launches and 2.09M transactions, and going through that activity has helped me get a much better feel for what’s actually happening onchain.

The graduation airdrop idea is the part I keep coming back to.

If someone trades, holds, talks about a project, helps bring attention to it or stays involved while it’s still early, I like the idea that some of that could actually matter.

It feels a lot more interesting than everything coming down to who got there first, farmed the launch and moved on.

And now you’ve got the fee structure, automated buybacks and burns, Vibe Vibers, XP, agents, tokenized stock rewards and the builder program all developing around the same ecosystem.

That gives me a much clearer picture of where Vibe/Vibe is heading and what might actually be worth building around it.

I want to keep learning how people are using Vibe/Vibe, understand where the real activity is and eventually build something people here would actually want to use.

text:
Why is everyone suddenly tokenizing stocks? @goodalexander has a clear answer: rate hikes pressure US debt markets, stablecoins have become major buyers of that debt, and stablecoins need things worth trading.

Onchain equities are that answer, and every major exchange now wants to own the wrapper.
author: Infinit_Labs
quoted_text:
I don't think the tokenization story is well understood - so let's break it down 

Basically - the US Government is in vast, unprecedented amount of debt. And its long term debt is selling off a lot (40%+ over 5 years) - while Gold is up 140%. Gold has crossed US treasuries as the #1 asset held by other Central Banks. 

The buyers for US debt - China, Japan and Europe are stepping away for different reasons. Geopolitical conflict. Currency related. Political difference. 

The government is afraid of running out of buyers for its debt. And it's worried about the liquidity of markets. Historically, this concern is much worse when the Fed is hiking and there's high inflation. As typically the response to unstable debt markets is easing (buying debt). 

Therefore, the US government is very incentivized to allow Stablecoins. Stablecoins hoover up US debt. Tether has different balance sheet behavior than banks and works closely with the US government. 

Stablecoins used to be assumed to be criminal operations and were prosecuted by the USG. Now they're welcomed to Washington DC.  

When you are worried about your reserve currency status, you also want to ensure the dollar is accepted in many places. So stablecoins not only serve as a buyer of US debt, but a promoter of the US dollar globally. 

Enter CBDCs. Europeans see the US government promoting US dollar stablecoins as a matter of foreign policy. Visa and Mastercard going heavy in the space. And see Tether freezing Balances along with the DOJ and say, "We cannot have this. We don't want Trump to be able to use the US dollar in negotiations with us. Therefore we have to digitize our currency" 

Europe and the UK also have fiscal and political problems. So the perverse incentive to digitize their currencies is not just to ensure 'monetary sovereignty' but also to potentially implement wealth taxes, or balance based transaction taxes. This is also the flip side of wide adoption of US dollar stables. We don't call it a CDBC, but its basically an extension of the government. Balances are frequently frozen. Other policies could be implemented under the left.

So rising global debt -> US support of stables -> pressure on Europe to do CBDCs to respond. 

The US is then incentivized to grow the stablecoin market as fast as possible. Stablecoin's usage is primarily driven by speculation. Holding it as collateral for perpetual swaps. Keeping it on exchanges. 

The problem: crypto doesn't have lots of good assets to trade. Bitcoin has been very volatile. Most altcoins collapsed. This slowed the growth of the Stablecoin market, which has basically flatlined year to date. Scott Bessent wanted us to be going at 40-50% CAGR not 0. 

The question then, is how to create appealing speculative markets. The answer: on chain stocks, and prediction markets. 

Big picture, if you want a lot of stablecoin balances. You need to have good things to trade. Over the past 6 months the 2x leveraged Micron ETF traded more than Bitcoin in dollar terms. Trade XYZ launched commodities, and stocks and commands a large % of volume on hyperliquid. Prediction markets are growing fast. 

The losses incurred by retail investors in these markets are substantial. They are allowed for the same reason Casinos are allowed on Native American reservations. Necessary evil due to funding pressure and the geopolitical factors I described above.

This is, at a high level, why we are talking about crypto in the middle of a war with Iran. And why its' consuming the executive department's attention. The US Dollar is ultimately a matter of national security. 

This is true regardless of whether Democrats or Republicans are in power. Both have debt and spending addictions. Both are reliant on the US Dollar. 

But now zoom out: what do you have? You have a bunch of governments adopting digital ledger technology in the middle of a war. Freezing peoples balances. People don't want their balances frozen. They don't want it to be subjected to a wealth tax. 

Enter Z Cash. Over the past 5 years, ZK technology has improved substantially allowing fast, private transactions. Orchard and Halo since 2022 evolved from something Niche to something usable. The EU tried to ban Monero. Exchanges delisted it. Its price increased. 

Z Cash is open source. Vitalik is also prioritizing adoption of ZK technology on ETH. You can move ETH relatively privately on Railgun already - but real private transactions are on the roadmap.

ZK proofs can be accelerated by GPUs. Due to the AI boom, the number of people with access to GPUs and agents capable of accelerating proofs has skyrocketed. Not only can this technology facilitate private transactions but also proofs of reserves that allow trustless accounting for portfolios. This tech is commonly used at crypto exchanges to prove reserves, and algo stables such as Ethena. 

Thus - it's not just that we are set to own a bunch of shielded Z cash, as a base asset. It's that you can swap anything on ETH privately. Including stables. Relatively soon. And you can do so for provable reserves. 

Privacy is incredibly important for large institutions doing financial transactions. They're not concerned with the tax authorities, but rather front running. Slippage. And people hunting their positions or slow moving exits. 

Many big institutions own multiple days of volume in equities that could drop the price 30%+ if the market sniffed out they were selling. And intervene in FX markets, routinely interacting with banks fined billions of dollars for illicitly trading ahead of their flows. 

So a meaningful increase in tokenized trading volume inherently will require privacy. As real institutional counterparties require it. Retail is a great market and is less privacy sensitive, allowing initial growth. But for the big players to enter -- you need that. 

It's not just trading desks that care about privacy. You cannot run corporate treasury functions publicly. People could sniff out that you're doing M&A, or figure out what you're doing -- giving up competitive positioning unnecessarily. At the same time blockchains can offer corporations major cost savings for finance functions. It's estimated - for example, that a properly implemented CBDC could save companies in Germany billions of dollars a year in corporate finance banking fees. 

There are three basic approaches to Privacy. Z cash style. Private, permissionless neutral chain. Canton style: basically segregated databases that interact with each other on chain as little as possible with a permissioned validator set. And private blockchains - which simply deal with the issue by not having a public ledger or bolted on cryptocurrency people are tracking 

The argument for a permissionless neutral chain (aka a cryptocurrency) winning is that 
1. there's no real reason to trust a banking consortium (i.e. what Canton does)
2. governments hate each other and are only doing CBDCs out of geopolitical pressure in a realpolitik environment. we wouldn't be here if Trump wasn't antagonizing Europe and Canada wasn't talking about joining the EU 
3. the tech exists, so why would you want a counterparty in between things if you don't have to 

The world in which crypto loses would be that governments come to an accord about how to do this. China and the US maybe resolve differences. Nationalism subsides. And people say, "You know what, the externalities of all this gambling and absurd crypto shit are not really worth it - we should just have a consortium of nations and corporations for a global CBDC" 

There is another world where crypto loses. The debt problems go away bc we enter an age of productivity and abundance. In my opinion, the reason AI people hate crypto so much natively is that crypto is a bet AGI isn't the economic Hail Mary it's marketed as. 

regardless, we are in neither of those worlds right now. But crypto hasn't done great either. Why? 

The big problem with crypto, from a valuation standpoint, is that it has never been clear how you pay for all the validators or miners without a block subsidy. And the only coherent way that happens is that on-chain volume, swaps, and trading 5-10xes. 

The way that you get there is that high quality assets get tokenized and traded. But probably less understood is that an entire swathe of new assets hit the blockchain, and defi functions like borrowing and looping create carry trade and FX trading opportunities. So rather than pendle looping Ethena, you have looping with RWAs. This already exists to some extent in niche markets like Brazilian credit card debt (looped 28%+ APY) but is relatively tiny. 

Just on this example, you might immediately say "that has huge FX risk", and you'd be right. Which brings a natural demand for FX hedging. Which will hit after you get internationalized RWAs on chain. Which will occur naturally after corporate finance functions hit CBDCs. 

So you have a sort of promethean progression:
0. bitmex and native perp yield 
1. weird crypto yield / credit risk [low quality pre FTX era]
2. ethena (systematized perp yield)
3. defi/aave/ pendle etc (levered yield)
4. on-chain stocks
5. on-chain perps 
6. leveraged stock vs perp yield 
< we are here >
7. private stock trading 
8. institutional lending 
9. direct corporate bond or equity issuance (USD)
10. CBDC facilitated corporate finance (EUR, GBP, NOK)
11. permissionless private fx swaps 
<the promethean explosion>
12. looped international corporate fixed income

Note that the entire time I've talked so far, AI hasn't really been mentioned. AI makes all of this easier. The most concrete example is that the Norgesbank is vibe coding their CBDC with Claude. But more profoundly - eventually agents will be able to trade assets directly on chain. 

investment management is becoming increasingly agentic already, with every major lab launching finance products. And banks rapidly adopting AI across workflows. 

By the time you get to step 9 on the table above, there will likely be investable AI agents. Perhaps in gated jurisdiction. But there will be a new primitive of an agent with a verified balance, and business model that you can buy. The same way you'd buy a stock or subscribe to a vault, or hedge fund. 

I think Step 9 (companies choosing to issue straight on chain) is therefore the most important thing to monitor given the sh1t show with Robinhood's CEO and AMC. Tokenized representations of stocks have major legal risk, and ADRs (American Depository Receipts) as an asset class have quite an ugly history of being banned or depegging (most recently YNDX just straight up went to 0 when Russia went into Ukraine). For you to get really clean on chain stocks, and fixed income that can be effectively looped for yield, you need the credit risk of the actual underlying legal structure to be very low. 

You'll also want to see a proliferation of privacy and ZK accounting products take hold that interact with OTC trades, portfolio swaps, and FX as CBDCs come online. That's the boring bridge to the eventual wild future everyone was envisioning in 2023 where we have a bunch of Accelerando esque corporations existing entirely on chain, compounding capital and investing in their own training

The Track to Financial RSI is paved with Fomo, hyperliquid, gambling on Robinhood and seemingly irresponsible regulatory actions. At least, it seems mad until you consider the alternative. Illiquidity. And currency failure. 

You can complain about Trump's ethics. You can stop Clarity. But the crazy train has already left the station. All aboard! It's not like you have a choice.

text:
weirdly people continue being confused about how exposure and volume calculation works in perps and prediction markets

tldr is people are dunking on conventions without understanding that they cannot really offer a consistent alternative that is both informative and makes sense

1) calculating volume based on economic exposure is natural, gives you actionable information, and can be compared to other metrics like open interest. It is also by no means crypto invention, this is how tradfi works too. In contrast it makes very little sense to report collateral as volume as it gives very little information about actual economic activity, nobody cares about this number except for people who come up with conspiracy theories about all volume being fake because its on leverage (🤯). Like I feel dumb even explaining this because its obvious to anyone with basic market structure understanding, but I sadly encountered a number of individuals who were genuinely convicted that is the case so here we are

2) people are also dunking on volume calculation (actually for the same reason in a way!) for prediction markets and I'll admit it is less intuitive (until you actually think more about it). If somebody buys $0.03 cents probability for Jesus returning this year, any prediction market (yes any, all of them are following this convention, not just kalshi!) would report $1 in volume. This bit is unintuitive but only until you understand there is somebody who is selling $0.97 on the other side! He can actually lose 0.97 and that cash is locked So what should we report, $0.03, $0.97 or $1? It kind of makes sense to report $1 because that's the combined financial exposure. It might make sense to report 0.97 because its the maximum p&l from this particular transaction, but this is honestly stratching it. And if you are in favor of reporting 0.03, are we then always reporting the lowest number (up to 0.5?), and more importantly, what information does this give us? At the end of the day you want to know how many contracts are being traded and based on the market make a decision about how much it tells you, so current volume convention makes sense to me personally. Special case (but not really) is parlays/combos - I think I agree that reporting volume in parlays should work on them being a standalone market and just like the Jesus market it doesnt matter, like whats the alternative here exactly, report 0.0003, but then what if He actually returns and ETH goes to $10,000 in 2050 and the poor market maker loses a small fortune on tiny volume?

thanks for coming to my volume reporting convention rant

author: kain
quoted_text:
Pi beats claude code and codex 

You can cut your agent API costs by 50% right now with literally 0% drop in benchmark performance.

Anthropic wants you to use Claude Code. OpenAI wants you to use Codex CLI.

But a new UC Berkeley study just exposed the "In House Myth": Frontier models actually perform better on minimal, open source frameworks 75% of the time. 

Stop paying the Big Tech "Harness Tax." Here is the data 

# UC Berkeley and Arena just dropped the "Harness Tax" paper. 

They benchmarked 21 model agent pairs on SWE-bench Lite and Terminal-Bench 2.0. They tested SOTA models (Claude Fable 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 4.8, Sonnet 4.6, Kimi K3) across 3 agent frameworks: 

Claude Code, Codex CLI, and a barebones open source harness, Pi.

The results prove we are all bleeding API credits for literally zero reason.

# Look at the chart:

- GPT-5.6 Sol scored 83.3% using the OS Pi harness. On OpenAI's own Codex CLI? It dropped to 78.9%. and cost nearly 2x as much ($0.42 vs $0.76).

- Claude Fable 5 hits 97.8% on Claude Code for $1.33/rollout. On Pi? It hits 96.7% for just $0.67. You are paying a 100% markup for a 1% gain.

# Why is this happening? First Call Bloat.

Proprietary coding agents load up massive system instructions, heavy guardrails, and verbose JSON tool schemas. Claude Code sends 10x the initial context of Pi. You are paying for their dead weight context on every single turn. (check out the replies for more data on this)

Pi gives the model exactly 4 tools: read, write, edit, bash. That's it.

The takeaway: 
As frontier LLMs get smarter, heavy agent scaffolding actually holds them back. If your agent API bill is too high, do NOT downgrade your model. Just ditch the bloated harness.

I've dropped more data and link to the study in the replies.

text:
在大暴涨中，很多人看到有巨鲸在链上做空浮亏越来越大，就觉得它们很傻在跟趋势做对，甚至有种“你也有今天，要爆仓了吧”的幸灾乐祸感。

但有没有一种可能，人家其实在稳定赚钱？

比如资管机构 Abraxas Capital 目前在 Hyperliquid 上积累了 12 亿美元的 BTC/ETH/HYPE 等空头仓位，账面浮亏超过 1 亿美元。

但链上监控通常只抓取合约数据。大家看到的 1 亿美元浮亏，仅仅是 Abraxas 在永续合约端的单边账面数据。

作为资管机构，肯定不会像赌狗一样在牛市去“裸空”赌方向。 

更符合实际的做法是，他们是在买入大量现货（BTC、ETH、HYPE）的同时，在 Hyperliquid 上开出等额的空头仓位。

现货上涨带来的盈利，抵消了合约做空的亏损，整体价格净敞口始终趋近于零，也就是一些投资博主们说的 Delta 中性策略。

那你可能会问，既然价格一涨一跌互相抵消了，机构两边开仓图啥？

其实赚的就是是资金费率（Funding Rate）的钱。 

在情绪狂热的多头市场里，合约价格往往略高于现货，多头需要向空头支付高昂的资金费。

Abraxas 利用 12 亿美元空单的资金体量，再配合现货持仓，先把价格暴涨暴跌的风险完全对冲掉，再安稳地坐在“空军”的位置上，每小时无风险地收取多头交纳的过路费。

仓位越大，这笔“无风险收益”就越惊人。

公开数据显示，这家机构的官方旗舰基金 Elysium Global Arbitrage Fund（市场中性套利）自 2018 年成立以来累计回报非常不错，官网披露欧元份额费后自成立回报超 260%，年化约 18%，2025 年费后回报 12.41%。

而其在 Hyperliquid 上被分析的一个主要地址，54 笔可统计交易盈利约 7811 万美元，胜率 64.81%；平台整体已实现利润多次被报道在 1.7 亿至 3 亿美元量级之间。

他们在 CEX 进出规模达千亿美元级别，属于链上非常活跃的大型机构玩家。

所以你看到人家链上浮亏，对他们来说仅仅是策略运行过程中的正常回撤和保证金占用，根本不是割肉流血。

这也是小编有时认为单纯盯链上聪明钱没有意义的原因，因为他的动机、利益诉求和位置并不与你完全相同，那么只跟单他做出的结果，有时并没有什么意义。

没有人会跟上涨趋势做对，但在上涨趋势里能稳定赚钱的人并不多。

真正的聪明钱或许不在于聪明，在于稳定。

text:
Circle 于今天（2026年9月22日）提交的 Form 8-K，确认 Binance 向 Circle 投资 1 亿美元，交易已于9月17日完成。

核心：
Binance 以1亿美元入股 Circle，同时双方升级为期五年的 USDC 商业合作。交易于2026年9月17日完成，9月22日披露。 

1、股权投资：每股80.84美元。 Binance 认购 1,237,011股新发行的A类普通股，Circle 获得1亿美元资金。文件明确认购价较交割前市场价格存在折价，未披露折价百分比。

2、商业合作：期限五年。 新协议取代2024年11月及2025年8月的旧协议，围绕通过 Circle 模块化智能合约钱包基础设施服务持有的 USDC 展开推广。

3、激励机制：Circle 按月向 Binance 付费。 费用按上述服务中的 USDC持有金额的一定比例计算，Binance 承担平台内推广义务。具体费率未披露，不能直接据此推算利润贡献。

4、股份原则上锁定两年，并限制对冲。 限制涵盖出售、质押及转移股份经济利益的衍生品安排。若 Binance 在特定情况下终止商业合作，锁定可能提前结束；关联方转让等存在例外。Binance 保留投票权。

5、双方均有条件性提前解约权。 五年合作期限具有特定终止条件，因此不能等同于无条件保证五年的业务收入。此次股份采用豁免注册的私募方式发行。以上均据8-K披露

投资层面的重点：股权绑定增强了双方扩大 USDC 使用的共同利益；最终盈利价值取决于新增 USDC 余额、持续时间，以及支付给 Binance 后 Circle 能保留多少收益。

text:
信息驱动交易可分两类：一类抢公告落地后的定价缺口，一类是公告前交易概率修正

听不懂吧，我也听不懂，人话翻译一下 ⬇️

第一类是「新闻交易」类似方程式资本这样，靠着极致的速度，在新闻出现的几毫秒内买入，几秒后便卖出

第二类是「新闻前交易」靠着对于蛛丝马迹的认真研判，在新闻发布前买入埋伏

前者拼的是带宽、网速、API、算法，后者拼的是信息整合、逻辑研判；前者困难异常，后者方法得当还是能赚钱的

Travix(@Travix_fi) 就是一款促成第二类新闻前交易的得力工具

Travix 不是再做一套永续交易所，它更像一个帮你做新闻前交易的工具
它把交易拆成三层

- 看什么，也就是交易哪些标的

- 何时买，也就是新闻出来前概率有没有先动

- 怎么买，也就是下单之后能不能回头复查

第一层是资产，先做芯片、存储这类算力标的，再加一些东亚资产，这些东西在传统市场里早就有人交易，链上却还缺少连续报价

第二层是时机，它不直接告诉你明天涨还是跌，它只看一件事发生的概率，有没有在新闻发布前先动了
概率先动、价格还没动，这就是它想抓的窗口

第三层是执行，普通 AI 交易多半是当下想一次，下次很难重复，它想把这次判断写成固定规则，还能回看当时为什么买

目前有 Amber Group 参投种子轮，具体金额没公布

测试网快结束了，真正的订单簿还没对外打开

所以现在只能先看产品，还不能把它当成已经能用的赚钱工具

text:
One of the things I have changed my mind on this cycle is that meme coin trading is a fad or short lived phenomena.

It's not. 

I thought it was a solved game, but the variance due to internet culture seems to keep the game going, alongside the addictive nature of gambling.

I am actually not a fan of gambling, and have a close family member who suffers from this addiction, but I accept that millions of people want to/need to gamble for various reasons: entertainment, desire to elevate one's station, desperation, boredom etc. 

The lottery has atrocious odds, but it is the gambling game that the majority of the world have played for almost the last 100 hundred years. If you add up the combined sum a regular person has lost in their life playing the lottery is significant. It is kind of like a tax on poor people. 

The internet + blockchains have enabled digital slot machines/lottery games in the form of infinite token creation. The dopamine hits that come with this form of gambling are the strongest of any gambling game imo. 

No matter how much you hate this it is simply not going away.

You now have many ways to invest in the underlying infrastructure related to this form of internet gambling. Last cycle the cleanest proxy was SOL. 

This time around you have launchpads with differing mechanisms that allow the game to be played in different ways.

Some are more aligned with their holders than others, but all are seeing rising interest and adoption metrics.

Other opportunities remain in the private markets like FOMO, but they possibly may airdrop one day who knows.

The activity will ebb and flow with manic peaks and big lows as the the flows are carried by speculation seen in other areas of the market, becoming more liquid as wealth trickles into onchain gambling. 

Again, hating on this is futile. You are better off ignoring it if it bothers you. Gambling is big business in the real world, and there are extremely profitable businesses in that sector. 

Everyone loses on slot machines in Vegas, and yet the people keep coming back to play them with the hope of hitting it big one day. 

There is a lot of total bullshit happening with KOLs, and bundling etc. I am not condoning that at all. And I steer away from that completely, and encourage you to do so as well. 

Redacted people are going to do redacted things even though they actually know they are being robbed and scammed. You can't stop this. 

You don't have to speculate on a single individual memecoin coin, and I actually don't think it is +EV to do so. 

But it's clear there are going to be giant onchain internet gambling infra winners here, and you can capture that opportunity if you want to.

text:
My favorite airlines are low cost ones like Easyjet, Air Asia, Transavia (and Ryanair if they'd not fly with 737MAX) and premium ones like Qatar

The entire middle section is the one I try stay away from and where everything is expensive but usually sucks

Usually there you have national flag carriers like KLM, British Airways, Lufthansa or Swiss which have very mediocre service for a high price

With low cost airlines you don't pay a lot, but you get a basic functional no frills service, and because it's so high volume (Ryanair for example does the most flights out of any airline in Europe!), they have their workflow dialed in well

With premium airlines like Qatar you pay a lot, but you get a very premium consistent service

Coretura, the software-defined vehicle company founded by Daimler Truck and Volvo Group, selected Alloy Kore as the safety-certified software foundation for its next-generation commercial vehicle platform.

Alloy Kore is jointly developed by Vector and BlackBerry’s QNX unit and is designed for high-performance vehicle computing, combining a real-time operating system with pre-integrated automotive software services.

This is insane. A novel recently published in France was hailed by the critics, won a literary prize and was expected to win more, but someone put it through @pangram and it turns out that it was almost entirely generated by AI 🙃

People will say that it shows that AI is not as good as human writers even for literary work, but to be honest, I doubt that's the explanation. I had a look at some passages, although you may think that I only say that with the benefit of hindsight, it seems very poorly written and obviously AI.

I think a more likely explanation is that critics aren't as used as I am to AI style and, perhaps even more importantly, the author is a Haitian refugee and the novel describes his exile, so they were probably inclined to promote it for ideological reasons.

Avez-vous entendu parler de ce roman ? C’est le « phénomène de la rentrée littéraire ». Il est lauréat du Prix Fnac, du Prix Méduse, du Prix Première Plume, fortement pressenti pour le Prix Renaudot, et il est en lice pour les prix Goncourt, Femina, Médicis et Décembre. Ah oui, il est aussi en cours de traduction dans 20 langues.

Eh bien selon Pangram, ce roman est rédigé presque intégralement par une Intelligence Artificielle. Nous avons testé plusieurs passages, à divers endroits du manuscrit, pour presque toujours le même résultat : 100% IA (cf les deux premiers chapitre dans le tweet ci-dessous).

Rappelons que Pangram est de loin le détecteur d’IA le plus fiable : son taux de faux positifs est de 0,0041%, soit environ un texte humain sur 24 400. Sur 996 273 textes antérieurs à 2022, Pangram en classe uniquement 14 (0,0014%) comme étant partiellement écrits par l’IA.

La probabilité que vingt passages d’un même livre (et il y a bien plus de 20 signalements dans le roman) soient identifiés à tort par Pangram comme étant produits par une IA s’élève donc à 0,0041% puissance 20, soit 0,1802 × 10⁻⁸⁵ %, c’est à-dire 0 suivi de 85 zéros après la virgule.

N’aurait-il pas été plus honnête que l’auteur crédite son co-auteur ?

text:
▪ 2011 年，看到 BTC，密码学硕士的我认为它是骗局，因为我没有去读白皮书，直接认为它就是 Q 币；

▪ 2014 年，刚刚开始创业，旁边的技术大佬说给儿子女儿各买了 20 个 BTC 当未来的财产，我无动于衷；

▪ 2016 年底，忙于自己创业，到访北京，遇到了华兴资本的高层，他说他的部下出来去做了 FBG 的合伙人，专门搞 Crypto 投资，接着第二年又遇到了 94，我认为是诈骗。

▪ 2017 年，一个好朋友在当时的朱波的基金当投资经理，出来做了自己的 VC+FA，一年时间直接 A 9，我又后知后觉。

▪ 2018 年，当我的创业公司撑不下去的时候，进场看看能不能做点项目的时候，遇到了矿难。

▪ 2019 年，因为加入了美元 VC，囊中羞涩，之前已经做好了算力和电力成本的估算，认为 BTC 的大底是 3300 左右，但完全没有资金抄底。

▪ 2019 - 2022 年，完全沉浸在美元 VC 的强势当中，投资了很多好项目，零食很忙、元气森林、得物、布鲁可等等一批非常优秀的新消费公司，不少都上市了；但是我依然用固有思维去思考 Crypto，一直认为 SOL 是中心化的，ETH 的 Defi 是旁氏骗局，直到我看到了 NFT 和 BAYC 的破圈。

▪ 2022 年，我毅然决然加入一家 VC，当起了 GP 和投资人，但很不巧碰上了 FTX 破产。

▪ 2023 年，投资了十几家创业公司，其中我一直引以为傲的投资是：投资了当时 BRC 20 的头部工具，但 BRC 20，我自己也没怎么赚到钱，因为我还是太用固有思维去判断一个新鲜事物了。

▪ 2023 年底，很多北美的 VC 因为 FTX 暴雷，有 LP 的机会，我记得当年 8 月份，有个基金告诉我去看看 TIA，我仔细研究了一下什么是 Modular Blockchain，开盘的价格跟当时市场在卖的额度差不多，机构的判断是 TIA 可能达到 ETH 的 1/10，确实第二年 TIA 的 ATH 就是大概是 ETH 市值的 1/10。

▪ 同年，我看到了 PEPE，但我那时候很看不起 meme，give a shit。

▪ 这一年，我们研究团队还发现了 TAO，因为我一直在研究 AI 怎么和 Crypto 结合，看了一眼，我就觉得这玩意是矿币 pass 掉了，结果涨了 20x。

▪ 2024 年，开始做了很多大 deal，估值很高很高很高，投资人阵容很好，但是就是不赚钱。

▪ 同年，在泰国的 Eth thailand，知道了 Virtuals，但是没看懂，等我上车的时候已经 3B了，就是因为当时非常懒惰，没有把资金放到 Base 上。

▪ 2025 年，年初普天同庆，懂王已经明确当选了。当时非常清晰记得 BTCDayu 大宇哥说：下一个大机会一定发生在链上，那时候他把很多的 SOL 都搬到了自己的钱包里，我不以为然；结果那个周六早上 9 点，Moonshot 上了 TRUMP，大宇哥在 $2 美金就喊上车，我看了认为是个垃圾，然后就 Pass 了，等到中午想提币到钱包，发现交易所的所有 SOL 都被提空了，结果我依然没有上车，只是买了点 SOL，吃到一点点。

▪ 2026 年，就是最近，大宇哥在 PONS 20 M 左右的时候说这个要重视一下，是 Robinhood 的 PumpFun，因为我对 meme launchpad 极其厌恶，我完全无视了。结果短短一个月时间验证，这不就是一个 30x 以上的机会吗？

其实我写这么多，就是想复盘一下给自己写个总结：

真正的赚大钱的机会，都是发生在有创新且有信息差的地方，回头看 BTC、ETH、SOL、TIA、TAO、GOAT、ACT、PEPE、VIRTUAL、ORDI、SATS、TRUMP、PONS 等等，哪个不是这样子的？

时刻提醒自己和告诫自己，Stay foolish and stay hungry。

写给过去的自己，也献给有幸看到这篇推文的你们。

PS：你以为国内很多的 VC 大佬都是傻子吗，殊不知我之前的几个大美元 VC 的老板，他们都是 BTC 和 ETH 乃至 SOL 的超级巨鲸 🐳

text:
If you are new to @longdotxyz 

Here is probably the easiest way to understand the entire ecosystem from zero:

Long xyz is basically a launchpad on Robinhood Chain where memecoins can trade directly against tokenized stocks.

So Long basically can create markets like:

MOO / MU
CPU / INTC
INCEL / INTC
SCHIFFY / GLD

The easiest way to think about it is:

The first token = the meme

The second token = the tokenized stock used as the other side of the market

And this distinction is important.

Buying MOO does NOT give you Micron shares.

Buying CPU or INCEL does NOT give you Intel shares.

The meme remains a memecoin.

What changes is what sits on the other side of the pool.

For example:

MOO is Memory Cow Moo.

Its market is paired with MU, the tokenized Micron asset.

So instead of trading MOO against ETH or USDC, you can trade:

MOO / MU

Then you have CPU.

CPU = Cat Processing Unit.

Its obvious narrative is Intel + processors + cats.

And its pair is:

CPU / INTC

INCEL uses INTC too.

Different meme.

Same tokenized stock underneath the market.

Then you have SCHIFFY, built around the Peter Schiff/gold narrative and paired with GLD.

So Long is effectively creating an entirely new category of meme pairs where the liquidity itself can be built around RWAs.

This can also work through Community Vaults.

Some Long tokens have vaults where part of the trading fees can accumulate automatically.

Anyone can also send Stock Tokens into these vaults.

So if you want to follow Long

There are basically four things I would watch:

- Volume in Stock Token pairs
- Liquidity accumulating around MOO, CPU, INCEL and SCHIFFY
- Growth of Community Vaults

And whether new Stock Tokens consistently produce successful meme markets

It's really interesting to see how fast the sentiment around Robinhood changes once the euphoria slows down.

"Robinhood is over"
"all roads lead to Solana"
"Robinhood was a psyop"

What if I told you that the chain doesn't matter anymore. 

Everyone is always talking about Robinhood or Solana attracting new traders but that's short minded.

The actual "retail" comes through Fomo. These people are regular guys that saw a Fomo ad on their FYP. They don't know anything about blockchains, fees, slippage or anything. They also don't need to know that.

They are here to make money. If they can make money they stick. If not they leave.

I have analyzed the frequency of trades among different levels of PnLs on fomo. It shows that "retail" (PnL of -$100 to $100) trades less coins than experienced traders. 

This supports my thesis that retail wants to trade a few coins and hold them for a high multiple instead of rotating from one to another.

That's why the launchpad / chain that produces more sustainable runners for retail to make money on wins. 

That's LONG on Robinhood because its the only launchpad that introduced mechanisms to produce runners that are sustainable. 
I have analyzed traders behavior in one of my latest tweets. It showed that traders are much more likely to win on LONG than any other launchpad.

An additional point is that coins on Robinhood can get the distribution through the main app once they are big enough. That's not possible on Solana.

text:
Making this post because more people are interested in how Derive V3 actually is.

V3 is basically rebuilding @DeriveXYZ into infrastructure for a much broader financial market.

The easiest way to understand it is through these 6 new features:

1. zkVM + Ethereum settlement

Execution and risk calculations happen efficiently in the zkVM, while proofs settle on Ethereum.

This lets Derive keep exchange-like performance while moving settlement and custody closer to Ethereum.

2. Much stronger portfolio margin

Instead of treating every position separately, V3 can understand the risk of your entire portfolio.

For example: Long ETH + short calls + perps + BTC options.

Some positions hedge others, so margin can be allocated much more efficiently instead of over-collateralizing every trade independently.

3. Cross-currency margin + non-cash borrowing/lending

This becomes important if Derive expands beyond USDC + crypto.

Imagine holding stocks, ETH, tokenized Treasuries or other assets and using them inside the same portfolio instead of constantly converting everything back into cash collateral.

That starts to look much more like a true multi-asset financial account.

4. Risk isolation

Different markets can have different risk pools. That matters when you start mixing crypto with assets like:

• tokenized stocks
• commodities
• credit
• other RWAs

ETH options and private credit obviously shouldn’t be treated as the same type of risk.

V3 makes it easier for very different markets to coexist without forcing everything into one risk bucket.

5. One-click vault deployment

Builders can package options strategies into much simpler products.
Instead of asking users to understand strikes, Greeks and IV, you can give them something like:

“Earn yield while being willing to sell ETH at $6,000.”

Underneath, it’s still an options strategy. The complexity just gets hidden.

6. Builder infrastructure + SDK

Apps can integrate market data, orders, RFQs, vaults, deposits, withdrawals, portfolios and session keys.

This is what allows Derive to become infrastructure rather than just a destination.

Wallets, trading apps, fintech products or structured-product platforms could all build on top.

And this is probably the bigger implication of V3.

Derive started as an onchain options exchange.

V3 is designed for a world where much more than crypto trades onchain.

Once stocks, Treasuries, commodities and other financial assets become tokenized, people will want to:

• hedge them
• borrow against them
• generate yield from them
• trade volatility on them
• build structured products around them

That’s where Derive starts looking less like just an options exchange and more like a financial infrastructure layer for onchain markets.

That’s why I think V3 is so exciting.

梳理一下本轮目前为止的主线逻辑：

山寨：
1、真实营收/回购/RWA
受益于Hyperliquid将绝大部分收入用于回购并销毁代币，很多项目方也开始跟进，但需要注意区分项目是能实打实产生营收并用于回购，还是刷数据左手倒右手。

而由于这波RWA带动的链上交易热潮，许多相关基建设施的交易量、TVL、营收等数据也迎来了爆发式增长，再配合上述的回购销毁机制，促成了这波山寨季。而且不同于以往的是，这次很多代币的上涨是由数据增长->收入回购这个正向飞轮驱动的，代币真正开始对协议价值捕获。

代表性的币种是$HYPE，$UNI，$RAY，$LIT，新兴的几个龙头发射台$PONS，$STONK，$AI也可以归入此类。

2、隐私/AI
这条线相对来说更注重叙事而非数据，拉盘自然有大儒辩经，最典型的就是$ZEC，其他较强势的币种包括$NEAR（隐私交易、全链交易、纳瓦尔转推），$VVV（隐私AI，算力代币化）。

链上：
主要由股票代币化驱动，按几条链看：

Robinhood
主打的就是股票代币化叙事，因此也在第一波行情中跑出了非常多的金狗，由两大发射台$PONS和$AI领衔，也有$CASHCAT这种纯Meme。可以感受到Robinhood是汲取了此前其他公链的经验和教训的，交易所和创始人都大力支持链上生态的发展，也因此不像此前大部分公链成了一波流。

近期因为币股配对叙事，该玩的基本都玩了一遍，再加上其他几条公链也在发力，所以Robinhood链上行情算是进入了一个冷却期。

Solana

I’ve been asked a lot what it’s like to partner with both Coinbase and Robinhood when they compete so fiercely.

The answer comes down to Morpho’s fundamental purpose: connecting.

Morpho is an open credit network designed to connect lenders and borrowers across any boundary (social, geographic, political, …). More borrowers create more demand for capital. More lenders create more competition to fund borrowers. Over time, that means deeper liquidity and better terms for everyone using the Morpho network.

Competitors sharing infrastructure isn’t unique to Morpho. Banks compete fiercely for customers while relying on shared payment networks like Visa. Tech companies compete while building on the same internet protocols like HTTP. Credit should work the same way: it works better when you are maximally connected.

Our ambition is to bring as much of the world's credit onto one shared network as possible. If you’re building on Morpho, expect us to keep connecting new companies, new markets, new ecosystems, including the ones you compete with, because this is what will make your financial products stronger!

text:
We had a conversation on this point yesterday, with both @ben_moll and @azeem pointing out that this has not historically been the case. There is now some evidence that real wages and labor share are going in opposite directions this time. 

https://t.co/TR0UqdcsHj
author: alexolegimas
quoted_text:
A simple point that many economists miss (and nearly all non-economists) is that a falling labor share and rising wages are not in tension. In fact, it is what we should expect when the capital share rises, and capital is free to accumulate. 

The reason is intuitive. In the long run, the supply of capital is perfectly elastic at a gross return determined by depreciation and the discount rate: households accumulate or run down capital until its return is back there. In comparison, the supply of labor is much more inelastic. 

That means the gains from a technological change that makes capital more important in production (short of making it the only factor) end up with the inelastic factor, not the elastic one. In the long run, capital owners cannot get a rent from a higher capital share of output, only a compensation for their patience. We learned that from David Ricardo over two hundred years ago!

To see this, consider the textbook neoclassical growth model with log utility (not needed, but it makes things easy).

In the table below, I compute the steady-state wage for different values of the capital share. Increasing the capital share from 0.33 to 0.6 multiplies wages by nearly five. Capital owners receive a much larger slice of output, but the net rate of return stays at 4.7%: all the extra income has gone into more capital. Now, you might not want capital owners to have so much capital for political reasons (rich people have a curious habit of buying newspapers), but that has nothing to do with wages being lower. They are higher.

I learned this lesson the hard way many years ago with my paper “Bargaining Shocks and Aggregate Fluctuations” with Thorsten Drautzburg and @pablo_guerron in the JEDC. We gave more bargaining power to capital owners (in our model, wages were not set competitively but through Nash bargaining), and workers ended up with higher wages! The logic is the same: give capital owners more power, and they compete it away. Karl Marx, by the way, already understood this. He was a much better economist than 99.99% of his followers and admirers.

Like all results, this one has exceptions: I can think of environments where a technological change that makes capital more important in production does not raise wages. And the transitional dynamics can get tricky. But the basic logic is hard to escape.

text:
How does revenue sharing actually work.

Protocols generate fees from real activity: trading, lending, swaps and other services.

Depending on the project, part of that revenue can be used in different ways:

• Buybacks - the protocol buys its own token from the market, creating additional demand.

• Burns - tokens are permanently removed from circulation, reducing supply.

• Revenue distributions - eligible stakers or token holders receive a share of the fees.

That's the whole idea behind revenue sharing.

Instead of keeping all the money they make, protocols use part of it to create value for the people holding their tokens.

text:
This guy build a copy of Call of Duty with one prompt & went stupid viral (20 million views). 

Now while building video games is cool, what's even cooler is that his process, called The Gauntlet Loop, can be applied to any type of professional work. 

Here's how @mattshumer_'s process works: 

Problem this solves: 
Agents stop at “good enough.” They do the ask once and declare done, especially in visual/creative work.

Even if you force more iterations, models judge their own work.

Like a student grading their own exam, they give themselves 100. That self-grading is the ceiling.

Step 1: Set a real, inspectable bar 
- “most recent Call of Duty” level, not “a great FPS”). If yours isn’t better, you’re not done.

Step 2: Split the job across specialist sub-agents instead of one overloaded agent.

Step 3: Loop each piece until it looks like a real game/ real work, not “pretty good for AI.” 
- Version 1 will be garbage.

Step 4: Blind critics compare your output to a reference and keep going until they pick yours (or you stop).

Why the critic must be blind
- In Claude Code / Codex-style harnesses, sub-agents often fork the main agent’s context, so a “critic” still remembers the builder’s rationale and rubber-stamps it.
- Fix: spawn critics with totally fresh context. They only see the artifacts (e.g. two images), pick which looks better, and don’t know which is yours.
- Until the critic picks yours, keep looping. That’s the whole loop.

How Claude of Duty actually ran
- Lead agent decomposes → each piece gets builder + critic → before/after per subsystem → fold back into the game → repeat waves.
- He did not hand-feed a big pile of Call of Duty reference images. He set the prompt and the agent went out and found comparison material itself.

References when the thing doesn’t exist yet
For something novel (e.g. a futuristic weapon), you can:
- Use a different game/object as a quality-level comp (critic judges “which looks better overall,” not identity match), or
- Generate target stills with an image model until you like them, then feed those as the bar.

Same loop outside games
- Writing (he called this the harder example): after each iteration, A/B paragraphs (or page/chapter) against strong recent comps. Avoid famous dead authors the model already “knows” as themselves (IP + identity). Use contemporary comparable writing.
- Websites: feed sites you think are world-class; don’t stop until blind critics consistently prefer yours. 
- How prescriptive on “what good means”: optional. Experimental runs he lets loose. Real work he gets more prescriptive and steers mid-loop (“like this direction, but pare back”).
- Growth: Something Big newsletter is already using the loop for growth strategies and conversion copy; he said subscriber CAC results are far above industry standard.

Cost and when to stop
The loop can run forever.
- Demos / toys: don’t max it. Too expensive for the value.
- Real work that matters: willing to spend a couple hundred dollars / hit subscription limits. If the artifact is valuable, $200 is cheap relative to what that demo would have cost a few years ago.
- He stopped Claude of Duty while it was still improving, because of cost and “already wow,” not because the bar was fully beaten. He bets a couple more days would get much closer to real CoD level.

Full episode: https://t.co/td6KqFQW4f

Been involved with @owndotmoney  for about a week now, so wanted to share some context on what it actually does.

Own is a DeFi protocol on Robinhood Chain built around eUSD — an overcollateralized stablecoin minted against eSPY (tokenized S&P 500 exposure). You deposit eSPY at 150%+ collateral, mint eUSD against it, and keep all the upside on the underlying. Stake it as sEUSD and you earn yield — but critically, that yield comes from real trading fees, not token emissions.

On top of that sits OwnX: the RWA layer with eTokens (tokenized stocks/ETFs), liquidity vaults, and borrowing. Every eToken is backed 1:1 by real tokenized stock reserves plus pooled LP collateral as a second layer — guaranteed exits, no liquidations for holders.

Now for where things stand: TVL up 2x, fees up 2x over the last few days. $MONEY staking climbing in parallel.

This isn't incentive farming — it's real usage translating into real fee revenue, which is what actually pays sEUSD yield. The peg mechanism follows the same design that's kept LUSD solvent since 2021, adapted for equity collateral.

Early days, but the fundamentals are moving the right way.

author: poopmandefi
quoted_text:
A lot of people are misreading the SEC’s new Innovation Exemption for tokenized stocks.

The market seems to be treating this as a blanket green light for anything related to “tokenized equities.”

It isn’t. The SEC’s exemption is much narrower.

The framework allows 

- qualifying Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs) to facilitate trading of tokenized NMS stocks through permissioned AMMs without registering as traditional exchanges.

- Certain liquidity providers can also receive conditional relief from dealer registration.

But the key is what actually counts as a “tokenized NMS stock.” The SEC basically recognizes two relevant models:

1. Issuer-native tokenization

- The company itself, or someone acting on its behalf, tokenizes the actual stock.
- Think of a transfer agent recording the actual shares onchain.
- The token Itself is the security, not a wrapper that merely tracks it.

2. Third-party custodial tokenization

- A third party holds the underlying stock within the traditional securities system and tokenizes the investor’s ownership interest / security entitlement.
- Again, the important part is that the token holder must receive the same rights and privileges as a holder of the equivalent traditional stock.
- That explicitly includes things like dividends and voting rights.

What does NOT qualify? → Synthetic exposure.

If a third party issues its own note, derivative, tracker certificate, security-based swap, etc. whose value simply tracks AAPL or NVDA, that instrument is not a “tokenized NMS stock” under this exemption.

This distinction matters because the market reaction has been much broader than the actual SEC framework. Anything vaguely connected to tokenized stocks or onchain trading got bid.

$BP, $ONDO, $HYPE, $LIT and other adjacent names were swept into the narrative, even though their exposure to the exemption is very different.

$ONDO at least has a legitimate connection: Ondo has been moving toward custodial tokenization structures where underlying securities remain within regulated custody while corresponding onchain tokens represent rights tied to those securities.

But HYPE or LIT equity perps? Those are derivatives. They are not what the SEC just exempted.

And this brings us to Backpack.

$BP rallied hard as the market started viewing Backpack as one of the obvious winners from tokenized U.S. equities.

The common thesis seems to be:

“Backpack tokens are redeemable 1:1 for real shares, therefore they are real-equity tokens, therefore the SEC exemption directly benefits Backpack.”

That skips an important legal distinction. Backpack itself describes the two forms very clearly:

Traditional Backpack securities:
→ UCC Article 8 security entitlement

Backpack tokens on Solana:
→ “Tokenized claim”
→ Claim on an SPV holding the underlying assets

Those are NOT the same legal instrument. When you withdraw a traditional Backpack stock position onchain, you are not simply moving the existing Article 8 security entitlement onto Solana.

The security entitlement is converted into a different tokenized instrument.

That token can later be redeemed 1:1 through Backpack Securities and converted back into the corresponding traditional security entitlement.

This is actually a meaningful improvement over many existing stock-token structures.

xStocks, for example, are bearer debt instruments / tracker certificates backed 1:1 by underlying shares.

Robinhood’s Classic Stock Tokens are derivatives against Robinhood Europe and explicitly do not give holders ownership rights in the underlying stock.

Backpack goes further because its token can be redeemed 1:1 into an actual traditional share position / security entitlement.

But redeemability ≠ the token itself being the underlying equity.

And that distinction matters for the SEC exemption.
The SEC does not merely require 1:1 backing or 1:1 redemption.

A tokenized NMS stock traded under the exemption must provide the holder the same rights and privileges as the corresponding traditional stock, including voting rights.

Backpack’s current documentation describes the Solana token as a “tokenized claim” designed to maintain economic equivalence with the underlying security.

It does not describe that token itself as an Article 8 security entitlement or as carrying the full shareholder rights required by the SEC framework.

So I would not classify Backpack’s current stock token structure as a direct beneficiary of the Innovation Exemption.

Could Backpack build a compliant structure around the exemption later? Absolutely. But that is different from saying its existing tokens already fit it.

The infrastructure that is much more directly aligned with what the SEC just described looks more like:

- @SuperstateInc: issuer-native shares recorded onchain through a registered transfer-agent model.
- @Securitize: issuer-sponsored tokenized shares and transfer-agent infrastructure.
- @Figure: blockchain-native registered public equity.
- @The_DTCC: tokenization of DTC-custodied securities with identical legal and ownership rights.
- @DinariGlobal: custodial tokenized equities designed to preserve the rights of the underlying securities.
- @Ondo: moving toward custodial tokenization models tied more directly to securities held inside the regulated custody chain.

I’m writing this because I’ve seen a lot of confusion in the community about what the exemption actually covers and which existing products legally fit that definition today.

Either way, the SEC’s latest announcement is undeniably a major positive for the tokenized equity ecosystem as a whole.

text:
I have been appointed to end the AI initiative I launched.

I'm the technology director at a distribution company. Last year the board wanted evidence that we were using AI. This year they want evidence that we know when to stop.

I have prepared a slide for each occasion.

This morning I attended a Griffiths Waite session at The Fable about ending AI innovation theatre. I wrote down a question: which initiatives should we stop?

Back at the office, I put it to my team.

They answered much faster than usual.

"Atlas," said Martin.

Atlas is my flagship. It reads our internal documents and answers questions. At the launch, I asked it where we kept the expenses policy. It found the expenses policy. The chief executive applauded before I had finished reading the answer.

Since then, most people have bookmarked the policy.

Martin showed me the usage figures. I asked him to exclude the launch month, which contained unusual activity, and August, which contained holidays. He did. I asked whether he had included the training sessions.

He had.

I asked whether we could have more training sessions.

Martin reminded me why we were meeting.

I thanked him. This is the sort of challenge I have spent considerable money encouraging.

We moved down the list.

The sales pilot belonged to our commercial director. He was willing to discuss closure once we had agreed who would tell the customers he had already told.

The finance pilot was too early to judge. It had been too early to judge at the previous review, but that was before we extended it.

Then we reached a small Power Automate flow that emailed branch managers when a delivery missed its promised date. It wasn't AI. Someone had included it in the portfolio last year because we needed another live deployment for the board pack.

That someone had been me.

Now its inclusion gave us a useful opportunity to improve governance.

The flow had been built by a depot administrator called Rob. It cost very little. The branch managers liked it. Rob had left, and nobody senior had inherited an interest in keeping his name on the list.

I marked it for retirement.

Martin pointed out that it was the only item with a measured benefit.

"Yes," I said. "We'll be able to demonstrate the savings."

He turned his laptop toward me. The saving was in staff time. The running cost was in another column.

I asked him to send me the editable version.

By Thursday, the retirement was complete. Branch managers began emailing the depot to ask where their deliveries were. The depot replied. Sometimes the reply went to the wrong manager, who forwarded it. People copied their regional directors so somebody would answer.

Atlas could read emails.

I called an emergency meeting about the increase in administrative work across the branch network. Everyone came. They had been copied into it.

I demonstrated how Atlas could summarize a delivery conversation. It produced a clear account of who had asked, who had replied, and what was still outstanding.

Our commercial director tried it on a thread he had spent 15 minutes reading that morning.

"This," he said, "is what we should have been doing from the start."

We arranged access for every branch manager.

Martin asked whether we could restore Rob's flow. I explained that we had just retired it under the new governance process. Reintroducing it would require a business case and an owner.

He offered to write the business case.

I made him the owner. He now reports to me every Friday on the risk of duplicating functionality already provided by Atlas.

At the board meeting, I showed the retired deployment, the rise in Atlas usage, and the time saved reading emails.

For once, all 3 figures were real.

The chief executive asked what had changed.

"We finally found a problem it could solve," I said.

text:
NEW | Special Report: What a Limited Russian Incursion Into Estonia Might Look Like: A Narva Scenario

A full-scale Russian invasion of a NATO state is extremely unlikely while Russia remains fully committed to war against Ukraine. But full-scale invasion is not Putin's only option to conventionally escalate against a NATO state. Russia could conduct limited ground operations leveraging drones against NATO states not to conquer them, but to break the alliance by causing it to fail to activate and act appropriately on its Article 5 commitments.

This scenario is notional — it is not an assessment or forecast that the Kremlin will conduct such an operation. The purpose of studying a Narva scenario is not to suggest that the Russians will conduct this specific operation, although they have set limited conditions to do so already, but rather to explore in detail what such an attack might look like, how the Kremlin might seek to use it to advance its own domestic objectives and to break the alliance, and how the alliance should act both to deter and to defeat any such attack, whether at Narva or elsewhere.

A number of NATO states will likely be very hesitant to invoke Article 5 over a limited incursion, fearing the consequences of appearing to launch the alliance into a full-scale war with Russia. NATO certainly has the ability to deter and, if necessary, defeat a Russian operation of this sort. It is not, at the moment, ready to do so at acceptable risk and cost. 

The US should take every measure possible to demonstrate its commitment to its alliance obligations. Strategic ambiguity invites Russian adventurism and significantly increases the odds that Putin might gamble. NATO must deter and, if necessary, defeat a limited Russian incursion at both the political and the military levels. European states can help deter scenarios like this by developing indigenous counter-drone capabilities, interceptor drones, and skilled drone units of their own that can rapidly identify and strike Russian drone operator positions.

text:
ecosystem grants and angel investments. it's about to get sensitive

i literally remember all the projects that reached out to me about that, and i ghosted, or used the phrase a man said to me a dozen times

"we shall see"

if put aside my morals and not being able to work as a relationship broker, i have my reasons

1) ecosystems now barely give "grants" in the classic sense. you can still a) fundraise through the foundations' intros, or b) participate in the hackathons

a) often comes with initial exclusivity or allocating massive development and marketing resources to that chain. i can distill "grant farming" very quickly, and i'm not able to help if you don't have a basic interest and technology alignment with that chain, say switching from EVM to Solana in weeks just to keep the project alive. to get the foundations' eyes (not reposts lol), you should be in the eco for months and show you're capable of driving volume or shipping smth independently

contractually, pre-seed/seed from the foundation or somebody of the founders is also a deal with the devil. i won't name names, but you can fuck your token even before thinking about one 

if you ask me now: 
- don't hope to get anything from the EF; build on your conviction for Ethereum, get support for public goods through Octant, theDAO, and similar
- Hyperliquid has an incredible supportive community, peers to learn from, and decent beta testers
- Arbitrum may give some marketing support; a safe start for many DeFi projects
- Monad's founder's studio is one of the best i've seen
- Solana ecosystem marketing is generous but competitive
- BNB (YZI Labs) support is almost impossible unless you're based in Asia. deals with Base also come with similar trade-offs; the eco team is smaller and hard to communicate with (not the best times for that chain)
- BTCfi chains and projects exist on their own; BTC maxis are conservative in what they use, and they're hard to trick with marketing slop 

b) hackathons and founders programs are great (big love for Colosseum and EthGlobal). you just need basic research skills and some dedication. ofc, hackathons only work for idea validation, and later stages will require you to do the heavy lifting (study Clawpump and Aqua0 cases)

2) "yes kate but there are grants from Canton, new corpochains, privacy chains, etc"

indeed. there are grants from bullshit L1s/L2s and investments from Tether, Circle, and Robinhood. if you want to build on a chain with questionable reputation only for the grant, i won't encourage this. if you want a serious investment, i'd recommend preparing a research foundation and appealing with a regional use case or new infra

3) angel investments became very difficult and rare this cycle

it's not impossible, but your personal relationships with the angel matter more than ever. i tried to ask around for friends, and i heard "sorry, but no" enough times to stop following up. people get burned and are not willing to repeat mistakes from 2023-2024

if you want to get an individual angel check, i can't be the proxy advocating; i may suggest accs to cold DM and build these relationships from 0, with warm intros only if you really match (sadly, super rare)

Legion/Metadao/Sonar sales are easier to organize, and even if they don't get 100% subscribed, it's still a bigger reach to potential angels

bottom line: i can suggest fundraising directions, but i will most likely refrain from intros with the objective "help me get the money". i can help to understand if it's worth going a particular way and connect with ecosystem builders to help you learn more

dms always open

text:
梳理一下本轮目前为止的主线逻辑：

山寨：
1、真实营收/回购/RWA
受益于Hyperliquid将绝大部分收入用于回购并销毁代币，很多项目方也开始跟进，但需要注意区分项目是能实打实产生营收并用于回购，还是刷数据左手倒右手。

而由于这波RWA带动的链上交易热潮，许多相关基建设施的交易量、TVL、营收等数据也迎来了爆发式增长，再配合上述的回购销毁机制，促成了这波山寨季。而且不同于以往的是，这次很多代币的上涨是由数据增长->收入回购这个正向飞轮驱动的，代币真正开始对协议价值捕获。

代表性的币种是$HYPE，$UNI，$RAY，$LIT，新兴的几个龙头发射台$PONS，$STONK，$AI也可以归入此类。

2、隐私/AI
这条线相对来说更注重叙事而非数据，拉盘自然有大儒辩经，最典型的就是$ZEC，其他较强势的币种包括$NEAR（隐私交易、全链交易、纳瓦尔转推），$VVV（隐私AI，算力代币化）。

链上：
主要由股票代币化驱动，按几条链看：

Robinhood
主打的就是股票代币化叙事，因此也在第一波行情中跑出了非常多的金狗，由两大发射台$PONS和$AI领衔，也有$CASHCAT这种纯Meme。可以感受到Robinhood是汲取了此前其他公链的经验和教训的，交易所和创始人都大力支持链上生态的发展，也因此不像此前大部分公链成了一波流。

近期因为币股配对叙事，该玩的基本都玩了一遍，再加上其他几条公链也在发力，所以Robinhood链上行情算是进入了一个冷却期。

Solana
本来许多人认为这一轮缺少了顶级CEX支持的Solana会就此沉寂，但它还是凭借强大的链上生态复苏了，一方面有配对ZEC的$ZCAT，也带动了许多和代币配对的Meme，SOL成了这种类型的第一选择。另一方面有主打Social Trading的$Cate，通过推出Poorgoat这样的领头人物，加上不断增长的Holder数来发展。这两者都在没有上线顶级交易所的情况下就突破了100M市值。

而这背后最大的受益者就是STONK，最初主打币股配对的时候上面跑出来的代币寥寥无几，但是项目方持续更新，不断加入新的山寨币和股票配对，最终杀出重围，目前STONK的营收已经持续好几天超越了PONS。

BSC
首先是Flap推出币股配对，上面诞生了作为BSC币股Meme龙头的$Marscoin和东西合力的Meme$牛来。

之后Four跟上，本来$4Stock是非常有机会作为“币股飞轮”这个叙事的完美代表的，因为只有BSC生态具备促成币股Meme->DAT公司BNC->代币BNB->公链BSC这一闭环的完整条件，可惜他们非要推一个高控盘，把情绪打没了。

最近Genius也推出了自己的发射平台，与其他平台的税收分红机制不同，https://t.co/TUH1ja2Rvr的税收是直接用于购买股票，目标是进入董事会，从这里能看出团队是针对目前的叙事专门做了设计的，再加上Genius本身就是CZ担任战略顾问的交易平台，因此目前$Gstock也反超了$4Stock成为了BNC币股Meme的龙头。

具体操作上，之前我主要持仓的山寨是$Hype，然后加入了$Uni，现在准备等回调再买入一些$Near和$Ray，链上则是持续关注看有没有新的催化剂带动一波新的风潮出现。
