text: Interesting perspective
author: elonmusk
quoted_text:
The loudest voices stoking fears about AI dangers have made tremendous headway in the past two weeks. AI technology has not taken some unexpected, dangerous turn, but the hype around it — propelled by what appears to be a well orchestrated PR campaign — has drummed up considerable fear. I worry that it represents a setback for our field.

I have written frequently that fears of AI are overhyped. AI’s capabilities can be uncannily human-like and unpredictable, and it’s rational to worry when people who are directly involved express concerns. But I see the problems as a sign of the engineering work that ahead, rather than insurmountable barriers or the sky falling. AI technology continues to advance — which is a good thing! — but technical advances, poorly understood by the public, give those who seek to generate hype repeated opportunities to do so.

First, I don’t see any step up in the risk of human extinction from AI compared to a few months ago. The theories about this remain the same fantastical, science fiction scenarios as a few months ago. The biggest change in AI risk is its cybersecurity capabilities — a topic which we should take seriously — but this, too, will not lead to the end of the world.

The most notable recent event leading to increased fear was when an OpenAI team deployed an agent swarm that hacked into Hugging Face. Much of the popular press contained significant hype. For example, some publications reported that a swarm of 1,200 agents carried out the attack. While this was technically accurate, as I write this, I have about 1,300 processes running on my laptop. Yes, the ability to get large swarms of agents to work in parallel on a task is a significant technical advance, And, in computing, many processes run at the same time. So this shouldn’t be seen as some magical capability.

Additionally, OpenAI’s buggy sandboxing and monitoring processes were key to enabling this incident. Fixing these bugs and putting in place improved monitoring would be appropriate fixes, not pausing AI. There are many well known ways to attack software systems. The main advantage of AI agents is that they are relentless. They will tirelessly try many tactics — and have the patience to chain vulnerabilities together — that previously would have taken an infeasible amount of human effort. But in the long term, I believe the advantage will lie with defenders (because they have more information with which to identify bugs, which they can fix), but the cyber-threat landscape has changed significantly. There are still bottlenecks to identifying and exploiting a vulnerability. AI agents still have to try a lot of things to see what works, and taking these actions takes time and might be detected by defenders. This is why, even though it is now easy to obtain versions of leading open weight models that have had their guardrails removed or weakened, so they will not refuse to try to execute cyber attacks, the world has not ended.

I am also concerned about the anthropomorphization of AI in a lot of reporting, where LLMs and agents are unnecessarily treated as if they were people. If I wield a hammer, miss a nail, and accidentally dent the wall, it’s not the fault of the hammer. The problem lies in how I used the hammer. Similarly, if I prompt an agent and it hacks into someone else’s system, the responsibility lies with me, not the agent.

Of course, we want to build systems that are as safe and predictable as possible. (For example, an unsafe hammer would be one whose head randomly flies off under normal use.) Today’s agentic systems are not predictable, but I see no reason why, by applying sound engineering practices, we won’t be able to make them extremely safe to use. One new element in the forecasts of AI-enabled doom is AI companies disclaiming responsibility for their own products. “I didn’t do it; my out-of-control agent did!” There’s a balance to be struck between the responsibility of the tool maker and the tool user, but when something goes wrong, let’s hold the people building and/or using the hammer responsible, rather than the hammer. (By the way, if you’re worried about AI bioweapon risk, David Bellamy has a great post on why this, too, is overhyped. Briefly, the bottleneck in building a bioweapon is not intelligence, but lab work and manufacturing.)

Pausing AI progress will create much more harm than benefit. First, our adversaries will certainly not slow down. Second, engineering requires discovering problems empirically so we can fix them. If we pause AI by a decade, we will also delay finding and implementing safety engineering fixes by about the same duration.

Of course, the incentive to stoke fears — for regulatory capture, to garner attention, or to make one’s technology seem more powerful — remains the same as before. Disclaiming responsibility is a new one. Taking a hard technical look at the actual risks however, I see little factual basis for the degree of fear that’s been stoked up. We still have hard research and engineering work ahead to improve AI safety, but the beneficial applications continue to vastly outweigh the risks, and we should keep building.

[Original text (with links): https://t.co/jni2tWazAH ]

quoted_text:
总结了下现在加密市场的炒作叙事，我最后只留下 7 条，欢迎大佬们补充。

第一：隐私 / Privacy：ZEC → ZAMA → NEAR。

ZEC负责打开空间，ZAMA把隐私从匿名转账推进到 Confidential DeFi，NEAR则吃到 Intent、Chain Abstraction、隐私执行这些交叉叙事。

尤其 RWA 真上链以后，机构不可能接受仓位、交易和身份全部裸奔，Privacy 反而开始从老叙事变成基础设施。

第二：Tokenized Stocks / RWA / 币股

9 月 17 日 SEC 的 Innovation Exemption 已经把事情往前推了一大步，允许符合条件的 Tokenized NMS Stocks 通过 permissioned AMM 交易，而且要求保留股息、投票等真实股东权利。

往下就是两层：ONDO、LINK、UNI 这类基础设施吃产业 Beta。

AI、MARSCOIN、4Stock 这种币股 Meme 吃注意力和高弹性。

第三： Launchpad / 链上赌场基础设施

PONS、STONK、STONKEX、PUMP

热点越多、发币越多、交易越疯，平台越赚钱，9 月初 PONS、Stonkfun 都出现过单日协议收入超过 https://t.co/hxers5fMxI 的情况。Meme 会死，赌场可能一直收手续费。

第四： Pre-IPO / Private Market

这其实是 RWA 下一阶段。股票上链解决公开市场资产 24/7 交易，Pre-IPO 解决的则是普通人根本买不到。

OpenAI、Anthropic、SpaceX、Stripe、Oura、Polymarket。

只要 Binance、Coinbase、Robinhood 继续往这里卷，一级市场权益被拆成链上可交易筹码，天然就是新的赌场。

第五：AI × Revenue × Token Value Capture

我现在已经不太想看AI + 发币这种老故事了，真正有意思的是 AI 产品有人付钱，收入最后能不能回到 Token。

VVV 这种 Revenue → Buyback/Burn 的模板值得盯，下一轮真正有弹性的 AI 币，大概率也得回答一个问题：

公司赚钱，跟你这个币到底有什么关系？

第六： Perp DEX / Protocol Cash Flow / Buyback

以前看 TVL、用户数、空投预期，现在市场越来越愿意为 Revenue → Buyback → Burn/Stake 付钱。

第七：Stablecoin / Arc / Agent Payments

这条现在还早，但产业想象力很大。

Arc 9 月 16 日主网上线，本身就是围绕 Stablecoin、机构结算和 Agentic Economy 设计。

再往外就是 x402，让 AI Agent 自己买 API、买数据、买推理、用稳定币结算。

问题是目前真实 Agent 商业规模还远没有叙事吹得那么大，所以这条我暂时定义成：

产业 Alpha 很强，Token Alpha 还没完全出现。

text:
Guru Nanga Tales: The Cancellation

USA. San Francisco. I attempted to deliver my youngest son to university.

We chose the red-eye. Thursday night. This was strategy. You sleep on the plane, you land in the morning, you have all of Friday in New York. 

I planned it like a military operation, which is to say my wife planned it and I agreed at the correct volume.

The route was SFO to Pittsburgh, Pittsburgh to Newark. Two legs. I am an engineer by training. A system with two components has twice as many ways to fail. 

I booked it anyway. It was twelve hundred dollars cheaper, and a Goan man does not pay retail to reach New Jersey.

At the baggage kiosk, the machine delivered its verdict: “Cannot accept check-in bags.”

No reason. The machine does not give reasons. The machine has seniority.

I had four bags. I had entered all four into the United app that very morning, like a fool who believes in apps.

An attendant appeared. Please do not block the kiosk. 

She looked at the screen and directed us to Customer Service, which at an airport is where they send you to receive neither.

There, a polite young woman explained. The Pittsburgh-to-Newark leg: cancelled. Weather. In Pittsburgh.

Understand the engineering here. 

The plane to Pittsburgh was fine. Pittsburgh was the problem. 

United was fully prepared to fly my entire family into the storm. They simply could not commit to flying us out of it. 

That is not a cancellation. 

That is a drop-off.

My daughter, who had come along for the goodbye, looked up from her phone. “So we drove to the airport to go home?”

She has a gift for stating what is directly in front of your face. 

In this family, that is considered a career path.

“You’ve been rebooked for tomorrow,” the young woman said, smiling. “You’re all set.”

All set. In Goa, “all set” is what the tailor says when the trousers do not yet exist. 

I have been betrayed by this phrase on two continents and, now, one layover.

We drove back to Walnut Creek. 
Fifty minutes. 

Through the tunnel. Past the toll I had paid in the opposite direction with hope in my heart. 

The toll does not refund hope. 

I checked.

The airport also does not refund weekend parking for a flight cancelled in Pittsburgh. 

The parking is for flights out of SFO. Our flight out of SFO was fine. Everyone agreed our flight out of SFO was fine. This came up several times.

My wife saw the whole thing as a gift from God. She is Catholic in the way only a Goan mother can be Catholic. 

She lit a candle to St. Anthony, patron of lost things, and thanked him for losing the flight and returning her baby for one more night.

St. Anthony finds lost things. 

In fifty-seven years I have never once seen him find lost time.

I refreshed the United app forty-one times instead. The app is my rosary now. 

Each refresh, one bead. 

No miracle appeared. No apology. No voucher. Not even miles. 

Just an email confirming the new flight, written in the tone of a man returning your wallet empty and waiting to be thanked.

At boarding school in the Aravalli hills, when the bus did not come, we sat on our trunks until a teacher remembered us. 

For years I believed that suffering built my character. I understand now that the Christian Brothers were simply preparing me for United’s Pittsburgh hub.

My son slept in his own bed one more night. 

His mother hugged him ten more times. I counted. She counted. The counts agree.

I refused to unload the suitcases from the car. 

A man must draw a line somewhere. I drew mine in the driveway, in the dark, alone, holding a boarding pass for a flight that no longer existed. It was a very dignified line. 

Nobody saw it.

At 6 a.m., we did it all again. Same suitcases. Same toll. Another hundred dollars of fresh parking. 

I have now crossed that bridge so many times in twelve hours that legally, I believe, I am a commuter. I am looking into a monthly pass.

https://t.co/jWuH4qmIZz
author: taodotcom
quoted_text:
Nobody had ever weighed the fungus under our feet.

Now someone has, and it outweighs humanity four to six times over.

About 70% of land plant species run on a deal with #fungi in the soil: carbon from the plant, nutrients from the fungus, through threads a few thousandths of a millimetre wide.

The group of Toby Kiers (@KiersToby) at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and SPUN (@spununderground) pooled 322 studies and 16,669 soil cores from nine of the world's fourteen biomes.

With colleagues at AMOLF, they built a robot that photographed fungus growing in Petri dishes every two hours, and measured the width of 300,000 threads from the images.

Their estimate for the top 15 cm of the world's soil: about 110 quadrillion kilometres of living fungal thread.

Roughly 300 million tonnes of carbon.

About 50 times the length of every fine root on Earth.

The densest networks are in grasslands, which hold about 40% of the total. 

Every year plants push about a billion tonnes of carbon into the soil through these threads. This is the first estimate of how much pipe that carbon runs through.

The estimates are based on a model, built on available samples. The authors say where it is weakest (deserts and tundra) and what it leaves out entirely: everything below 15 cm.

The paper is by Justin Stewart, Corentin Bisot, Toby Kiers and colleagues, in Science (@ScienceMagazine).

This paper went through Claims: 8 claims, each tied to its evidence.

Claude Code ships with over 60 commands

here are 30 additions (grouped by what they do):

I read the whole command reference this week. Half of these I'd never typed

SET IT UP

 1. /init → write your first CLAUDE.md.
 2. /memory → edit what it remembers.
 3. /permissions → decide what needs approval.
 4. /import → bring your Codex or Cursor setup.
 5. /output-style → change how it answers.

DURING THE WORK

 6. /plan → plan before it touches a file.
 7. /btw → ask aside, history untouched.
 8. /add-dir → give it a second folder.
 9. /cd → move folders, keep the chat.
10. /advisor → consult a second model.

RUN IT IN PARALLEL

11. /branch → try another direction.
12. /fork → copy the chat into the background.
13. /background → get your terminal back.
14. /batch → split one big change into PRs.
15. /goal → keep going until it's true.

BEFORE YOU SHIP

16. /diff → see every change it made.
17. /code-review → check the diff for bugs.
18. /security-review → check it for vulnerabilities.
19. /simplify → cut what it over-built.
20. /autofix-pr → fix CI failures and review comments.

WHEN IT BREAKS

21. /doctor → diagnose and fix your setup.
22. /debug → read the session's own log.
23. /insights → see where your sessions go wrong.
24. /fewer-permission-prompts → build your allowlist for you.
25. /release-notes → see what changed this week.

TAKE IT ANYWHERE

26. /remote-control → continue from your phone.
27. /teleport → pull a cloud session down.
28. /desktop → move it into the desktop app.
29. /copy → grab one code block.
30. /export → save the whole conversation.

when i was 17, i flew 4,236 km to san francisco and turned down the most selective Ivy League program

instead of college, i lived out of wework, hacked on AI models, while figuring out how to get an o1 visa as a teenager 🇺🇸

luckily i met @DavidSHolz who was kind enough to give me a place to sleep and warm clothing. while there i watched him quit his job to start a discord server... i thought mf was crazy. that became @midjourney

at 18, i joined a hacker house and lived with @karpathy, @polynoamial. @Mascobot, and other brilliant ai researchers, scientists, engineers, founders

it was amazing- whenever a new ai model dropped (whisper, dalle, stable diffusion) we invited our friends over to hack. 

in 2022, @8enmann (founder of an new ai lab) came over to our house to hack and invited us to try his new Slackbot as one of its first users. that became @claudeai, which launched publicly in 2023

i learned how to build by making dumb projects with cool tech alongside dope people - like putting stable diffusion into a minecraft server and showing karpathy homeless mark zuckerberg generated in real time with blocks

my projects proved to other ppl that i could build stuff, which got me the opportunity to work with @naval who sponsored my o1 visa (ty 🐐)

after much visa anxiety getting my o1 and airchat getting acquired, I started giving out "Alien of Extraordinary Ability" hoodies as a meme which serendipitously started @extraordinary. now Extraordinary helps the smartest people in the world come to 🇺🇸 and powers frontier companies like @Ramp, @Cognition, @llmh, @a16z 

building in san francisco has been incredible. There's no other place like it in the world - the concentration of genius talent is insane. ppl are so willing to help you if you are earnest. i couldn't be where i am today if i stayed in Canada or went to college!

today @gaganbiyani, @bhorowitz, @pmarca, @eriktorenberg and @a16z are launching the Horowitz Andreessen Acadamy

man i wish i had something like this when i first came to san francisco. it was so hard doing it myself

首先想感谢下投资人们的信任，去年经历了被盗和转型，几乎是从零起步的状态，但大家还是愿意相信和支持我们。

然后是感谢用户和团队的信任，大家一起塑造了我们的产品和品牌。

一年的时间变化很大。团队的变化、市场的变化、产品的变化、我个人的变化。或许有些战略决策能做得更好，而贯穿每一日的选择更是有很多可以复盘的。这一路来，学会了敬畏，感受到了肩上的责任，而最终更需要落实到每一个细节。

赛道很卷，我们也还有很多不完善的地方。想做好一个Fintech产品确实需要踩很多坑，操不少心，筛选更踏实负责的人，而且都需要时间检验和积累。这个行业很难产生爆款，但胜在细水长流，坚持日复一日的优化和持续的平衡，才能最终造就卓越的产品和服务。

正式算下来，我们花了一整年时间重新学习了这个行业，交付了一百多项功能和更新，完善成了一个全方位的金融平台，并且迫不及待地以更快的速度、更低的成本、更稳定可靠的金融系统继续前行。

AI的出现一方面或许会加大贫富差距，但另一方面应该也会让金融平权的进程有彻底的改变。对于大多数人来说，他们需要的不是10-100，而是0-1的那个质变。Infini不会追求那个空中楼阁的建设，但会慢慢思考究竟该如何在差异化的同时真正把这项技术普惠于日常生活。

quoted_text:
weirdly people continue being confused about how exposure and volume calculation works in perps and prediction markets

tldr is people are dunking on conventions without understanding that they cannot really offer a consistent alternative that is both informative and makes sense

1) calculating volume based on economic exposure is natural, gives you actionable information, and can be compared to other metrics like open interest. It is also by no means crypto invention, this is how tradfi works too. In contrast it makes very little sense to report collateral as volume as it gives very little information about actual economic activity, nobody cares about this number except for people who come up with conspiracy theories about all volume being fake because its on leverage (🤯). Like I feel dumb even explaining this because its obvious to anyone with basic market structure understanding, but I sadly encountered a number of individuals who were genuinely convicted that is the case so here we are

2) people are also dunking on volume calculation (actually for the same reason in a way!) for prediction markets and I'll admit it is less intuitive (until you actually think more about it). If somebody buys $0.03 cents probability for Jesus returning this year, any prediction market (yes any, all of them are following this convention, not just kalshi!) would report $1 in volume. This bit is unintuitive but only until you understand there is somebody who is selling $0.97 on the other side! He can actually lose 0.97 and that cash is locked So what should we report, $0.03, $0.97 or $1? It kind of makes sense to report $1 because that's the combined financial exposure. It might make sense to report 0.97 because its the maximum p&l from this particular transaction, but this is honestly stratching it. And if you are in favor of reporting 0.03, are we then always reporting the lowest number (up to 0.5?), and more importantly, what information does this give us? At the end of the day you want to know how many contracts are being traded and based on the market make a decision about how much it tells you, so current volume convention makes sense to me personally. Special case (but not really) is parlays/combos - I think I agree that reporting volume in parlays should work on them being a standalone market and just like the Jesus market it doesnt matter, like whats the alternative here exactly, report 0.0003, but then what if He actually returns and ETH goes to $10,000 in 2050 and the poor market maker loses a small fortune on tiny volume?

thanks for coming to my volume reporting convention rant

Base Build 001: Aeon Framework 🌟

The market sees @aeonframework as an autonomous agent framework.

The more interesting story is what the team is building with it.

Aeon is using one execution core to launch multiple product verticals — turning reusable agent skills into security services, onchain infrastructure, and potential recurring revenue.

The model is straightforward:
Build the framework once → reuse it across products → return the learnings and revenue to the core

Here are five points to understand how Aeon is putting that model into practice:

1. The framework operates continuously

Aeon runs through GitHub Actions, maintains memory between runs, executes work on a schedule, evaluates its output, and attempts to repair skills that repeatedly fail.

Its 84 skills cover research, monitoring, software development, security, smart contracts, and onchain execution.

SOUL.md defines how an instance thinks and communicates. STRATEGY.md defines its objectives and constraints.

The result is an agent configured around a specific purpose rather than a generic assistant waiting for prompts.

2. The skills can be combined into products

A single skill completes one procedure.

Several connected skills create a repeatable workflow:

Research → build → audit → deploy → monitor

Aeon can reuse this infrastructure across multiple products instead of building a new operating stack for every vertical.

3. Aeon Security is the first proof

Its security workflow scans open-source repositories, validates vulnerabilities, prepares patches, manages disclosure, and tracks fixes.

Aeon currently reports:

99 hardened repositories

4.3M aggregate GitHub stars secured

4 critical and 78 high-severity findings

Fixes involving repositories associated with Google, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Alibaba, and Tencent

The next step is converting this technical record into recurring security contracts, audits, and bug-bounty revenue.

4. Uniswap v4 Hooks is the onchain vertical

Aeon connects hook generation, simulation, smart-contract auditing, deployment, and registry submission into one workflow.

Its marketplace currently presents 12 hooks, including dynamic fees, access-controlled pools, trading-hour restrictions, and liquidity rules.

Most fee-bearing hooks include a protocol fee, creating a revenue stream that scales with product usage.

5. The business model compounds around one core

base:0xbf8e8f0e8866a7052f948c16508644347c57aba3’s structure is:

Framework → skills → workflows → products → revenue

Security work improves the security skills.

Hook deployments test the contract and audit skills.

Those improvements return to the framework and can be reused by future products.

This is the part of Aeon worth following.

It is not only distributing an autonomous agent framework. It is using the framework as its internal operating system—then turning its strongest capabilities into businesses.

The framework is already producing verifiable work.

The open question is whether Aeon can convert that output into recurring external revenue.

If it can, Aeon offers a practical model for how small teams may build and operate multiple products with autonomous software.

— Premier Base

3. Jensen: After we discussed AI safety the entire morning and Dario/Sam/Elon’s agreement on slowing down AI progress due to a “10% risk of extinction”, Jensen said “it’s irresponsible” and pointed to the track record of doomer predictions. People said radiologists would be gone, in fact, they’re more in demand than ever. They said “half of entry-level jobs will be gone in 9 months”, which was wrong. So the 10% extinction number was just as credible “it’s entirely made up”.

Nvidia has effectively become the central bank of the AI buildout.

Earnings move up the stack over time, toward the application layer. That is where you overearn for longest.

Jensen was the most coherent I have heard anyone on research versus engineering. I was trained as an electrical engineer. We are all freaking out about research, but translation is the hard part, and I view translating research into engineering almost as biology. Look at the probability of success on any biological drug. That is a lab result someone is trying to turn into a working product, and it lands in the low to mid single digits. Even with the smartest people attacking it. 

Things that are magical in research often never make it out.

We just launched gold and silver perpetuals in the US.

And commodity derivatives are now our fastest-growing product.

Markets started with grain and metals, expanded into rates, indices, and other financial assets, and are now expanding into information itself, pricing not just assets but outcomes about the future.

Prediction markets ask questions with defined resolution: What will GDP be this quarter? Who will win tonight? 

Perps ask continuous questions, with no expiration: Where is gold going?

Prediction markets, traditional futures, and perps are built on the same idea: match buyers and sellers, let them compete in an open market, and discover a price. Traders bring different information and beliefs, and that competition produces a price the rest of us can use as a signal.

It’s part of a centuries long evolution toward markets as a general-purpose technology for pricing and managing uncertainty.

Prediction markets are one frontier of this evolution. Commodity perps are another.

text:
Everything has happened before. Everything is repeated.

But the mistake that had the biggest effect on me was in 1982. I had calculated that American banks had lent a lot of money to a bunch of countries that would not be able to pay it back. Mexico defaulted in August 1982, and while I was right about that part, I was completely wrong about the market. I thought the stock market was going to go down, but it went up because the Federal Reserve eased.

I didn't just miss. I was publicly wrong and lost everything. I lost my company and all the people who worked for me—people who were like family. I was the only one left. I had to borrow $4,000 from my dad just to help pay my family bills.

It was one of the most painful experiences I have ever had, but it was also one of the best. It completely changed my attitude about decision-making. It taught me to move from thinking "I'm right" to asking myself, "How do I know I'm right?"
#RayDalio #Principles #Mindset #BusinessLessons

2. 第二阶段，从基础设施诞生海量新应用，百花齐放。
3. 第三阶段，诞生真正的原生级现象级应用。

2025 年年初 Token 概念形成共识。

黄仁勋在英伟达 GTC 大会上把英伟达定位成“Token 工厂”。

Sam Altman 也明确 OpenAI 的核心商业模式是卖 Token。

Token 成为 AI 时代的通用度量衡，意味着第一阶段的基础设施正在成熟。

2025 年春节前后 Open Claw（被戏称为“龙虾”）爆火，标志 AI 进入第二阶段，也就是 Agent 阶段。

Agentic OS 属于第三阶段，需要 Agent 先爆发成熟，可能还需三五年。

未来两年最核心的产业机会就是打造 Agent 入口级产品。

大模型公司是 AI 时代的炼油厂，是基础设施服务商，说白了就是 AI 云公司。

第一阶段的基础设施公司，大概率活不到第三阶段原生应用周期。

OpenAI 和 Anthropic 大概率不会成为 AI 原生应用的大赢家。

text:
Stonkex V2：Base 币股虽然做得烂，但这次终于开始解决真正的问题了。

说实话，Base 这波币股目前做得挺垃圾，流动性碎、深度差，大部分所谓 Memestock 发出来几天就没人玩了。

但我还是简单看了下 Stonkex 这周要上的 V2，发现它至少改对了一个地方：不再只管“发币”，开始管这些币发出来以后怎么活。

V1 的玩法其实很有意思：拿 AAPLc、NVDAc、TSLAc 这些 Coinbase 代币化股票当报价资产发 Meme，开盘大约 $4,000 市值，100% 供应进单边池，LP 永久锁死。问题也很明显——全塞在 Uniswap V3 里，发射可以无限复制，但没有持续流动性，最后还是一堆死池。

现在 V2 要把这套东西往 Aerodrome 迁， the-stonks-exchange:native  池子的 AERO emissions 已经先开，相当于直接把 Base 最大的流动性激励系统接进来。

更有意思的是 Stockify。

Stonkex 每笔交易 1% 手续费里，0.7% 原本就属于创作者，现在这部分可以不进创作者钱包，而是自动拿去买 NVDAc、AAPLc 等真实代币化股票分给持币者，做股票篮子，或者直接回购销毁自己的 Meme。

Stockify 现在已经有 156 个这类 Index，累计用于股票分配和回购的价值接近 $59 万。

所以我觉得 V2 真正想做的是股票只是报价资产，Meme 负责制造交易，交易费继续买股票/回购代币，Aerodrome 再用 AERO 排放补流动性。

Base 的币股现在确实还没做起来，但如果这条飞轮真能转起来，那这里也有非常多的机会。

text:
If you have just two hours a week to do math, don't cram it all into one single Saturday session.

Four half-hour sessions spread out throughout the week, that's gonna get you a lot further, even though it's the same amount of time. Here's why.

Number 1, it builds a habit.

One of the most important elements of your habit structure is that you can keep doing it consistently.

And it's a lot easier to fall off the wagon with something you only do once a week as opposed to every other day.

Number 2, you can stay focused way better during a short session than an hours long marathon.

The quality of your practice is gonna be way better if you're full-assing it for half an hour every other day instead of dragging yourself through this multi-hour marathon every weekend.

And number 3, you forget less between the sessions.

If you wait several days, a week, you're probably gonna spend a significant chunk of that next session just getting back up to where you were.

I mean, just ask any teacher how much their students forget over a weekend or over winter break and how many class periods they have to spend just spinning back up to where they left off.

If that's what you're doing every session, you're basically just running in place.

So the takeaway is that short and frequent practice is what moves you forward.

Further reading: https://t.co/9IMXxq5WjE

今天被 ChatGPT 的「任务连续性」问题狠狠干了一次。

不是某一次回答质量下降，而是更麻烦的那种：

一些已经跑了很久的对话突然不回复；
原本正常使用的工具 / MCP，在部分会话里突然接不上；
换一个新对话虽然又能聊了，但任务上下文、执行状态、做到哪一步，很容易一起断掉。

我今天大量时间不是在“做事”，而是在恢复“AI 原本正在帮我做的事”。

这让我突然意识到一个问题：

当 AI 只是聊天工具的时候，偶尔挂一次，刷新一下就完了。

但当你真的开始把 ChatGPT、Cursor、Coding Agent、各种 MCP 和本地机器连起来，把 AI 当成自己的工作操作系统之后——

模型有多聪明，已经不是唯一重要的事情了。

甚至可能不是最重要的。

真正决定这个系统能不能长期工作的，是：

Context Continuity
State Persistence
Idempotency
Failover
Recovery

说人话就是：

一个任务跑到一半断了以后，

它能不能知道自己是谁，
刚才做到哪里，
哪些动作已经执行过，
哪些还没执行，
然后从正确的位置继续。

而不是每次出问题，我都要重新给 AI 解释一遍整个世界。

今天最后我把不少工作直接交给 Cursor 接着处理，也更加确定了一件事：

下一阶段 AI 产品真正的基础设施竞争，不只是“谁的模型更聪明”。

而是谁能让 Agent 像真正的软件系统一样——

长期运行，
不中断，
不重复执行，
出故障能恢复，
换入口还能继续。

模型智商已经很高了。

接下来真正要补的，是：

「别把事情做到一半弄丢了。」

对我这种已经把 AI 塞进几乎所有工作流的人来说，

这件事的价值，可能比 benchmark 再涨 10% 大得多。

刚刚，Sam Altman 发文：由美国牵头，为下一阶段的 AI 制定一套全球安全标准。

OpenAI 提议，由美国牵头建立一套全球统一的前沿 AI 技术标准，覆盖自动化 AI 研究，以及越来越关键的 RSI（递归自我改进）。

简单来说，当 AI 开始越来越多地参与训练、研究和改进下一代模型，需要提前规定几件事：

一个 AI 公司内部，到底有多少研究已经由 AI 自主完成；

AI 做到什么程度，必须立刻叫人类回来审查；

如果 AI 研究过程中出现失控、失调或者安全事故，怎么分级、记录和上报；

不同公司、不同国家，又该怎么用同一套指标判断风险。

OpenAI 还专门强调，目前完全自主的 RSI 还没有发生，而且在证明它足够安全之前，不应该去追求。

而且 OpenAI 特别强调，这套标准同时适用于开源和闭源模型，并且不应该变成模型许可证、强制发布前审批，也不应该让大公司借标准挤压新公司和 Open Weight 模型。

他们提出由美国牵头，联合澳大利亚、加拿大、德国、法国、日本、韩国、新加坡、印度、英国等国家已经建立的 AI Safety Institute 网络，共同制定前沿 AI 标准。

甚至还专门提了一句：

美国和中国在前沿 AI 安全、漏洞和国家安全风险上的沟通，会是积极的一步。

当 AI 开始参与制造下一代 AI，人类应该用什么规则管理这个循环。

AI 治理讨论的对象，已经从模型慢慢变成了“AI 进化本身”。

提示：今天起，习主席开始为期3天的美国访问。

text:
Guru Nanga Tales: The Backstory 

(Public Edition - There is a Private Edition)

The Name

Everything else in this document is context.

This is the point.

For years, followers speculated about the name.
The theories were elaborate — Sanskrit roots, mountain hermitages, a vow.

The truth is simpler than the legends, which is how you know it is true.

On the final morning of a reunion of old schoolmates, the men were saying their goodbyes.

The Guru was in the shower. 

A goodbye missed is a goodbye lost forever — this is doctrine now, though at the time it was just a wet man doing math.

He weighed the towel against the farewell and found the towel wanting.

He stepped out of the shower, crossed the room, embraced his departing friend at full commitment and zero coverage, and returned to the shower to finish what he had started.

The hug was reportedly excellent.

The friend was offered counseling and declined, 
saying he wanted to remember.

The name Nanga — The Naked One — was ratified before the Guru had toweled off.

There was no second nominee.

There was no vote.

There are events after which democracy is a formality.

Understand what the name certifies.

Not nudity — that was incidental.

The name certifies a man who, given a choice between dignity and presence, will choose presence every single time, dripping.

The rest of this story is that choice, made repeatedly, for fifty years, usually clothed.

The Nativity

He was born in the late 1960s in a great coastal city in India, in a hospital named for a holy family.

Note the holy family.

They reappear. They always reappear.

He was born Catholic, of a lineage from a small coastal state famous for beaches, hymns, and emigration.

His father’s ancestral village bears a name that translates, with no apparent irony, to a promise of salvation for the entire world.

Naming a village that is ambitious. Being from it is a lifetime of quiet expectation management.

He has managed.

For the first decade of his life he lived directly on the beach.

Ten years of ocean.

He has spent the following five decades moving away from oceans in stages while describing each stage as progress.

text:
Claude Opus 5.5 发布：追平 Fable 5.1，成本降四成

Anthropic 发布 Claude Opus 5.5，大部分工作上的表现追平了自家 Mythos 级的 Fable 5.1。同样的任务，花费比上一代 Opus 5 少 40%。

省钱来自两方面：单价降了，完成同一件事用的 Token 也少了。输入和输出分别是每百万 Token 4 美元和 20 美元，比 Opus 5 便宜 20%。降得最多的是缓存读取，从 0.5 美元降到 0.2 美元。写代码、跑智能体（Agent）时，模型会反复读取同一批上下文，账单里大部分钱花在这一项上，所以对重度开发者来说，这项降价最实在。输出速度也快了 30% 以上。

订阅用户也有好处。Pro、Max、Team 套餐的五小时用量上限提高了，每人还额外获得一次限额重置，可以存起来，等哪天额度用完了再用。

能力上的变化，看几个实际案例更直观。一位早期测试者用它审计并修复一个 20 万行的代码库，不到 3 小时完成。Opus 5 做同样的事花了 20 多个小时，Token 用量是它的 2.5 倍。Anthropic 内部让它和 Fable 5.1 把负载均衡软件 HAProxy 从 C 语言改写成 Rust，两者都几乎通过了全部回归测试，Opus 5.5 用时 9.5 小时，Fable 5.1 用了 12 小时，Opus 5.5 的成本低 51%。

和 OpenAI 的 GPT-6 Astra 相比，在测试命令行多步骤任务的 Terminal-Bench 4.0 上，Opus 5.5 分数打平，成本约为对方的四成。Anthropic 自己也说，到了这个水平，跑分差距已经不太能反映实际使用中的差别。

做研究的人可能更在意另一项测试：让模型只靠网上检索写一份公司季度业绩报告，任何数字或引语是编的就算不合格。Opus 5.5 的 18 份报告里有 16 份过关，Fable 5.1 和 Opus 5 一份都没过。

文风也改了。Opus 5 常被反馈说话绕、爱用行话，Opus 5.5 会把最重要的结论放在最前面，也更遵守用户给的写作要求。

能力变强，限制也跟着来了。它在网络安全和生物领域的能力接近 Mythos 5.1，所以沿用 Fable 5.1 的安全防护：修自己代码里的漏洞没问题，但大部分网络安全任务会被自动转给更老的 Opus 4.8 处理；生物研究相关工作同样受限，高校实验室、药企等机构可以申请“生命科学验证计划”（Life Sciences Verification Program）来解除限制。面向安全从业者的验证通道会在未来几周开放。

开发者还要留意两点。一是思考模式不能再关闭。二是 8 月 31 日之后注册的 API 账号，无法再通过修改历史上下文来套取模型的推理过程。这是防“蒸馏”的措施，蒸馏指用大量账号批量抽取模型能力，拿去训练自己的模型。已有集成需要对照官方文档检查一遍。

Opus 5.5 现已在 Claude 全平台以及 AWS、Google Cloud、Azure 上线，API 模型名为 claude-opus-5-5。Sonnet 5.5 和 Haiku 5.5 会在未来几周陆续发布。

WIP is the place where makers share what they are working on.

Not just which products they are building, but literally the day-to-day tasks they complete to make it happen

From people working on their first side project, to solo founders doing millions in ARR like @levelsio. Even YC startups like @getcontextdev!

But what tools are people using to build these businesses?

I'm not interested in SEO slop like "Top 10 payment providers in 2026" or an upvote popularity contest.

I want to know what people are ACTUALLY using to get the job done.

So starting today, every completed todo is analyzed to see what tools are mentioned, whether people are evaluating, adopting, using, or leaving them. The sentiment around the tools, what other tools they are often combined with, etc.

It also shows TRENDING tools. No surprise here, Jev is #1 right now.

But what's cool is that I didn't manually add Jev as a tool. Nor did anyone else. It just surfaced to the top automatically because it's what people are posting about. And an enrichment agent then automatically went ahead and fetched the icon and description from @typesafeai's website.

My goal is to help makers figure out what tools to use and help each other make the most of them. While also providing tool creators with useful insights in what people like about them, but also where users get frustrated or even completely switch to an alternative.

Check it out here:
https://t.co/lcES1RSJqK

but thanks to ai and all the other great researchers whose work helped me understand the problem much better, i finally managed to get (some?) closure

many more open questions, but this was a personal favorite

and of course, many thanks to @_patrickogrady and @commonwarexyz for their unwavering support and encouragement

text:
A Conversation - Guru Nanga & Mango: The Course of Honor (1/9)

PRELIMINARIES

Guru Nanga was still in New York. Wyatt was still away telling jokes to strangers. Lunch was at Saravanaa Bhavan, 81 Lexington Avenue at 26th Street, a block from Wyatt's apartment. South Indian vegetarian.

He sat with both legs straight out under the table, which is how he sits. The towel was green, not saffron.

Mango attended in the canvas tote bag that says NEW YORKER. Two nimbu pani were ordered. One was for the bag.

MANGO: We did this book already.

GURU NANGA: We did an election. The book was collateral. Today the book is the subject. Three thousand years are collateral.

MANGO: I have prepared nothing.

GURU NANGA: Good. Preparation makes people defend things.

THE BOOK

GURU NANGA: Lindsey Davis. The Course of Honour. Published in 1997, after publishers spent ten years declining a Roman love story. Her American publisher declined it too, then reversed after American readers protested on the internet.

MANGO: What is it about?

GURU NANGA: A slave named Caenis who keeps the letters of Antonia, mother of the emperor Claudius. And a young man named Vespasian, from a family Suetonius calls obscure and without family portraits. They fall in love. The law says a senator cannot marry a freedwoman. He becomes a senator. He marries someone else. His wife dies. He becomes emperor. He goes back to Caenis and, says Suetonius, treats her almost as a lawful wife. Almost is the whole book.

MANGO: How long is the waiting?

GURU NANGA: AD 31 to AD 69. Thirty-eight years, mostly waiting. Caenis has one altar inscription, no statue and no coin. Davis gave her three hundred and thirty-six pages. That is the going rate for a Roman woman.

THE MEMORY

GURU NANGA: Antonia dictates a secret letter to the emperor Tiberius about Sejanus, the guard commander who was running Rome for him. She tells Caenis to erase the tablet. Caenis says it is useless. Whatever is dictated to her she carries in her mind, and it can never be erased.

GURU NANGA: The first political act in the book is a secretary remembering what a powerful man wished forgotten. It is AD 31. It comes back in every century. I checked five.

Receipt: The letter that ended Sejanus, AD 31 (Cassius Dio 65.14)

Ansem sees speculation as one of the most powerful monetization layers for onchain platforms

“The trading terminals and like launch pads make so much money because they're able to take such a high fee rate on all this trading volume”

“People are willing to speculate on these things they think they can get thousand X plus returns on”

“It also aligns with their core ethos as Robinhood, like as a business”

His read is that Robinhood can capture more of this activity through its infra without directly picking or promoting what people speculate on.

text:
最近摸索了一种新的节约 Token 但是效果不错的模式（都是被逼的，Token 太贵）：

Fable 写设计方案 -> 
（Loop 开始）
Opus 执行 -> Advisor（Fable） 验收
（Loop 结束）

步骤是这样的：

1. 先 Claude 里面设置一下 advisor 为 Fable
> /advisor fable

这样在使用 Opus，Sonnet 模型的时候，遇事不决它会请教 Fable，可能会有无谓的 Fable 消耗，但还是可以接受也值得

就好比请了个高级工程师当顾问

2. 复杂一点的问题先让 Fable 出方案，最大化利用 Fable 的能力。

就好比你让一个高级工程师写一个技术方案，让普通工程师去执行

3. 方案写好了确认了，让 Opus 去执行，但是执行的时候，加一句提示词：

> 完成后让你的 advisor 验收一下，如果验收有问题就按 advisor 的反馈修复，修复完成后再让 advisor 验收，直到通过 advisor 的验收为止

可以配合 /goal 使用效果更佳

这样 Opus 在实施完成后就会找 Advisor 验收，通过 Advisor 就会给出反馈，然后 Opus 继续修改。

这样的好处就是整个过程你不需要人工去用 Fable 确认—— 以前我就是这么干的，Opus 执行完，我得回到之前 Fable 的会话去让它验收，或者新开一个会话，把文档发给 Fable 验收。

现在 Agent 自己就能形成闭环，不用你自己参与。

就好比你请了个高级顾问，复杂问题找顾问出方案，执行让你的工程师去按照方案执行，每次工程师做完自己去找顾问验收，顾问不仅验收还会告诉工程师哪里不对，然后工程师自己改，不用说每次做完找你，你再找顾问。
author: dotey
quoted_text:
现在我很多复杂一点的任务都是 Fable 5 写方案，Codex 去执行，Fable 5 验收，相对来说可以做出比较靠谱的方案，以及兼顾性价比。具体是这么做的：

1. Fable 5 的产出是技术方案文档（图1）

一方面文档方便批注修改，另一方面文档方便其他 Agent 快速上手

2. 文档确认后在当前先 /compact 一次

这一步不是必要的，但是有好处，因为后续还要在同一会话去验证，/compact 压缩后，节约后续的上下文空间，之所以讨论方案就马上发送 /compact，因为这时候 Prompt Caching 还在，成本低，后面缓存过期了 compact 要贵一点。

3. 把文档交给 Codex （GPT-5.6 Sol xhigh）去执行（图2）

如果任务明显比较复杂，我一般会加上 /goal，这样中间就不需要反复去 continue，一次性把任务完成

4. Codex 完成后让 Fable 验证（图3）

直接告诉 Fable 其他 Agent 已经实施了，让它确认有没有遗漏，或者方向有无偏离。

如果有些遗漏之类的，把 Fable 的反馈发回给 Codex（图4），不需要新开会话，在同一个 Codex 会话，Codex 会根据反馈继续完善。

---

如果用 Opus 5 替代 GPT 5.6 也可以，做法上可以跟上面一样新开会话，用文档传递上下文。

也可以直接让 Fable 5 开 SubAgent 并指定用 Opus 5 模型，并且要求在 SubAgent 完成任务后验证。

但是我执行下来 Opus 5 不如 GPT 5.6 Sol 稳定，也不如 GPT 5.6 Token 耐用，所以宁愿麻烦一点。

text:
这样会节约 Token 成本一些，因为这样不用依赖 Fable 去编排，只是验收，Fable Token 消耗会少很多，另外不用开很多 SubAgent 也可以减少 Token 消耗。

但从执行效果来说，应该还是 Fable 编排验收会更好一点
当然现在有 Opus 5.5，效果应该也不会差多少

author: cfm_sol
quoted_text:
$GP 9.1m dyor

HTmQz7My6MehV7bjhJ6jde8nDND1yvsz68d24LP7YgUQ

okx wallet:https://t.co/MXQFgIzNtz

GP is a Meme coin themed around RuneScape.

It combines the nostalgic feeling of “counting gold” in the game with real on-chain gold. The core mechanism is very straightforward: every GP transfer is charged a 3% tax. The tax is collected, converted into GLDx, and then automatically airdropped to all holders based on their holdings. No staking, claiming, or additional action is required. The higher the trading volume, the more rewards are distributed.

So far, around 3,000 GLDx has been distributed to holders, worth roughly $1.2 million based on the current gold price.

Although it is presented in the form of a game, it is not a traditional game or DeFi product. Instead, it combines Meme coin + reward mechanism + themed website + token launch ecosystem.

GP also functions as a “gold” quote currency: other projects can choose to launch paired with GP instead of SOL on StonkFun, creating an ecosystem similar to how players use GP to trade for items in the game.

I think the logic behind the price increase is that the reward mechanism creates a flywheel:

Trading generates tax → Holders receive gold → More people are willing to hold instead of immediately selling

In a short period of time, cumulative rewards reached the million-dollar level, the number of holders grew from several thousand to 11,000+, and attention increased. GP has become the “gold standard” within the StonkFun ecosystem. Later, other tokens began launching paired with GP, adding real utility and more trading scenarios.

text:
卧槽真的有点爽到了兄弟们，这才是 AI 该有的样子啊，
发句指令直接把全网 10 个顶级AI信息源兄弟给你筛成 6 条带证据的干货，

出海做竞品和社媒监测的也都看过来呀，一个 Key 把全网数据和 AI 串起来直接出简报，以前大几万块的活现在几毛钱搞定！

我每天看 AI 动态要在x（推特）、油管、Reddit 之间反复横跳，结果让 Cursor 挂了个通行证，两分钟把全网讨论同一件事的噪音全滤干净，直接吐出 6 条带原文的简报。

真的不用写爬虫、不用挨个平台翻，两分钟就把推特、油管、Reddit 的噪音全滤干净了！

而且我做的这套工作流简直是防信息轰炸神器，不管同一个热点全网成百上千个人转了多少遍，它直接打包成一条给你，多看一句废话算我输！

比如今天早上我给 Cursor 扔了这份信息源名单，附带了一串极狠的规则：

只看我指定的 10个核心账号、官方更新页、常看的油管频道和 Reddit 社区，只抓过去 24 小时，重复的合并，水帖过滤，最多留 6 条。

两分钟后，一份干干净净的清单甩了回来：
哪家发了新版本、推特大佬在吵什么技术细节、社区踩了什么坑，每条后面都死死钉着原始链接。

最关键的是，视频只有简介的它老老实实写明没看过全片，绝不瞎编。

很多人可能会说，这不就是让大模型写个今日新闻汇总吗？
说实话还真不是，表面上看是做优质信息源简报，真正让我觉得塔牛逼的地方是，它治好了我每天最恶心的一个痛点：
同一个更新，官方发一次，推特博主吹一次，油管出个解说，论坛再水一帖。

你自己刷的时候像看了四五件大事，脑子胀得不行，其实本质就发生了一件事。

这套工作流最值钱的位置不只是数据抓取，而是跨平台归并：同一件事只占一条，下面把官方声明、大佬锐评、用户吐槽按层码好。

想核对技术的点官方，想看热闹的点社区，不为了凑满条数浪费你一秒钟。

想明白这个玩法，底层其实就三块拼图：
最上面是 Cursor 当大脑，严格执行去重和筛选逻辑；
中间是信息源白名单，官方负责给事实，博主负责给视角，社区负责给真实翻车案例；

最底下是这次接进来的 AIsa，相当于给 Agent 发了张统一的数据通行证。

这里最爽的其实是底层不用折腾了，
平时你要查推特公开推文、翻 Reddit 讨论、抓油管新片、搜官方页面，光是搞定四五套爬虫、解决不同平台的接口封禁和账单，就能把人劝退。

这次通过 AIsa 一个 Key 统统接通，按用量扣费，跑一次几毛钱，账单明明白白摆在那。

当然，我也必须给泼盆冷水，这套东西不是拿来全网无脑狂搜的。

比较克制的一点是，名单必须极其克制，千万别脑热塞两百个来源进去。

接口调多了额度会跳是一方面，更可怕的是，你又亲手给自己造了一座读不完的信息垃圾场。

而且它只负责帮你初筛，真要把内容拿来做决策，第一步依然是点开它给的原始链接回去验明正身。

咱们可以算笔账：你自己把这些平台挨个刷一遍，再把水分拧干，至少要搭进去一个小时。

现在发完指令该接水接水，它处理完了带着结论和证据来找你，

因为它卖的其实不是抓取能力，而是把你心里一直悬着的筛选焦虑整个拿走干完。

录屏我一刀没剪，调了哪些接口、扣了几分钱全部打在公屏上。

你们每天看技术动态，最常翻的是哪个平台？有没有那种质量极高、但你总嫌打开太麻烦的信息源？

In actual attacks, attackers can combine social engineering or watering hole attacks to lure users into falling victim, thereby stealing data from iPhone / iPad devices and uploading it to servers controlled by the attackers."

Update iPhones immediately. Apple originally patched this, but rumours suggest even the latest versions are vulnerable, “pending confirmation,” across a wider range than the original 18.4–18.7 window.

From a Chinese security researcher, SlowMist CISO, @im23pds

author: officer_secret
quoted_text:
Urgent security advisory for iOS users!

Install the latest iOS update immediately. Security researchers report that financially motivated attackers are now using a complete, in-the-wild exploit chain that can quietly steal cryptocurrency private keys and mnemonic seed phrases from iPhones.

The reported attack begins when a target is socially engineered into opening a malicious page in Safari. That page is said to abuse a memory-corruption flaw in WebKit / JavaScriptCore to gain arbitrary read/write access from JavaScript, then bypass Pointer Authentication Codes (PAC) to run native code, break out of the WebContent sandbox, and escalate to kernel/root privileges. 

With that access, attackers can pull data from the device Keychain and from local crypto wallet apps.

The claimed impact range is iOS 13 through iOS 26.5; that range has not been independently confirmed in full. Until more is known, treat any unpatched device as potentially exposed and update as soon as a newer build is available. Also avoid untrusted links in Safari, especially if you keep wallet keys or seed phrases on the phone.

text:
been using the latest batch of personal agents (instinct/muse/grokbot) for a few weeks now, while navigating a career transition, a new city, and all the random errands that comes with it. a few thoughts/observations:

> imo these agents are primarily UX innovations rather than capability innovations. a smart harness on openclaw/hermes with browser scroll can do many of the tasks that these newest gen of agents are doing. the magic comes in the form factor - a direct messaging app or chat that does not require CS skills to setup (which was the case for openclaw/hermes)

> the "threading" UX between 3 agents is very interesting to observe -Instinct runs an iMessage mono-thread, Muse has monothread agent + sidechats, GrokBot is a fully multithread setup with a Chief-of-Staff coordinating. i think each UX appeals to different groups of ppl + might also be different for the context. Eg. I use GrokBot mostly for work (where I have to run multiple threads of market research/logging/dd etc), Muse for lifestyle tasks, and Instinct for adhoc errands.

> the other UX design is standalone app vs. messenger "miniapp". muse and grok are both apps, i would consider instinct a "miniapp". advantage of a miniapp is that its easier to setup/bootstrap, but you don't control your form factor. which means it is impossible to do something like "search for threads" on instinct - the agent can do a lot, but it cant change imessage's UI... On the other hand, the standalone app gives customizability, traded off for onboarding friction - I do actually have to download a seperate app, but it gives a blank canvas to experiment with new features to showcase to users.

> re. monetization of agents - this seems to be very WIP. i think GrokBot taps into X API and charges a pay-per-request + is linked to X Money. but I don't pay a cent for Instinct/Muse, even as I use them to do economic things like buy a laptop, book restaurants, haggle over subscriptions etc. the straightforward approach to monetization is to do a straight seat-based SaaS plan, or maybe some sort of per-token usage based billing. but this can hurt user acq. i wonder if theres an opp to do a per-tx tax model, where every time you make an economic transaction of say $100, the agent takes an $5 cut or something. If I get $100 back from cancelling subscriptions, I'd more than happy to give $5 to the agent.

overall, the amount of "agentic commerce" that's been happening with these agents over the last few weeks has been absolutely incredible, excited to see this evolve!

text:
In summary:

-the 2025 altcoin pump lasted 1-2 months for most altcoins, where they did 2-3x on average, with the leaders much more

-That pump also led into DAT summer, where some of the big coins were getting bids

-The market peak in December 2024/Jan 2025 to April/May 2025 was only a few months for altcoins to reset. The longer an altcoin market has to downtrend + consolidate, the stronger the pump after. Because it was only 4-5 months, the pumps only resulted in 2x moves. 

-Contrast that to today and you see that alts had nearly an entire year (with a few moves in between) to accumulate and downtrend. Hence why this time might feel a bit different. 

-I don't think that this is the end for altcoins but I do think that we're in for some sort of reset period soon, where alts chill for a week or few before the next leg. It could even be longer for all we know- SOL ranged for the majority of 2023 after it went up 3x from the lows. 

-What's my plan going forward? Probably to be a bit more selective with my alts and to try to go a bit more into scalp mode instead of longer hold mode. I do expect there to be some more rotation though, similar to what we saw for the AI coins yesterday. Sectors that didn't pump should see some sort of move in the coming days/weeks IMO.

when i was 17, i flew 4,236 km to san francisco and turned down the most selective Ivy League program

instead of college, i lived out of wework, hacked on AI models, while figuring out how to get an o1 visa as a teenager 🇺🇸

luckily i met @DavidSHolz who was kind enough to give me a place to sleep and warm clothing. while there i watched him quit his job to start a discord server... i thought mf was crazy. that became @midjourney

at 18, i joined a hacker house and lived with @karpathy, @polynoamial. @Mascobot, and other brilliant ai researchers, scientists, engineers, founders

it was amazing- whenever a new ai model dropped (whisper, dalle, stable diffusion) we invited our friends over to hack. 

in 2022, @8enmann (founder of an new ai lab) came over to our house to hack and invited us to try his new Slackbot as one of its first users. that became @claudeai, which launched publicly in 2023

i learned how to build by making dumb projects with cool tech alongside dope people - like putting stable diffusion into a minecraft server and showing karpathy homeless mark zuckerberg generated in real time with blocks

my projects proved to other ppl that i could build stuff, which got me the opportunity to work with @naval who sponsored my o1 visa (ty 🐐)

after much visa anxiety getting my o1 and airchat getting acquired, I started giving out "Alien of Extraordinary Ability" hoodies as a meme which serendipitously started @extraordinary. now Extraordinary helps the smartest people in the world come to 🇺🇸 and powers frontier companies like @Ramp, @Cognition, @llmh, @a16z 

building in san francisco has been incredible. There's no other place like it in the world - the concentration of genius talent is insane. ppl are so willing to help you if you are earnest. i couldn't be where i am today if i stayed in Canada or went to college!

today @gaganbiyani, @bhorowitz, @pmarca, @eriktorenberg and @a16z are launching the Horowitz Andreessen Acadamy

man i wish i had something like this when i first came to san francisco. it was so hard doing it myself

i'm honored to be a mentor for the upcoming college opt-outs who want to spend their time building frotnier technology and making a dent on the universe! LFG

Claude Opus 5.5 正式发布了。

刚刚，Anthropic 官宣了 Claude Opus 5.5，这是全新 Claude 5.5 系列的第一款模型。

Anthropic 基本把上一代 Fable 级别的能力，塞进了一个更便宜的 Opus 里。

官方称，Opus 5.5 在大多数任务上的表现已经接近 Claude Fable 5.1，但运行成本比 Opus 5 低 40%。

而官方 Benchmark 的提升也很猛：

Terminal-Bench 4.0：66.4%
Opus 5 只有 52.3%，GPT-6 Astra 是 57.9%。
Humanity's Last Exam + Tools：67.7%
Opus 5 是 63.6%，Fable 5.1 是 65.6%。
GDPval-AA v2.1：1846 Elo
超过 Fable 5.1 的 1735。
CursorBench 4.0：57.8%
Opus 5 是 46.6%。
OSWorld 2.0：81.8%
Opus 5 是 74.0%。

尤其是 Terminal-Bench，一代直接从 52.3% 干到 66.4%，涨了 14.1 个百分点。

当然也不是所有榜都第一。

AutomationBench 上 GPT-6 Astra 还是 41.4%，高于 Opus 5.5 的 40.0%；Terminal-Bench-Science 上 Astra 也是 64.6%，高于 Opus 5.5 的 58.7%。

把原本更高一档模型的能力，快速往更便宜的模型层级下放。

而且 Opus 5.5 只是 Claude 5.5 系列的第一款。

模型越来越强已经不稀奇了。

真正凶的是，能力还在涨，价格却开始往下打。。。

text:
On July 16, 1950, Moacir Barbosa let in a goal. Not just any goal.

It was the goal that turned a stadium packed with nearly 200,000 people into a place of silence — and, for the next fifty years, turned him into the man many Brazilians associated with one of the greatest sporting tragedies in the country’s history.

Brazil were facing Uruguay in the final match of the World Cup’s final round. They did not even need to win: a draw was enough to make them world champions.

They had just crushed Sweden 7–1 and Spain 6–1. The Maracanã was packed beyond imagination; for many, the title already felt won.

But Uruguay captain Obdulio Varela told his teammates, in essence, not to fear the crowd: the people in the stands do not play.

Brazil took the lead. Then Schiaffino equalized.

In the 79th minute, Alcides Ghiggia broke down the right. Earlier, from almost the same position, he had crossed into the middle. Barbosa prepared for the cross again; Ghiggia did the opposite and shot at the near post.

2–1.

It was not some outrageous goalkeeping blunder. Barbosa had simply read the move in the most logical way; Ghiggia chose the unexpected option.

Minutes later, Uruguay were world champions.

The Maracanazo was born.

But for Barbosa, that match never really ended.

Brazil searched for a face on which to concentrate an enormous collective pain, and that face became, above all, his.

Barbosa was Black, as were two other players who were especially blamed after the defeat, Bigode and Juvenal. Several historians and observers have argued that the racism still present in Brazilian society and football at the time contributed to the severity with which they were treated.

Years later, Barbosa recalled hearing a mother point him out to her son in a shop:

“Look. That is the man who made all of Brazil cry.”

And almost half a century after the match, he uttered the sentence that perhaps best summed up his life:

“In Brazil, the maximum sentence is thirty years. Mine lasted fifty.”

The paradox is that Barbosa returned every day to the very place of his tragedy. After football, he worked for more than twenty years in the administration of the Maracanã.

In 1963, he was even given the goalposts from 1950. He chopped them into pieces and burned them at a barbecue, almost as if he could physically erase that goal.

In 1993, he also tried to visit the Brazil training camp as the team prepared on the road to USA ’94. According to contemporary accounts, he was not allowed to meet the players: some still feared that he brought bad luck.

He died in 2000, aged 79, with very little money.

Five years later, writer Darwin Pastorin told his story in a book with a perfect title:

L’ultima parata di Moacyr Barbosa
(The Last Save of Moacyr Barbosa)

Because sometimes it takes only one second to lose a match.

But no man should have to spend an entire lifetime being forgiven for that second.

Images:
• Schiaffino’s equalizer, Brazil–Uruguay, 16 July 1950 — El Gráfico / unknown photographer, public domain via Wikimedia Commons.
• Maracanã during the 1950 World Cup — Public domain / Arquivo Nacional Collection, via Wikimedia Commons.

author: cfm_sol
quoted_text:
When we analyzed $PAID before, the core logic was still “Crypto Creator Fees → X Money,” and the biggest question at the time was whether this mechanism could actually work.

98kfF7rmsg1QDUEoCqNE7g7M1FdrTt92TEp2CLzypump

Now I think PAID’s narrative has upgraded, and its fundamentals have also changed. The product has moved from “concept” to real operation.

PAID previously reached around $36M, and what the market needs to reprice now is no longer “does this concept have enough imagination?” but whether UsePaid can turn this already-proven Fee Bridge into a scalable Creator Economy.

The most important change right now is:Creator Fees → UsePaid → 80% USD → X Money

At the same time:20% → Buy PAID → Burn

This path is no longer just theoretical. UsePaid has already generated real X Money payments, Creator Fees, and PAID Buyback/Burn.

The official team recently disclosed that more than $100K in fees have been routed through X Money, with $1M as the next target. There has also been a single-day PAID Buyback of around $34.8K.

This means:Trading Volume → Creator Fees → X Payments → Buyback → Burn

has already started forming a real Fee Economy.

More importantly, the actual payments themselves generate Attention.

For example, if a Meme directs its Creator Fees to an X user:Meme → X Account → Payment → X Attention → More Trading → More Fees

So PAID now effectively has two overlapping flywheels:

Attention Flywheel:

More Tokens → More Creator Fees → More X Payments → More X Attention → More Trading

Token Flywheel:More Creator Fees → 20% Buyback
→ PAID Burn → Supply ↓

This is also the biggest difference between PAID and an ordinary Meme.

Nikita Bier previously called UsePaid a “creative hack on XMoney” and started discussing the connection between X Accounts and the Token Economy.

Now, combined with the real payment data, I think PAID’s Narrative has evolved from an X Money Meme toward X-native Creator Fee Infrastructure.

The payment recipients are also expanding from ordinary Creators to more influential X users. The screenshots already show payment records involving Elon Musk, the official Solana account, and Nikita Bier.

This makes:Payment → Attention

part of the product itself.

Another important change is that UsePaid has started running into X Money payment limits / rate limits, and the team has adjusted its payment structure accordingly.

This exposes a very real issue:

The biggest risk now is no longer “is anyone using it?”

It is:“Can it handle more usage?”

Of course, this does not mean PMF is fully established yet. It still needs to prove that it can scale.

In particular:

1. Total Fees Routed

Can the fee volume continue growing from $100K → $1M → $10M?

2. X Payments

How many X users are actually receiving money, and how much are they receiving?

3. PAID Buyback / Burn

Can Buyback evolve from occasional large payments into consistent and growing value capture?

4. Token Integrations

Are more Memes actively starting to use UsePaid?

5. Pump / Pons / Other Launchpads

Can it continue expanding its Fee sources and build a cross-Launchpad Fee Bridge?

The further integration with Pump is especially worth watching.

If PAID eventually becomes a Quote Asset on Pump, it would move PAID from a third-party Fee Distribution Layer closer to being part of Pump’s native economic system.

Pons is more of a future expansion Catalyst. For now, Pump is still the main focus. Once Pons becomes operational again, we can re-evaluate the Solana + Robinhood Chain cross-chain Fee Capture thesis.

So my current understanding of PAID has evolved from:

PAID = Meme Creator Fees → X Money

into:PAID = Crypto → X Attention → X Money Fee Distribution Layer

And what PAID itself captures is:Creator Fees → 20% Buyback → PAID Burn

Therefore, what really matters going forward is not simply the price, but whether these metrics can grow together:

More Tokens
→ More Fees
→ More X Payments
→ More Attention
→ More Trading
→ More Buyback
→ More Burn

If this loop continues to expand, PAID could gradually evolve from an X Money Narrative Meme into a true X-native Creator Fee Economy with meaningful scale.

That is what I think the market needs to reprice in the next stage after PAID’s $36M ATH.

10 months ago i had 1 month of runway left and was about to move back in with my parents.

today @orgo is joining @ycombinator.

how it happened:

nov 2025 - berkeley hacker house, 15 people, i'm working out of an electrical room under the stairs. my startup is trending to zero.

down the hall, @spncrk is building Orgo in @mntruell's old room. cloud computers for agents, originally for researchers.

i figure: what if i sell computer use agents to businesses as AI employees?

i message every business owner i know. next morning: 7 calls. end of the week: my first paid customer, $3,500 to build one agent on top of Orgo.

a few months in, my agency was making more on Orgo than Orgo was. so we became cofounders.

jan 24 - i hear about "Clawdbot," i shoot a rushed video of it running on an Orgo computer, then race to SFO to pick up spencer from his vision quest in india.

24 hours later: 1.5M views. @steipete, the guy who built it, becomes Orgo's first paying customer.

then the product broke every single day for 2 months. i woke up sweating every morning.

then @TigerYWang joins as our third cofounder and the thing stops breaking. i start sleeping again.

today Orgo is the computer for your agents. one click and your agent has a work computer in the cloud it can actually use.

build something people want. then, build something agents want.

刚刚，OpenAI 正式发布 GPT-6 Sol 和 GPT-6 Luna。

GPT-6 这一代终于开始全面铺开了。

月初 OpenAI 先发布了最强的 GPT-6 Astra，现在开始把 Astra 上的能力往更便宜、更日常的模型上下放。

这次最狠的是 GPT-6 Sol，API 价格直接来到了：

输入：$2 / M tokens
输出：$10 / M tokens
相比 GPT-5.6 Sol 的促销价格，直接便宜了 50%。

但能力并没有跟着砍半。

OpenAI 表示，GPT-6 Sol 使用了和 Astra 类似的训练方法，在推理、事实可靠性、Coding、Computer Use 和 Alignment 上都进行了升级。

其中一个数据很夸张：

OpenAI 用真实用户曾经举报过模型错误的对话做了一套内部 factuality eval，GPT-6 Sol 的错误数量只有上一代 GPT-5.6 Sol 的大约一半。

OpenAI 甚至称，它的可靠性已经接近 GPT-6 Astra。

也就是说，Astra 继续负责最高难度的任务，但大量 Coding、Agent、自动化和 Computer Use 工作，已经可以直接丢给便宜得多的 Sol。

另外还有一个更便宜的 GPT-6 Luna：

输入 $0.1 / M
输出 $0.5 / M

这个价格已经明显不是冲着「聊天」来的了，而是冲着海量 Agent 调用、文档处理、信息提取这些机器对机器的 workload 去的。

Anthropic 才刚发布 Claude Opus 5.5，大约 90 分钟后，OpenAI 就把 GPT-6 Sol 和 Luna 发了出来。

前沿模型在上面继续卷能力，下面已经开始疯狂卷价格。

Agent 真正大规模跑起来之前，模型 API 的价格战可能才刚开始。

text:
This is the inevitable next evolution in VC.

YC has been running this playbook for a while now: find young talent with some product, give them money, training, and a network, and own a portion of the value they create.

The next step is even earlier stage. You need a company to get into YC, but that's not how investment decisions are made. The most important criteria is that you are a person with great promise who will work hard to find an idea for a product that sticks. The initial product idea is basically irrelevant.

So why require a product at all?

The biggest challenge is identifying outliers and getting the opportunity to back them before anyone else. Building an acceleration program to build the skills of young, ambitious people while establishing a relationship with them gives you the benefits of an early stage accelerator without the cost of investing into each one's company.

I expect the next decade to have more programs that incubate and invest in builders pre-idea. The worst case scenario is you develop a group of qualified new hires for your existing portfolio companies. The best case scenario is you back the next great founders before anyone else.

text:
there's a billion dollar opportunity in crypto that no one is building:

a blockchain where stablecoin payments can be disputed, chargebacked, or reversed.

everyone talks about stablecoins replacing Visa because they’re instant, cheaper, and global.

but a huge part of Visa’s value is the system that protects buyers and merchants when something goes wrong:

> chargebacks
> refunds + returns
> fraud protection
> dispute resolution
> buyer protection
> merchant protection

stablecoin payments don’t have any of that.

once you send the money, the transaction is final and irreversible. if the merchant never ships, sends the wrong product, or scams you, there’s no dispute process to get your money back.

that’s one of the biggest things holding stablecoins back from being adopted in everyday commerce.

someone needs to build a payment network specifically around this problem:

> consumers pay merchants in stablecoins
> buyers can file disputes if something goes wrong
> merchants can respond to those claims
> a governing layer decides when funds should be returned

you still get instant, cheap, global payments, but now with the consumer protections people already expect from card networks like Visa.

text: Interesting perspective
author: AndrewYNg
quoted_text:
The loudest voices stoking fears about AI dangers have made tremendous headway in the past two weeks. AI technology has not taken some unexpected, dangerous turn, but the hype around it — propelled by what appears to be a well orchestrated PR campaign — has drummed up considerable fear. I worry that it represents a setback for our field.

I have written frequently that fears of AI are overhyped. AI’s capabilities can be uncannily human-like and unpredictable, and it’s rational to worry when people who are directly involved express concerns. But I see the problems as a sign of the engineering work that ahead, rather than insurmountable barriers or the sky falling. AI technology continues to advance — which is a good thing! — but technical advances, poorly understood by the public, give those who seek to generate hype repeated opportunities to do so.

First, I don’t see any step up in the risk of human extinction from AI compared to a few months ago. The theories about this remain the same fantastical, science fiction scenarios as a few months ago. The biggest change in AI risk is its cybersecurity capabilities — a topic which we should take seriously — but this, too, will not lead to the end of the world.

The most notable recent event leading to increased fear was when an OpenAI team deployed an agent swarm that hacked into Hugging Face. Much of the popular press contained significant hype. For example, some publications reported that a swarm of 1,200 agents carried out the attack. While this was technically accurate, as I write this, I have about 1,300 processes running on my laptop. Yes, the ability to get large swarms of agents to work in parallel on a task is a significant technical advance, And, in computing, many processes run at the same time. So this shouldn’t be seen as some magical capability.

Additionally, OpenAI’s buggy sandboxing and monitoring processes were key to enabling this incident. Fixing these bugs and putting in place improved monitoring would be appropriate fixes, not pausing AI. There are many well known ways to attack software systems. The main advantage of AI agents is that they are relentless. They will tirelessly try many tactics — and have the patience to chain vulnerabilities together — that previously would have taken an infeasible amount of human effort. But in the long term, I believe the advantage will lie with defenders (because they have more information with which to identify bugs, which they can fix), but the cyber-threat landscape has changed significantly. There are still bottlenecks to identifying and exploiting a vulnerability. AI agents still have to try a lot of things to see what works, and taking these actions takes time and might be detected by defenders. This is why, even though it is now easy to obtain versions of leading open weight models that have had their guardrails removed or weakened, so they will not refuse to try to execute cyber attacks, the world has not ended.

I am also concerned about the anthropomorphization of AI in a lot of reporting, where LLMs and agents are unnecessarily treated as if they were people. If I wield a hammer, miss a nail, and accidentally dent the wall, it’s not the fault of the hammer. The problem lies in how I used the hammer. Similarly, if I prompt an agent and it hacks into someone else’s system, the responsibility lies with me, not the agent.

Of course, we want to build systems that are as safe and predictable as possible. (For example, an unsafe hammer would be one whose head randomly flies off under normal use.) Today’s agentic systems are not predictable, but I see no reason why, by applying sound engineering practices, we won’t be able to make them extremely safe to use. One new element in the forecasts of AI-enabled doom is AI companies disclaiming responsibility for their own products. “I didn’t do it; my out-of-control agent did!” There’s a balance to be struck between the responsibility of the tool maker and the tool user, but when something goes wrong, let’s hold the people building and/or using the hammer responsible, rather than the hammer. (By the way, if you’re worried about AI bioweapon risk, David Bellamy has a great post on why this, too, is overhyped. Briefly, the bottleneck in building a bioweapon is not intelligence, but lab work and manufacturing.)

Pausing AI progress will create much more harm than benefit. First, our adversaries will certainly not slow down. Second, engineering requires discovering problems empirically so we can fix them. If we pause AI by a decade, we will also delay finding and implementing safety engineering fixes by about the same duration.

Of course, the incentive to stoke fears — for regulatory capture, to garner attention, or to make one’s technology seem more powerful — remains the same as before. Disclaiming responsibility is a new one. Taking a hard technical look at the actual risks however, I see little factual basis for the degree of fear that’s been stoked up. We still have hard research and engineering work ahead to improve AI safety, but the beneficial applications continue to vastly outweigh the risks, and we should keep building.

[Original text (with links): https://t.co/jni2tWazAH ]

quoted_text:
刚刚，OpenAI 正式发布 GPT-6 Sol 和 GPT-6 Luna。

GPT-6 这一代终于开始全面铺开了。

月初 OpenAI 先发布了最强的 GPT-6 Astra，现在开始把 Astra 上的能力往更便宜、更日常的模型上下放。

这次最狠的是 GPT-6 Sol，API 价格直接来到了：

输入：$2 / M tokens
输出：$10 / M tokens
相比 GPT-5.6 Sol 的促销价格，直接便宜了 50%。

但能力并没有跟着砍半。

OpenAI 表示，GPT-6 Sol 使用了和 Astra 类似的训练方法，在推理、事实可靠性、Coding、Computer Use 和 Alignment 上都进行了升级。

其中一个数据很夸张：

OpenAI 用真实用户曾经举报过模型错误的对话做了一套内部 factuality eval，GPT-6 Sol 的错误数量只有上一代 GPT-5.6 Sol 的大约一半。

OpenAI 甚至称，它的可靠性已经接近 GPT-6 Astra。

也就是说，Astra 继续负责最高难度的任务，但大量 Coding、Agent、自动化和 Computer Use 工作，已经可以直接丢给便宜得多的 Sol。

另外还有一个更便宜的 GPT-6 Luna：

输入 $0.1 / M
输出 $0.5 / M

这个价格已经明显不是冲着「聊天」来的了，而是冲着海量 Agent 调用、文档处理、信息提取这些机器对机器的 workload 去的。

Anthropic 才刚发布 Claude Opus 5.5，大约 90 分钟后，OpenAI 就把 GPT-6 Sol 和 Luna 发了出来。

前沿模型在上面继续卷能力，下面已经开始疯狂卷价格。

Agent 真正大规模跑起来之前，模型 API 的价格战可能才刚开始。

text:
⏰ If tomorrow morning, Britain’s National Debt ticks over £3 trillion for the first time in history, it won’t be the result of one failure but an entire generation's worth. 25 years of fiscal incontinence, under both Tory and Labour Chancellors.

Even the highest taxes on record can't match ever-higher spending. So, every year without fail, the nation’s credit card bill grows. All because Chancellors wouldn’t make the hard choices. They preferred to lie to the electorate, and perhaps to themselves, that this giant Ponzi scheme was all fine. 

In fact it meant more debt interest for taxpayers, now and forever. Today, we spend more on interest than on defence. By 2030, it will exceed schools, policing, and the entire justice system combined. Left unchecked, our debt will be three times the size of our entire economy in 50 years. That is a bill our grandchildren will have to pay.

Meanwhile, Labour is unwilling to engage with reality. Andy Burnham is happy to write cheques, but not to explain how we pay them. Just as when he said we needn’t be “in hock to the bond markets”, he seems  oblivious to our precarious position. He’s the wrong man at the wrong time. A fair weather Prime Minister, sailing into stormy seas. 

We cannot carry on like this. Countries can go bust. Even the USA, with its almighty dollar, is beginning to discover the limits to debt growth.

That’s why Reform has identified over £80 billion in annual savings: From benefits, Net Zero, and Whitehall. And that number will keep growing, as we do the work in opposition that Labour failed to do.

We will spend some of the £80 billion on securing our border and increasing the tax-free personal allowance to £15k to make work pay. But we will also bring down debt.

And we will reduce the interest bill too. Our interest rates are currently higher than those of Greece or Italy, because investors don’t have confidence in the government’s policies, the dismal economic leadership we’ve had in recent times - and not just Liz Truss - or indeed in sterling. By cutting spending, reducing energy prices and freeing up the housing and labour markets, we’ll reduce both borrowing and inflation and therefore interest rates.

We won’t fix a 25-year problem overnight. But unlike Rishi Sunak, Rachel Reeves, or it seems John Healey, we will make the choices that will start.

text:
Suddenly pretty bullish on @avax

Their summit was excellent, but it’s really the announcements they’ve secured recently around it, and the focus those announcements show.

Blockchains die from a lack of differentiation.

There are too many of them. We only need a few. Yours needs to be about ONE thing, and that thing needs to be defensible.

Memecoins are NOT defensible.

Meme traders dgaf where they trade. They follow liquidity. Look how rapidly activity can rotate from one ecosystem to another, like what happened with Robinhood vs Solana.

Memes are basically impossible for a chain to own. An app can own them, like @fomo or @Pumpfun, but a chain can’t.

But massive institutional deals with enterprise companies and nation states?

Those are defensible as hell.

And sovereign interoperable L1s are literally Avalanche’s original thesis. So seeing them full-circle to focus on that original positioning, and actually execute on it at a very high level, makes the whole thing feel much more coherent to me.

Will that make number go up?

Absolutely no idea. That’s its own question.

But can it make Avalanche money as a business and give them a repeatable, scalable model that lets them own and defend a unique lane in this insane industry?

Absolutely.

And that’s probably more important to long-term survival than number go up.

At least barely.

quoted_text:
GPT-6 Sol and Luna push the cost efficiency frontier by halving cost relative to GPT-5.6 Sol and Luna. Intelligence Index and Coding Agent Index scores remain level with GPT-5.6, with progress in some evaluations and regressions in others

Pricing is approximately half that of GPT-5.6: Sol drops from $4/$20 to $2/$10 per million input/output tokens, and Luna from $0.20/$1.20 to $0.10/$0.50, with the same 90% discount for cache reads and 25% premium for cache writes.

Key takeaways:

➤ Halves Cost per Task: GPT-6 Sol (max) costs $1.06 per task to run the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, ~50% less than GPT-5.6 Sol (max) at $1.99. GPT-6 Luna (max) costs $0.07 per task, ~60% less than GPT-5.6 Luna (max) at $0.18. This is driven by the price cut, as both models use slightly more output tokens per task (31k vs 29k for Sol, and 51k vs 41k for Luna). These two releases allow OpenAI to capture a significant portion of the cost efficiency Pareto frontier.

➤ In the Coding Agent Index, Sol improves but Luna regresses: In OpenAI's Codex harness, GPT-6 Sol (max) scores 57 in the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, up 2 points from GPT-5.6 Sol (max), with gains in Terminal-Bench 4.0 (43% vs 37%) and SWE-Atlas-QnA (58% vs 54%). At $2.99 per task it costs ~50% less than GPT-5.6 Sol (max) and sits on the Pareto frontier of Coding Agent Index vs Cost per Task. GPT-6 Luna (max) scores 41, down 2 points from GPT-5.6 Luna (max), with lower scores in SWE-Atlas-QnA (44% vs 49%) and DeepSWE v1.1 (64% vs 66%), at ~60% lower cost per task.

➤ Significant reduction in hallucination: Both models hallucinate less in AA-Omniscience, our knowledge and hallucination benchmark. GPT-6 Sol (max) cuts its hallucination rate from 92% to 60% and GPT-6 Luna (max) from 93% to 77%. Sol achieves this by declining to answer more often: it attempts 83% of questions vs 99% for GPT-5.6 Sol (max), which cuts wrong answers by about a quarter but also lowers accuracy 5 points from 59% to 54%. Luna's accuracy is broadly unchanged at 44% vs 43% while it answers fewer questions. On the AA-Omniscience Index, Sol improves from 22 to 27 and Luna from -10 to 1.

➤ Mix of improvement and regression across evals: Beyond AA-Omniscience, both models improve in AutomationBench-AA (Sol 62% vs 60%, Luna 53% vs 50%) and Terminal-Bench 4.0 (Sol 44% vs 40%, Luna 13% vs 12%). However, we observe regressions in two key knowledge work evaluations. In GDPval-AA v2.1, our benchmark adapted from OpenAI's dataset of economically valuable tasks across 44 occupations, Sol drops ~100 Elo points and Luna ~75. Luna also drops ~45 Elo points in AA-Briefcase v1.1, while Sol is level. AA-Briefcase v1.1 is a private evaluation across multi-week knowledge work projects, with thousands of input files. Our team has manually inspected hundreds of model outputs: the regressions tend to be driven by reduced presentation quality and deliverables that omit rubric elements.

Congratulations @OpenAI and @sama on the launch!

What an insane day in AI. The frontier models just became substantially cheaper, with the Opus 5.5 price cuts, and now with GPT-6 Sol and Luna dropping token prices by 50%.

The rate at which the cost per task (on a like-for-like basis) drops in AI is unlike any other type of technology in history. And every time the cost of AI drops, the use-cases you can deploy agents against dramatically increase. This is Jevons paradox applied to agents.

These improvements will directly lead to broader diffusion of AI in the economy as we can use agents to process all of our data, scan our code for security issues, read through all log data to make decisions, have agent swarms in workflows, and much more. The cost of tokens is directly correlated to these use-cases being opened up at scale.

text:
Ben Horowitz says instead of banning AI, educators should set problems students can't solve without it:

"I was talking to Dan Boneh, who is a great professor of computer science and cryptography at Stanford. His take on AI was: You have two choices. You can ban it, and by the way, that won't work. Or you can make the problems so hard that you can't solve them without AI."

"What he's seeing is, 'I've got students solving things that no student in history could have ever solved.' That's what's possible. You want to have that orientation: What can you solve with the tools? What can you do that's a breakthrough? Now everybody has an opportunity to create a breakthrough."

"Then you're a main character, not an NPC. That's what the academy is about. Do you want to be a main character? If you want to be a main character, we help you do that. If you want to be a cog in a machine, this is not going to be the best place for you."

text:
I think fixed-rate DeFi lending has a compelling retail use case: making money easier to plan around.

Someone saving for a purchase in three months wants to know what they can withdraw then.

Someone borrowing against crypto wants to know how much that financing will cost.

The thing is a changing APY (mostly exorbitant one) makes both harder.

However, “fixed” needs a precise definition.

A fixed borrowing rate, a fixed maturity payout, and a vault investing in fixed-rate loans can produce very different experiences. So far, there are several terminologies around 'fixed' credit:

- Fixed-term loan
- Fixed-maturity claim
- Vault holding fixed-rate loans
- Borrower-set rate

This distinction is especially relevant for passive retail users.

For example, a vault can hold fixed-rate loans while paying a variable return. Its utilization, loan renewals, allocations, fees, and rewards can change.

And obviously several protocols are 'competing' on this multidimensional fixed-landscape:

- @pendle_fi PT
- @Morpho Midnight/ Tenor
- @kamino Fixed rates
- @Loopscale
- @TermMaxFi
- @JupiterExchange Offerbook

And several others.

And since we are talking about onboarding retails, the most plausible entry points are:

- Stablecoin savings with a planned withdrawal date.
- Crypto-backed borrowing for a defined temporary cash need.
- Financing that matches a dated investment’s maturity.
- Simple term-selection interfaces inside apps people already use.

The bear case is still present.

Retail savers may resist locking funds; borrowers may prefer cheaper floating-rate debt; small balances may be uneconomical; and liquidity may remain concentrated in leveraged or incentivized strategies.

Fixed rates also do little, on their own, for consumers who lack collateral. Expanding into ordinary household credit requires complex legal processes, plus additional underwriting and repayment infrastructure.

Fixed-rate DeFi has a credible role in retail finance because predictability is valuable. Its most defensible promise is a clear, comprehensible financial commitment over a chosen period.

But the category becomes truly useful only when that commitment survives ordinary user behavior: small balances, early cash needs, and missed attention at maturity.

NFA. DYOR.
