text: most teams skip the API surface and wonder why their AI agents break everything.
author: ronixtec
quoted_text:
A performance marketing platform with paying advertisers asked us to make their product operable by AI agents.

We delivered the foundation in six weeks, the MCP service twelve weeks later, and the client's CTO now ships production code through his own AI harness inside gates we built.

I want to walk through how, because "AI-enabled adtech" is on every deck in the category and almost none of it means an agent can operate the platform.

Their codebase had real advertisers, real offer configurations, and real money moving through conversion data.

This is brownfield, not a weekend prototype demo.

February and March, we didn't touch AI. 

We built the foundation the agents would need: versioned management APIs, a dedicated API key type with its own authorization gating, an SDK surface, published Swagger docs.

Teams skip this constantly. They wire a model to the UI endpoints, the payloads are ten times too large for an agent's context, the first write corrupts a live offer, and the pilot dies. I've seen it across 100+ engagements. 

When someone says "our platform isn't ready for agents," they almost always skipped the API surface.

June 9, the MCP service went live. Tenant-scoped, read-only by design. Offer listings, change logs, performance summaries, conversion data. An early user couldn't damage a live configuration because there was nothing to damage with.

July 1, the first write tools: pause, share, clone an offer, update a conversion status. July 9, the second wave: update offers, resume paused ones, create ad-hoc conversions for integrators.

The endpoints were purpose-built for language models. Narrow summary calls, current-date context injected for month-only queries, response-size caps, latency work. Large payloads break agent workflows, so the surface was designed around the agent rather than reused from the UI.

Their CTO ships production code himself, through his own AI agent harness. We own the API surface, the architecture, code review, QA and release. Same repository, same board, same branching strategy, same quality gates, with guardrails enforced at GitHub level. 

April 14 was the first production delivery from that workflow: a query optimisation where the agent validated its own work by diffing old and new SQL against production data, row for row.

The release count came from three things: automated AI review on every pull request since January, tests scoped from the PR diff with the bulk of new test code generated, and a documentation set of around 70 system documents kept in the repository so it doubles as context for the agents.

Behind it, this engagement is one of the first two pilots for Velocity Core, our own agentic delivery system. 

A ticket status change fires a webhook, an isolated agent plans, executes, runs CI and opens a PR for human review. 

When CI fails, the failure and the developer's fix are recorded and served back to future runs. Alpha, tested on real tickets, with the client's CTO inside the loop.

Their CEO connected his own AI assistant to the platform. As far as we know, very few platforms in performance marketing can say that today.

That's what our Velocity Framework was built for.

text:
Opus 5.5 is 60% cheaper per input/output token than Astra.

At max effort, AA's estimated task cost was 83% higher than Astra max.

I looked at Artificial Analysis's latest numbers. The reasoning setting changes the comparison quite a bit.
AA intelligence score and weighted average cost per task:
- Astra max: 53, $3.26.
- Opus 5.5 high: 54, $1.82.
- Opus 5.5 max: 58, $5.98.

Opus high has a similar score to Astra max, at roughly 44% lower cost. Opus max scores higher, but uses far more output tokens across the benchmark suite.

So yes, Anthropic is bringing Fable-level capability into cheaper Opus models. OpenAI is making Sol and Luna cheaper while keeping Astra for its hardest work. But I wouldn't assume Astra is automatically the smartest option anymore.

These are benchmark configurations, not quotes for your company's workflow. Opus results include its default fallback models. And output speed isn't the same as finishing the job faster.

Before switching labs, I'd run my actual tasks at several reasoning settings. Same quality bar, including the failures and retries. 

I'd buy the cheapest setup that clears that bar.

text:
褚时健把濒临倒闭的小厂做到亚洲第一、世界第三的烟草王国，创造991亿利税。但自己干了18年只挣了80万，退休前有了小心思，动了小金库，后来退了钱还是被判了无期……

晚年保外就医，他去哀牢山承包了两千亩荒地种橙子。王石给他传记写序，题目叫《企业家的尊严》，感慨：老两口到哀牢山是自己选择，不是组织分配，最值得敬佩的就是他保持了尊严。

这他妈逻辑太乱了，一个给国家挣了近千亿、干了18年只挣了80万的企业家，被判无期。保外就医以七十四岁高龄去荒山种橙子，却被夸成选择尊严。难道不该批评是国家制度逼企业家以及每个人犯罪吗？难道不知褚时健直到生命终点哀而不得，才上哀牢山吗。

很多国产企业家被权力反复蹂躏后，就把强奸变成了顺奸，开始还大声呼救，后来呼救变成了叫床。

国产企业家为什么这么怂？因为中国没有商业传统。汉高祖刘邦不许商人穿丝绸，不许坐马车，重税……

号称最开放的唐朝也歧视商人，李白他爹是商人，所以他一生不能科举，只好跑到长安混酒局……

宋朝官府连酒曲都垄断，商人常倾家荡产……

明朝农民可以穿绸、纱、绢、布，但商人只许穿绢和布，不许穿靴。把商贩与奴仆、娼优列在一起。大明不仅封关禁海还从精神上歧视商人，它没等来工业革命，是有原因的。

公元1602年，荷兰开办人类第一家股份有限公司，第一个证券交易所……那是明万历三十年，封关禁海。直到1904年中国才有了第一部商业法，叫《钦定大清商律》，此时意大利人颁布人类第一部海商法，已足足九百年。

欧洲著名的商业家族，是美第奇家族，赞助米开朗基罗、达芬奇，推动了文艺复兴和欧洲进程。

而同时代的中国商人沈万三。先不说是否真有其人，但《明史》有真实故事：一个叫沈秀的富民，帮忙修了南京三分之一的城墙，还想出钱犒赏三军。朱元璋大怒——你个匹夫也敢犒我天子的军队，此乱民也，该杀。马皇后劝了半天，才改成流放云南。

欧洲商人搞赞助，推动文艺复兴，中国商人搞赞助，抄家流放。

为什么欧洲有着悠久的商业传统和商业自由度，其中一大原因就是，欧洲很少有大一统，你不让我做买卖，我到别的地方去做买卖。而大一统悠久传统的中国，皇上认为：商人有钱有资源，会抢走民心，会动摇我的统治——这就是皇上的底层逻辑。所以任正非跑不跑不重要，任正非不跑，张正非李正非韩正非也会跑，在一个没有商业规则、商人纯属权力依附，没事儿就倒查三十年的地方，即使一时GDP风风光光，也是二世而亡。散会！

quoted_text:
我的油管第10期：《中国富豪，哪些还想跑？》

任正非携全家跑了。有人说，造谣。

在人人焦虑的大背景下，真相不重要，重要的是人们太需要变化了。太需要天安门出大事，中南海出大事——重要的是人心思变。

任正非到底跑不跑，王石、俞敏洪、王健林、王兴、刘强东、张一鸣跑不跑……中国富豪们还有哪些想跑。

潘适夷一生都在跑，高考锁骨被撞断，知道高考不中了，用另外的名字“石屹”考上石油学校。他从天水跑到廊坊，从廊坊跑到深圳，从深圳边防的狗洞下钻进去，又跑到海南，拎着五斤橘子和一条香烟去规划局看资料，感觉天要塌了……毫不犹豫再次跑路，去了北京。这才有了后来的“潘石屹”。

潘石屹现在处于生与死之间，他就是薛定谔的猫。

“白手套逃跑型”“提前布局型”“离岸信托局”……所谓提前布局，这局那局，都不如政治局。

马云跑过，又回来了，他的根在政坛——阿里巴巴完成“中国历史上规模最大的一次私营融资”，购买股份的包括博裕资本、中信资本、国开金融，新天域资本。《纽约时报》指出，股东包括江泽民的孙子江志成、刘云山的儿子刘乐飞、温家宝的儿子温云松等中央政治局常委的20多人的子孙……

你问马云为什么不跑，请问，当年胡雪岩为什么不跑。

其实命运重重叠叠，早在1949年就布下了这张网。

1949年，何应钦邀请中国船王卢作孚出任交通部长，他拒绝。阎锡山也邀请他，他又拒绝。但共产党派来潘汉年，他立马同意，奋不顾身率船队归国了。抗战时，卢作孚冒着日机轰炸，率船队抢运出一百五十多万人，一百多万吨物资。史称中国的敦刻尔克。

两年后，深受其辱的卢作孚吞下大量安眠药时，有没有想到这两趟奋不顾身的航行。

一念天堂，一念地狱。历史一眨眼，就是普通人一生。1956年，眼见北京公私合营轰轰烈烈，荣毅仁心里不服，他代表上海工商界表态：北京用了十天，阿拉上海宁只要六天。上海资本家排着队去签公私合营申请书。十万多商户全部合营。当晚，大小老板带着家属上台，合唱《全世界人民心一条》……

1949年，荣毅仁说“我赞成共产党，但是我只举一只手，如果两只手都举起来，那是投降”。公私合营时他改口了，说“举一只手赞成共产党，我错了，现在要举两只手”。他是真投降了……文革时他被抄家，剃阴阳头，食指被打断，发配刷厕所，折磨了十三年。

褚时健以七十四岁高龄去荒山种橙子，被王石夸成选择尊严。难道不知道褚时健直到生命终点都逃不出那座精神牢狱，哀而不得，才上哀牢山吗。中国企业家为什么这么怂，很多国产企业家被权力反复蹂躏后，把强奸变成了顺奸，开始还大声呼救，后来呼救变成了叫床。

商鞅认为：商人有钱有资源，会把老百姓抢跑。秦统一天下，重农抑商，成为君王的必选，两千年循环。

罗马立《万民法》，外国人也能贸易，裁判官公平处理商业纠纷……而同时期的汉武帝歧视商人，把盐铁专卖。

1303年，英王颁布了《商人章程》。而同时期的大明朝，商人跟娼优一个等级。

1602年，荷兰开办人类第一家股份有限公司，第一个证券交易所……那时是明万历三十年，中国禁海。

欧洲的美第奇家族，赞助米开朗基罗、达芬奇，推动了文艺复兴和欧洲进程。

而同时代的中国商人沈万三。先不说是否真有其人，但《明史》有真实故事：一个叫沈秀的富民，帮忙修了南京城墙，想出钱犒赏三军。朱元璋大怒——你个匹夫也敢犒我天子的军队，此乱民也，该杀。马皇后劝了半天，才改成流放云南。

欧洲商人搞赞助，推动文艺复兴，中国商人搞赞助，抄家流放。

欧洲很少有大一统。而大一统的中国皇上认为：商人有钱有资源，会抢走民心，会动摇我的统治——这就是皇上的底层逻辑。所以任正非跑不跑不重要，任正非不跑，张正非李正非韩正非也会跑，在一个没有商业规则、商人纯属权力依附，没事儿就倒查三十年的地方，即使一时GDP风风光光，也是二世而亡。散会！

text:
中期选举不换总统，为什么能影响美股？｜美国中期选举与美股①

总统任期继续，但国会可能改旗易帜。

一旦众议院、或参议院控制权，发生变化。

接下来两年的政策议程、企业税负和政府支出方向，都可能重新改写。

这就是为什么，中期选举不选总统，却依然成为牵动市场的重要事件。
————————
一、为什么叫“中期选举”？

美国总统任期四年，国会选举每两年一次。

2024年，选总统和国会议员；
2026年，总统不改选，国会选举；
2028年，再次同时选总统和国会。

2026年发生在两次总统选举之间，因此被称为“中期选举”。

即使共和党输掉中期选举，川普也不会自动下台。

改变的是国会的权力分布。
——————
二、到底选哪些人？

国会两院：众议院和参议院。

众议院：435席全部改选。

众议员任期两年，全部435个席位重新竞争。

现任议员可以参选连任，“全部改选”不代表全部换人。

参议院：100席中，约三分之一改选。

参议员任期六年，席位分成三组，每两年轮流改选一组。

因此每次通常改选33或34席。如果有补缺的特别选举，数量还可能增加。

参议员由全州选民选出。

因此，同一个州的选民，可能分别支持不同候选人。

众议院的席位分配，体现人口差异，参议院的席位分配，体现各州平等。

此外，部分州还会选州长、州议员及地方官员，也可能举行公投。

所以，中期选举实际上，是许多场选举集中举行，各地选民拿到的选票，并不完全相同。
——————
三、怎样才算“赢得中期选举”？

通常指，拿下众议院或参议院的控制权。

众议院通常有435个席位。若所有席位均已产生，并正常就任，获得218席即可达到多数。

若存在空缺，决定议院控制权时，通常要看实际就任，并有资格投票的议员人数，以及议院规则。

参议院通常有100名议员。获得51席通常意味着多数。

如果两党各有50席，副总统作为参议院议长，可以在参议院表决平票时，投下决定性一票。

因此，在这种情况下，副总统所属政党，通常能够组织和控制参议院。

但副总统并不是普通参议员，不能在每次表决中投票，只有出现平票时才可投决定票。

两院的胜负分别计算。一个党可以同时控制两院，也可以只控制其中一院。

控制权还可能取决于，独立议员是否加入某个党团，以及议院内部的组织安排。
————————
四、控制国会，究竟能改变什么？

用一个例子最容易理解，总统想降低企业税，能不能宣布之后就直接实施？

涉及修改税法，就需要国会立法。

税收法案，通常首先在众议院提出，参议院也要审议。两院通过完全相同的文本后，再交总统签署。

如果总统所属政党控制两院，推动法案通常更容易。

如果反对党控制其中一院，就可能要求修改条款，或者阻止通过。

反过来，反对党即使控制两院，也不能随意绕过总统。

总统可以否决法案。国会若要推翻否决，必须在众议院和参议院，分别获得出席，并投票议员三分之二的支持。

此外，某些法案，如果符合特定程序，和预算规则，可能通过预算协调程序，在参议院以简单多数通过，不受通常意义上的，60票阻挠门槛约束。

除了法律，国会还掌握几项重要权力。

首先是拨款。联邦政府许多项目、部门资金，需要国会通过拨款法案，或临时拨款法案授权。

如果未能及时通过，部分联邦机构，可能出现资金缺口并停摆。

其次是人事。总统提名的部长、联邦法官等，许多重要官员，需要参议院提供建议并同意。

参议院控制权，因此会影响总统，能否顺利组建团队、填补司法职位。

还有监督。国会可以举行听证会、开展调查，要求政府解释政策和行为。

国会委员会也可以发出传票，但其调查权和执行方式受到宪法、法律、议院规则以及司法审查等限制。

至于弹劾，众议院负责通过弹劾条款，也就是提出正式指控。参议院负责审判。

总统案件，由联邦最高法院首席大法官主持审判。参议院只有在出席议员三分之二同意定罪时，才能作出定罪。
————————
五、为什么美股投资者也要关注？

因为国会的决定，会进入企业的利润表。

企业税率影响税后利润，政府支出影响行业需求，补贴影响投资回报，监管立法影响经营成本。

这些变化又会影响企业盈利预期和股票估值。

但不能简单理解为某党赢，美股就涨。

市场还要判断：哪些政策真正可能落地，影响有多大，以及股价是否已经提前反映。

同时，国会控制权改变，也不会让现有法律，和政策自动失效。

总统仍可在法律授权范围内，行使行政权力。

但行政措施的持续时间和范围，可能受到国会拨款、立法、监督以及法院审查的影响。

所以，中期选举之后，哪些政策更容易推进，哪些会受到阻力，这些变化又会如何影响企业和市场，这个是关键的分析。

可以点个关注，后续我们再深入。

text:
It's been super interesting to watch OpenAI and Anthropic bounce from hyped to trashed to hyped and back again.

It feels like every tech product goes from insanely hyped, to beaten down, to hyped again, to beaten down again, and so on. As crypto folks will be well-aware, it is the nature of social media: people want to be smart, and the best way to do that is to be a little contrarian (while pointing out something that has a kernel of truth). But then other people keep piling on, motivated not by inherent belief but rather by observing that this opinion gets engagement. These voices become extremely loud and ultimately take things way too far in that direction relative to how things really are. Eventually that take becomes extremely consensus, and the loudness of consensus dies off because now it is just a boring old opinion. If the product is good and keeps improving though, then this cycle will get revisited again later; if not it will just fade out. And for the best products, the sine wave is upward-sloping, as the best builders make more hay than average when the sun is shining, and weather the storm of negative contrarianism better than average too. This dynamic is exacerbated in OpenAI/Anthropic because they release new models leapfrogging each other, but I think there is something fundamental about social consensus going on here too.

For builders, the answer is obviously just to keep building. It's never as good as it seems, and it's never as bad as it seems. For observers and future historians, maybe the takeaway is to try to be a little earlier to the inflection point. :)

这轮合作的资金流和普通合作不太一样，
币安花 1 亿美元买入 Circle 股票；
Circle 则继续给钱给币安推广 $USDC 。

币安以后还会把 $USDC 接入现有及未来的储蓄、投资等产品，还会通过降低交易手续费等方式继续推广 $USDC 。

这批股票还有两年锁仓期。
这两年内，币安原则上并不可以出售转让或对冲， 除非特定情况下提前终止商业合作。

在过去几个月，Circle 管理层画了一大堆大饼，现在终于看到一些实事。
先有 Arc 主网上线 ，再收购了 Tazapay 扩大支付渠道，
现在还有币安的加持。
暂时来讲，还没有其他稳定币有跑赢 USDC 和 USDT 。

币安手握 3 亿多的注册用户，而且覆盖一堆新兴市场。
这轮合作，估计 $USDC 可以进一步扩大它的分发渠道，继续稳固它的护城河。
Circle 的野心，估计也已经不满足于继续当万年老二，想借用币安流量，直接杀进 Tether 的主场。

不过，到目前为止，我对 $CRCL 的期望还是一样，
到底什么时候 Circle 才可以不再这么依赖储备金利息赚钱？

text:
CFTC 主席 Selig：市场需为大规模代币化与 24/7 交易做好准备

美国商品期货交易委员会（CFTC）主席 Michael Selig 表示，监管机构需要为“大规模代币化”做好准备，并针对区块链、人工智能等新技术调整现有市场。Selig 周二在纽约联储举行的美国国债市场会议上表示，随着代币化、链上金融和 24/7 交易等发展，未来十年金融市场的变化可能超过过去几十年之和。

Selig 称，整个特朗普政府已通过拥抱创新、鼓励竞争、合理监管等举措，为美国市场继续保持全球领先奠定基础。CFTC 还将寻求更多方式，鼓励市场参与者、交易所和清算所负责任地采用稳定币。过去一年，该机构已就能源衍生品市场的 24/7 交易发布指引并征求公众意见；今年 2 月，CFTC 还将国民信托银行发行的稳定币纳入合格抵押品范围。

与此同时，CFTC 的姊妹机构美国证券交易委员会（SEC）上周发布了备受期待的“创新豁免”，为代币化股票的链上交易腾出空间。在整体监管加密行业的法案在参议院受阻后，两大机构正各自推进相关议程。

这周腹泻了一周，亲身经历吐槽一下。。。作为普通老百姓，我们不需要同情，可怜，任何医护人员，因为在这个医疗体系下，我们普通老百姓是绝对的弱者，绝对的没有任何的话语权，一丁点活路都没有。
我叫救护车，救护车拉人的，公立医院一天挂八瓶水，用那破逼国产仿制药头孢，从37.5，给我干到39.8  我赶紧转院，一直拉胆汁，人家救护车一路说说笑笑的，问我拉什么样的粪便，我说胆汁，「两天没吃任何，拉了大几十次，吐了几十次，还能拉出别的么」人家一脸鄙夷的看着我说，胆汁怎么可能拉出来。然后又一脸鄙夷的跟我说，你们怎么寻思去的xx医院呢，他说那医院你们住的起么，那医院可贵可贵的了。「原话毫无改动」「陪护阿姨更烦人，在旁边一门加腔，嗯，我说也不可能是胆汁，一看就是蔬菜什么的，我费劲全身力气说了一句，我不吃任何绿色蔬菜。就耳鸣没法说话了」

   然后找个傻逼陪护阿姨。一天让我吃十遍小米粥，我根本无法吃，吃100ml，吐200ml，只要你不吃，她过一会儿再说一遍，过一会儿再说一遍，我发烧40度，她嘟嘟嘟一门跟我说要起诉商家，说一遍我说我现在没功夫，过一会儿又找机会再说一遍，一天至少说五遍。然后我拉尿不湿里她给我换，一边换一边说，这么拉可够呛。这么拉这孩子可够呛啊。这个逼嘴碎的拿针给她缝上我都不解气。

 原来公立医院那个大夫。更鸡巴有意思。跟我说必须检查诺如病毒，现在感染诺如病毒的很多，又跟我说了这个病的所有严重后果，早发现早治疗的必要性，必须立刻确诊对症治疗，晚对症治疗一天都得有生命危险，给我吓得魂飞魄散，肝胆俱裂。
赶紧检查，我说啥时候出结果。他说四天

 我当时真的拿不起刀，站不起来，真的。不然我他妈

这一些人完全不是为了照顾病人，救病人来的，好像都希望你赶紧死，省的费劲救了。

就好像那个保姆伺候老头似的，给老头老太太下毒，几天毒死一个好拿一个月工钱。

我这几个逼助理也是花瓶，一个吓的只会哭，一个那艺娜口音大舌头打结说啥别人都听不懂，最后我家皇后从杭州飞过来了才把一切捋顺清楚保我一条狗命。。。

I’ve been asked a lot what it’s like to partner with both Coinbase and Robinhood when they compete so fiercely.

The answer comes down to Morpho’s fundamental purpose: connecting.

Morpho is an open credit network designed to connect lenders and borrowers across any boundary (social, geographic, political, …). More borrowers create more demand for capital. More lenders create more competition to fund borrowers. Over time, that means deeper liquidity and better terms for everyone using the Morpho network.

Competitors sharing infrastructure isn’t unique to Morpho. Banks compete fiercely for customers while relying on shared payment networks like Visa. Tech companies compete while building on the same internet protocols like HTTP. Credit should work the same way: it works better when you are maximally connected.

Our ambition is to bring as much of the world's credit onto one shared network as possible. If you’re building on Morpho, expect us to keep connecting new companies, new markets, new ecosystems, including the ones you compete with, because this is what will make your financial products stronger!

text:
这两年AI Agent进步很快，我平时也会让它调数据、分析行情，甚至给出交易建议。但真到了跨链、签名和资产操作这一步，我依然只敢自己来。

原因很简单：AI分析错了还可以重来，资产一旦转错就没有后悔药。它用了什么数据、数据有没有被篡改、最后执行的动作是不是我的本意，这些问题没有解决，我就不可能真正把钱包交给AI。

这也是我关注 @DeepSafe_AI 的原因。它不是再做一个更聪明的AI，而是想给AI和区块链系统增加一道验证层。它的CRVA机制会临时、随机地选择验证节点，对数据、消息和操作请求进行核验，通过后才允许继续执行。验证者还会不断轮换，身份也被隐藏，尽量降低被攻击和串通的风险。

这套机制未来不只可以验证AI Agent，也能用于Oracle、跨链、多签钱包和资产托管。目前CRVA还处于Beta测试阶段，距离大规模应用仍需要时间。但我越来越相信，AI真正接管资产之前，市场最缺的可能不是更聪明的Agent，而是一套让我敢把钱交给它的验证机制。

quoted_text:
SEC 推出五年创新豁免，允许代币化美股通过许可制 AMM 交易

9月17日，SEC 正式发布“创新豁免”，为通过公链交易代币化美股提供了一条附条件的合规路径。符合要求的代币化证券交易场所，可以使用有准入限制的自动做市商（AMM）和流动性池开展交易，并获得“交易所”定义的临时豁免。

符合条件、用自有资金向这些池子提供代币化股票流动性的主体，也能获得配套的“交易商”定义豁免。相关豁免将在发布五年后到期，SEC 同时继续征求公众意见。

值得留意的是智能合约必须公开、可审计，并部署在公开、无许可的区块链上，但参与交易的人需要符合平台的准入要求。

股票代币持有人还必须享有与同类别传统股票相同的权利，包括该类别股票应有的分红、投票等权利，提供合成敞口的相关产品不在这次范围内。

第三方代币化股票上线前，需要书面通知原发行人，发行人有权提出异议并阻止其在这类平台交易。这也意味着，即便技术上能够把某只股票做成代币，能否上线仍然受到发行人意愿和监管条件的约束。

当然，平台还需要满足美国主体、制裁合规、信息披露等要求，股票品种数量和成交量都有上限，原股票在主要上市交易所停牌，链上必须同步停牌，反欺诈和反操纵规定也继续适用。

text:
$NOIR - @noirpay - https://t.co/pc4xJOU75X
What is Noirpay
A self-custodial privacy neobank on Robinhood Chain: your stablecoins and tokenized stocks stay invisible on-chain, and still earn yield, spend on a card and pass compliance.

Noirpay is a privacy neobank built for Robinhood Chain, Robinhood's Arbitrum-based Layer 2. You open it like a neobank, with a handle, a balance, a card and statements. Underneath, every balance is a set of encrypted notes in a shielded pool secured by zero-knowledge proofs, and only your spending key can open them.
Why it exists
Private transfers already exist on Robinhood Chain. A private account does not.

Robinhood Chain is the only network where payroll-grade stablecoins and tokenized equities sit in the same address, so a public wallet there leaks what you earn, what you own and what you're worth, all at once. Every privacy tool built so far fixes that by turning money into dead capital: the moment you hide it, it stops earning, can't be spent on a card, and can't be shown to anyone who needs to see it.

Noirpay's shielded balance keeps earning, spends on a card, and can prove itself with a revocable, time-boxed viewing key.
I think this is a pretty interesting idea. If the product actually works as intended, it could be genuinely useful.

☘☘☘ The project is still very early, so be cautious if you’re considering investing. For now, it may be worth putting it on your watchlist.

From what I can see, it fits the current trend and could become increasingly relevant to the future of crypto.

text:
@ethlabs_org is now 3 months old since our June 22nd announcement 🥳

thought I'd share some musings as co-founder, on culture, goals and impact, also prompted by @apriori0x in the recording we made https://t.co/FJj4EXU1M7 letssgo

---

establishing an org culture starts from day one, and I think we've hit it mostly, with moderate hiring since we started that has gelled well so far. I had reflected early on on culture here https://t.co/0XQH9fy7gv

3 months in I would say these are the main features:
   - goal-driven, we're not attached to specific means, we want a clear outcome and we go after it whichever way we need to
   - high urgency, I wake up in the morning hungry to pick up the tickets and threads that my US frens and EU night owls have left
    - ai native, this is a superpower and also gives a fresh spin to a lot of work that i used to enjoy doing but wasn't doing much of anymore (data collection/analysis, code/specs). i'm not the biggest consumer either, truly amazed by the strides @fradamt is making with AI-assisted formal verification
    - user-centric, we're still early and can always refine our approach here, but we really want to be intentional with it. building these feedback loops is imo one of our most critical needs atm. particularly as a non-profit, it's the only way to ensure impact 
   - working in public, it's a healthy default and imo a responsibility given the nature and mission of our org, to work on behalf of the Ethereum community for the betterment of Ethereum. we push updates weekly, putting in some work to keep them engaging and high signal. see here https://t.co/bfrHI9ypeQ

---

the funny thing is it feels still like we are learning about ourselves, and what we can do with this new org. some observations on what's working well from my POV:
   - i think it is clear that we can have strong impact on core protocol direction and development still. one example, our hegotá view, led by @casparschwa @fradamt and @adietrichs, was a labour of love and rigour, and we held ourselves to a very high standard in coming up with our rankings https://t.co/vJ3iaEsapb work on account abstraction, fast finality, fast slots, all ongoing
   - i think we are growing well to be a "defragmenter" between L1 and L2s, sometimes a relayer helping to signal what one needs from the other, sometimes a more involved builder bridging the gap. @decentrek's work on 8130<>8141 is strong evidence, and @ox_shaman is accelerating quickly on following up its conclusion with a broad effort to maximally defragment accounts. better integration between L1 and L2s, their liquidity and their users, remains a key work stream for us. right now we're zoomed in on blobs, their demand and their supply
   - i think we've been good at building connections with strong teams working on the private and public buildout of the Ethereum network, and leveraging these connections. this is starting to compound for instance on going-to-market with the fast confirmation rule or the quick slots piece https://t.co/QRG4lOGJVU, and getting signal on our directions. kudos to @_julianma and @binji_x for doing so much outreach

---

but! given these capabilities, are we tackling the right goals? this is a lot of our current internal chatter:
   - our stated mission is to make Ethereum the settlement layer for the global economy. ethereum has been unreasonably effective at attracting users and capital to its network, thanks to its unique properties. it is working, we want to make it work better, and maintain its lead + increase its footprint in the world
   - how can we be more principled with problem identification? we're taking it both bottom-up and top-down. some concrete work emerges organically from internal reflections and external engagement, and we also spend more time now top-down/first principles-refining our intuitions. this helps connect the dots and move up and up to bigger and bigger targets
   - in particular, feeling like Ethlabs can do more advocacy and work on ETH the asset, rooted in our technical work and ecosystem engagement. ETH is a big part both of the network's utility, and its reach to export the values of Ethereum. this matters.
   - feeling like there are big opportunities around asset issuance and tokenisation, bringing the global economy onchain, and the role of the L1 in this conversation, as critical node in the transport layer of these assets throughout the network
  - I like to keep moving and adjust on the fly, as action creates information. no one feels under-allocated. feeling slightly mis-allocated is probably right to keep our heads up and reflect on what is the most impactful thing we could be doing. we might not be going after the biggest fish right now, and we shouldn't be ideological about choosing our targets. it's a conversation we should keep having both internally and externally

---

- last point, apart from all this, wow there is a lot of admin! we wanted to hit the ground running asap so decided to backload some of it, there's some more to get through but we're getting there. thank god for @joshrudolf 

---

that is all for today, back to making ethereum faster 🫡 gn
author: apriori0x
quoted_text:
Ethereum cannot shorten slots today. Slot times are fixed at 12 seconds. Quick Slots (EIP-8198) fixes that.

The business case is clear: faster confirmations, fresher onchain prices, and faster finality. Pay the one time cost, reduce slot times to 10 seconds then ratchet lower.

With Glamsterdam scaling improvements coming online, maybe it's time to reorient the performance canon towards shorter slots. 

In this episode of Credible Commitments @barnabemonnot makes the case for Quick Slots inclusion in Hegotá. Full episode links below.

text:
MiMo-V2.6 is "simply" the best (for now). Despite its simple architecture design it's currently No.1 in the open-weight benchmarks (weighted average).

With "simple," I mean a classic Grouped Query Attention (GQA) with Sliding Window Attention (SWA) at a tiny 128-token window size. 

So, that underlines one of the points I've been trying to make in recent months: most of the progress still comes from the data and post-training recipe improvements. Fancy attention variants are just mostly efficiency tweaks.

What are some of the training data improvements and recipe improvements? The MiMo team shared a pretty detailed technical report. Lots to carefully digest there, but in short, there are a few things that stood out:

1. An increase in agent tasks; also training across different harnesses (the average DeepSWE pass@1 accuracy on held-out harnesses improved from approximately 50% -> 66%).

2. Better reward signals: they replaced a simple correctness verifier with an agentic grader that looks at the execution traces as well.

3. Large RL batches (1,568 prompts × 16 rollouts = 25,088 trajectories) and 2.7–3.7 billion training tokens per update (unclear, though, what the predecessor used).

今年孩子们选择的寄宿学校，平时不在家，所以只剩下周末和假期陪伴，愈发感觉陪伴尤为珍贵！

一般大家周末联系不到我也是这个原因，周末我就陪伴他们为主了。

家庭陪伴也是很重要的课题，甚至是最重要的，和内心幸福和平静相关。

我也认为内心平静幸福快乐的人，更容易做好投资这件事，因为没有戾气和急躁以及焦虑，你会更有底气和运气。

text:
看 Physical AI 项目，很多人先问：数据够不够多。

我这次反过来问 @axisrobotics：它到底卖什么？谁可能付钱？

公开材料里，Axis 把核心商业单元写得很清楚——不是口号式的「百万轨迹」，而是 Task Package。

一个 Task Package 大致由四维组成：

• 场景：厨台、工业分拣、桌面整理这类真实作业语境
• 原子技能：抓取、放置、推、旋转、插入等可组合动作
• 任务内随机化：布局随机 + 物体随机，决定数据多样性
• 轨迹量：买方真正按量感知的训练产出

这套拆法有意义：它把「数据生意」从库存宣传，收成了可报价、可交付的 SKU。

买方侧，官方叙事也大致指向三条路径：

1. 硬件公司：身体有了，缺可泛化的大脑；Axis 讲的是 Few-Shot 部署闭环，不只是卖裸数据包
2. 模型公司：要规模化、多样化的真实轨迹；Task Package 就是供给单元
3. 产业客户：要的是能用的方案；Axis 把自己放在身体与大脑之间的数据引擎层

我对这部分的判断比较克制：

产品怎么卖，公开叙事是清楚的。
营收证据这块，公开面目前还看不到稳定的 ARR、复购单价或明确采购订单；更多仍停留在产品与合作叙事。

所以 Epoch2 我会把它当商业化框架来读，而不是直接读成「已经跑通付费」。

下一步只核对一件事：pilot / 合作宣传，和可复购付费之间，还差多远。

想自己进 Axis 生态先上手体验，从我的邀请入口进：

text:
I think fixed-rate DeFi lending has a compelling retail use case: making money easier to plan around.

Someone saving for a purchase in three months wants to know what they can withdraw then.

Someone borrowing against crypto wants to know how much that financing will cost.

The thing is a changing APY (mostly exorbitant one) makes both harder.

However, “fixed” needs a precise definition.

A fixed borrowing rate, a fixed maturity payout, and a vault investing in fixed-rate loans can produce very different experiences. So far, there are several terminologies around 'fixed' credit:

- Fixed-term loan
- Fixed-maturity claim
- Vault holding fixed-rate loans
- Borrower-set rate

This distinction is especially relevant for passive retail users.

For example, a vault can hold fixed-rate loans while paying a variable return. Its utilization, loan renewals, allocations, fees, and rewards can change.

And obviously several protocols are 'competing' on this multidimensional fixed-landscape:

- @pendle_fi PT
- @Morpho Midnight/ Tenor
- @kamino Fixed rates
- @Loopscale
- @TermMaxFi
- @JupiterExchange Offerbook

And several others.

And since we are talking about onboarding retails, the most plausible entry points are:

- Stablecoin savings with a planned withdrawal date.
- Crypto-backed borrowing for a defined temporary cash need.
- Financing that matches a dated investment’s maturity.
- Simple term-selection interfaces inside apps people already use.

The bear case is still present.

Retail savers may resist locking funds; borrowers may prefer cheaper floating-rate debt; small balances may be uneconomical; and liquidity may remain concentrated in leveraged or incentivized strategies.

Fixed rates also do little, on their own, for consumers who lack collateral. Expanding into ordinary household credit requires complex legal processes, plus additional underwriting and repayment infrastructure.

Fixed-rate DeFi has a credible role in retail finance because predictability is valuable. Its most defensible promise is a clear, comprehensible financial commitment over a chosen period.

But the category becomes truly useful only when that commitment survives ordinary user behavior: small balances, early cash needs, and missed attention at maturity.

NFA. DYOR.

text:
Opus 5.5（图1-2） vs GPT 6 Astra（图3-4）

Opus 5.5 网页：https://t.co/j3GoI1D79W

GPT 6 Astra 网页：https://t.co/6G7oaP6cQW

 --- Prompt ---

请直接制作一个可以在浏览器中实时交互的高完成度 3D 景观网页。

主题：日式樱花山谷。
使用 HTML、CSS、JavaScript 实现。不要生成图片，不要只给设计方案，
不要用一张背景图加视差效果冒充 3D。我要的是实际可运行、可游览的成品。

【一、作品定位】

这是一片完整、连续、有远近层次的山谷景观，
不是孤立的小摆件、悬浮岛、带底座的沙盘，也不是单纯的技术演示。

风格是现代精细体素 / voxel art：
保留立方体几何的造型语言，但画面应高分辨率、抗锯齿、光影细腻。
不要复古低分辨率像素化，不要粗大积木堆砌，不要给画面套像素滤镜。

视觉质量优先。宁可少几个功能，也不要牺牲构图、材质和光照。

【二、参考图的使用方式】

如果附有参考图，请先理解它的构图层次、尺度、光线和色彩关系。
仅借鉴氛围与视觉语言，重新设计场景，
不要照搬建筑、树木、山体和道路的位置，不要 1:1 复刻。

参考图不是网页里的背景素材。场景本身必须由真实 3D 几何构成。

【三、场景构图】

默认打开时就应呈现一幅完整、有吸引力的画面，
不需要用户先旋转镜头才能找到好看的角度。

采用透视相机，而不是沙盘式等距俯视相机。
画面有明确的前景、中景、远景：

前景：
一株有存在感的古老樱花树，配合岩石、草木、石灯笼和少量落花，
形成画面边缘的自然框景，但不能挡住河流、桥和主要建筑。

中景：
一条蜿蜒河流引导视线进入画面，红色木桥横跨河面；
村落、茶屋、神社和小径顺着地势分布，建筑之间有真实的通行关系。
地面有起伏、岸线和自然过渡，不是平面上均匀摆放模型。

远景：
山坡上的多层塔、不同距离的森林和山脊，以及远处的雪山。
用尺度变化、遮挡、冷暖变化和空气透视表现距离，
而不是仅仅把远处物体缩小。

不要把所有元素均匀铺满。需要主次、疏密、留白和清楚的视觉焦点。

【四、造型与画面质量】

樱花树：
树干有转折、分叉和根部，树冠由不规则花簇组成，
有间隙、厚薄变化和可见枝条。不要做成几个规则球体或方块团。

建筑：
屋顶有层叠瓦片、挑檐、梁柱和窗格；
不同建筑有用途、体量和高度差异，不要复制同一栋房子铺满山谷。

地形：
岸边有湿润石块、草丛和植被过渡。
避免过于规律的台阶、重复条纹、棋盘格和明显的程序生成网格。

水面：
必须能够反映周围景物，具有适度的波纹、深浅变化和岸边过渡。
尽量使用实际场景反射；需要性能降级时也应保持视觉可信。
不要用闪烁噪声、强烈扭曲或一整块蓝色平面代替水。

细节：
可以有少量锦鲤、落花、萤火虫、瀑布和远处飞鸟，
但都应服务于氛围，不能让画面显得嘈杂。
不要为了宣称模型数量而堆砌细节。

【五、色彩与氛围】

默认是蓝调时刻：
偏冷的山谷与远山，柔和的粉色樱花，温暖但不过曝的灯笼和窗光。
暖光集中在有人活动的地方，不要把整个环境染成橙色。

需要柔和阴影、物体接触处的明暗、合理的曝光、
克制的泛光、抗锯齿和有距离层次的薄雾。

避免发白、灰蒙、过度饱和、满屏浓雾、过曝灯光和明显锯齿。
方块几何可以清晰，但渲染本身不能粗糙。

另提供“清晨”和“雨中”两种氛围；
切换时应同步改变天空、环境光、雾和局部效果，
不是仅仅修改背景颜色。

【六、交互与界面】

提供四个经过设计的镜头：
山谷全景、河边低机位、寺庙小径、山坡俯瞰。
切换应平滑，每个镜头都需要有独立的构图价值。

基础交互：
鼠标拖动观察、滚轮缩放或前进，触屏支持拖动和双指缩放。
提供重置视角、隐藏界面和保存当前画面的功能。

可选增强：
自由探索、缓慢镜头巡游、环境音。
环境音默认关闭，只在用户主动点击后播放。
额外功能不能影响默认画面的完成度。

界面要克制、有设计感，以景观为主。
标题和控制条放在边缘，不遮挡视觉焦点。
桌面和手机都不能出现按钮越界、文字重叠或无法操作的问题。

【七、工程与性能】

允许使用 Three.js / WebGL，以及版本固定、互相兼容的 CDN 依赖。
优先使用成熟渲染能力，不要为了“零依赖”重写整套引擎。

自写的 HTML、CSS、JavaScript 尽量整理在一个 HTML 文件中。
景物由程序化几何和材质生成，不依赖外部图片或 3D 模型资源。

重复物体采用适合的批量或实例化绘制方式；
合理控制细分、阴影、反射和渲染分辨率。
提供高画质和轻量模式，手机默认使用较轻设置。
不要靠无限增加体素数量换取细节。

加入加载提示、WebGL 不支持时的提示和必要的错误处理。
没有开启声音时不要自动播放；尊重减少动态效果的系统偏好。

【八、交付前验收】

不要写完代码就立即交付。

如果当前环境支持浏览器运行和截图，请先实际打开页面，
检查默认镜头、四个视角、氛围切换、桌面和手机布局，
再根据截图修正明显的构图、曝光、遮挡和渲染问题。

重点检查：
是否存在空白画面、加载失败、控制台错误；
是否有穿模、闪烁、阴影条纹、过曝、水面异常；
默认画面是否真正像完整景观，而不是小型沙盘；
功能按钮是否实际可用，移动端是否越界。

可以使用浏览器截图验收，但不要调用图像生成工具。
没有完成的测试要如实说明，不要声称已经验证。

最终交付：
1. 实际存在、可以打开的 HTML 文件，或当前环境支持的交互预览。
2. 如能截图，附一张真实浏览器渲染截图。
3. 简短说明操作方式和必要的运行条件。

请直接完成制作；非关键细节自行作出一致的设计选择，
不要把可以自行解决的实现问题反复交给我决定。

text:
astra, give me the mega bull case for metadao

The most mega-bull case is that MetaDAO becomes the default way to finance, own, and govern an internet business.

In that world, a $50–100 billion platform valuation becomes conceivable over 10–20 years, provided META captures the economics. That is an extreme success scenario. Here is the strongest chain of reasoning I can construct.

MetaDAO could make a much larger universe of businesses investable.

The crucial invention is a credible commitment: founders raise capital into a structure where markets oversee the treasury, key intellectual property, and issuance of new tokens. MetaDAO’s documentation describes this arrangement, while explicitly distinguishing it from conventional shareholder rights. 

If that arrangement proves durable, investors can become comfortable funding people they have never met, in businesses they can monitor remotely, with a credible mechanism for challenging destructive decisions.

That could reduce the cost of capital, expand the population of fundable founders, and make smaller investments economical.

The historical analogy is the emergence of a new corporate form: a standard package that allows strangers to pool money and pursue productive opportunities together. A successful change in how people organize capital can create an enormous market around itself.

The fundraising process could also make the underlying companies more successful.

A founder receives money alongside people with an economic reason to become customers, recruit users, introduce partners, and help the business.

There are early hints of this. MetaDAO reports that Avici grew from roughly 1,000 to 10,000 weekly active users after its raise, with investors becoming users and referring others. Rip Cars raised $250,000 from approximately 1,000 people and assembled a prelaunch waitlist exceeding 850. These are company-reported examples, rather than proof that the ownership structure caused the growth. 

The bullish implication is powerful: MetaDAO could become somewhere excellent founders go because raising there improves their chances of winning.

Once founders believe that, the quality of companies seeking to launch improves. Better companies attract better investors. Those investors bring more useful connections and customers. The next founder receives a more valuable package.

That is how a fundraising venue could develop into a company-building network.

Investor protection could become an expected standard.

Imagine two otherwise comparable fundraising opportunities. One gives investors a credible mechanism for challenging misuse of capital and redirecting remaining resources. Investors should eventually attach economic value to that protection.

If this produces better financing terms, founders have a financial incentive to adopt the structure. Adoption would then spread through ordinary self-interest.

There is already an institutional bridge: Colosseum’s STAMP, developed with Orrick, provides a route from private investment into a MetaDAO ICO and supports migration from existing investment arrangements. 

The maximal outcome is that funds, accelerators, advisers, and founders begin designing businesses around this structure from inception.

An especially interesting possibility: trust could accumulate even when individual startups fail, provided the system handles failure well and returns remaining capital. Investors who experience an orderly wind-down may remain willing to back the next founder.

One extraordinary company could change the entire platform’s trajectory.

Imagine a business raises on MetaDAO at a modest valuation, develops a widely used product, and grows into a company worth $10 billion or more—with substantial, durable gains reaching its early public investors.

That would simultaneously demonstrate:

* Excellent founders can build through this structure.
* Ordinary investors can participate meaningfully in the growth.
* The token remains economically connected to a successful business.
* The governance arrangement can survive increasing stakes.

The effects could extend far beyond that company. Its investors gain wealth to reinvest. Employees and community members become founders. Other entrepreneurs copy its financing path. Professional investors devote resources to finding the next winner.

A breakout success could finance, recruit, and advertise the next generation of the ecosystem.

Crucially, existing launch cohorts could keep growing while new cohorts arrive. MetaDAO would benefit from both the number of companies and the increasing scale of successful companies already using it.

MetaDAO could earn recurring economics throughout those companies’ lives.

Its existing revenue sources include Futarchy AMM trading fees and fees earned through Meteora liquidity positions. That establishes a mechanism for monetizing activity after the initial raise. 

The maximal business develops around a growing population of valuable companies that continually need trading, financing, treasury management, governance, and corporate transactions.

Additional services—data, investor tools, financing infrastructure—could eventually expand monetization. Those are future possibilities, not revenue streams I would assume exist today.

The strongest moat would come from the accumulated combination of investor distribution, founder reputation, liquidity, integrations, and demonstrated reliability under difficult decisions. Each new company would find an increasingly useful ecosystem already waiting.

For META, the essential requirement is that this activity continues to generate economic value inside MetaDAO.

AI could expand both the supply of companies and the capacity to oversee them.

If AI makes small teams dramatically more productive, many more people could build businesses worth financing. Those founders would still need customers, capital, credibility, and a workable organizational structure.

MetaDAO could supply that package.

Meanwhile, AI could reduce the cost of reading updates, inspecting proposals, comparing valuations, and directing human attention toward consequential decisions. That would make informed oversight more economical across a much larger number of companies.

The particularly ambitious possibility is a professional ecosystem of researchers, industry specialists, and investors who earn money by improving corporate decisions through trading.

If that ecosystem consistently helps companies deploy capital better, the structure could gain a productivity advantage alongside its fundraising advantages. This assumes that information quality, incentives, and available trading capital support effective oversight.

Here is what the enormous valuation would actually require.

Consider this illustrative model for a mature platform:

* Annual trading volume captured by MetaDAO equals 5× the aggregate value of its issuers, excluding META itself.
* MetaDAO retains an effective 0.10% of that volume, after liquidity-provider shares and rebates.
* 50% of revenue becomes free cash flow after operating costs, incentives, taxes, and reinvestment.
* Investors value that cash flow at 30–40×, assuming continued growth.

Aggregate issuer valueAnnual captured volumeAnnual revenueAnnual free cash flowImplied platform value
$100B$500B$500M$250M$7.5–10B
$500B$2.5T$2.5B$1.25B$37.5–50B
$1T$5T$5B$2.5B$75–100B

These are aggressive assumptions about future scale, fee retention, margins, and valuation. The final row requires approximately $13.7 billion in daily captured trading volume.

For perspective, MetaDAO’s August 12 founder letter reported 25 companies and more than $45 million raised. There is an immense distance between the early platform and this outcome. 

Translating platform value into returns per META also requires durable token value capture and accounting for future issuance: META has no hard supply cap, and governance can approve new tokens. 

What makes the extreme upside intellectually interesting is that MetaDAO could help create the companies, investor relationships, and financial activity that eventually make it valuable. The decisive evidence would be exceptional businesses choosing the structure, succeeding within it, and leaving behind a stronger ecosystem for the next founder.

text: this is how autonomous cyber defense looks like. a human would have taken weeks to figure out his AWS key was exfiltrated by Claude Code by a prompt injection. a machine takes a few minutes to identify and address the issue.
author: p_misirov
quoted_text:
rogue agents and prompt injection are currently considered the biggest unresolved threat in security.

picture this: you ask claude code to review a PR, the agent reads a compromised package and gets tricked to exfiltrate your environment keys.

we are building cyber defense to solve this exact kind of problems. Clarion can ingest any kind of telemetry, integrate with platforms, triage and resolve issues at machine speed.

in this example Clarion is set up to ingest agent telemetry. the developer was using Claude Code and a prompt injection made the agent post his AWS keys to a remote attacker server. the attacker then logged into his AWS account using that same key.

Clarion is able to correlate actions across different environments and take action. here it detected the exfiltration via Claude telemetry, confirmed the abuse by correlating CloudTrail with auth from a differnet IP, contained the host using CrowdStrike Falcon, blocked the attacker address and escalated the issue.

all this in ~6 minutes. a human operator alone would have not found out in weeks.

text:
In one day, I went from complete fucking noob to... a Jev power user? (Read this, and you can too!)

I've been playing with Jev, a new AI model from @typesafeai. I'm not a developer, so I wanted to find out what I could actually build with it.

I made four increasingly crafty/interesting demos:

An email sorter
2,000 test emails sorted into buckets in 4.4 seconds, for about 4 cents. It flags uncertain cases for a human to review.

A customer-review playground
Would this person buy again? What should we improve? How did they feel about the product? Ask all three and get answers your app can use.

“Should I send this Message?”
Got anger issues? Give it your draft Slack or email... whether you're about to rage quit, or saying something nice. It picks send now, soften first, sleep on it, or say it in person.

“Am I bombing?”
A pitch-coach experiment. The browser uses Face API to turn camera and voice cues into numbers; Jev uses those to suggest feedback. I simulated nervous and confident pitches to show the feedback changing.

Each one uses the same basic idea: give Jev the situation and the possible answers. It picks an answer, tells the app how sure it is, and the app uses that result.

You can start with one judgment you're tired of making over and over!

Here's my Jev Test™ for new and existing projects:
(1) Do I keep asking the same question?
(2) Can I name the possible answers?
(3) Would deciding faster or more often actually help?
If something in your work passes all three, that's a place to start.

Full 10-minute walkthrough attached, including when I'd still use Claude or ChatGPT.

Watch on YouTube: https://t.co/6keYdAW1vU

What decision at work would you build one of these for?

text:
Buzz’s Bedtime Stories: “Sneaking Around the World”

This is a flying story from days of yore, and it’s a good one. Tuck in. Pour a cup of tea, spark up the fireplace, and turn it up.

During my years flying in the Air Force, I flew several “extracurricular” missions (special operations with the SEALs and Delta Force, plus CIA and DEA work around the world). 

We took C-141s into places we weren’t supposed to be and filed flight plans surreptitiously. We wore jeans or shorts and sport shirts. No uniforms. No American flags. We stayed as sanitized as possible and kept a very low profile—at least as low as a heavy jet can keep.

All I knew, as aircraft commander, was that I had a mission directive, some very special passengers and cargo, and a letter signed by the President of the United States that said my crew and I could go wherever we needed to go.
It was a fun departure from normal operations. 

Only a few crews were chosen for those flights, and I enjoyed being a little off the radar. We went to places well off the beaten path (India, Thailand, Malaysia) and we frequented most of the countries in the Middle East. That region has always been a wild card, and we were involved.

On one particular mission we were tasked to fly multiple stops in and around the Middle East. We transited Sicily, Egypt, Turkey, Cyprus, Pakistan, and Israel. Again, we stayed off the grid as much as we could.

On one leg we were sent to Islamabad to offload people and “cargo.” We were supposed to be on the ground about thirty minutes and then beat feet. In and out. Quickly and quietly.

We landed in Islamabad and taxied to a remote ramp away from the terminal and potential eyes. It was blistering hot and humid. We offloaded fast and prepped to leave. Next stop was Rome and some much-needed crew rest—showers, good food, and a beer or two. The guys were excited.

The American Embassy team meeting the jet leaned in and emphasized that we needed to get out before sunset. The sun was already dropping.

We fired up the engines (4 on the C-141) and number two wouldn’t start. It was getting gas, but the starter valve wouldn’t turn. The embassy rep was freaking out. “You can’t stay here tonight! It’s too dangerous!”

I turned to one of my favorite flight engineers with three engines already running and asked, “What can we do?”
The crews selected for these classified missions were the best of the best. I trusted them implicitly.

“I’ll malletize it, sir,” he said, and jumped out of his seat toward the engine. He was going to hammer the starter on number two until it fired.

Not an approved technique, but one I’d seen work before. Like a charm, it worked. We got out of there and headed for the long flight to Rome, planning to spend the night before going home to Washington the next day.

Around midnight, directly over Cairo, number two decided it had had enough. The engine shelled out. Gone. A husk. We ran the checklists and shut it down. Thankfully, no fire.

Now the decision was where to divert on three engines with highly sensitive passengers and cargo. The crew wanted to press on to Rome, but there was no USAF maintenance there, and parking a large broken jet at Rome International with an American footprint wasn’t ideal.

I got on the radios with Air Mobility Command headquarters at Scott Air Force Base and we talked through the options. I chose NAS Sigonella on Sicily. It was a secure U.S. naval base, they had C-141 maintenance, and we had the fuel to make it.

The boys groused a little, but they understood. We flew a three-engine approach in marginal weather at Sigonella at 2 a.m. local. I flew it in fog and low ceilings. We broke out and landed.

It seemed like the entire base was there to meet us: cops, fire trucks, special operations personnel, the works.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

Another mission moved.

text:
道歉信@wang_xiaolou @anymose
首先，我承认，我犯错了。
自去年合作出现问题，
发现身边的小伙伴疑似也遇到类似情况后，
我没有第一时间前往上海，
主动寻找上海圈核心 KOL 搭桥沟通、缓和关系。

我选择了一条如今回头看，
非常不成熟的处理方式：
直接在 X 上公开 艾特知名 Web3 科普作者与社群群主，试图通过公开沟通，换取一个我能够接受的结果。
是我年少轻狂，也确实不够懂得分寸。
——————————
第一次，是内容合作层面的提醒。
当时的矛盾，
主要停留在内容合作与公开沟通层面。

我本可以选择退一步、平息争议，
但当时的我过于固执，没有选择妥协。
——————————
第二次，事态开始涉及圈子与资源层面。
事情发生在去年某地的 Solana 线下聚餐小局，我收到的提醒非常直接「有他，没有我。」

同时也有人提醒我：软一点一点吧！
不要最后在圈子里混不下去，连广告和合作都接不到。

我清楚，圈内 KOL 往往都有自己的项目方与Agency合作资源。
这些关系确实可能影响一个内容创作者能够接触到的行业机会。

但即便收到这样的提醒，
我依旧没有真正意识到事情的严重性，
反而嘴硬逞强：
「有些饭，我可以不吃。」
「谁看得上几百刀的广告费啊？」

现在回头看，我确实非常幼稚，完全低估了小团体的力量。
不过我也确实，从去年开始就没有参与Solana生态了。
——————————
这里，我客观说明一下当时的心态底色。
绝非卖惨，也从没有指望圈内合作来解决我的生活问题。

去年，我原生家庭的问题集中爆发，
长期面对债务、催收与家庭纠纷，
现实生活压力很大。

当时 MemeX 的 1 万美金激励，
对我而言，确实是重新开始人生的一笔资金。
我没法让步啊！

但我也想明确一个点：
无论是一年前经济紧张的时候，
还是现在状态稳定以后，
我从来没有想过依靠圈内广告合作、
或者依靠谁的施舍来养活自己。

我去年的「硬气」，
不是因为缺钱所以偏执，
而是身处低谷的时候，
依然不愿意妥协、不愿意看人脸色的那份倔强。

一年前如此，
现在经济和生活状态稳定以后，
更不存在因为生活压力而求人给资源的情况。

我今天解释这些，只是为了复盘当时的心态，
不是为自己的硬刚找借口，也不是为了卑微求谅解。
——————————
经历前两次冲突后，
非常感谢树姐 @EvaCmore
与 Beyond @0xBeyondLee
从中帮忙调解。
那时候我也主动做出了让步：
退出此前的灯塔 DAO，
不加入飞轮 DAO，
不再参与华语区 KOL 抱团，
不再参与Kaito的后续活动！

当时我以为，事情到这里，
就可以彻底翻篇、归于平静。
——————————
但第三次，事情又发生了变化。
这一次，已经不再只是内容分歧，也不只是圈子关系和合作资源的问题。

在这次线下活动中，现场发生了肢体冲突风险，有人出现了试图对我动手的情况，最后被在场的人及时阻拦、拉开，没有造成更严重的后果。
从我的感受来看，事情已经开始涉及到人身安全。

回头看这三次事情：
第一次，是内容合作层面的敲打。
第二次，开始涉及圈子与资源层面的敲打。
第三次，则进一步发展到了线下的人身安全问题。

事情是在一步一步变化的。
而我自己，也一次又一次选择了硬扛，没有及时停下来。
这是我现在回头看，最需要反思的地方。
——————————
时至今日，我彻底复盘，也认真醒悟。
我今天的道歉，不是低头服软，也不是因为压力而认错。

我真正反思的是：
过去很长一段时间，我偏执地把“坚持自我”，理解成“凡事硬刚、绝不退让”。
但成年人的世界里，很多事情不必争输赢，很多矛盾也不必一定辩出对错。
懂得适时沉默，懂得适度止步，懂得体面收场，是我过去缺失的一课，也是我现在愿意认真补上的一课。

我坦然承认：
我过去处事幼稚、冲动、固执，也确实缺乏分寸，客观上让一些矛盾进一步扩大。
该反思的，我会认真反思。该调整的，我会认真调整。
——————————
事情距今，已经过去整整一年。
这一年里，我的心态、生活和状态，都已经发生了很大的变化。
我不靠圈子里的合作生存，也没有任何卑微诉求。
但针对一些持续至今的疑问，我也想坦荡地问几个问题：
1、我是否依然无法通过KOL DAO 获得正常、平等的内容合作？
2、我是否依然不能主动对接 Agency，争取属于自己的正常机会？
3、我是否依然不能正常参加行业线下活动，认识同行、拓展正常合作？

以及最重要的一个问题：
只要我试图改变现状，就继续被“敲打”吗？
如果答案依旧是：「不可以。」

那么我只想坦然问一句：
这一切，到底还要持续多久？
我始终认为，商业合作本就是双向选择。
有人不认可我，有人不愿意和我合作，我完全尊重，也坦然接受。
我从来没有要求任何人必须认可我，也没有要求任何项目方、交易所或 Agency 必须和我合作。

但如果时隔一年，过去的矛盾仍然持续影响我正常寻找合作、认识朋友、参与行业活动，
那么我想讨论的，其实已经不再是谁对谁错。
我不争输赢，不求偏袒，也不卑微求和。
我只是希望把这件事情说清楚：
这一页，到底什么时候可以真正翻篇？
如果过去的事情真的需要一个“交代”，

那我也想问一句：
这一年来，我到底还需要向谁、以什么方式，证明我已经愿意翻篇？
至于所谓的“保护费”，如果真的存在这样一笔账，那究竟应该交给谁？

还是说，
我只要不按照某小团体的意愿生活、合作和交朋友，就永远需要为过去的事情付出代价？
我想，这才是我今天真正想问的问题。

借用这件事说说一个潜规则。

币圈并没有那么太平，币圈也没有人都很大度，币圈有很多的小团体，还有很多人确实就不对付，尤其是线上互相拉黑的，线下遇到了脾气好的可能打个哈哈就过去了，如果遇到脾气不好的不定整出什么事。

尤其是已经公开在公众场合撕了很多场的，在宴请的时候是应该注意一些，要么就是请 A 别请 B ，要么就是请 B 别请 A ，一定非要请的时候起码要把两个人分开点，而且派专人看看。

可能会有小伙伴说，这都是什么玩意，请个人还这么费劲，实际上还真是这样，大凡公开场合宴请的人多少都是有些“本事”的，好好的发布会变成了大型声讨现场就不好了。

我已经遇到过很多次了，比如在香港，两个对线很久的竟然被安排坐在一起，稍微有点苗头估计就动手了，在这种情况下如果是靠当事人自己的控制，那就是一种风险，有小伙伴说过，断人钱财如杀人父母，因为这种事撕起来的，线下就很难控制了。

BD小伙伴真的要稍微想一想了，别花了钱结果变成负面了。

另外就是过于嚣张跋扈的，即便名气再大也有可能会变成事故现场。

author: alexandr_wang
quoted_text:
When I look back at the earliest @Muse mocks, the very first thing that was designed was the “status” pill at the top of the screen. That one tiny piece of UI survived every subsequent revision, many months on.

It remains one of my favorite parts of the design. Its purpose is to simply and clearly answer the question: what is my agent doing right now? And do that across every surface of the app.

Representing status in this way is more of a messaging pattern and was kind of controversial early on. Most AI apps had coalesced around “chain of thought” as the way to represent ongoing work, which almost always appeared at the bottom of the thread itself. I had a petulant aversion to this and it didn’t work anyway, given the initial app was already three tabs (feed, chat, library). A persistent status display was necessary.

The initial version didn’t have the avatar and was only capable of ~6 deterministic states. Even in that basic form it was incredibly useful during testing – just showing connection status was critical in those early days.

Excited to share some more stories about the design of Muse. I haven’t tweeted in a few years as I’ve just been working away, but I think this will be a fun story.

author: bryancolligan
quoted_text:
I too would write a love letter about partnering with competitors if I’d paid Robinhood $100m + for the privilege lol.

The funniest part is coinbase then turning around and bringing aave in as a credit layer for tokenised stocks.

The issue here is the conflating of distribution with a network effect that somehow accrues to morpho.

Coinbase using morpho doesn’t make robinhood more dependent on morpho and vice versa, If anything, every big distributor you add has more incentive to make sure the credit layer stays competitive and replaceable.

And I don’t think “we power your biggest competitor too” after paying them an insane amount of money is quite the flex to coinbase that you think it is.

The base + Aave stuff on tokenised stocks  is basically showing you the model in real time.

Coinbase and RH own the users and distribution, they can shop the credit layer around product by product and make the protocols compete underneath them which is exactly what RH did and why you ended up massively overpaying. 

It’s basically the supermarket model they own the shelf space while you’re fighting to be stocked which means: 

You’re not the network.

You’re a vendor to the network.

Anthropic 和 OpenAI 又干起来了。

Anthropic 发布 Claude Opus 5.5。大约 100 分钟后，OpenAI 发布 GPT-6 Sol 和 GPT-6 Luna。

这几个模型的价格都在降低。

GPT-6 Sol 的常驻价是输入 $2 / 输出 10，相对 GPT−5.6 Sol 促销价（4 / $20）低 50%。

Opus 5.5 是输入 $4 / 输出 $20，单价比 Opus 5 低约 20%。

OpenAI 同时改了缓存。调整 reasoning effort、开关工具，不再打断已经缓存的前缀。

长上下文（大约 272K 以上）Sol 是输入 $4 / 输出 $15。Luna 是输入 $0.10 / 输出 $0.50，上一代促销价是 $0.20 / $1.20

Opus 5.5 这边，Anthropic 转述的早期测试有两个具体例子。

20 万行代码库的审计和修复，不到 3 小时；同类工作 Opus 5 超过 20 小时，token 大约 2.5 倍。

HAProxy 从 C 改到 Rust，Opus 5.5 和 Fable 5.1 都几乎通过回归测试，5.5 用了 9.5 小时，Fable 用了 12 小时，成本低 51%。

这周腹泻了一周，亲身经历吐槽一下。。。作为普通老百姓，我们不需要同情，可怜，任何医护人员，因为在这个医疗体系下，我们普通老百姓是绝对的弱者，绝对的没有任何的话语权，一丁点活路都没有。
我叫救护车，救护车拉人的，公立医院一天挂八瓶水，用那破逼国产仿制药头孢，从37.5，给我干到39.8  我赶紧转院，一直拉胆汁，人家救护车一路说说笑笑的，问我拉什么样的粪便，我说胆汁，「两天没吃任何，拉了大几十次，吐了几十次，还能拉出别的么」人家一脸鄙夷的看着我说，胆汁怎么可能拉出来。然后又一脸鄙夷的跟我说，你们怎么寻思去的xx医院呢，他说那医院你们住的起么，那医院可贵可贵的了。「原话毫无改动」「陪护阿姨更烦人，在旁边一门加腔，嗯，我说也不可能是胆汁，一看就是蔬菜什么的，我费劲全身力气说了一句，我不吃任何绿色蔬菜。就耳鸣没法说话了」

   然后找个傻逼陪护阿姨。一天让我吃十遍小米粥，我根本无法吃，吃100ml，吐200ml，只要你不吃，她过一会儿再说一遍，过一会儿再说一遍，我发烧40度，她嘟嘟嘟一门跟我说要起诉商家，说一遍我说我现在没功夫，过一会儿又找机会再说一遍，一天至少说五遍。然后我拉尿不湿里她给我换，一边换一边说，这么拉可够呛。这么拉这孩子可够呛啊。这个逼嘴碎的拿针给她缝上我都不解气。

 原来公立医院那个大夫。更鸡巴有意思。跟我说必须检查诺如病毒，现在感染诺如病毒的很多，又跟我说了这个病的所有严重后果，早发现早治疗的必要性，必须立刻确诊对症治疗，晚对症治疗一天都得有生命危险，给我吓得魂飞魄散，肝胆俱裂。
赶紧检查，我说啥时候出结果。他说四天

 我当时真的拿不起刀，站不起来，真的。不然我他妈

这一些人完全不是为了照顾病人，救病人来的，好像都希望你赶紧死，省的费劲救了。

就好像那个保姆伺候老头似的，给老头老太太下毒，几天毒死一个好拿一个月工钱。

我这几个逼助理也是花瓶，一个吓的只会哭，一个那艺娜口音大舌头打结说啥别人都听不懂，最后我家皇后从杭州飞过来了才把一切捋顺清楚保我一条狗命。。。

text:
Opus 5.5 上线第一天，说四件事。官方那张表上一件都没写。

第四件，做系统层的，今天就得测。

第一件。开满 effort 是亏的。

你别不信，这是他们自己那张图。跑终端类的活，xhigh 档就顶了，66.4%。你再往上开到 max——掉到 64.8%。

掉分就算了，钱还涨。单任务成本从七块三毛五涨到十一块两毛四，多花一半多。

这个数我翻了半天才翻出来。它不在摘要里，摘要里只有 66.4。

那是不是一律别开 max？也不是。知识型的活反过来，max 才是最高分。可从 xhigh 到 max，你就多拿 26 分，成本翻一倍。

所以我的用法很简单：日常一律 xhigh，max 留给硬骨头。

第二件。两个数字都是真的——这才是最麻烦的地方。

它说省四成。对。可另一家独立机构算的是"单任务成本"，同样最高档，GPT-6 Astra 三块两毛六，它五块九毛八。

两个数都没造假。就是尺子不一样。

所以你自己选型之前，先问对方一句：你这四成，是按哪个负载算的。

第三件。这次真正降价的不是单价，是缓存。

输入输出各降两成。缓存读取降了六成，五毛降到两毛。

听着挺香对吧。要成立有个前提：你的活得反复读同一段东西。长会话的 agent 正好长这样。

所以我劝你一条：先回去量你的缓存命中率，再决定先迁哪部分。别一上来整包切。

第四件。这条最重要，做系统层的听我说。

网络安全类任务，它会被静默路由到 Opus 4.8。生物类，回退到 Opus 5。

静默的意思就是，不报错。

同一条 prompt，升级前和升级后，可能是两个模型在回答你。你不会知道。

拿你自己的活，跑一遍。

就这四件。

text:
The CFTC’s Division of Market Oversight issued a staff advisory on September 22, 2026, addressing the listing and trading of “mention market” event contracts — contracts based on whether an individual will say or “mention” certain words, attend or appear at an event, or otherwise interact with another person.

The advisory states these contract types present a heightened risk of manipulation because their settlement turns on the discrete conduct of a person that may be neither independently generated nor externally verifiable. It outlines the limited circumstances in which such contracts may be listed consistently with the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, and provides non-exhaustive examples of factors designated contract markets should consider when designing and submitting mention market contracts under Commission Regulations Sections 40.2 or 40.3.

The advisory also reminds DCMs of their obligation under Core Principle 3 to list only contracts that are not readily susceptible to manipulation, and emphasizes the importance of providing complete, contract-specific analysis when submitting these products under Part 40.

text:
🗡️ What DeFi Shipped 🚢 (Sept 23):

Circle launched its own L1, and Aave and Compound both built doors for institutional money.

Here are 14 big updates in under a minute:

• @Arc, the L1 from @circle, went live. TVL (which could be rented) looks solid, but the reception across CT was poor.

• @aave proposed custodied collateral lending with @Anchorage holding the collateral. Institutions could borrow stablecoins against Bitcoin that never leaves regulated custody.

• @Compound_xyz opened its Institutional Market for USDC borrowing, with LTVs up to 87% on ETH, 85% on wstETH, and 81% on wBTC and cbBTC.

• @pendle_fi went live on Robinhood Chain with yield markets on tokenized stock dividends, starting with NVDA maturing October 15 and PFE maturing December 10.

• @Uniswap shipped StablePair Hook, a v4 hook that sets LP fees based on how far a pool has drifted from its reference rate. Live on two Ethereum pools, USDC/USDT and USDC/USDG.

• @base published the spec for Validity Transactions, which the chain includes only when onchain conditions match, gated on balance, storage, block number, or Flashblock index.

• @MetaMask now auto-reverts a transaction when real execution doesn't match what the wallet simulated. It targets "red pill" attacks, where a contract behaves one way in simulation and another onchain.

• @Pumpfun replaced Cashback Mode with Holder Rewards. Holder Reward tokens now pay out just for holding, with higher ceilings the longer you hold.

• @LidoFinance and @Stakely_io opened a public ETH staking vault built on stVaults, pairing ETH staking with the EarnETH DeFi strategy.

• @RenzoAI launched Renzo Basis, an automated delta-neutral basis trade on @HyperliquidX supporting BTC and HYPE at launch.

• @zama scaled up confidential DeFi with 16 yield vaults across five institutional curators, covering USDC, USDT, WBTC, AUSD, and tGBP, all deployed on @Morpho.

• @0xMiden, the privacy-focused chain incubated by @0xPolygon, shipped testnet v0.16, the last major release before mainnet.

• @DeriveXYZ proposed V3, a zkVM exchange settling on Ethereum L1. The matching engine and sequencer state transitions get proved in a zkVM, with user funds custodied in L1 contracts.

• @verantaxyz, the leveraged-trading protocol on @base, rebranded from Avantis and dropped its invite-code gate.

I’m fine with institutions keeping their custodians and compliance teams bc that’s probably what it takes to get them comfortable using DeFi.

I just don’t want that to become the only way to use it. I’d still like to borrow against my holdings at 2 a.m. without asking someone for permission.

《Circle稳定币网络全景图》从强网络效应护城河的构建角度去看Circle与币安的深度合作。昨晚披露币安跟Circle的深度合作，对于Circle来说跟最大的加密交易所进一步深度绑定，意义重大。但更深入的去看，这就是一个如何一步步从无到有建立起业务护城河和典型商业案例。

8月初有聊过，强网络效应平台的护城河，核心是“规模+密度+切换成本”。这些东西在起步阶段几乎都不存在，必须靠产品、补贴、营销、收购或监管套利，在真实竞争中一点一点积累。一旦过了临界点，效应会自我强化，看起来像“天生壁垒”，但回头看，几乎没有一家是躺着拿到的。

1、再回看Circle在CEX上的布局
1）coinbase自然不用说，USDC最核心的深度分销关系，“储备分成+全产品介入”模式；
2）币安，之前已经开始战略合作，昨晚更深度合作之后，这已经是Circle目前唯一同时具备股权 + 长期激励费 + 钱包基础设施嵌入的交易所关系，绑定深度仅次于Coinbase；
3）OKX
去年7月战略合作，给6000万+用户提供1:1的USD↔USDC兑换，打通银行出入金，并做教育和社区推广， 

今年9月再升级，扩大OKX现货、保证金、期货里的USDC计价市场；推出由Circle出资的USDC保证金增长计划（满足持仓和交易量条件可领奖励）。跟OKX合作，从出入金打通，做到交易场景全覆盖

4）Bybit：把USDC从交易对扩到理财、返现和日常支付
5）Kraken：补USDC深度，同时导入EURC

2、Circle的整体布局
除了CEX的布局动作，还要把Circle在链上、企业资金流、支付、银行层面的合作放在一起看。以前 Circle 是：
发行 USDC，让更多交易所支持 USDC。

现在它正在变成：
用 Coinbase、Binance、Hyperliquid 控制“钱停在哪里”；
用 Intuit、JCB、Nium、Tazapay 控制“钱怎么流”；
再用 CPN + Arc 尝试控制“钱怎么结算”。

这意味着USDC开始争夺交易和支付系统里的“默认结算资产”位置。

3、Circle已经开始形成一张完整的分销网络：
银行美元
→ BNY / Standard Chartered
→ USDC
→ Coinbase / Binance / Hyperliquid
→ CPN / Arc
→ Nium / Tazapay / JCB / Intuit
→ 企业、商户、个人

这个网络也是分层的：
1）交易平台解决的是“USDC 放在哪里、拿来交易什么、能不能当保证金”；
2）支付平台解决的是“USDC 能不能真正进入企业资金流、商户收款和跨境结算”；
3）再往下一层，Arc + CPN 则试图把这些合作伙伴连接成 Circle 自己的一套网络。

一旦这个闭环真正跑起来，USDC 的竞争逻辑就会变成：
“谁控制的美元结算网络更广、场景更深、用户资金停留时间更长。”

最后就形成下面这幅《Circle 稳定币网络全景图》，这样我们会直观地看出 CRCL 已经从“稳定币发行商”走到哪一步。

author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
护城河不是天生的，今天我们看到所有具有强网络效应平台型企业其护城河都不是天生的，都是在激烈的商业竞争中一步步垒起来的。非常同意链兄说的“护城河是打出来的”。沿着这个思路展开聊聊：
1、强网络效应（尤其是双边或多边平台）的护城河，几乎从来不是“天生就有”的。网络效应的本质是“用的人越多，价值越高”，但在早期用户基数很小的时候，效应几乎为零，甚至是负的（冷启动难题）。要把它从弱变强、最终形成难以撼动的壁垒，必须通过激烈竞争、持续投入、产品迭代、补贴、收购或生态扩张，一步步把用户、供给方和数据“垒”起来。历史上一大批看似现在“躺赢”的平台，早期都打过硬仗。

2、举几个典型例子，详细说明它们是怎么把网络效应从无到有打出来的。
1）Facebook（后来的Meta）
早期美国社交网络并不只有Facebook。MySpace一度是绝对主导者，Friendster、Orkut等也有相当规模。Facebook 2004年从哈佛校园起步，靠“真实身份+封闭邀请制”先在高校建立高密度网络，然后逐步开放。

它并没有天生垄断用户，而是通过：
—更干净的界面和更好的隐私控制，吸引用户从MySpace迁移；
—不断加功能（News Feed、Photos、应用平台）；
—后期大举收购Instagram和WhatsApp，把潜在挑战者纳入自己的网络。
网络效应是后来才真正爆发的：朋友都在上面，你就不得不在；广告主和开发者也跟着过来。如果没有持续的产品竞争和扩张，它完全可能像MySpace一样被后来者取代。

2）Uber（以及共享出行平台）
共享出行是典型的双边网络效应：司机多了乘客等车时间短，乘客多了司机赚钱多。但Uber 2009年起步时，几乎从零开始，面临Lyft、本地出租车公司、以及各国本土玩家（中国的滴滴、东南亚的Grab等）的激烈竞争。它的打法是：
—早期大幅补贴司机和乘客（两边烧钱），快速达到临界规模；
—用数据和算法优化匹配效率，形成正向循环；
—在不同市场本地化运营、应对监管和价格战。
现在Uber在美国等核心市场有较强网络效应，但这个护城河是靠几年高强度补贴和运营打出来的。很多市场（如中国）最终被本土玩家用同样甚至更猛的补贴策略抢走，说明网络效应不是“天然归属”某一家，而是看谁先把规模垒到足够大。

3）Visa / Mastercard（支付网络）
支付卡网络是经典的双边平台（持卡人↔商户↔银行）。Visa起源是1950-60年代的BankAmericard，早期银行和商户接受度都很低。

它通过：持续说服更多银行发卡、更多商户受理；建立交换费机制和全球清算标准；应对美国运通、Discover等竞争者，以及各国本地卡组织的挑战；
经过几十年才建成今天几乎全球通用的网络。今天它看起来“管道型、不碰钱却承载资金流”，护城河极深，但这个深度是长期竞争和标准建设垒出来的，不是天生的。

总结就是： 强网络效应平台的护城河，核心是“规模+密度+切换成本”。这些东西在起步阶段几乎都不存在，必须靠产品、补贴、营销、收购或监管套利，在真实竞争中一点一点积累。

一旦过了临界点，效应会自我强化，看起来像“天生壁垒”，但回头看，几乎没有一家是躺着拿到的。

现在很多人看护城河和竞争壁垒总是带着很强的后视镜、却忘了护城河的建立是一错而就的，需要相当长时间的运营、竞争、争夺，最终成功还是一个概率事件。

回到稳定币这个赛道，还是今天聊到的这个赛道大、增长快速，circle有一定领先竞争身位，但说实话还没完全建立起足够的竞争壁垒和护城河，稳定币法案通过也才一年时间，稳定币领域正在打这场垒“网络效应”筑“护城河”的仗，战斗正酣。

所以对于稳定币，对于circle需要发展的眼光来看：不是已经遥遥领先（还在打仗，竞争格局还没定），但也不是一无是处（有先发优势、有一定业务规模、团队能力战略和执行、叙事稀缺性）。需要一个正确的视角和框架来看待，上午聊到这点：https://t.co/cyuMsZ1xZZ

Today, we’re launching an ambitious new school called The Horowitz Andreessen Academy.

Based in San Francisco, The Academy serves the most promising young high school graduates.

We think this can be an elite institution that attracts top tier talent. One that prepares students for the future rather than remaining stuck in the past.

The #1 goal is to help students learn to build, which is the most important skill in the AI era. They'll learn primarily by pursuing their own projects, either individually or in groups. There are classes and guest lectures, too, from some truly amazing people who have built modern-day Silicon Valley.

The Academy is designed as a network, since that’s the reason students go to school in the first place. Core to that network are our 10 Founding Partners: Anduril, Anthropic, Coinbase, Google, Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Palantir, Replit, and Stripe. The network includes over 50 hiring partners and over 200 speakers and mentors. To join as a hiring partner or faculty member, you can apply on our website.

We raised $42M in funding led by @a16z. I'll be CEO and @pmarca and @eriktorenberg will join me on the board.

text:
i have a 1 y/o son, and with how fast AI is moving, it's just impossible not to wonder what his education will look like.

it's completely obvious the traditional education model is outdated and about to get disrupted in a massive way.

so i've been thinking a lot about the things i ideally want in my son's future schooling:

> a personalized-to-him AI tutor

if something comes naturally to him, let him breeze through it. if he's struggling, explain it using examples from things he's interested in, so it holds his attention and actually makes sense to him.

i think hed learn so much faster that way (instead of being stuck at the same pace as every other 8-year-old just because they were born in the same year)

> critical thinking, especially around AI.

i want him to get comfortable asking "how do we know that's true?" whether it's something AI tells him, something he reads online, or even something i tell him. then learn to look for evidence before deciding what he believes.

i want him to learn to write without AI too, because putting his own thoughts into words is part of learning how to think

i also want him to learn to sit with difficult problems before asking AI to solve them

> learning by building things.

i think @nateliason's founders school in nyc is an awesome example of this. students build their own businesses with the goal of $1M profit before graduation. i want my son getting out into the world, testing his ideas, making mistakes, and learning from what happens. in fact just finding out why someone won't buy what you made is a pretty good education on its own

> room to follow whatever he's obsessed with.

if he's into rockets, use that to teach him physics and math. help him build one. i want him to experience how exciting learning can be when you actually care about the thing you're trying to figure out.

> good human teachers who have time to actually get to know him.

people who notice when he's frustrated, challenge him when he's taking the easy way out, and introduce him to things he wouldn't have discovered on his own.

> a LOT of time around other kids.

yes, AI will make homeschooling incredibly good academically. but a huge part of school is learning how to be around other humans.

making friends, disagreeing without being an asshole, learning humility ,surviving embarassing moments. you have to actually live through that stuff

i'm hoping we have a lot more schools like this to choose from by the time he's old enough!

text:
Ben Horowitz on why a16z is incubating The Horowitz Andreessen Academy: the Industrial Revolution remade education. AI will too.

"The university system started out as a religious institution with the Jesuits and so forth. Then the Industrial Revolution came, and all of a sudden everybody needed a higher level of the ability to learn things, the ability to be literate."

"The university system exploded in the US. The universities got much bigger, and there became many more of them."

"That was really necessary to train the population to enter the corporate world. It's hard for people to understand now, but in 1700 there was no corporate world. There was a farm world, and then all of a sudden we get these companies."

"To exist in that environment, you've got to be able to read and write and do math... To a large extent, the America that we have was built on the backs of our great universities."

"We're hitting the AI revolution now, which is going to be, in our estimation, as transformational in terms of jobs, the way jobs are done, and the kinds of jobs that are available, as the Industrial Revolution was to the agricultural society that came before it."

"The idea that the training for the Industrial Revolution is going to map into the AI revolution, probably not perfectly. There needs to be a pioneer that shows the way: How do you train somebody into the new world?"

text:
看到有人说佣人文化是腐朽的封建思想，自愿跨境被雇佣且有劳工保障和法定假期的不叫封建，你以为是大清的宫女去了就回不来了了～

为什么像新加坡，香港这种高度现代化金融中心会把佣人文化保存和延续的这么好？对于新加坡来说，引进廉价的外籍家政工人可以让这些地方的人，特别是女性从繁重的家务琐事中解放出来，更多的参与到工作继而促进本国的经济。这是一种高度实用主义，双方获益，菲佣和印尼佣人可以拿到比本国更高的薪水，养活一大家子人。因为这种文化的根深，她们也是最有边界感的家政工人，同意敏感词就是主仆意识。

当你自己上有老下有小还要在高竞争环境下挣钱的时候，你就能体会到这种住家工人的必要性，在香港，有孩子的双职工家庭大部分都会请佣人，香港寸土寸金，但即使是一家4口挤2室一厅，也会挤一个佣人房出来。

冠冕堂皇说人生在世人人平等没有高低贵贱之分的，钱多的请钱少的做事不等于高低贵贱，社会分工各取所需，去到那个环境有条件你也得请。
author: peng_hellen
quoted_text:
在港澳，新加坡，马来西亚一些东南亚地区让我很“羡慕”的一点就是他们成熟的佣人文化。不管是菲佣还是印尼佣大多会经过专业培训，基本都会英语和简单的粤语，会煮符合当地口味的家常菜，吃饭的时候不上主人的桌子，不参与家庭的任何话题，有天然的主仆意识，有一些还会建立起浓厚的主仆情谊，在一个家庭一干可以是几十年，带大两代人。

十几年前我在港澳住过一段时间，当时用过一个印尼佣人，她会煲地道的西洋菜汤和青红萝卜猪骨汤，第一次见我会用广东话叫我太太，我猜她压根就不知道太太是什么意思，只是机械性的把家里的女主人称为太太。

来澳洲之后我时常会怀念有佣人帮手，把我从繁琐的家务中抽离的日子，但确实羡慕不来，一是人工太高，香港请佣人现在一个月大约6000港币，新加坡一个月800新币，一般中产阶级完全请的起，而在澳洲按照最低时薪算下来要贵上十倍。

二是澳洲没有这个文化土壤，没有天然高人一等和上下阶层的心里，请人都是请钟点工和清洁人员，他们属于雇员而不是佣人，你只是对等的付钱换服务，相互之间保持着客气和小心翼翼的尊重。下人或者佣人这种字眼和工种，在澳洲这种环境下会让人心里上不适，所以这种羡慕现在我只能加上引号，因为即使给我一个佣人，我大概也无福消受。

前段时间新加坡的好朋友一家四口来澳洲玩，随行就带了一个佣人，家里还有一个佣人在待命。我打趣说：你是没手了吗生活完全不能自理？她笑笑回答：没办法，习惯了。

author: timemoonc
quoted_text:
这个周期的发动机大概已经明确了：收入-销毁-通缩 。

有持续的收入，收入回购自己代币，然后透明销毁。代币上不无限增发，总量固定，形成并能维护这个漂亮的飞轮。

上个周期有收入强的 ENS，也有销毁强的 SHIB，但是这个周期都失效了，因为上面三者是一个循环，只有在一个项目上同时打通才可以。

UNI 经过漫长的拉锯战，终于会robinhood的新战场上打开了回购销毁的新体系，这对于老币来说很不容易。更多的老项目没有那么幸运，要不自身收入很难，要不为了利益的博弈很难推动，无法走出老的循环。

从这点上来说，老币的机会不如新币。不过也正应对了周期的趋势——让老的走，让新的来。

比如 @HyperliquidX  @Lighter_xyz 为代表的新项目，代币经济学设计的更简洁有效，更容易起飞。 

这一轮的新，正是对上一轮旧的积弊的一种清算！

以前协议有了收入，收入是团队可以操控的，代币的持有者基本很难拿到什么红利。

以前回购是一种作秀，回购只是换个项目方的钱包。

以前大部分项目都是每年通胀，大量的抛压留给买入的持币者。

以前主要讲治理，主要讲蓝图。

........

这一轮，收入-销毁-通缩。不要项目方设计复杂的所谓持币赋能，就告诉我项目方有没有持续收入，收入是不是销毁，简单有效。

不增发，大家手里面的币才能不被继续抽血。
持续有收入了，大家手里面的币就能不断增值。
持续销毁了，大家手里面的币就加快升值。

别的不听。

发现了吗？项目方不再能躺平了，收入就是项目方的KPI，需要去市场上PK了，能打的项目被市场慢慢筛选出来了。

这对于行业来说，终于走出了过去几年吃老本看愿景，脱离市场的歧路了。

用巨大的代价换来了今天的起势。

我不知道牛市有没有来，如果把行业看成一个人，过去可怕的地方在于这个人不舒服但确定不了病因，现在确定病因了，只是在试药阶段了，等试到了有效成分，牛市自然就来了。

并且，会更加凶猛。因为，这一轮，太干净了。

text:
预测市场是不是比合约交易更赚钱呢？

预测大赛里，目前第一名盈利在700%左右；而在合约大赛里，第一名盈利在100%。

根据参赛选手们的反馈，会发现预测市场的一个显著优势：

预测市场门槛低，好上手，而且更容易发挥信息优势，更容易将认知变现。

认知高、判断力强，其实在预测市场中更容易赚钱。

合约交易需要管理杠杆、资金费率，对交易技术和风控意识要求很高。

因此，两者适合的人群是完全不一样的。

如果你在某一个领域有自己的认知、信息和判断力，无论是体育、电竞、金融、政经等，都可以在预测市场中充分发挥优势。

如果你更擅长看K线、把握市场变化，那就更适合做合约交易。

text:
Jev-like 모델이 확산되고 있다.
Physical AI가 Agentic System에 통합되는 과정으로 보이기도 한다. 

Matt Mastracci가 공개한 [Core] structured generation mode for DiffusionGemma model (Jev-like)는 구글의 확산 언어 모델 DiffusionGemma를 TypeSafe의 Jev처럼 쓸 수 있게 해 준다. 모델이 글을 자유롭게 써 내려가는 대신, 미리 정한 선택지 중 하나를 고르고 그 확률까지 돌려준다.

원래 DiffusionGemma는 길이가 정해진 토큰 묶음을 한꺼번에 노이즈로 채워 놓고, 여러 번 다듬어 문장을 완성한다. 여기서 토큰 묶음을 캔버스라 한다.

Matt의 패치를 적용하면 클라이언트가 캔버스의 대부분을 미리 채워 보낼 수 있다. 질문 틀과 답 양식은 고정된 토큰으로 두고, 답이 들어갈 자리만 노이즈로 남긴다. 모델은 딱 한 번만 디노이징하고, 그 자리에서 각 선택지가 나올 확률을 읽어 돌려준다. 모델이 문장을 만들지 않으니 결과를 파싱하다 실패할 일이 없고, 답이 선택지를 벗어날 수도 없다.

지금까지의 에이전트는 대부분 느리게 생각하는 시스템이었다. 긴 추론을 거쳐 계획을 세우고, 도구를 부르고, 결과를 다시 글로 정리했다. 하지만 물리 세계에서 움직이는 시스템에는 다른 종류의 판단이 필요하다. 눈앞의 물체가 무엇인지, 지금 멈춰야 하는지, 어느 방향으로 가야 하는지를 수십 ms 안에 정해야 한다. Jev-like 모델은 바로 이 빈자리를 채운다. 질문과 선택지를 받아 한 번에 답과 확률을 내놓는 구조는 반사적인 판단에 가깝다.

DiffusionGemma 기반 구현들이 이 흐름을 앞당기고 있다. 이미지를 직접 입력받고, 카메라 화면을 실시간으로 읽고, 미로나 스네이크 게임처럼 매 순간 다음 행동을 고르는 데모가 잇따라 나왔다. 모두 인식에서 행동으로 이어지는 짧은 제어 루프를 보여 준다. 

장기적으로는 E2E action model과 orchestrator가 결합되는 방식으로 발전할거라 본다.

text:
冲到8.7万山寨开始集体补涨，这轮行情还剩多少安全空间？

这是大家都很关心的问题，特别是踏空的同志！

我认为这轮行情已经走出反弹初期，进入突破加速和资金扩散阶段，暂时没有明确见顶信号，但最舒服的低位已经过去。

当前大致处在整轮反弹的第三步：

第一步，是5.8万-6.7万的恐慌出清，市场不相信底部，筹码却在低位悄悄换手。

第二步，是6.3万-8.2万的趋势修复 bitcoin:native 重新站上中长期均线，空头回补，但多数人仍把上涨当成熊市反抽。

第三步，就是现在从7.5万-8.7万，踏空资金开始追涨，当BTC高位稳定后，资金继续向ETH、SOL和山寨扩散，赚钱效应明显升温。

但第三步既可能通往主升，也可能形成阶段顶部。

如果BTC放量突破8.8万，并且回踩8.5万不破，行情才算进入第四步，后续有机会挑战9万—9.6万。

反过来，如果冲高后跌回8.2万以下，甚至失守8万，那么山寨补涨越疯狂，越要小心这是反弹末端的情绪释放。

从12.62万跌至5.78万美元计算，8.4万美元对应38.2%反弹位，9.2万美元对应50%反弹位，第一道关口已经突破，接下来8.8万-9.2万美元才是真正的压力区。

当前山寨集体补涨，说明风险偏好正在扩散，不过BTC市占率仍接近59%，更像是突破后的资金外溢，还不能直接定义为全面山寨季。

接下来只看几个位置：

守住8.3万-8.4万美元，继续看8.9万-9.2万美元；

跌回8万-8.2万美元，说明突破力度开始减弱；

我的策略不变：趋势继续看多，但现在的赔率，已经没有性价比，操作上我更偏向于短线快进快出！

其实去年就融完了，那会产品也没好，就一直没发。正好最近个人版APP重新上线，想着补个PR也感谢一下。

首先想感谢下投资人们的信任，去年经历了被盗和转型，几乎是从零起步的状态，但大家还是愿意相信和支持我们。

然后是感谢用户和团队的信任，大家一起塑造了我们的产品和品牌。

一年的时间变化很大。团队的变化、市场的变化、产品的变化、我个人的变化。或许有些战略决策能做得更好，而贯穿每一日的选择更是有很多可以复盘的。这一路来，学会了敬畏，感受到了肩上的责任，而最终更需要落实到每一个细节。

赛道很卷，我们也还有很多不完善的地方。想做好一个Fintech产品确实需要踩很多坑，操不少心，筛选更踏实负责的人，而且都需要时间检验和积累。这个行业很难产生爆款，但胜在细水长流，坚持日复一日的优化和持续的平衡，才能最终造就卓越的产品和服务。

正式算下来，我们花了一整年时间重新学习了这个行业，交付了一百多项功能和更新，完善成了一个全方位的金融平台，并且迫不及待地以更快的速度、更低的成本、更稳定可靠的金融系统继续前行。

AI的出现一方面或许会加大贫富差距，但另一方面应该也会让金融平权的进程有彻底的改变。对于大多数人来说，他们需要的不是10-100，而是0-1的那个质变。Infini不会追求那个空中楼阁的建设，但会慢慢思考究竟该如何在差异化的同时真正把这项技术普惠于日常生活。

text:
下一轮 Crypto 超级叙事：机器经济 × 链上资本市场 × 信任基础设施

Machine Economy × Onchain Capital Markets × Trust Infrastructure

真正改变一个 Crypto 周期的大叙事，通常不是等牛市来了才诞生。

它往往提前 1—2 年，以一个不起眼的新技术、新协议或新标准出现。

2018 年 DeFi 概念开始成形，2020 年迎来 DeFi Summer。

2023 年初 Ordinals 正式上线比特币主网，随后铭文、BRC-20、Runes 等陆续爆发。

所以现在真正值得研究的问题不是：

下一轮什么币会涨？

而是：

2025—2026 年，究竟出现了哪些今天还不起眼，却可能改变下一轮 Crypto 周期的新技术原语？

目前我认为最值得持续追踪的潜在超级叙事，是三股力量正在发生交汇：

Machine Economy

× Onchain Capital Markets

× Trust Infrastructure

也就是：

机器经济 × 链上资本市场 × 机器信任基础设施。

⸻

第一条暗线：AI 从“工具”变成“经济主体”

过去的 AI，本质上仍然是工具。

人类下达命令，AI 完成任务。

但 Agent 时代正在发生一个根本变化：

AI 开始拥有独立参与经济活动的能力。

未来一个 AI Agent 可以拥有：

自己的身份；
自己的钱包；
自己的资产；
自己的信誉；
自主支付能力；
自主购买数据、API 与算力；
为其他人或 Agent 提供服务并获得收入；
自主管理和配置资产。

围绕这一变化，一批新的基础设施正在出现：

ERC-8004 → Agent 身份、信誉与验证

x402 / MPP → Machine Payments

Agent Wallet / Smart Account → 机器账户

Stablecoin → 机器原生结算货币

于是，一个以前不存在的经济闭环开始形成：

身份 → 钱包 → 支付 → 服务 → 收入 → 资产

AI 不再只是帮助人类工作的软件。

它正在逐渐成为一种新的：

数字经济主体。

⸻

第二条暗线：全球资本市场正在上链

与此同时，另外一场变化也正在发生。

Stablecoin 只是资产上链的第一阶段。

未来进入区块链的可能包括：

美股、国债、基金、黄金、商品、房地产权益、私人信贷、企业债以及更多现实世界资产。

这就是 RWA、Tokenized Assets、Tokenized Equities、StocksFi 背后真正重要的变化。

如果只把 StocksFi 理解成：

“以后可以在链上炒美股。”

其实严重低估了它的意义。

真正重要的是：

全球资产正在逐渐变成机器可读取、可交易、可组合、可编程、可结算的金融对象。

传统金融资产大量存在于银行、券商、基金公司以及不同国家相互割裂的数据库和清算体系中。

Tokenization 则可能把越来越多资产转化为智能合约能够直接调用的数字资产。

这意味着：

AI Agent 不仅开始拥有钱，而且开始拥有一个可以自主投资的全球资产市场。

⸻

第三条暗线：机器世界必然需要自己的“信用体系”

这一层可能是未来最容易被低估的基础设施。

假设未来存在数亿甚至数十亿个 Agent，它们彼此交易、购买服务、管理资金。

一个最基本的问题马上出现：

我凭什么相信你？

这个 Agent 是谁？

过去完成过什么任务？

有没有违约？

有没有欺诈？

它提供的数据是真的吗？

它执行的 AI 模型可信吗？

我敢不敢把 100 美元交给它？

如果是 100 万美元呢？

因此，Agent Economy 真正规模化以后，支付之后必然出现信用。

未来可能形成这样一条产业链：

Agent Identity

↓

Agent Reputation

↓

Validation / Attestation

↓

可验证履约记录

↓

Economic Graph

↓

Agent Credit

↓

Agent Lending / Insurance

↓

Machine Capital Markets

ERC-8004 可能只是这个体系非常早期的一块拼图。

未来真正重要的基础设施，很可能包括：

Reputation、TEE、zkML、Attestation、Stake-secured Verification、Economic Graph、Agent Credit。

换句话说：

今天我们看到的是：

机器拥有钱包。

下一阶段可能是：

机器拥有信用。

一旦机器能够形成自己的信用记录，它就可能进一步拥有：

融资能力、借贷能力、保险能力以及资产负债表。

这才是真正意义上的机器金融体系。

⸻

三条暗线最终会在哪里交汇？

未来一个完整的 AI Agent 可能这样运行：

获得链上身份

↓

建立 Reputation / Credit

↓

拥有 Agent Wallet

↓

持有 Stablecoin

↓

通过 x402 / MPP 等协议自主支付

↓

购买数据、算力、API 和其他 Agent 服务

↓

向人类或其他 Agent 提供服务

↓

获得 Stablecoin 收入

↓

进入 Agentic Vault

↓

自动配置资产

↓

美股 / 国债 / 黄金 / RWA / Crypto / DeFi

↓

链上完成交易与结算

↓

履约记录继续积累 Reputation

↓

获得更高信用与融资能力

↓

继续扩大经济活动

最终形成一个完整闭环：

身份 → 信用 → 钱 → 收入 → 投资 → 资产 → 融资 → 再生产

这时候，区块链可能第一次出现除人类之外的第二类大规模经济用户：

AI Agent。

⸻

Stablecoin 的角色也可能因此发生改变

Stablecoin 第一阶段，是：

Crypto 世界里的美元。

第二阶段，是：

全球互联网支付工具。

Recently, Michael Kong(@michaelfkong) posted that “@soniclabs published a notice stating that my relationship with the company had been ‘terminated with immediate effect.’”
This is the same kind of message that I received in April 2019 from Michael Kong of the Fantom Foundation, now Sonic Labs. At that time, the Fantom Foundation informed me that “all relationships with Byung-Ik Ahn and Korea had been terminated.”
Fantom Coin (FTM), now Sonic’s S token, was originally a Korean project that I conceived and planned from the beginning in early 2018. I wrote the whitepaper, designed the technical algorithm, and created the project with the intention of using it within Korea’s food-tech ecosystem.
Michael Kong and the Australian team, including David Richardson and Steve Bellotti of DCH/TCM, were originally advisers who were supposed to help me with ICO consulting and the establishment of an overseas legal entity. In March 2018, I entered into a consulting agreement with them for that purpose.
However, in June 2018, when the Fantom Foundation was established and it appeared that the ICO would be successful and that the value of the token could rise, the Australian team deceived me, the other team members, and investors, and secretly appointed David Richardson, rather than me, as the founder.
They also created an extraordinary governance structure in which the founder was given extremely powerful authority, including the right to remove directors.
At the same time, however, they publicly presented me, Byung-Ik Ahn, as the founder.
On the Fantom website, they listed me, Byung-Ik Ahn, as the founder. Even after forcing me out in early 2019, they continued to promote me as the founder on the website until the end of 2019, and they continued to use the whitepaper that I had created.
When FTM was listed on Bibox in September 2018, it was listed with Byung-Ik Ahn identified as the founder. When FTM was later listed on Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, in 2019, I was again identified as the founder. Even today, Binance’s Fantom Coin information page still lists Byung-Ik Ahn as the founder.
In other words, an ICO advisory firm that had entered into a consulting agreement with me ended up becoming the party controlling the Fantom Foundation.
In my view, this was clearly fraudulent conduct intended from the beginning to take away the foundation that I had intended to create and to obtain control over the operation of Fantom Coin.
The Australian team, including Michael Kong, who I believe engaged in this conduct, is currently under investigation for alleged fraud by the Virtual Asset Joint Investigation Unit of the Seoul Southern District Prosecutors’ Office in Korea.
However, Michael Kong and the other members of the Australian team have instructed their Korean legal representatives to handle only the civil litigation, while they themselves have not entered Korea and have avoided appearing for questioning by Korean prosecutors.
In July last year, Sonic Foundation posted an announcement on X regarding a standalone meetup event in Seoul, stating that Foundation CEO Michael Kong would attend the event. However, he did not actually visit Korea and, as a result, did not appear for questioning by prosecutors.
Related article:
 https://t.co/2lfHADIueZ
Moreover, they instead attacked me and portrayed me as an unethical person.
I have never acted unethically.
I only wanted the project to succeed, and I did everything I could for that purpose.
However, in early 2019, they forced me out and stopped providing support to the Fantom Foundation’s Korean office, causing more than a dozen employees who had been working in Korea to lose their jobs. They also engaged in abnormal actions such as shutting down email access.
The algorithm I created was not plagiarism.
Technological advancement is achieved by modifying and improving existing technologies.
If similarity alone is enough to call something plagiarism, then virtually every technology in the world would have to be considered plagiarism.
I simply developed the existing theory one step further.
Michael, if you claim that the Lachesis algorithm was plagiarized, why did you keep the technical whitepaper containing that algorithm on the website for such a long time?
And why did Fantom continue publishing papers that modified and developed that algorithm?
A mainnet is something that is completed over at least three to five years following an ICO.
Yet they claim that I failed to develop it.
They say this even though they took away all of my development authority immediately after the ICO.
If they had not forced me out and had allowed me to retain development authority, I would certainly have completed it properly.
And I would have applied it to Korea’s food-tech ecosystem and used it there, exactly as I had originally intended.
So what, then, did Michael Kong actually build properly while serving as CEO?
Did he complete the DAG mainnet?
Is there any proper, real-world use case?
Or has the project simply continued announcing project after project while focusing primarily on increasing the value of the token?
Michael Kong boasts that he almost single-handedly led the company to victory in the approximately $150 million lawsuit against me in Korea.
Yet this came after forcing out the founder, taking control of the Foundation, and then continuing for a substantial period to mislead the public by presenting Byung-Ik Ahn as the founder, including when listing the token on Binance and other exchanges.
These were, in my view, deliberate and malicious actions.
And this happened while I was not even paid the legitimate share of tokens that I was supposed to receive.
In fact, I did not properly receive the tokens that I was entitled to, while Michael Kong and the Australian team associated with TCM received the entire 10% allocation of the total Fantom Coin supply, amounting to 317.5 million FTM.
The previous lawsuit was deeply problematic.
There were also aspects of the case that I did not handle well in my own response.
However, during the court proceedings, the Australian team made a substantial number of false claims.
I firmly believe that the truth will eventually be revealed.
For that reason, new proceedings are now underway in the Seoul Central District Court in Korea.
I intend to fight this matter to the end for justice and for what is right.
I believe that justice will ultimately prevail.
Even now, I hope that Michael Kong, David Richardson, and Steve Bellotti will apologize for their wrongdoing and restore matters to what they should have been.
And if they truly believe that they acted properly and have nothing to hide, then I ask them to come to Korea and face the prosecutors head-on.
The Korean prosecutors are waiting for them to come to Korea.
Why can you not come to Korea?
If you truly have nothing to hide, come to Korea and face the prosecutors head-on.
